6.5.5. Altering a certified voucher invalidates the certification. A DO who determines that a certified payment voucher is improper must return it for correction and a new certification. However, post-payment printing and scanning of paid vouchers that were properly certified electronically do not invalidate the original certifications.

6.5.6. Translation of accounting data for a certified voucher is acceptable as long as the correct appropriation or funds involved align with the appropriation or funds cited on the legal obligation to make the payment (e.g., a contract). The translation process must be auditable and reliable, so the certified line of accounting can be mapped to the translated line of accounting. See Volume 1 for more on data translation. DOs and COs may rely on data from reliable automated systems certified as FFMIA-compliant.

6.6    RANDOM REVIEW OF DISBURSEMENT VOUCHERS

6.6.1. Payment review officials are not subject to pecuniary liability because they are not in accountable positions. State their responsibilities in their position descriptions and performance standards, or appoint them by means other than a DD 577.

6.6.2. Examination Requirements

6.6.2.1. Title 7 of the GAO Manual, which implements 31 U.S.C. § 3521(b)(1), requires pre-payment examination of payments over $2,500. For payments of $2,500 or less, statistical sampling procedures may be used instead of examining all payments (see subparagraph 6.6.3). Several publications provide guidance on statistical sampling and pre- and post-payment reviews, including GAO/Accounting and Information Management Division report 21.3.2 (May 2000), Streamlining the Payment Process While Maintaining Effective Internal Control; OMB Circular No. A-123, Management's Responsibility for Enterprise Risk Management and Internal Control; and Appendix C to OMB A-123, Requirements for Effective Estimation and Remediation of Improper Payments. GAO reports provide examples for the pre- and post-payment phases, but no single procedure suits every type of disbursing system.

6.6.2.2. Pre-payment reviews may occur any time before payment, at the stage of the voucher-preparation process management judges most appropriate. These reviews ensure vouchers are substantiated by documentation for lawful and proper payment; under manual processing systems, they include verifying the accuracy of computation.

6.6.2.3. Pre-payment review officials who determine that proposed or actual certified payments are of questionable legality, propriety, or correctness must send inquiries to the COs challenging the decision to certify those payments and must keep files of these inquiries and any received from other sources. Inquiries must be resolved within 30 days.

6.6.3. Statistical Sampling Plans

6.6.3.1. DoW Components may use statistical sampling plans for vouchers not exceeding $2,500. Agencies must establish their own dollar limitations within that maximum, based on a cost/benefit analysis of their voucher-examining operations. A CO who uses an approved pre-payment statistical sampling procedure and reviews only the sampled vouchers as a basis for certification must identify the vouchers selected for review. A DoW Component that determines an alternate voucher-examining plan is required must send a written request through the Director, DFAS, to the USD(C) for approval under subparagraph 6.6.3.3. The request must identify the reason for the alternate plan, including a description of the plan, alternate statistical sampling procedures, and a business case showing savings without jeopardizing the Government's interest.

6.6.3.2. Sampling plans must be statistically valid and adhere to technical guidelines in professional Federal and non-Federal texts and publications. Each plan must include the purpose, scope, review frequency, a definition of the population from which the sample will be selected, the sample size and element selection method, procedures to analyze the sampled records, and methods to document and report the results. Sampling plans require review and approval (in most cases, original preparation) by qualified statisticians before submission for final approval. Review and update them periodically to reflect the most recent occurrence-rate trends and to allow population estimates within predetermined sampling probability and precision levels.

6.6.3.3. The Director, DFAS, or designee approves statistical sampling plans for payment vouchers DFAS processes and ensures their implementation at locations for which DFAS is responsible. The USD(C) approves statistical sampling plans for other DoW Components, whose officials ensure implementation.

6.7    PECUNIARY LIABILITY

6.7.1. COs and DOs, but not DAOs, are automatically pecuniarily liable when a fiscal irregularity occurs, based on the "presumption of negligence" under 31 U.S.C. § 3527. A fiscal irregularity is either a physical loss of cash, vouchers, negotiable instruments, or supporting documents, or an erroneous (e.g., illegal, improper, or incorrect) payment. Physical losses generally apply only to DOs and their agents. Under 28 U.S.C. § 2512, DOs must prove they were neither negligent nor the proximate cause of the irregularity to gain relief of liability. See Section
7.0    for policy on relief and liability of accountable officers.

6.7.1.1. Under 31 U.S.C. § 3325, DOs are pecuniarily liable for payments not made per the vouchers certified to them and for errors in their accounts. DOs who make payments per the certifications of properly appointed COs may be relieved of their liability.

6.7.1.2. Under 31 U.S.C. § 3528, COs are pecuniarily liable for payments resulting from improper certifications.

6.7.1.3. DAOs are not subject to the presumption of negligence but may be held pecuniarily liable under 10 U.S.C. § 2773a(c) for illegal, improper, or incorrect payments resulting from information, data, or services they negligently provide to COs and on which the COs relied to certify payment vouchers. A DAO's pecuniary liability for such losses to the U.S. may be individual or joint and several with that of other liable U.S. officers, employees, or members of the uniformed services.

6.7.2. Under 31 U.S.C. § 3521(c), COs and DOs who pursue diligent collection action are not pecuniarily liable for payments on vouchers in a population subject to sampling but not reviewed. See Section 7.0, paragraph 7.5, for a fraudulent or suspected fraudulent payment.

title: Section 7.0: Physical Losses of Funds, Erroneous Payments, and Overages
content:
7.0    PHYSICAL LOSSES OF FUNDS, ERRONEOUS PAYMENTS, AND OVERAGES

7.1    GENERAL

7.1.1. An accountable official is a member of the U.S. Armed Forces or a DoW civilian employee responsible for or having custody of government funds. Accountable officials include certifying officers and departmental accountable officials (DAO) and disbursing officers (DOs), deputy DOs (DDOs), cashiers, imprest fund cashiers, change fund custodians, paying agents, and collection agents. Accountable officials are personally liable for the physical loss or improper payment of funds for which they are accountable unless granted relief. The Secretary of War decision to grant or deny relief is binding. The Secretary of War has delegated authority to the Director, DFAS, to determine whether to grant or deny all requests for relief of liability, and the Director, DFAS, has re-delegated this authority to the Director of Strategy, Policy and Requirements (DFAS-ZP).

7.1.2. All accountable officials are subject to the pecuniary liability standard under Title 31, U.S.C. Except for the DAO, an accountable official's basic legal liability arises automatically by virtue of the loss, regardless of fault or negligence. Relief is a separate process that considers the official's lack of fault or negligence, to the extent authorized by the following:

7.2    DEFINITIONS

7.2.1. A physical LoF can be minor or major. A minor loss is a physical loss of less than $750 without evidence of theft or fraud within the disbursing office.

7.3    DISCOVERY OF PHYSICAL LOSS OR ERRONEOUS PAYMENT

Any person who believes an official entrusted with public funds is misusing those funds, or who suspects a fraudulent erroneous payment, must notify the Commander having jurisdiction over the alleged offender within 24 hours of discovery. A physical LoF does not initially affect the DO's Cash Treasury Account Symbol (TAS). The LoF is maintained as part of the DO's accountability and does not affect that balance until recovery, recoupment, or relief of liability is granted.

7.4    PHYSICAL LOSSES

7.4.1. Responsibilities

7.4.1.1. On notification of a possible loss, the DO must:

7.4.1.1.1. Report the loss in writing to the Commander if the loss is not resolved within 24 hours of discovery and is a major physical loss; and

7.4.1.1.2. Request the Commander to direct an immediate audit of all disbursing assets by a Cash Verification Team, per Appendix A, to confirm that a loss has occurred.

7.4.1.2. On notification of a possible loss, the Commander must request that the Cash Verification Team audit the DO's account. If the discrepancy is not resolved and qualifies as a major LoF, report the loss to the DFAS LoF Team within 24 hours, sent to the Disbursing Policy mailbox (dfas.indianapolis-in.zpf.mbx.disbursingdebtmanagementpolicy@mail.mil) or by mail to the LoF Team, DFAS Accounting and Finance Policy Division, DFAS Indianapolis (DFAS-ZPTC), Location 211X, 8899 E. 56th Street, Indianapolis, IN 46249. When the Commander commands the DDO, agent, or cashier, a copy of the report must be provided to the
DO.

7.4.2. Accounting for Physical LoF

7.4.2.1. All physical losses, major or minor, discovered in the DO's account, including those incurred by deputies, agents, cashiers, imprest fund cashiers, and change fund custodians, must be recorded on the DD 2657 using an Optional Form (OF) 1017-G, Journal Voucher, to document the movement of money from one line to another. All losses must continue to be shown on the DD 2657 and the Standard Form (SF) 1219, Statement of Accountability, until the loss is recovered, recouped, or relief of liability is granted. Foreign currency loss must be converted and recorded in U.S. Dollar equivalent (USDE) using the exchange rate at the time the loss occurred.

7.4.2.2. Forward the DD 2667 to the LoF Team within 5 calendar days after the end of each month, sent to the Disbursing Policy mailbox (dfas.indianapolis-in.zpf.mbx.disbursingdebtmanagementpolicy@mail.mil) or by mail to the LoF Team, DFAS Accounting and Finance Policy Division, DFAS Indianapolis (DFAS-ZPTC), Location 220V, 8899 E. 56th Street, Indianapolis, IN 46249.

7.4.2.3. Physical losses of funds incurred by DDOs, disbursing agents, cashiers, paying agents, collection agents, imprest fund cashiers, or change fund custodians are physical losses within the agent's accountability documents. The DO must be notified of all physical losses as soon as possible, must reduce the DD 2657 for that agent, and must record the loss on the cumulative DD 2667.

7.4.2.4. For a change fund or imprest fund loss, the DO must record the amount of the loss on the DD 2667 and DD 2657.

7.4.2.5. For a counterfeit currency loss, the DO must record the amount of the loss on the DD 2667 and DD 2657.

7.4.3. An investigation is required for all physical LoF unless the loss is recouped, recovered, or paid back.

7.4.3.1. The type of loss determines the type of investigation required.

7.4.3.1.1. For a loss of $300 or less with no fraud, the DO or DDO (if the DO is not co-located with the DDO) conducts the investigation and completes the written investigatory report. If the loss is attributable to the DO, the primary DDO conducts the investigation and the report. Under no circumstances may the official incurring the loss prepare their own written investigatory report. In all cases, the report must be completed and submitted to the DFAS LoF Team within 30 days from discovery of the loss.

7.4.3.1.2. For a loss over $300 with no fraud, the Commander must appoint an IO to conduct the investigation and complete the written investigatory report. The appointed official must be someone other than the DO or disbursing office personnel (for example, a member of the Cash Verification Team) and must have knowledge of disbursing office operations, especially the required internal controls, pertinent laws, and applicable directives. In all cases, the report must be completed and submitted through the Commander to the DFAS LoF Team within 30 days from discovery of the loss.

7.4.3.1.3. An IO must be appointed to conduct a formal investigation of a major physical loss.

7.4.3.1.3.1. The following individuals have the authority to appoint an IO: the Commander of the DO who incurred the loss; and for DFAS sites, the Director of the DO who incurred the loss.

7.4.3.1.3.1.1. When the accountable official and the DO are not in the same location, the Commander over the accountable official must appoint the IO.

7.4.3.1.3.1.2. When the Commander is not authorized to convene an investigation, the Commander must request an investigation through the chain of command.

7.4.3.1.3.2. The Commander must provide a copy of the official appointment notification to the DFAS LoF Team within 5 days of appointment.

7.4.3.1.3.2.1. The investigation must be completed and submitted to the DFAS LoF Team within 90 days from discovery of the loss.

7.4.3.1.3.3. An IO must be a commissioned officer (O-3 or above) or a civilian employee senior in rank or grade to the person(s) under investigation and must:

7.4.3.1.3.3.1. Not have a vested interest in the outcome of the investigation.

7.4.3.1.3.3.2. Not be in the chain of command of the DO or accountable officials involved in the irregularity; and

7.4.3.1.3.3.3. Have knowledge of financial accounting controls and pertinent laws and directives. Use Comptroller personnel only when there is no feasible alternative to appoint an IO from another organizational element. The comptroller, staff judge advocate, or DFAS Office of General Counsel (DFAS-HG) must provide technical guidance to IOs who lack extensive investigative or financial backgrounds.

7.4.3.1.3.4. If the IO recommends denial of relief to the DO or any other accountable official(s) pecuniarily liable for the loss, the IO must provide a copy of the report to those officials.

7.4.3.1.3.5. The IO must report the status of the investigation every 30 days through the Commander to the DFAS LoF Team.

7.4.3.1.3.6. When extraordinary circumstances require an extension to complete the ROI, the IO may request an extension from the Commander. The Commander must notify the DFAS LoF Team of any authorized extensions.

7.4.3.1.3.7. Unless granted an extension, the IO must submit the ROI through the Commander (who appointed the IO) to the DFAS LoF Team within 90 days after discovering the loss.

7.4.3.1.3.8. Upon receiving the ROI from the IO, the Commander must:

7.4.3.1.3.8.1. Immediately review the ROI for compliance;

7.4.3.1.3.8.2. Determine if the ROI is complete; if not, return it to the IO explaining the discrepancies and request further documentation or information. The Commander must notify the DFAS LoF Team if the ROI cannot be completed and submitted within 90 days from discovery of the loss.

7.4.3.1.3.8.3. The Commander must forward to the DFAS LoF Team any documentation or information that becomes available after the ROI has been forwarded. If there is evidence of fraudulent or wrongful conduct under investigation by authorized law enforcement, the investigative entities may request the Commander to withhold the report until their investigation is complete. If so, the Commander must continue to follow up on the status of their investigation and advise the DFAS LoF Team of the status every 30 days. Copies of the investigative reports may be added as exhibits before forwarding the report through the chain of command to DFAS.

7.4.3.2. DFAS LoF Team (DFAS-ZPTC) must

7.4.3.2.1. Review the ROI upon receipt; and

7.4.3.2.2. Forward the final decision to the appropriate individuals and, where individuals are held liable, must inform them of their right to submit a rebuttal.

7.4.4. Funding

7.4.4.1. Appropriated funds must be made available to remove the deficiency from the DO's SF 1219 if the losses are not recovered. This includes when relief of liability is denied and recoupment cannot be made from the accountable official, or when relief of liability is granted.

7.4.4.1.1. If the accountable official responsible for the LoF was a DFAS employee or a military member assigned to DFAS when the loss occurred, DFAS must identify the necessary appropriation and funding to resolve the loss.

7.4.4.1.2. If the accountable official responsible for the LoF was a military member or employee of another DoW Component when the loss occurred, that DoW Component must identify the necessary appropriation and funding to resolve the loss.

7.4.4.2. The DO must clear the LoF from the DD 2667 and DD 2657 based on the instructions given by DFAS.

7.5    ERRONEOUS PAYMENTS (ILLEGAL, INCORRECT, AND IMPROPER)

7.5.1. Responsibilities

7.5.1.1. Upon notification of a fraudulent or suspected fraudulent erroneous payment, the Commander must:

7.5.1.1.1. Notify the DFAS LoF Team within 24 hours of notification, through the chain of command;

7.5.1.1.2. Appoint an IO to conduct a formal investigation;

7.5.1.1.3. Ensure the investigation is completed and forwarded to the DFAS LoF Team within 90 days from the appointment of the IO.

7.5.1.2. Upon notification of a fraudulent or suspected fraudulent erroneous payment, the DO must:

7.5.1.2.1. Determine if the erroneous payment occurred due to fraudulent actions of accountable officials under the direct cognizance or control of the DO and, if so, prepare a DD Form 1131, Cash Collection Voucher, transferring the amount of the fraudulent payment back into the appropriation from which it disbursed, increase the DD 2657 if the loss is a predecessor loss, and record the loss on the DD 2667.

7.5.1.2.2. If the erroneous payment occurred due to fraudulent actions of individuals not under the direct cognizance or control of the DO, the payment(s) must remain charged to the appropriation originally charged.

7.5.1.3. Upon notification of an erroneous payment, the certifying officer must:

7.5.1.3.1. Ensure collection action is taken against the recipient of the payment, per Volume 16. This may require submission of the debt to the DO or other responsible area.

7.5.1.3.2. Notify the Commander if the recipient of the erroneous payment does not voluntarily repay the amount owed.

7.5.1.4. The DO does not need to take any action if the erroneous payment was properly certified.

7.5.1.5. If the erroneous payment was not properly certified:

7.5.1.5.1. The DO must ensure collection action is taken against the recipient of the payment, per Volume 16. This may require submission of the debt to another responsible area. If the erroneous payment is recouped from the recipient, collect the proceeds into the appropriation originally charged, unless the appropriation is canceled. If the appropriation is canceled, refer to Volume 4 for disposition of the collection.

7.5.1.6. Upon notification of an erroneous payment, the Commander must:

7.5.1.6.1. Determine whether a formal or an informal investigation is required;

7.5.1.6.2. Appoint an IO; and

7.5.1.6.3. Ensure the investigation is completed and submitted to the DFAS LoF Team.

7.5.2. Investigation of Erroneous Payments

7.5.2.1. Formal investigations are required when:

7.5.2.1.1. Fraud is suspected on the part of the payee, disbursing office personnel, certifying officer, or any other accountable official; or

7.5.2.1.2. The Commander determines it to be necessary.

7.5.2.2. The investigation must be submitted to the DFAS LoF Team through the Commander who appointed the IO within 90 days of the IO's appointment.

7.5.2.3. The IO must prepare investigatory comments.

7.5.2.4. The investigation must be submitted to the DFAS LoF Team within 60 days of the Commander's notification of the erroneous payment.

7.5.3. When feasible, all actions required to reach a determination of liability for a LoF due to an erroneous payment should be completed within 3 years after the SF 1219 is certified.

7.5.4. Generally, the DO will not carry an erroneous payment as a LoF on the SF 1219, because an appropriation was charged when the payment was disbursed. Exceptions to this general rule occur when Treasury applies check-issue overdrafts against a disbursing station symbol number, or when an accountable official under the direct cognizance or control of the DO made a fraudulent payment.

7.5.4.1. If the erroneous payment is recovered from the recipient, credit the amount recouped or collected to the appropriation initially charged, unless the appropriation is canceled. Refer to Volume 4 for disposition of the collection of a canceled appropriation.

7.5.4.2. If the erroneous payment cannot be recovered from the recipient and relief of liability has been denied, the loss must be collected from the DO, certifying officer, and/or accountable official(s) involved. Credit the collection proceeds to the appropriation originally charged unless the appropriation is canceled. For disposition of the collection of a canceled appropriation, refer to Volume 4.

7.5.4.3. The amount of the erroneous payment must remain charged to the appropriation it originated from when: relief of liability is granted, or recovery attempts from the recipient are unsuccessful.

7.5.4.4. If an adjustment to the appropriation account to which the payment was charged is necessary, the amount of the erroneous payment must be charged as stated in 31 U.S.C. § 3527(d)(1).

7.5.5. Retain all documents with the facts of the case to ensure proper response to audits conducted by the Government Accountability Office.

7.6    REQUEST FOR RELIEF

7.6.1. Requests for relief must be in the form of a memorandum and submitted within 30 days after the investigation is completed. A copy of the IO's report must be attached to the request for relief. Erroneous payments paid through the Treasury Direct Disbursing process follow the same process as those paid through a DoW disbursing office. Accountable officials must submit their request for relief as follows.

7.6.1.1. DOs. Submit the request for relief through the Commander or DFAS site director to the DFAS LoF Team.

7.6.1.2. DOs Settling Accounts of Former DOs. Submit the request for relief on behalf of a former DO to the DFAS LoF Team.

7.6.1.3. DDOs, Disbursing Agents, Cashiers, Certifiers. Submit requests for relief through the DO responsible for the account to the DFAS LoF Team.

7.6.2. Evidence Required for Granting Relief

7.6.2.1. An accountable official is strictly liable for any erroneous payment or physical LoF placed in the official's care, subject to relief of liability. If the Government establishes that a loss has occurred, strict liability applies to the accountable official involved. The accountable official bears the burden of proving that it is more likely than not that the official: was not negligent; or official’s fault or negligence was not the proximate cause of the loss.

7.6.2.2. Generally, the findings of a related court of inquiry, investigation, court-martial, or other proceedings (including endorsements) will provide the information required for the loss. When such information is not available, the requestor must supply the required information for consideration in the request for relief and/or the forwarding endorsements. Failure to include all required information could contribute to unfavorable consideration of a request for relief.

7.6.2.3. Each addressee in the requestor's chain of command (including the DO) must provide a forwarding endorsement. The endorsement must include a specific opinion as to whether the loss occurred while the accountable official was in the line of duty and regarding fault or negligence, and a specific recommendation on granting or denying relief.

7.6.3. The general authority to relieve accountable officials from liability of a physical loss is stipulated in 31 U.S.C. § 3527.

7.6.4. The general authority to relieve accountable officials from liability of an erroneous payment is stipulated in 31 U.S.C. § 3527(b)(1)(B), which incorporates by reference 31 U.S.C. § 3528(b)(1)..

7.7    DECISIONS ON LIABILITY

7.7.1. If relief is granted, the DFAS LoF Team will provide a memorandum with instructions for removing the deficiency or authority to leave the payment charged to the original appropriation.

7.7.2. If relief is denied, the DFAS LoF Team will advise the accountable official(s) of the decision and of their right to submit a rebuttal. The rebuttal must be submitted to the DFAS LoF Team within 30 days of notification of the adverse determination. Based on the additional information received, the team will recommend to the Director, Strategy, Policy and Requirements, through the DFAS Office of General Counsel, whether to affirm or reverse the previous decision.

7.7.2.1. If the decision is reversed, the DFAS LoF Team will advise the accountable official(s) accordingly and provide the DO instructions for removal of the LoF or authority to leave the payment charged to the original appropriation.

7.7.2.2. If the decision stands, the DFAS LoF Team will advise the Commander and/or DO to take immediate collection action against the accountable official(s). Cash recouped from a loss and retained for future operating use does not impact the DO Cash TAS balance. Volume 16 provides guidance for completing collection of irregularities.

7.8    OVERAGES OF PUBLIC FUNDS

7.8.1. Do not offset an overage of funds against a physical LoF unless the relation between the two is obvious (e.g., foreign currency on hand is short and U.S. currency on hand is over by equal USDE amounts). Do not offset overages against shortages if the shortage and overage occur on different business days. An overage of funds must be collected into the DO's accountability and reported by CTA transactions to Treasury's Budget Clearing Account (Suspense), F3875, citing the collection Business Event Type Code (BETC) along with the DO Cash TAS/BETC. If the proper location of the overage cannot be determined, the overage must be transferred to Treasury's Forfeiture of Unclaimed Money and Property, R1060, using a CTA transaction. Track overages by recording each occurrence on a separate DD 2667, maintained specifically for overages. Start a new DD 2667 for overages at the beginning of each quarter.

7.8.2. Overages of funds that are $750 or more must be reported to the Commander. However, unless there is an indication of fraud or other criminal act, there is no requirement to report or investigate as in losses of funds. A copy of the DD 2667 must be retained with the original voucher transferring the funds to the R1060 account.

title: Section 8.0: U.S. Treasury Checks
content:
8.0    U.S. TREASURY CHECKS

8.1    POLICY

8.1.1. Drawing and Dating Checks

8.1.1.1. Inscribe checks drawn on the Treasury to the payee by name, or to a financial institution for credit to the named payee's account, except for checks drawn as exchange- for-cash. Never make a check payable to "Cash."

8.1.1.2. DOs must not issue checks in payment of salaries before completion of the service for which payment is made or before the scheduled payday, unless authorized (for example, advance pay). A DoW Component may mail checks to payees before a military or civilian payday to ensure payments are available when due. When mailing a check before payday, do not date it before the scheduled payday. Agencies using this delivery method must have internal controls that alert the DO when a payee becomes ineligible for scheduled pay (for example, unauthorized absence or separation) and ensure pay intercept procedures can be initiated.

8.1.1.3. A check may be drawn to the order of a legal representative of the estate of a deceased person (for example, "John K. Smith, Executor of the estate of James R. Jones"). Do not make a check payable "to the estate of" a decedent or to a deceased person.

8.1.1.4. A check may be drawn to the order of a legally appointed committee, guardian, or other legal representative of a mentally incompetent payee when specifically authorized (see Volumes 7A).

8.1.1.5. The payee may authorize another person to receive a Treasury check by a specific power of attorney that clearly states the holder is entitled to receive the check on the payee's behalf. The person receiving the check signs his or her own name on the voucher followed by "Attorney-in-Fact for" and the name of the person granting the power of attorney. The DO verifies the holder's identity and keeps a copy of the power of attorney. Process payments to a power of attorney holder that require "secret" or "confidential identity" using a cover voucher insert. Transmit a copy of the original voucher and of the power of attorney to the supporting DFAS site for handling and storage.

8.1.1.6. Signing blank checks is prohibited.

8.2    PROCUREMENT OF TREASURY CHECKS

8.2.1. The DFAS Enterprise Solutions and Standards Directorate's Tax and Disbursing Division (DFAS-IN/JTDCO) is the sole check sourcing agency for DoW activities. Contact DFAS-IN/JTDCO for current check formats, the procedure for obtaining check stock, and advice on alternative payment methods (DFAS-IN, 8899 E. 56th Street, Indianapolis, IN 46249-2700; dfas.indianapolis-in.jjf.mbx.ess-disbursing@mail.mil). To ensure continuity of operations, DOs must not allow check stock to fall below a 6-month supply, must seek replenishment at the 9- month level, and a DO at a newly established DSSN must request check stock at least 4 months before disbursing operations begin.

8.2.2. Receipt of Treasury Checks

8.2.2.1. If a check shipment contains more than one check with the same serial number, in addition to notifying DFAS-IN/JTDCO, the DO must destroy each check bearing a duplicate number. Because the remaining checks bearing those serial numbers may be issued normally, do not report the duplicate check serial numbers as zero-dollar amounts in the check issue report. Mark the duplicate numbered checks "Void - Not Negotiable" and destroy them locally within 30 days.

8.2.2.2. If checks are discovered missing during receipt verification or at any time thereafter, notify both DFAS-IN/JTDCO and the nearest DoW Component investigative service for referral and liaison with the U.S. Secret Service (USSS).

8.2.3. Count checks transferred between DOs as part of the relief from disbursing duty process by both the transferring and receiving parties when they are not in the original packages (see Section 3.0, subparagraph 3.4.6.1.3).

8.2.4. Security, Storage, and Issuance of Blank Checks

8.2.4.1. Store blank Treasury checks in a secure container (see Section 4.0, paragraph 4.2) in the DO's or deputy DO's (DDO) safe or under lock and key. The DO or designee ensures storage conditions prevent deterioration of the check surface tint and design, which are sensitive to moisture, light, and heat, and may accept checks of satisfactory color and strength and obtain a replacement supply if deterioration occurs later. Give only one individual primary responsibility for maintaining the check stock and related control records, and limit others' access to occasions when the designated custodian is absent.

8.2.4.2. The DO or designee maintains control of the check stock and is always accountable for it. Under joint custody, the DO or designee ensures no break in accountability occurs, providing access to the check stock during brief or unexpected absences of the individual with normal day-to-day responsibility for it.

8.2.4.2.1. The DO or designee maintains a blank check control log for each series of checks to keep a perpetual inventory of checks on hand and control their release. The DO or designee must examine the log daily to ensure all checks drawn and returned unused are accounted for and that no checks have been removed without authority.

8.2.4.2.2. Use the prescribed blank check control log:

8.2.4.2.2.1. The DO or designee issues blank checks to check writers from the check stock in blocks of appropriate size by serial number and monitors the return of blank, voided, or spoiled checks to the vault. The DO or designee also uses the control log to control issuance and return of checks between the DO and sites external to the disbursing office that prepare checks.

8.2.4.2.2.2. The DO or designee must obtain receipts for checks issued. The designee in charge of working checks must keep a record of checks issued daily to each clerk, examine daily the record of checks drawn and returned unused to account for checks issued, and ensure no checks are removed without authority.

8.2.4.2.2.3. The DO or designee must inventory the check stock at least once every 90 days. Count individually the checks in any open container, and open and individually count any damaged or tampered cartons. Keep a record of the on hand inventory in the disbursing office and provide it to the cash verification team for attachment to the quarterly cash verification report (see Appendix A).

8.2.4.2.3. When blank checks are lost or stolen:

8.2.4.2.3.1. The DO or designee immediately notifies the Commander, the nearest USSS office (by email or telephone), and Fiscal Service at
(304) 480-7777. Confirm by letter to Fiscal Service's Physical Security Branch, 6505 Belcrest Road, Suite 613, Hyattsville, MD 20782, with copies to the USSS, the appropriate DoW Component investigative service, DFAS-IN/JTDCO, and appropriate local banks. Include the DSSN, the ICNs or serial numbers of the checks, complete information on the loss or theft, and the date the loss was referred to the USSS for investigation.

8.2.4.2.3.2. If the loss involves a range of consecutive serially numbered checks, report only the beginning and ending serial numbers of the range. Void all checks discovered missing, lost, or stolen before issuance, and report the circumstances per I TFM 4-5040.20.

8.3    ISSUANCE OF TREASURY CHECKS

8.3.1. Check Preparation

8.3.1.1. Issue checks in strict numeric sequence within each series. Essential check information includes place and date of issue, DSSN, serial number, payee, amount, drawer signature, designation of title, and other identifying information. Do not print legends such as "Salaries and Expenses" or "Drawn for Above Object" on the face of a check. Check explanations (for example, exchange-for-cash or salary) and other special information unique to a disbursing activity may be entered at the bottom of the check to the left of the signature area; keep extraneous data to a minimum. Use spaces on the printed check form only for their intended purposes, and do not leave any space unfilled in a manner that would allow or facilitate alterations or additions that could lead to forgery or fraud.

8.3.1.2. A completed check must have an orderly appearance and good legibility for accurate reading in rapid handling; avoid overprinting, intersecting, and crowding. No check may be issued for more than $99,999,999.99; when the total payment exceeds that amount, issue two or more checks totaling the required payment. No deviation in check writing procedures is permitted unless authority is first obtained from DFAS-IN/JTDCO (see I TFM 4-5000).

8.3.2. Check Print Requirements

8.3.2.1. Data printed or typewritten on checks must be permanent and unaffected by erasure, smudging, moisture, handling, the passage of time, or other methods that might intentionally or unintentionally remove or alter the printing without affecting the check itself.

8.3.2.1.1. Impact printers may be used. Laser printers that fuse the toner into the check may be used. Do not use laser printers that only lay an image on the paper surface. Do not use correctable ribbons for manual check preparation, as they lack the permanence required to protect against undetectable alteration.

8.3.3. DOs must not release checks with erasures, alterations, overprinting, or imperfect figures or letters. Spoil or void such checks and issue replacements.

8.3.4. Each DO must maintain a record of checks issued under their DSSN. The record must contain at least these data elements: payee, amount, DSSN, check serial number, and date of the check. Other information (purpose, document number, voucher number, local identification code) is optional and at the issuing DO's discretion. The record may be kept on paper or an electronic medium designed for data processing.

8.4    CHECK-SIGNING MACHINES

8.4.1. Select check-signing machines that meet Treasury regulations and standards (see I TFM 4-5045.20). Impact check signers using rubber signature dye, or approved laser check printers containing digitized signatures, may be used. The machines must have the following features:

8.4.1.1. Use a key controlled DO signature feature or a removable computer chip containing the digitized signature for laser check printers with digitized facsimile signature capability. Keep the key or the chip controlling the signature capability in a locked safe or vault, or under other equally effective safeguards, when not in use.

8.4.2. Signature Media

8.4.2.1. Normally, a DO and authorized DDOs use only one signature medium. A DO or DDO may obtain multiple signature media only with DFAS-IN/JTDCO approval, and requests for additional media must include justification of the need. If the check-signing machine uses one set of two plates for signing, additional media require DFAS-IN/JTDCO approval.

8.4.2.2. DFAS-IN/JTDCO will not accept facsimile signatures that do not meet required standards. Design facsimile signature media so that the frame or border enclosing the facsimile signature is a single wavy line containing no identifying characteristics. The signature impression must have sharp lines, a continuous and homogeneous deposit of ink, no filling, and no pronounced ribbon pattern.

8.4.2.3. After receiving the signature media, the DO whose signature is reproduced runs 14 specimens of each facsimile signature, certifies two copies as true facsimiles, and mails all 14 copies to DFAS-IN/JTDCO with a memorandum requesting approval of the facsimile to sign checks. The approval reply authorizes use of the check-signing machine. If the specimens do not match, or the medium does not meet required standards, DFAS-IN/JTDCO advises DFAS- IN/ZTA and requests correction. Do not sign checks by facsimile signature before receiving DFAS-IN/JTDCO approval.

8.4.2.4. The DO must establish and implement controls to prevent unauthorized use of signature media. Maintain custody receipts for all signature media held by authorized deputies, keep a record of each run of checks through the check signer, and reconcile that record with the report of checks issued. When not in use, keep signature media in an approved safe or vault. If the signature media are not removable from the check-signing machine, keep the machine keys in an approved safe or vault.

8.4.2.5. Only the DO or designated DDOs should sign checks using signature media. When necessary for efficient operation of the disbursing office, the DO may authorize, in writing, the holder of a specified position other than a DDO to perform this function. Do not appoint individuals as DDOs solely to sign checks by signature media.

8.4.2.6. If a signature medium is withdrawn from service (for example, it will not be used again, the DO is retiring, or the medium is unserviceable), destroy it locally. The destruction must be performed by someone other than the DO and witnessed by two individuals equal to or senior in rank to the DO.

8.4.2.6.1. Before destruction, the DO verifies the signature plate number or the serial number of the digitized signature medium and witnesses the information on the certificate of destruction.

8.4.2.7. If a digitized medium containing the DO's signature is destroyed and that signature had been loaded to a printer or check signer software, the DO verifies that the signature has been permanently removed from the printer or check signer software. The destruction must be performed by someone other than the DO and witnessed by two individuals equal to or senior in rank to the DO. The DO signs the certificate of destruction only after the medium is actually destroyed. Immediately after destruction, give the certificate identifying the specific plate and date of destruction to the DO and to the federal entity official responsible for maintaining specimen signature files. Follow applicable federal and industry information technology regulatory requirements and standards when destroying an electronic file of a facsimile signature (see
I TFM 4-5025.20).

8.5    PROMPT DELIVERY OF CHECKS

8.5.1. Once checks are prepared, deliver them promptly to payees. DoW requires participation in the direct deposit program for all newly enlisted, reenlisted, appointed (commissioned), or retired military personnel and all newly hired civilian personnel. Title 31, U.S.C. § 3332 requires that contractors be paid by EFT.

8.5.2. Safeguarding and Handling

8.5.2.1. Properly safeguard checks, handling them as few times and by as few people as practical.

8.5.2.2. Ensure proper custody, signing, and delivery of checks. If checks are handed to payees, require that payees identify themselves. Use the payee identification process in
Section 10.0, subparagraph 10.4.3.

8.5.2.3. Promptly return to the disbursing office any checks not delivered within the time the DO specifies.

8.5.2.4. Keep checks in a safe, vault, or locked fireproof cabinet pending distribution or return to the DO.

8.5.2.5. Designate in writing the personnel engaged in pay delivery activities and supervise them to help prevent unauthorized, fraudulent, or other irregular activities.

8.5.3. The normal method of check delivery is by mail through the USPS to payees' residential mailing addresses or post office boxes. At overseas activities, payees' organizational addresses are treated as their residential mailing addresses; organizational addresses are otherwise not valid. When mail delivery is impractical, commanders or their designees may provide specific locations where payees may receive their checks. If checks are mailed to specific locations for delivery, the DO appoints a person in writing at each location to deliver the checks as a designated third party.

8.5.4. Outside the Continental United States (OCONUS)

8.5.4.1. Under Title 31, Code of Federal Regulations, 211.1 (31 CFR § 211.1), the Secretary of the Treasury prohibits agencies from sending checks to the Republic of Cuba (except to the Naval Base, Guantanamo Bay) and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea). DOs instead withhold payment and establish the liability on their books. See the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control website for a complete listing of designated nationals and blocked persons.

8.5.5. Personal delivery of multiple checks may be impractical for the DO, or mailing them to addresses of record may not be expedient. In those circumstances, the DO may deliver or mail checks to a designated third party for distribution. A third party is any individual authorized to distribute a quantity or bulk shipment of checks to payees. A person who maintains pay accounts or prepares checks is not authorized to distribute checks.

8.5.5.1. A DO may appoint individuals to serve as third parties for bulk check delivery; Fiscal Service (FS) Form 210DA, Designation for Agent to Receive and Deliver Checks, is available for this purpose. A DO may appoint one or more alternates to prevent distribution delays when the designee is absent, and alternates may also assist in check distribution when conditions warrant. The DO must ensure appointments are revoked when an appointee transfers, when bulk delivery is no longer needed, or as other circumstances warrant.

8.5.5.2. Package bulk shipments of prepared checks separately from other correspondence and send them by registered mail. Send bulk shipments for a unit or group of units to a third party for distribution or delivery to payees, or reship them to another third party for delivery where the military unit is located. Include the checks, transmittal letter, and documentation needed for the specific payments.

8.5.5.3. Designated third parties may not release checks to anyone other than the designated payee. When payees are absent at the time of delivery, see subparagraph 8.5.5.5 for handling checks.

8.5.5.4. When advance payments are issued for witnesses subpoenaed for trial, a representative from a DoW Component investigative agency, or a judge advocate charged with serving the subpoena, delivers the checks when the payees are absent at the time of delivery.

8.5.5.5. Unless otherwise directed, return checks for payees not present to the DO before the close of business that day. Inform absent payees to call the disbursing office to receive them. If locked fireproof file cabinets or safes are available, the DO may authorize the designated third party to hold undelivered checks for a specified short period. When payees are on extended leave or absence, return their checks to the DO for disposition. Return checks found to be in error to the DO, and the DO issues a new check to the payee after appropriate corrective action.

8.6    EXCHANGE-FOR-CASH CHECKS

8.6.1. Report all exchange-for-cash checks through PIR, citing the DO Cash TAS and the proper BETC code. Spoiled exchange-for-cash checks not yet reported to Treasury are not affected by daily reporting and must follow the guidance in subparagraph 8.8.1. Resolve spoiled checks already reported to Treasury by one of the following methods.

8.6.1.1. Accommodation exchange-for-cash checks are allowed only when satisfactory banking facilities do not exist, and are typically only OCONUS. In OCONUS areas and for ships afloat, the DO's commander may authorize cashing negotiable instruments (see
Section 5.0, subparagraph 5.2.1.2.). DOs may prepare and issue these checks for official purposes to a DDO, agent, or cashier as an advance of cash; to the USPS for remitting collections for the sale of postal money orders; or to Western Union for remitting collections for personal messages of military personnel transmitted over DoW communications facilities to points inside the continental United States (CONUS).

8.6.1.2. The DO issues these checks to advance cash to a DDO, agent, or cashier. Checks issued as advances must be endorsed to the order of the bank or other institution furnishing the cash, or, when cashed by another DO, to that officer by title and activity rather than by name, as "Pay to the order of the Disbursing Officer (name of ship, station, activity, or unit)." Make checks issued to remit collections for the sale of postal money orders or personal messages payable to the DO, USPS, or Western Union, as appropriate.

8.6.1.3. See subparagraph 8.9.5.1. for guidance on disposition of canceled available checks. Deposit exchange-for-cash checks in the Over-the-Counter Channel Application (OTCnet) using the DO Cash TAS.

8.6.1.4. Exchange-for-cash checks that are lost, stolen, or destroyed must follow the unavailable check cancellation (UCC) guidance: enter a Standard Form (SF) 1184, UCC, using the DCRM's UCC subsystem with stop reason code "D" (for stop reason codes, see I TFM 4-7055.20c, Appendix 1) and, on receipt, process a Classification Transactions and Accountability (CTA) transaction reducing both the budget clearing account **F3880 (UCC and Overpayments, Suspense) and the DO cash account.

8.6.2. Do not show the name of the remitter or identifying references to invoices on exchange-for-cash checks. DOs may draw these checks payable to themselves, a DDO, or an agent to obtain operating cash. When authorized in writing by the DO, DDOs may draw these checks payable to themselves to obtain operating cash.

8.6.3. Cash Belonging to Deceased or Missing Persons

8.6.3.1. Exchange cash found in the personal effects of a person who has died or is missing in action for a Treasury check. Make the Treasury check payable to the payee designated by the officer having custody of the personal effects. State the purpose for which the check is drawn as "Exchange-for-cash; personal effects of (name, rank or rate, file or service number)." Draw a separate check for safekeeping deposits of each person (see Section 17.0, paragraph 17.3).

8.6.3.2. Collect cash found in the personal effects of a person whose whereabouts are unknown, including absentees and deserters, into a deposit fund account. Funds held in a deposit fund for more than 1 year may be transferred to account 20X6133 (Payment of Unclaimed Moneys) or to account R1060 (Forfeitures of Unclaimed Money and Property). Make a separate collection for safekeeping deposits of each person.

8.6.4. Do not cancel exchange-for-cash checks issued for advances to DDOs, agents, or cashiers and returned to the DO as "not required." The payee's endorsement on the check is not required. The DO endorses the check and deposits it as prescribed in Section 12.0, subparagraph
12.6.5. DOs may not accept the return of exchange-for-cash checks from any payee other than a DDO, agent, or cashier. Other exchange-for-cash checks are issued to the purchaser and must be negotiated by the payee.

8.6.5. Exchange-for-Cash Checks Lost, Stolen, or Destroyed

8.6.5.1. When the payee of an exchange-for-cash check reports the check as lost, stolen, or destroyed, the DO follows paragraph 8.10. For UCC, the DO may not issue a recertified payment to the payee before receiving credit for the original check from the Treasury, because the original check was issued in exchange-for-cash rather than for an entitlement chargeable to an appropriation.

8.6.5.2. For lost, stolen, or destroyed exchange-for-cash checks issued to advance cash, the DDO, agent, or cashier remains accountable for the cash.

8.6.5.2.1. The DDO, agent, or cashier accounts for the check as a loss of funds. A DO may replace the lost check with a recertified payment check, or a new advance of cash, if the DO considers it necessary due to operational requirements.

8.6.5.2.2. If the lost check is later negotiated after Treasury cancellation (in which case Treasury reverses the previous credit), the DDO, agent, or cashier is accountable for the original lost check and must re-establish the loss of funds.

8.7    CHECK ISSUE DISCREPANCIES

8.7.1. Treasury accepts only one issue/paid record for any given DSSN and check serial number, and will issue a debit voucher to charge the disbursing office for a second check received for payment with the same DSSN and check serial number. If a DO receives a debit voucher for a duplicate check to which the payee is entitled, the DO requests that NPIRC reverse the debit voucher for the correct check serial number of the duplicate check. The DO must also provide a copy of the debit voucher to NPIRC (see I TFM 4-6040.10).

8.7.2. SF 1219, Statement of Accountability Adjustments

8.7.2.1. A common reason for an SF 1219 adjustment made by the DO is a prior- month check issue adjustment. Do not report prior-month check issues as current-month checks issued, because this causes check issue discrepancies for both issue months. An SF 1219 adjustment is necessary to realign the check issue reporting to the proper issue month.

8.7.3. Underdrafts and overdrafts are illegal, incorrect, or improper payment irregularities in the DO's account. The DO has the authority and the means to correct underdrafts. Overdrafts frequently are not within the DO's power to correct. If a check issue overdraft results in an overpayment of a payee, the overpayment amount is an erroneous payment debt. When the DO has attempted to contact the payee and failed, or the payee has been notified and has neither the ability nor the inclination to make restitution, the DO must transfer the debt to the supporting DFAS site for further collection action. To meet relief of liability standards, the DO must transfer uncollectible overdrafts to the supporting DFAS site within 180 days. After the debt is transferred, the DO may request relief of liability for the illegal, incorrect, or improper payment (see Section 7.0).

8.8    SPOILED AND VOIDED CHECKS

8.8.1. When a check is spoiled during the issue process, the DO must void the check. Spoiled checks are treated as voided checks. The DO must void a check that is misprinted or mutilated during the issue process, or is determined not to be a proper payment and has not been reported as a check issue with a dollar amount greater than zero. The DO must report destroyed unused and lost or stolen blank checks as voids. The DO must render voided checks non- negotiable by typing or stamping the words "Void - Not Negotiable. No Check Issued Under This Number." If a DO cannot report the voided checks as required, it must email Fiscal Service at RRB.OSD-NPIRC-PM@fiscal.treasury.gov (see I TFM 4-6030).

8.8.1.1. A check reported to the Treasury as a valid check in a dollar amount greater than zero may not be voided under any circumstances. The DO stamps the check "Not Negotiable - For Deposit Only. Credit of Agency Location Code ######." The DO deposits the check using OTCnet to credit the proceeds to the appropriation from which it was issued and processes the check as either an available check or UCC, as appropriate, per paragraph 8.9.

8.8.2. The DO must store spoiled and voided checks in the vault or safe, segregated from other checks.

8.8.3. The DO must destroy spoiled and voided checks locally as soon as possible, per the destruction guidance in paragraph 8.14.

8.9    AVAILABLE CHECK CANCELLATIONS

8.9.1. The Competitive Equality Banking Act of 1987 (CEBA) amended 31 U.S.C. § 3328 and created 31 U.S.C. § 3334, which establish time limits on the payability of Treasury checks. CEBA affects the time allowed for negotiating Treasury checks, initiating and processing claims, recovering monies from financial institutions, and requesting replacement check payments. The underlying obligations for which Treasury checks were issued are not affected. CEBA does not impose the same payability restrictions on check payments made from limited depositary accounts. CEBA requires that Treasury checks be negotiated within 1 year of their issue dates. A DO may cancel checks within this 1-year period when the check is drawn under the DO's own DSSN, under the account of a predecessor DO of the same activity and DSSN, or under an account being settled by the DO. A DO may not cancel a check over 1 year old. Checks may be canceled when the disbursing account is closed or current, or the proceeds are for repayment to an appropriation or fund account that is current or expired (see I TFM 4-7030).

8.9.2. Exceptions Include:

8.9.2.1. The DO stamps checks recovered or returned to its possession after being submitted for a UCC with "Not Negotiable, Previously Treated as Canceled SF 1184 dated ######." The DO retains these checks for 90 days and then shreds them. A DO receiving a returned check for an activity or DSSN no longer in operation stamps the check "Not Negotiable" and sends it to the successor or settlement DO.

8.9.3. The DO must keep a record of undeliverable checks on DD Form 2658, Returned and Undeliverable Check/Bond Record. An electronic system is acceptable to record undeliverable checks if it includes all the same information as DD 2658. The DO provides the information or a copy of DD 2658 to agents, cashiers, and appropriate entitlement offices for their use. The DO must not remove undelivered checks from the safe or vault or allow deputies, agents, or cashiers to hold them except for immediate delivery to payees or for cancellation and deposit.

8.9.3.1. DOs must keep undeliverable checks in a safe or vault, filing them in an order best suited for ready identification when claimed, or for mailing upon obtaining a proper address. At a minimum, DOs must:

8.9.3.1.1. Open mail with returned Treasury checks in the presence of two people.

8.9.3.1.2. Limit access to the returned Treasury checks processing area.

8.9.3.1.3. Secure the checks in a locked container if there is a delay between when the checks are received and when they are defaced.

8.9.3.2. The issuing DSSN must promptly cancel checks payable to deceased military members and credit the value to the individual's pay account pending payment to a properly designated beneficiary.

8.9.3.3. When a DO is relieved by another DO, or the DSSN is deactivated and disbursing for that activity is assumed by another activity due to consolidation, transfer of function, or other reason, the relieving DO or gaining activity must assume custody of and process the undelivered checks. If the DO is transferred from disbursing duty without a relief, or the disbursing function is not assumed by another activity, the DO must process the undelivered checks as collections on SF 1098, Schedule of Canceled or Undelivered Checks, and deposit them whether or not the three-workday holding period has elapsed.

8.9.3.4. When canceling a military pay and allowances check, the DO must ensure the adjustment is also processed on the member's Master Military Pay Account.

8.9.3.5. When canceling a check in payment of civilian pay, the DO must notify the payroll office to make the appropriate payroll adjustment.

8.9.4. SF 1098

8.9.4.1. The DO must credit a check that is undelivered, within three workdays of receipt in the disbursing office, to the appropriation originally charged using an SF 1098 prepared in triplicate.

8.9.4.2. If the proper appropriation to be credited cannot be determined immediately, the DO collects the amount of the check into account **F3875 (Budget Clearing Account, Suspense). The DO includes on the SF 1098 all available information on the identity and location of the payee and keeps a copy of the documentation in a separate file to support each item in the suspense account. The DO must act aggressively to identify the proper appropriation and remove the item from the suspense account as soon as possible. If the proper appropriation remains unknown after 60 days, the DO must transfer the funds to Treasury's miscellaneous receipt account **R1060 on an SF 1081, Voucher and Schedule of Withdrawals and Credits.

8.9.5. Disposition of Canceled Available Checks

8.9.5.1. The DO must ensure each canceled check is defaced by stamping the legend "Not Negotiable" in a color other than black (preferably red) and in a size prominent enough to remove all possibility of negotiation.

8.9.5.2. Checks received for cancellation do not need to be deposited daily but must be canceled within three business days of receipt. These checks may be held in the DO's safe or vault pending preparation of a consolidated deposit ticket. Where check deposit volume is minimal, or where electronic deposits using OTCnet are not available, the DO must send deposits to the Federal Reserve Bank (FRB) no later than the 25th of the month of receipt. Checks received after the 25th of the month may be retained and deposited the following month. All CONUS DOs deposit canceled Treasury checks with the nearest FRB. DOs in Alaska, Hawaii, and foreign countries deposit them with the general depositary normally used for deposits-for-credit to the Treasury's General Account. See Section 12.0, subparagraph 12.8.2. for deposit reconciliation requirements.

8.9.6. When a claim is received for the proceeds of a canceled available check, and all or part of the amount is due to the claimant, the disbursing office that collected and deposited the original undeliverable check pays the claim on payroll or other vouchers prepared, processed, and certified the same as a current payment. This does not preclude the issuing DO from canceling an undeliverable military paycheck so the member may be paid at a new duty station. The DO uses an SF 1034, Public Voucher for Purchases and Services Other than Personal, to make these payments and charges them to the accounting data credited on an SF 1098, referencing the original undeliverable check by serial number, amount, DSSN, month, year, and account in which it was collected. The DO pays claims received for items transferred to the **R1060 account from the 20X1807 (Refund of Moneys Erroneously Received and Covered) account.

8.10    UCC

8.10.1. The DO cancels unavailable Treasury checks less than 12 months old as lost, stolen, mutilated, or not received by the payee, and also cancels when the DO determines the payee is not entitled to the proceeds. To file a non-receipt claim against a Treasury check, the DO must submit a UCC online through TCIS or via file transmission (see I TFM 4-7045.10). Treasury credits canceled checks to account **F3880 through the Intra-governmental Payment and Collection (IPAC) system. The DO uses a CTA transaction to move the funds out of account **F3880 to the proper program TAS, deposit fund account, or DO Cash TAS along with the proper adjustment BETC code. Such situations include death of the payee before the check issue date, non-receipt of a recertified payment when the original check has been received and cashed, and receipt of both a cash payment and a check payment for the same entitlement.

8.10.1.1. Checks unavailable to the payee or the DO, and for which entitlement to the payment exists, may be replaced by a new check called a recertified payment check. Such a payment bears a new check serial number and is vouchered, certified, and recorded as a new disbursement. The DO must control, cross-reference, and track original and recertified payments indefinitely, or until both have been paid, recovered and destroyed, or canceled.

8.10.2. The DO must maintain DD 2662, Recertified Payment Register, to provide the necessary cross-reference and control over UCCs. An electronic log is acceptable if it contains the same information as the form (see Volume 1, for records retention).

8.10.3. SF 1184

8.10.3.1. An SF 1184 is required for all cancellations. Bulk losses of original checks require the preparation of a separate SF 1184 for each check.

8.10.3.1.1. Use this form to stop payment, obtain photocopies, or check the payment status of unavailable Treasury checks. Input stop reason codes to designate the desired action. Although this form attempts to stop payment on a check, there is no true stop payment action. The payee may still negotiate the check, and the DO is responsible to recoup the money.

8.10.3.1.2. If a check is presented for payment after Treasury has given the DO a credit to the **F3880 account, Treasury reverses the credit and provides the DO the documentation, including a photocopy of the paid check. The DO must then research and take the appropriate corrective action, including collection efforts when dual negotiation has occurred. See Supplemental Guidance, subparagraph 8.11.2. for guidance on preparing and submitting an SF 1184, and paragraph 8.10.8 for handling the credits and reversals of credit in the **F3880 account.

8.10.4. Claims of Non-receipt, Destruction, Loss, or Theft

8.10.4.1. The DO sends the FS 1133, the FS 3858, the photocopy of the check, and any other supporting documentation for the claim to Treasury for processing. If the payee files an FS 1133 to claim forgery or unauthorized endorsement against the check, a recertified payment is not authorized before receipt of a Claims Disposition Notice (CDN) from the Treasury.

8.10.5. DD Form 2660, Statement

8.10.5.1. A payee who reports the loss, theft, mutilation, or non-receipt of a Treasury check must submit a written statement to the DO. DD 2660 is the preferred form for the required statement, but a DO may accept a signed letter from the payee in lieu of DD 2660, provided the letter contains the required information and the certification statement found on
DD 2660.

8.10.5.2. A payee who submits a statement in lieu of DD 2660 must include the payee's name, SSN, and address; the member's name and SSN if different from the payee; type of payment entitlement; whether the check was received and, if so, whether it was lost, stolen, destroyed, or mutilated; whether the check was endorsed by the payee or had a limited endorsement such as "for deposit only"; the circumstances surrounding the loss, theft, destruction, or mutilation if the check was received; and the payee's signed statement of certification. The statement must contain the signed certification statement exactly as cited in blocks 12-15 on DD 2660. Failure to include this statement could hinder collection efforts if a dual negotiation occurs. If the payee negotiated both checks, the statement could also be used to establish fraudulent intent.

8.10.5.3. Upon receipt of the signed statement, the issuing DO or settlement officer completes the information required to identify the check (issue date, check number, amount, and voucher number). Before entering an SF 1184, the DO must verify the check has not been returned as undeliverable.

8.10.5.4. If the check was re-mailed at a later date, the DO notifies the payee of the later mailing date and allows two weeks' delivery time before processing the claim of non-receipt. If the check has not been returned and enough time has passed for mail delivery, the DO uses the information on DD 2660 to enter an SF 1184 for the unavailable check. The DO must not submit an SF 1184 involving non-receipt of future dated checks, such as those issued for pay and allowance entitlements, before the date of payment.

8.10.5.5. The DO must not enter an SF 1184 involving non-receipt until the third working day after the check payment date.

8.10.5.6. The DO sends a copy of the claimant's DD 2660, or other written statement, and a copy of the SF 1184 documentation to the appropriate entitlement area, which must certify that the entitlement for payment still exists before the DO may issue a recertified payment.

8.10.6. DAS

8.10.6.1. Except for the transmittal documents, Treasury returns a DAS on every SF 1184 received. An essential control technique is for DOs to keep a complete file of submitted SF 1184s. Periodic review of the file shows, either by copy of the DAS or by copy of the agency receipt of batch transmittals, that Treasury received and processed all submissions. The DO must follow up incomplete file items within 30 days through the supporting DFAS site by telephone and, if necessary, by submitting a second SF 1184 (see I TFM 4-7045.20).

8.10.6.2. Once Treasury issues a DAS with a status indicating "check canceled; crediting agency," future requests to cancel or obtain photocopies of the canceled check receive the response "outstanding check was canceled; agency credited." A photocopy of the check is not available until the check is presented for payment through the banking system. Therefore, once a disbursing office has received a DAS with a status code of "Outstanding," no additional SF 1184s may be submitted for that check number. If the original check is presented through the banking system for payment, the DO receives notification that Treasury has reversed the credit to the **F3880 account. Treasury then provides a photocopy of the original check and the claim forms FS 1133 and FS 3858.

8.10.7. Authorization to Issue Recertified Payments

8.10.7.1. Treasury delegates authority to DOs to replace checks they originally issued, including checks lost, stolen, or destroyed in transit or after receipt by applicable payees (see 31 CFR 245 and 31 CFR 248). DOs may issue a recertified payment when the SF 1184 is prepared, based on available facts. Subject to the restrictions that follow, DOs may issue recertified payments as replacements for original checks at any time beginning with submission of the SF 1184. The circumstances of each unavailable check govern this timing.

8.10.7.2. Do not issue a recertified payment check if:

8.10.7.2.1. The payee of the original check is not entitled to the proceeds;

8.10.7.2.2. The payee died before the original check issue date;

8.10.7.2.3. Insufficient mail time has lapsed from the date the original check was mailed or re-mailed to allow for its delivery and possible return;

8.10.7.2.4. The payee has an outstanding obligation which the payment can offset; or

8.10.7.2.5. The original check is more than 12 months old.

8.10.7.3. Before issuing a recertified payment, consider all circumstances involving high-dollar-value unavailable checks, payees in adverse actions that could result in early discharge or termination, or nonpermanent employees with no vested retirement benefits or sustained work history. Also consider the payee's ability to repay in cases of double negotiation and the possibility of offsetting a double negotiation against money other than salary due to the payee. For deactivated and closed DSSNs:

8.10.7.3.1. The designated settlement office normally issues these payments. In some situations (for example, consolidation), the DO supporting the activity that assumed disbursing and accounting responsibility for the deactivated or closed office may issue a recertified payment for that office; and

8.10.7.3.2. Except as prescribed in paragraph 8.8, issue recertified payments only as a disbursement from the appropriation charged for the original check or, if that appropriation is no longer available, a current appropriation available for the same general purpose, subject to limitations on its use.

8.10.7.4. Delays in issuing checks may affect military and civilian employees' personal financial affairs, DoW relations with private business, and other intangible benefits, so immediate issuance of replacement checks may be appropriate. DOs may use stop reason code "A" on the SF 1184 to support immediate issuance replacing undelivered, lost, stolen, mutilated, or destroyed original checks issued under their DSSN if less than 31 days have elapsed since the check issue date.

8.10.7.5. Submit UCCs using stop reason code "D" or "G," and issue a recertified payment only after Treasury reports the check status as outstanding.

8.10.7.6. Do not issue a recertified payment check when the DAS from Treasury indicates the check status is paid (see subparagraph 8.10.11).

8.10.8. Accounting for Recertified Payments

8.10.8.1. Treasury provides credits for canceled unavailable checks and charges from negotiation of previously canceled unavailable checks through budget clearing account **F3880. This account is restricted to unavailable check transactions; do not use it for any other purpose. It holds credit or chargeback amounts only pending identification of the appropriation or fund charged for the original check issuance. Do not charge the **F3880 account directly for any payment; transfer amounts in this account to the original appropriation as quickly as possible. Do not allow transactions in this account to become stale or unidentifiable, because an unidentifiable balance may result in a DO loss of funds and associated pecuniary liability.

8.10.8.2. Treasury transfers to the **F3880 account via IPAC. By the end of each month, DOs must reconcile their CARS activity by TAS/BETC to their internal accounting system of record and reclassify any transactions to the correct TAS/BETC in the CARS CTA Statement if necessary. After reporting a credit or charge to the **F3880 account on its internal accounting records, the DO must prepare a JV to clear that credit or charge from the account, returning the funds to the appropriation or fund account the DO identifies. Any credit or charge processed after the Treasury Receivable Accounting and Collection System closes on the last business day of the month is accounted for in the next accounting month.

8.10.8.3. Under 31 U.S.C. § 3334(a)(2), return canceled check proceeds to the appropriation(s) charged when the check(s) were originally issued, and treat the canceled check(s) as account(s) payable. Within 15 days of receipt, DFAS-IN and DFAS-CL send the check cancellation and credit detail information to the disbursing office that issued the check(s) (except as noted in subparagraph 8.10.9.1.) and to that office's supporting accounting office. Send any reversal of previous Treasury cancellation credits in the same manner to the applicable disbursing and accounting offices.

8.10.8.4. The DO reviews the **F3880 account monthly to ensure necessary actions are taken to clear these transactions. Each time the DO's account is transferred, the incoming DO validates balances in this account. If the departing DO cannot provide the incoming DO with documentation supporting the **F3880 items, the departing DO processes the unsupported items as losses of funds under Section 7.0.

8.10.8.5. On receipt of a DAS indicating cancellation credit or reversal information from the supporting DFAS site, the DO researches the check issue data submitted to Treasury to confirm the accuracy of the detail (for example, the DSSN, check serial number, date of issue, and issue amount), which must agree with the original check issue data reported to Treasury. Research any discrepancy to determine its cause and correct it. For a reversal, the DO determines whether a dual negotiation occurred by verifying the status of the replacement check, then submits an SF 1184 on the replacement check using stop reason code "F" for non-entitlement.

8.10.8.5.1. If the check for the recertified payment is outstanding, the DO receives a credit offsetting the charge for the reversal previously received. If the check has been paid, the DO receives a photocopy of the paid check, a claim form, and a claims document. If both the original and recertified payment checks have been negotiated, the DO begins collection action as outlined in subparagraph 8.10.11. The disbursing office must also notify the appropriate entitlement or subject matter area (for example, military pay, civilian pay, travel pay, or commercial accounts payable), and provide a copy of the DAS, when Treasury returns a credit because the check was not negotiated or reverses a credit previously received.

8.10.8.5.2. The DO requests the accounting department re-obligate funds to cover issuance of a recertified payment. Once assured that funds are re-obligated and available, the DO may issue a recertified payment check citing the original appropriation. If the original appropriation is closed, use a current year appropriation for the same or similar purpose.

8.10.8.5.3. When Treasury provides a reclamation credit, the DO requests the accounting department re-obligate funds to cover issuance of a recertified payment.

8.10.8.6. When notified that an unavailable check has been canceled, the credit received, and a recertified payment requested, the appropriate entitlement or subject matter area determines whether the liability for the underlying obligation is valid before preparing a recertified payment. A recertified payment is prohibited if the entitlement to payment no longer exists.

8.10.8.7. All recertified payments (including immediate replacements under stop reason code "A") must be vouchered, certified by a certifying officer, and charged to the appropriation or fund charged for the original payment. Making a recertified payment under the first two provisions listed in this paragraph requires establishing an accounts receivable, supported by a copy of the SF 1184 and/or the DAS, in the appropriation or fund for the amount due on cancellation of the original check. Recertified payments may be made when the disbursing office submits the SF 1184.

8.10.9. Preparation and Disposition of Replacement Checks

8.10.9.1. When a payee returns a replacement check after the original check it replaced is found and negotiated by the payee, cancel the replacement check on an SF 1098 and credit the proceeds to the appropriation charged when it was issued. Deposit the check with the nearest FRB or branch on a deposit ticket as prescribed in paragraph 10.4. Transfer the **F3880 chargeback from Treasury for the negotiated original check to the appropriation charged when the original check was issued.

8.10.10. CFIF

8.10.10.1. The CFIF is a revolving fund established under 31 U.S.C. § 3343 to settle payee/claimant claims of non-receipt when an original check has been fraudulently negotiated. Only Fiscal Service may adjudicate forgery claims against Treasury checks. A claim against the CFIF is governed by the 1-year statute of limitations in the CEBA; a forgery claim must be presented within 1 year from the date the check was issued, or the claim is barred and the payee is not entitled to payment from the CFIF. The DO must submit an SF 1184 on the check within 13 months from the check issue date.

8.10.11. Collections of Double Negotiations

8.10.11.1. A double negotiation occurs when an original check and its replacement have both been reported as paid by Treasury. The loss occurs on negotiation of the replacement check; the order in which the checks are cashed is irrelevant. A double negotiation is an illegal or improper payment for purposes of pecuniary liability. The DO initiates collection action to recover illegal or improper payments made by the DO's office. If the payee separates from government service, the DO remains responsible to pursue collection action. Collections for illegal or improper payments are normally one-time cash refunds or lump-sum collections by salary offset and do not warrant installment liquidation. Limit installment repayments to cases of extreme personal hardship.

8.10.11.2. When Treasury notifies a DO that it has reversed a credit to the **F3880 account from a previous cancellation, the DO researches the situation to determine whether a double negotiation occurred by checking the payment status of the replacement check. Once a Treasury response confirms a double negotiation, the DO immediately begins collection action. In each case, afford the payee the due process rights of collection specified in Volume 16. Recovery is most effective when the DO presents the payee a photocopy of the paid original and replacement check and a copy of the claimant's signed statement acknowledging the payee was not entitled to both payments. Due process rights include the opportunity to contest the validity of the debt; in double negotiation, the payee's right to complete an FS 1133 provides this opportunity.

8.10.11.3. If the payee asserts that one of the checks was negotiated over a forged endorsement, delay collection until the NPIRC adjudicates the payee's forgery claim. If the NPIRC determines the check was forged, the payee does not owe the debt. If the NPIRC denies the claim, the full amount of the check is due and subject to immediate collection. If the payee fails to provide the properly completed FS 1133 within the period allowed to show why the debt is not owed, the payee is deemed to have acknowledged the debt and the DO takes immediate collection action. In either situation, complete collection action within 90 days of receiving the DAS from Treasury indicating the canceled unavailable original check has been paid, or within 90 days of receiving the CDN from Fiscal Service indicating the forgery claim is denied.

8.10.11.4. The DO documents all attempts to collect illegal or improper payments. If all reasonable steps have been taken and the illegal or improper payment becomes uncollectible within the 90-day time limit, the DO transfers the debt to the office designated to pursue collection of uncollectible debts (see Volume 16 for debt collection processes).
