Although the debt is transferred for further collection action, the DO remains pecuniarily liable for the illegal or improper payment until the debt is collected or relief is granted (see subparagraph 8.10.11.).

8.10.11.5. Double negotiations could indicate fraudulent intent or misrepresentation. A DO who suspects this reports the situation using the guidance in Section 7.0, for possible investigative or disciplinary action. Pursue collection action as specified in Volume 16.

8.10.12. A DO may request relief of liability for uncollectible illegal or improper payments under 31 U.S.C. § 3527 (see Section 7.0).

8.10.13. The payment recertification process is subject to the same management controls as other routine disbursements. The same individual must not authorize, process, and review recertified payment transactions.

8.10.13.1. The minimum acceptable separation of duties consists of: preparation of the SF 1184 by one individual; review and approval of the DD 2660 and SF 1184 by the DO or a DDO; preparation and certification of a disbursement voucher by an individual in the appropriate entitlement area; review and approval of the voucher with supporting documentation by a first line supervisor other than the DO or DDO authorizing the transaction; and authorization of the disbursement by the DO or a DDO.

8.10.13.2. When the disbursement voucher is prepared in disbursing because of automated disbursing system limitations, or because the entitlement and disbursing functions are combined into one unit (as at small activities and most tactical units), the DO must ensure that preparing the SF 1184, preparing the disbursement voucher, reviewing the transaction and supporting documents, and preparing the check are performed by different individuals.

8.11    TREASURY CHECKS CANCELED UNDER LIMITED PAYABILITY

8.11.1. Treasury checks issued on or after October 1, 1989 bear the legend "Void After 1- Year," and Treasury declines payment of checks not negotiated to a financial institution within 1- year of their issue dates. Stamp checks returned to the disbursing office as no longer negotiable "Void - Not Negotiable" and shred them after confirming receipt of the limited payability cancellation credit. Treasury checks issued before October 1, 1989 were mass canceled; shred them without confirming receipt of a limited payability cancellation credit.

8.11.2. A claim on a Treasury check is barred unless presented to the issuing agency within 1-year after its issue date. DOs must reject as time-barred all claims against Treasury checks not received before the 12-month period of negotiability expires. DOs must notify claimants that claims of nonpayment of the underlying obligation must be filed with the appropriate entitlement office (for example, the contracting officer for vendors or commercial payees, or the military pay, civilian pay, or travel office). Under 31 U.S.C. § 3702(e), the Secretary of War may waive this time limitation on canceled checks for claims under $25,000.

8.11.3. Accounting

8.11.3.1. Under 31 U.S.C. § 3334(a)(2), DFAS-IN, DFAS-CL, and DFAS-CO must return the proceeds from canceled checks to the appropriation that originally paid them and treat the proceeds as accounts payable. Within 15 days of receipt, they must send the check cancellation and credit detail to both the disbursing office that issued the check and the supporting accounting office, and must forward any Treasury reversal of previous cancellation credits to the applicable disbursing and accounting offices.

8.11.3.2. Upon receiving the detailed limited payability cancellation credit or reversal information from DFAS-IN, DFAS-CL, and DFAS-CO, the DO must research the check issue data submitted to confirm the detail is accurate (for example, the DSSN, check serial number, date of issue, and issue amount), all of which must agree with the original check issue data reported when the check was issued. The DO must determine the cause of any discrepancy and correct it.

8.11.3.2.1. The DO must also research disbursing records to determine whether a claim of loss, theft, or non-receipt has been filed on the canceled check, including whether the check was previously replaced by a recertified or other payment. The disbursing office must notify the appropriate entitlement area (for example, military pay, civilian pay, travel pay, or commercial accounts payable) that Treasury has returned the credit because the check was not negotiated within the prescribed period.

8.11.3.2.2. On request of an entitlement area, the DO must perform the verifications described in subparagraph 8.9.5.1. and advise the entitlement area whether the original Treasury check was canceled, negotiated, or previously replaced.

8.11.4. Claims

8.11.4.1. If the payee submitted a timely claim and has not been paid, the claim must be sent through the appropriate Component's Assistant Secretary for Financial Management to the General Counsel of the DoW requesting a waiver of the statute of limitations. If the General Counsel determines the claimant is entitled to payment, and a payment voucher with supporting documentation is sent to the disbursing office, the DO determines whether to issue a replacement check.

8.11.4.2. On receipt of a claim approved by the designated settlement authority, a certified payment voucher from the appropriate entitlement area, and the proper supporting documentation, the issuing DO (or the officer assigned to settle accounts for the issuing DO) issues the replacement check.

8.12    HOLDER-IN-DUE-COURSE

8.12.1. Lost-in-Transit Check Lost-in-transit

8.12.1.1. If a DO receives a request to reissue a check that has not been canceled and is less than 1-year old, the DO must return the request to the financial institution and advise it to submit the request to the FRB Atlanta, Government Check Adjustment Department.

8.13    CHECK ISSUE REPORTING

8.13.1. Disbursing offices must report detailed check issue transmittals to the Treasury in Level 8 format to update TCIS with check issue detail. The DoW uses DCRM for direct submission of the check issue detail to the Treasury.

8.13.2. Submission Requirements

8.13.2.1. DOs must submit all check issue transmittals to the Treasury no later than the close of business at the end of the week in which the issue dates occur and at month end. DOs who submit through their supporting DFAS site must ensure the DFAS site receives their check issue data at least weekly and at month end.

8.13.2.2. Failure to report check issue data timely increases the risk of loss from banking system errors, check alterations, and counterfeits. If a loss from an altered or counterfeit check occurs because of delinquent check issue reporting, the DO may be held liable for the loss. Until check issue data is reported in TCIS, the Treasury will not recognize the check as issued or process claims or limited payability cancellation credits against it, and cannot complete a final reconciliation and clearance of the DO's account. If the DO is habitually delinquent for 60 days or more, the Treasury may suspend further print orders for blank Treasury check stock until all delinquent reporting is accepted into TCIS.

8.13.3. The disbursing office is responsible for ensuring the check issue data submitted to the Treasury is accurate. DOs must notify their supporting DFAS site immediately after finding an error and must correct all errors before the file transfer process. Once TCIS accepts an erroneous check issue transmittal, the file cannot be deleted. If an erroneous data file has been sent to DCRM but not yet forwarded to the Treasury, place the whole file in a "replace" or "suspended" status and contact the local DCRM manager or supporting DFAS site immediately to change the file from accepted status in DCRM.

8.13.4. Voided Checks

8.13.4.1. Report voided checks as zero-dollar amounts in the proper sequence with other checks issued in the same check range. A DO who reports check issue detail by sending it to another disbursing office for conversion or upload to DCRM must ensure the voided checks are reported and clearly marked. Stamp or mark the hardcopy check issue listing to show that a check is voided with a zero-dollar amount, and do not obliterate the serial number of the voided check from the listing. If a voided check has not been dated, report a date to facilitate check issue reporting. DOs submitting their own check issue data to the Treasury must include the serial numbers and dates of voided checks in the transmission with zero-dollar values.

8.13.4.2. A DO who erroneously reported a voided check with a dollar value greater than zero, and the check is under 1-year old, must initiate corrective action as soon as the error is discovered, without waiting to receive the FMS 5206, and must send Treasury a written request to adjust the check issue detail in TCIS.

8.13.4.3. If the issue date of the erroneously reported check is over 1-year old, the voided check cannot be adjusted in TCIS, and Treasury will issue a limited payability credit for it. On receipt of the credit in the **F3880 account, the DO must report the check as a check issue on the monthly SF 1219 and debit the **F3880 account to clear the limited payability credit.

8.14    DESTROYING CHECKS

8.14.1. DOs must not destroy unwanted or excess blank check stock that is otherwise still usable without first contacting DFAS-IN/JTDCBO.

8.14.2. Destroy checks by burning or shredding. Checks destroyed by burning must be burned completely. Checks destroyed by shredding must be reduced to fragments no larger than 1/8 inch wide and 3½ inches long, using a crosscut shredder as Treasury requires. Use the burning method only, subject to environmental regulations, when a disbursing office does not have shredding equipment. In either case, prepare a certificate of destruction (see Figure 8-2 in the Supplemental Guidance).

8.14.3. The DO and at least one witness must examine the checks to verify they are the actual checks to be destroyed, verify the check numbers and DSSN against the certificate of destruction, and sign the certificate only after witnessing the actual destruction.

8.14.4. The DO must notify the Fiscal Service of the destruction of blank check stock by emailing the certificate to RRB.OSD-NPIRC-PM@fiscal.treasury.gov, and must keep a copy in the DO's blank check inventory control records (see I TFM 4-5040.50b).

title: Section 9.0: Collections
content:
9.0    COLLECTIONS

9.1    GENERAL

9.1.1. Under 31 U.S.C. § 3302(c), DoW DOs must deposit public money not held for current expenditure in the Treasury or with a depositary designated by the Secretary of the Treasury.

9.2    TYPES OF COLLECTIONS

9.2.1. Receipts are collections into a Treasury miscellaneous receipt or other legally authorized account or fund. DOs collect them into their accountability using a DD Form 1131, Cash Collection Voucher, and recognize them by the absence of a fiscal/program year in the accounting classification. Disbursing from a receipt account is not authorized. Adjusting out an over-collection requires processing a collection voucher as a negative receipt.

9.2.2. Reimbursements are amounts earned and collected for property sold or services furnished to U.S. Government agencies or to the public, amounts collected from outside sources for payments made in error, overpayments, or adjustments for previous amounts disbursed. They are recognizable by the presence of an accounts receivable sales code within the accounting classification and shown as positive amounts on the DD 1131. A "negative reimbursement" occurs when a reimbursement is over collected and requires a return of funds to the remitter and is vouchered as a bracketed (negative) amount on a DD 1131.

9.2.3. Refunds are recoveries of payments collected into a DO's accountability as positive amounts on a DD 1131 using the same accounting classification as the original disbursement voucher, or as offsets shown as bracketed amounts on disbursement vouchers; they reduce disbursements rather than constitute collections. Report refunds documented on collection vouchers on the DD 2657, Daily Statement of Accountability, separately from those occurring as negative disbursements, which are reported as net of disbursements. Do not report refunds separately on the SF 1219, Statement of Accountability, but include them in net disbursements.

9.3    COLLECTION TRANSACTIONS

9.3.1. Collections are transactions that increase a DO's accountability but do not apply to acquiring U.S. and foreign currencies through purchase with dollars or accommodation exchange transactions. All collection vouchers reported in DoW business systems must meet standard line- of-accounting requirements. DOs must document collections on the appropriate collection forms and verify and record them in the accounting records. Funds not creditable to appropriations (for example, recoveries of losses of funds or dishonored checks) are not collections because they do not change a DO's accountability.

9.3.1.1. Any portion of the cash associated with a DD 1131 not deposited the same day but collected into the DO's accountability must be reported as a CTA transaction, which feeds the CARS daily account statement and increases both the DO Cash TAS and the program TAS on the collection voucher. DOs may consolidate multiple collection vouchers under one transaction reported to Treasury if they share the same TAS/BETC and agency location codes. DOs must ensure consolidated transactions retain an audit trail that can be validated at the individual- transaction level.

9.3.2. Accept cash, checks, or other recognized credit instruments payable on demand, including certified or uncertified personal checks, corporate checks, bank drafts, Treasury checks with issue dates less than 1 year old, postal money orders, money orders issued by banks or other financial establishments, credit union share drafts, and warrants payable on demand. Draw these negotiable instruments in favor of a DO's official capacity (position title, not name). Visa and MasterCard credit and debit cards are acceptable when presented for payment at locations participating in the Card Acquiring Service.

9.3.2.1. Commanders may authorize commissary officers to accept Treasury checks from authorized patrons to pay for sales when banks and other facilities cannot furnish check-cashing services, but may not authorize or require DOs or their agents to advance additional change funds to commissary officers to cash those checks. Commissaries may use the cash they receive for this purpose.

9.3.2.2. DOs must establish procedures to control receipt and processing of checks and other negotiable instruments received by mail. An individual independent of the collection function must receive these remittances and must not be the same individual who maintains the accounts receivable records. DOs must establish controls using the DD 2658, Returned and Undeliverable Check/Bond Record, or another effective method to record the transmittal of instruments between functional areas.

9.3.3. DOs may acknowledge collections made by remote cashiers only upon receipt of certification of the actual monetary amounts.

9.3.4. Performance

9.3.4.1. DOs receiving remittances (for example, checks, bank drafts, and money orders) as deposits for performance or bid bonds must deposit them immediately in deposit fund account X6501, to be held pending settlement with the contractor.

9.3.4.2. Under 31 CFR part 225, contractors may deposit certain U.S. bonds with contracting officers instead of furnishing corporate or individual sureties on performance and payment bonds. DOs may not accept these bonds, whether electronic or hardcopy, for other than temporary safekeeping (for example, overnight or over a weekend). For temporary safekeeping, DOs may provide space in a safe or vault by placing the bonds and related documentation in a sealed package indicating custodianship and giving the contracting officer a receipt for the package. The contracting officer is responsible for transferring the bonds to the FRB.

9.3.5. Negotiable Instruments

9.3.5.1. Remitters must make checks and other negotiable instruments payable to the order of the specific organization maintaining the account to be credited, not to the Treasury. If a check is made payable to the Treasury, accept and process it immediately. Do not accept checks payable to a DO or to federal government employees, whether by check or through electronic means.

9.3.5.2. Keep limited depositary accounts in the name of the activity to which the DO is assigned. Instruct the remitter not to inscribe instruments payable to the DO by activity name.

9.4    ISSUANCE OF RECEIPTS FOR COLLECTIONS

9.4.1. Turning in Funds

9.4.1.1. Individuals other than DOs, DDOs, cashiers, or agents who receive funds belonging to the United States (including funds held in trust) must promptly turn them over to their supporting DO or deposit them in an authorized general depositary. These individuals, who may work within commissary, property disposal, personnel, and other offices authorized to receive funds due the United States, are responsible for safeguarding funds in their possession pending deposit or turn-in. Collecting officers number documents sequentially by fiscal year. The DO, DDO, or agent receiving the funds signs and returns two copies of each DD 1131 (other than the original) to the collecting officer and distributes additional copies as required.

9.4.1.2. A DO, DDO, agent, or cashier receiving a collection directly from a remitter prepares a collection voucher for the amount collected, and the supporting DFAS site determines the number of copies to give the remitter. Issue receipts for payment of bills received by mail only if the remitter requests it. Furnish receipts only for amounts received and verified by actual count. DOs, DDOs, and agents may not use subject verification to issue receipts, give receipts in blank, or accept receipts in blank.

9.4.1.3. Where an automated system is used, cashiers may sign receipts in their own name; otherwise, DOs, DDOs, or agents must personally sign the receipts. Signatures are not required for collection vouchers electronically validated by an approved public key infrastructure method. Before signing, the cashier or collecting official must ensure that remittances are authorized collections in the correct amounts. The person accepting the remittance must not be the same person updating the accounts receivable record.

9.4.2. Collections by Agent Officers

9.4.2.1. Agents of appointing DOs may sign receipts for funds.

9.5    RECORDING AND CONTROLLING COLLECTIONS

9.5.1. Unless the supporting DFAS site directs otherwise, the affected functional area maintains a pending payment file and an associated copy of the uncollected billing documents, and sends the original and duplicate copy to the customer from whom reimbursement is expected. Arrange the files in the order most convenient to the person maintaining them, and reconcile the file quarterly to the accounts receivable subsidiary ledgers.

9.5.2. Process an overage in a DO's account as a collection to F3875 no later than the business day after the overage occurs. Resolve overages no later than the fifth business day after the end of each quarter or, upon the DO's relief from disbursing duty, no later than the fifth business day following the date of relief. Consider collections and returns from agents when determining the source of an overage. When the reasons for an overage are explained and there is reasonable assurance no claim will be made, credit it directly to the Treasury's receipt account R1060, Forfeiture of Unclaimed Money and Property.

9.5.3. Maintain a daily DD 2659, Voucher Control Log, for collection vouchers the disbursing office receives or prepares. The DO determines the functional areas and assigns individuals to maintain this form. Assign each functional area or branch disbursing office a separate series of voucher numbers. Include the collection voucher number, the remitter's identity (name of the remitting individual or organization), the amount, and the instrument of remittance (for example, check, cash, traveler's check, EFT, or a no-pay adjustment). Annotate a check or EFT trace number in column d, OTHER.

9.5.4. When a remitter overpays an amount due by $1.00 or less, collect the overpayment into receipt account 1099 (Fines, Penalties, and Forfeitures, Not Otherwise Classified), and refund it only if the remitter requests. If a payee underpays an amount due by $1.00 or less, prepare an SF 1080 charging the DoW Component's Operations and Maintenance account and credit the applicable appropriation or receivable for the underpayment. Do not pursue collection action for underpayments of $1.00 or less.

9.5.5. Agencies not co-located with or supported by a disbursing office that receive collections must do the following.

9.5.5.1. Use a log to control collections from the time of receipt until they are transmitted to the disbursing office. At a minimum, show the date of receipt, remitter, check or money order number, collection voucher number, amount of collection, and date transmitted to the disbursing office.

9.5.5.2. Prepare a collection voucher the same day the DoW Component receives the collection.

9.5.5.3. Safeguard the collection and supporting documents.

9.6    DOCUMENTING AND PROCESSING COLLECTIONS

9.6.1. Verification of Funds Received

9.6.1.1. Functional areas must ensure that collections are proper, that vouchers have complete and accurate data, and that required copies are available. A disbursing office that detects an improperly prepared voucher returns it to the functional area for correction.

9.6.1.2. Include the purpose of a collection (for example, contract lease, applicable regulation, schedule, cost list, or other document that authorizes the collection) on, or as an attachment to, a collection voucher. If a sales contract is involved, cite the contract in the reference information. If the purpose of a collection cannot be determined, account for it in F3875 and F3885 (Budget Clearing Account (Suspense)) or in Shared Accounting Module default clearing accounts F3500 for proprietary payments and collections and F3502 for IPAC, as appropriate.

9.6.1.2.1. Transfer to account 20X6133, Payment of Unclaimed Moneys, amounts of $25 or more held for more than 1 year that are authorized to be refundable but cannot be refunded because the individual's location is unknown.

9.6.1.2.2. Transfer to R1060 unclaimed amounts of less than $25, or amounts of $25 or more held for more than 1 year, for which the rightful owner can be neither identified nor located.

9.6.1.3. DOs must ensure the legibility of all copies of vouchers prepared for distribution.

9.6.2. Signature on Collection Vouchers

9.6.2.1. DOs, DDOs, or agent officers must sign original collection vouchers in permanent, non-erasable ink; this duty may not be delegated or reassigned. Officers using cash- control machines or mechanized equipment to validate vouchers are exempt from this requirement, except when a DD 1131 is processed for further action by a disbursing office not collocated with the processing office, so long as the machines and their controls meet minimum security and audit requirements. The DO or DDO controls the keys for these machines. Digital signatures may also be used following the guidance in Section 2.0, subparagraph 3.6.3.

9.6.2.2. The DO must implement controls to ensure that all funds received by the cashier are accounted for properly. The DO or DDO holds copies of the vouchers bearing the cashier's initials and, in making daily settlement with the cashier at the end of the business day, uses these copies to determine whether the amounts the cashier reported were proper. The receiving officer's signature is required where applicable. The DO or certifying officer, as applicable, signs transfer, cancellation, or adjustment vouchers (SF 1081) and an SF 1098, Schedule of Canceled or Undelivered Checks. If the same voucher is both a disbursement and a collection, the disbursement is the original subject to the signature requirements in subparagraph 9.6.2, and the collection is a copy that does not require a signature.

9.6.3. Preparation of Documents Used to Transmit Funds

9.6.3.1. An officer depositing or transmitting funds to a disbursing office prepares the proper forms. Except for collections from over-the-counter sales (for example, commissaries), include the remitter's name, the specific authority for the collection, and information sufficient for the DO to identify the collection and confirm the correct amount on each collection document. The preparing officer also furnishes the complete accounting classification as prescribed, the fiscal code (including the Disbursing Station Symbol Number of the station maintaining the appropriation cited), and the country code when the collection is made in an overseas area.

title: Section 10.0: Disbursements
content:
10.0    DISBURSEMENTS

10.1    GENERAL

10.1.1. Overview

10.1.1.1. All disbursements must be supported by disbursement vouchers (for example, SF 1080; SF 1081; SF 44, U.S. Government Purchase Order-Invoice-Voucher; or SF 1034, Public Voucher for Purchases and Services Other Than Personal). A disbursement voucher may combine a payment and a collection by voucher deduction (for example, a civilian payroll voucher crediting deductions for federal tax, U.S. savings bonds, and civil service retirement to the appropriate accounts, with net pay disbursed to the payee).

10.1.1.1.1. A disbursement voucher for a payment to a non-federal entity that creates pecuniary liability under 31 U.S.C. § 3527 or 31 U.S.C. § 3528 must be certified by an appointed Certifying Officer who has completed Certifying Officer Legislation (COL) training, per 31 U.S.C. § 3325(a)(1) and (b) (see Section 6, subparagraph 6.1.1.). A disbursement voucher that transfers funds between appropriations or funds, makes payments entirely within the Federal government, or does not support or execute a subsequent payment transaction does not require a COL certified Certifying Officer.

10.1.1.1.2. Report EFT disbursements (including International Treasury Services for payments in foreign currencies) and U.S. Treasury check disbursements to the Payment Information Repository, citing the proper Treasury Account Symbol (TAS)/Business Event Type Code (BETC).

10.1.1.1.3. Report a no check/voucher for transfer by using a Classification Transactions and Accountability (CTA) transaction, citing the proper two-sided credit and debit entries with the proper TAS/BETC.

10.1.1.1.4. Report cash and LDA check disbursements by using a CTA transaction citing the Disbursing Officers' (DOs') Cash TAS/BETC and the program TAS/BETC listed on the disbursement voucher. DOs may consolidate multiple disbursement vouchers under one transaction reported to Treasury if they fall under the same TAS/BETC and Agency Location Code (ALC). DOs must ensure consolidated transactions have an audit trail that can be validated at the individual transaction level.

10.1.2. DoW authorizes DOs, under 31 U.S.C. § 3321(c)(2), to disburse public funds on receipt of vouchers certified by an appointed certifying officer (see 31 U.S.C. § 3325 and Section 6.0, subparagraph 6.1.1.).

10.2    POLICY

10.2.1. Legality and Propriety

10.2.1.1. Examine payment transactions for legality, propriety, limitations, and time frames under the statutes governing the various classes of expenditures, and for validity under general provisions of law.

10.2.1.2. A DO may request an advance decision on the propriety of any prospective payment, following the procedure in each section's standard operating procedure (see
Section 13.0, paragraph 13.2). DOs are not pecuniarily liable for payments they make based on advance decisions.

10.2.2. Substantiating Vouchers

10.2.2.1. Unless otherwise mandated by law, each transaction by an officer, agent, or employee of the U.S. Government that requires payment of money from the Treasury, or payment by a DO or agent, requires a written or approved electronically signed document, or series of documents, that includes a complete record of the transaction.

10.2.2.2. Each disbursing office that processes disbursements must maintain a detailed written agreement with its supporting Federal Reserve Bank (FRB), Treasury's fiscal agent. The DO must implement internal controls to confirm that the FRB successfully receives EFT payment files.

10.2.2.3. A DO need not make payment merely on the submission of formal evidence. If the facts do not justify payment, the DO must require a reasonable explanation or further evidence.

10.2.3. Using public funds to pay the expenses of a commission, council, board, or other similar body is prohibited by 31 U.S.C. § 1346 unless the creation of the body has been specifically authorized by law.

10.2.4. A DO generally may not make advance payments, prepayments, or overpayments of public monies; 31 U.S.C. § 3324, the Joint Travel Regulations, and Volumes 5, 7A, 8, 9, and 10 allow limited advances and prepayments.

10.2.5. Payments to Third Parties

10.2.5.1. Unless specifically authorized by law, monies the government owes to an individual are not subject to attachment, garnishment, or other legal processes. Do not certify or make payment to a third party even if the payee requests it. This restriction applies to all funds, including those held in trust by the DoW.

10.2.5.2. A civilian employee or military member may file a bankruptcy petition under 11 U.S.C. § 109, and the bankruptcy court may order the individual's pay sent to the bankruptcy trustee. Such payments are proper, and DOs incur no additional liability as a result (see Volume 8 for civilian employees and Volume 7A for military members).

10.2.5.3. Under 31 U.S.C. § 3332, Federal wage, salary, and retirement payments must be made by EFT to financial organizations for credit to payees' accounts (see also Volume 7A; Volume 8; and Volume 9).

10.2.6. Claims not founded on contracts, expressed or implied, but on merely equitable or moral grounds, are permitted only after direct authorization by Congress.

10.2.7. The government is self-insured (or bonded). Neither a DO nor any of the DO's agents may insure public funds or property.

10.2.8. Absent specific statutory authority, a DO may not pay for municipal services (for example, police and fire protection) if those services must be furnished to private citizens at no cost (see Volume 10).

10.2.9. Certified Disbursement Vouchers

10.2.9.1. DoW authorizes DOs, under 31 U.S.C. § 3321(c)(2), to disburse public funds on receipt of vouchers certified by an appointed certifying officer. When the disbursement voucher is certified by someone independent of the disbursing process, the DO has discretion to make the payment.

10.2.9.1.1. Certified vouchers must contain complete and accurate data, though content may vary slightly by disbursement type and form used. Write signatures and other information that become integral parts of original vouchers in permanent, non-erasable ink. Handwritten information must be legible. Approved electronic signatures are acceptable.

10.2.9.1.2. Return certified vouchers requiring correction to the functional area. Disbursing office personnel may not make these corrections. Corrected vouchers require recertification before disbursement.

10.2.9.1.3. Accept a legible copy of a signed travel voucher and its supporting documents, received in lieu of the original, for processing and payment as if it were the original. This includes copies received by facsimile transmission or scanned images forwarded via email.

10.2.9.2. Certified disbursement vouchers must contain the following minimum essential data:

10.2.9.2.1. voucher heading/date;

10.2.9.2.2. accounting classification;

10.2.9.2.3. the total amount;

10.2.9.2.4. the method of disbursement;

10.2.9.2.5. the individual or organization entitled to the payment.

10.2.9.3. A DO is pecuniarily liable for payments based on forged or fraudulent vouchers. A DO, Deputy DO (DDO), agent, or cashier who makes such a payment may request relief of liability (see Section 7.0).

10.3    DISBURSEMENT FORECASTING

10.3.1. Treasury's Bureau of the Fiscal Service (Fiscal Service) manages the government's daily cash position. DOs must follow current Fiscal Service guidance for reporting their anticipated aggregate level of planned disbursements for each disbursing method (for example, wire, Automated Clearing House (ACH), check). Forecasting is also addressed in I TFM 4A-4025.

10.4    DISBURSEMENT VOUCHERS

10.4.1. Keep a DD 2659, Voucher Control Log, daily for disbursement vouchers received or prepared in the disbursing office. The log must include the disbursement voucher number, payee name, amount, form of payment (for example, EFT, check, cash), and check/EFT trace number under "other." The log ensures all vouchers enter the accountability records and serves as a cross check against the DD 2657, Daily Statement of Accountability, and DD 2665, Daily Agent Accountability Summary: it compares vouchers paid by check to total checks written and vouchers paid by cash to cashier paid vouchers, associates returned and undeliverable checks with applicable vouchers, and transmits vouchers showing numbers used, unused, or voided.

10.4.2. Certification of Vouchers

10.4.2.1. The applicable entitlement areas (military, civilian, travel, and vendor pay) must ensure that all payments are proper, prepare the correct number of copies, and ensure that all vouchers contain complete and accurate data.

10.4.2.2. Certifying officers must examine payment vouchers before certification to confirm that the information agrees with all supporting documentation.

10.4.2.3. DOs must have access to the DD 577, Appointment/Termination Record
- Authorized Signature, to verify that vouchers submitted for payment were certified by persons authorized to certify them, and must disburse money only on vouchers certified by authorized certifying officers. A disbursing office that detects an improperly prepared voucher must return it to the functional area for correction and recertification.

10.4.3. An individual entitled to a payment (the payee) must receive the cash and sign the voucher. All cash payments require receipts; do not prepare duplicate receipts. DOs or their agents making cash payments must positively identify the payee using the photograph on the payee's DoW Common Access Card; other acceptable identification includes a driver's license and other identification normally accepted in the banking community to cash checks or bonds. The responsibility for payee identification may not be delegated. The exchange of currency and the receipt for it must be simultaneous. Requiring receipts in advance of actual cash payments is prohibited.

10.4.4. Responsible entitlement areas must send or deliver cash payment vouchers to the cashier area. Payees may hand carry vouchers when distance between the entitlement area and cashier area makes delivery impractical, but only if the total voucher amount is inscribed in words on the bottom of the voucher (for example, "sixty dollars and twenty cents"). Space words or enter lines to preclude alteration by inserting additional words, particularly at the start of the writing.

10.4.4.1. If the voucher deduction block is used on a payment voucher, the cashier must verify that it contains an appropriation and that the total to be paid is net of any deductions. After verifying these items, the cashier must initial the original voucher to identify who made the payment.

10.4.4.2. Cashiers must obtain the payee's signature in the space provided, or for multiple payments, on the sub-voucher or supporting documentation. The payee signs for receipt of cash using permanent, non-erasable ink; facsimile signatures and signatures in pencil are unacceptable. When payee signatures are on a sub-voucher or supporting documentation, annotate the "payee signature block" on the cover voucher with "See attached." Positively identify payees before making payments, comparing the voucher signature to identification cards or other acceptable identification. The signature form must match the payee as shown on the voucher. In the signature block, the payee must sign the first name, additional initials if any, then the surname, except as explained in the following subparagraphs.

10.4.4.2.1. A payee unable to write may indicate receipt of payment by signing an "X." A disinterested party, whose address must appear on the form, must witness it. If the payee is physically unable to write and asks someone to sign in his or her presence, a disinterested witness must verify the signature, which is then regarded as the payee's signing. File a physician's note addressing the payee's inability to sign with the original disbursement voucher.

10.4.4.2.2. Do not pay a mentally disabled payee who cannot comprehend a signature except in the presence of an appointed legal guardian. File certified copies of the court papers appointing the legal guardian with the original disbursement voucher. The legal guardian signs the payee's name followed by his or her own signature as legal guardian. On future payments, refer to the first disbursement voucher by DO voucher number and date paid to substantiate the guardianship. If the payee is in an asylum, file the superintendent's certificate that the payee was alive when payment was due with each disbursement voucher.

10.4.5. Check Disbursement Vouchers, Manual Voucher Processing Responsible

10.4.5.1. Make checks payable to the payee stated on the disbursement voucher. Number disbursing vouchers sequentially, using the lowest check number to pay the lowest numbered disbursement voucher or the first name on a payroll, to keep an unbroken sequence that supports check issue auditing and reporting. Consolidate multiple same day payments to the same payee into one check. DOs must ensure that inscribed checks duplicate the voucher information and may review this before or after signing the checks. The DO must ensure appropriate records are completed to control check writing. Automated systems producing disbursement vouchers must contain edit and validation controls so the exact voucher information passes to the check printer.

10.4.5.2. Entry of check numbers on automated disbursement vouchers is not required if the voucher processing system maintains complete audit trails between disbursement vouchers and hard copy records.

10.4.6. Do not collect an overpayment to a payee. Prepare an SF 1080 to charge the DoW Component Operation and Maintenance account and credit the appropriation originally charged for the payment. Do not issue a supplemental payment when a payee is underpaid unless the payee requests it.

10.4.7. Transmittal of Vouchers and Recording

10.4.7.1. DDOs, agents, and cashiers must include payment vouchers on the DD 2665 as prescribed in Section 16.0, subparagraph 16.2.1.2., and settle with the DO at the end of each business day.

10.4.8. The disbursing office supervisor must not routinely certify vouchers for payment but may certify cover vouchers supported by properly certified sub-vouchers. In those cases, the approving official of the supporting documentation must not be the cover voucher certifier. If an emergency requires the deputy, who also supervises the disbursing office, to certify a voucher not supported by certified sub-vouchers, the DO or another DDO must date and sign the voucher with a statement such as "Payment approved by Lieutenant John Doe, Disbursing Officer". For adequate internal control, neither the disbursing office supervisor nor other disbursing office personnel may input data into the computerized accounting system.

10.4.9. Deferred vouchers are paid vouchers not recorded in an accounting system, usually vouchers paid by an agent that must be returned for correction or paid by an agent but not yet examined by a DO. They do not impact the DO Cash TAS until processed. Responsible entitlement areas must act promptly to clear them and must keep a chronological record of actions taken, showing the expected clearance date. DOs or their DDOs must review those actions weekly to ensure prompt correction of irregularities causing deferment.

10.4.10. Classified Payments

10.4.10.1. A DO making payments classified for security purposes must prepare a covering disbursement voucher that contains no information requiring a security classification. On the original and all copies, show only the payee's name and address, amount, date of payment, complete accounting data, voucher number, check number, DO's name, DSSN, and disbursing office payment data in the "Paid By" (or "Brief") block. Payments under classified contracts must include instructions requiring the supplier to limit invoice information so supplies or services are identifiable only by reference to the contract. The DO (for collateral classified programs) or the voucher preparing office (for special access programs) must allow access to classified documents only to persons who need it to perform official duties.

10.4.10.2. Personnel who process classified documents must hold a security clearance equal to or higher than the documents they process. DOs or voucher preparing offices must assign duties so that only a minimum number of persons need access to classified information. Mark and store classified documents per prescribed security regulations. Do not attach classified essential supporting documents, invoices, or certificates to the original disbursement voucher; instead, identify them by the DO's name, voucher number, DSSN, and account period. Retain them at the paying disbursing office (for collateral classified programs) or the voucher preparing office (for special access programs) with other classified material. Include one of the following statements in the voucher portion describing the articles or services purchased:

10.4.10.3. Distribute the original and required copies of the covering disbursement voucher in the normal manner. Do not attach the classified supporting documents.

10.4.11. Use a DD 281, Voucher for Emergency or Extraordinary Expense Expenditures, to make payments from contingency funds.

10.4.12. Hand Carrying Disbursement Vouchers

10.4.12.1. Send payment vouchers prepared outside the disbursing office to the disbursing office so the payee cannot access them.

10.4.13. EFT Payments

10.4.13.1. EFT payments go to the FRB on debit vouchers showing the date payment is due. The DO must implement internal controls to confirm the FRB receives the payment files successfully and on schedule, and must retain the memorandum copy of the debit voucher. DOs that transmit payment files electronically use the FRB's summary of ACH activity report instead of the debit voucher; in either case, the FRB issues a confirmation debit voucher to the DO. For an EFT transaction, record the debit voucher as a negative deposit, with the payroll, travel, or vendor payment recorded as a gross disbursement.

10.4.13.2. When a financial institution returns one or more EFT/ACH payments to a paying office, the DO must prepare and process a collection voucher to account for the returned funds, crediting the appropriation from which they were originally disbursed. EFT returns must be submitted back to the originating ALC, crediting the TAS from which they were originally disbursed. Record the collection on the DD 2657 with an offsetting transaction for the FRB deposit ticket. The DO must notify the appropriate entitlement area by providing a copy of the collection voucher and any rejection information received, such as the reject code (see Treasury's Green Book, Section 5, for payment rejection codes). The entitlement area must track, monitor, and research the cause of the return and provide a recertified voucher to initiate an appropriate EFT/ACH payment within 5 business days.

10.4.13.3. When notified of the death of a military retiree or annuitant, the DFAS Cleveland (DFAS-CL) DO must contact the decedent's bank to request the return of all payments made since the death. The DFAS-CL DO has three years from the date of the Financial Management Service (FMS) Form 133, Notice of Reclamation, to submit FMS 135, ACH Reclaims (see Treasury's Green Book, Section 6, for detailed instructions).

10.5    DEPOSIT FUND AND BUDGET CLEARING ACCOUNTS

10.5.1. Disposition of Funds in Deposit Fund Accounts

10.5.1.1. For withdrawal applied to an appropriation, receipt account, or other deposit fund account, use an SF 1081 for the disbursement and collection and submit it as substantiation for either or both. The SF 1081 must not be used for check or cash payment.

10.5.1.2. Only one deposit fund account may be charged on a single voucher. Submit charges to accounts F0109, Federal Tax Withheld from Payments to Nonresident Aliens, and F3875, Budget Clearing Account (Suspense), on separate vouchers.

10.5.2. F3875, Budget Clearing Account (Suspense)

10.5.2.1. After determining the proper disposition of funds in this account, transfer the amount on an SF 1080 or SF 1081 to the proper account and explain the charges on that form (see I TFM 2-5135 for guidance on using F3875). Use this account to hold unidentifiable collections temporarily for no more than 60 days, or use other business processes approved by the Fiscal Service. Payment from the F3875 suspense account is prohibited.

10.5.2.2. When the accounting office notifies the DO and requests the documentation needed to process a rejected transaction, the DO must send the requested documentation to the accounting office within 30 days.

10.5.2.2.1. When supporting documentation is maintained locally, the DO must send it to the accounting office immediately.

10.5.3. Overages

10.5.3.1. For an overage that should not have been accounted for as a collection, the responsible functional area prepares an SF 1034 payable to "Adjustments" to reverse the erroneous collection and permit proper accounting. Do not issue a check or cash payment for this voucher.

10.6    PAYMENTS IN SUPPORT OF ADVANCE PAYMENT POOL AGREEMENTS

Advance payment pool agreements may be established under FAR 32.408 and DFARS 232.470 to finance performance of more than one contract held by a single contractor. Cash advanced to a contractor must be reported on the DD 2657 and reflected on the DO Cash TAS until the money is returned or disbursed. Follow Volume 10 for processing advance payments.

title: Section 11.0: Smart Cards for Financial Applications
content:
11.0    SMART CARDS FOR FINANCIAL APPLICATIONS

11.1    POLICY ON SMART CARD UTILIZATION

11.1.1. DFAS has management and oversight responsibility for the functional aspects and use of financial Smart Cards within the DoW, except for GSA SmartPay products. Written DFAS approval is required for all pilot and full rollout Smart Card usage (e.g., stored value or debit) employing single-purpose or multifunctional applications. This chapter follows I TFM 4-9000; Treasury guidance supersedes any conflicting information in this chapter.

11.1.2. Smart Card Program Approval

11.1.2.1. To establish a new Smart Card program, a DoW agency must submit a request for approval to DFAS-Indianapolis Center, Enterprise Solutions and Standards, Disbursing (DFAS-IN/JJFKCD). A separate request is required for each financial application.

11.1.2.2. An approval request must indicate whether the program is a pilot effort or a full rollout program.

11.1.2.2.1. Pilot programs are temporary and must operate for no less than 90 days and no more than 180 days. Pilots test card programs before full rollout.

11.1.2.2.2. Full rollout programs are non-temporary and must operate longer than 180 days. A full rollout should follow a pilot.

11.1.2.3. An approval request must be submitted as an application package to DFAS-IN/JJFKCD and must be completed before approval of any pilot or full rollout. The package must include the items below.

11.1.2.3.1. The agency headquarters, or designated representative, should request approval of the pilot or full rollout program via memorandum. It should be addressed to DFAS, Enterprise Solutions and Standards;

11.1.2.3.2. All pilot and full rollout programs are required to submit a completed DoW Financial Smart Card Application;

11.1.2.3.3. The CONOPS document should contain guidance on the use of the Smart Card program by the agency;

11.1.2.3.4. The package must contain copies of coordination documentation, including the agency or component leadership’s and servicing Disbursing Officer’s (DO) endorsement of memoranda;

11.1.2.3.5. A copy of the letter designating the agency Smart Card project manager must be submitted with each package. See subparagraph 11.1.4 for information on project managers; and

11.1.2.3.6. If the request is to move from a pilot Smart Card program to a full rollout, include an analysis showing:

11.1.2.3.6.1. Any savings realized from the pilot program;

11.1.2.3.6.2. How the pilot program is an improvement over the pre-pilot environment; and

11.1.2.3.6.3. The results of relevant performance measures used during the pilot and proposed for the full rollout.

11.1.3. Fiscal Service and the implementing agency must establish a memorandum of understanding (MOU) before implementing a new Smart Card program. The MOU sets the program terms, the respective responsibilities of the agency and Fiscal Service, the program and card types, the funding schedule, and the fees and costs each party pays.

11.1.4. Agency Smart Card Project Manager

11.1.4.1. The agency must designate a Smart Card project manager and alternate in writing before implementing a Smart Card program.

11.1.4.2. The agency must specifically identify the tasks for which the Smart Card project manager is responsible. The project manager must manage the Smart Card program and the activities in this chapter per the MOU between Fiscal Service and the agency, the Smart Card standard operating procedures (SOPs) and other instructional documents, and program-specific policies and procedures the agency develops in consultation with Fiscal Service.

11.1.5. Smart Card AO(s)

11.1.5.1. The agency must designate one or more Smart Card accountable officials (AOs). If the AO is already appointed as a Disbursing Officer (DO), Deputy DO (DDO), or Disbursing Agent and the card-program responsibilities fall within that appointment, no additional appointment documentation is needed. Otherwise, the agency must appoint the AO by Letter of Appointment or DD Form 577, which lists the individual's responsibilities; a further letter is required when the individual no longer serves as the AO.

11.1.5.2. The agency must specifically identify the tasks for which the Smart Card AOs are responsible and must segregate those duties appropriately per agency policy. As applicable, AOs carry the duties and liability of a certifying officer or a DO, depending on the AO's designation, under 31 U.S.C. §§ 3322, 3325, and 3528 and other applicable laws. The AOs must manage the Smart Card program and the activities in this chapter per the MOU, the Smart Card SOPs and other instructional documents, and program-specific policies and procedures the agency develops with Fiscal Service.

11.1.6. DoW agencies responsible for the card programs in this chapter must develop and maintain detailed SOPs that comply with all current applicable regulations and cover all aspects of their card program for daily operations and contingencies.

11.1.7. The DO is accountable for physical loss of funds and for overage of Smart Card funds. If a loss or overage occurs, the DO or designated representative must follow the guidance in Section 7.0.

11.1.8. The program point of contact and designated agency representatives must establish procedures to determine card usage and a secure method of card delivery.

11.1.9. Smart Card stock must be treated like blank check stock. Storage and security requirements for blank check stock are in Section 8.0, subparagraph 8.2.4.

11.1.10. For all stored value and combination cards reported lost, stolen, damaged, or malfunctioning, a locally produced list must be created for audit purposes. If a Smart Card is reported lost, damaged, or malfunctioning, follow the procedures in the applicable MOU and SOPs; for the U.S. Debit Card, contact Fiscal Service's financial agent.

11.1.11. Agencies participating in a Smart Card program must do the following.

11.1.11.1. Include a process for reporting and educating Smart Card cardholders on how to promptly report any loss, theft, fraudulent, and unauthorized use of Smart Cards, PINs, passwords, or other security breach or malfunction involving the Smart Card program to Treasury or Treasury's financial or fiscal agent, and to the agency Smart Card Project Manager;

11.1.11.2. Aggressively investigate and prosecute (or assist in investigations, and prosecutions of) end-user theft, fraud, unauthorized use, or improper use of the Smart Card service that occur in agencies’ areas of operation, and assist in obtaining restitution for the party suffering the loss;

11.1.11.3. Ensure that appropriate anti-money laundering controls and procedures are in place, to document the flow of monies onto or off a Smart Card; and

11.1.11.4. When a funds pool is used to fund an SVC; compensate the SVC funds pool for losses that result from theft, fraud, unauthorized use or other improper use of SVC equipment or resources for which agencies are responsible; unless the funds pool has been reimbursed from other sources, or the Treasury determines that such compensation is unnecessary or does not serve the SVC program’s best interests.

11.1.12. Audit Requirements

11.1.12.1. An initial inventory must be completed and recorded on receipt of Smart Cards from Fiscal Service or other designated representatives, and a signed receipt must be provided to the issuing representative. The DO or designated representative must complete an SVC inventory log when releasing Smart Card stock to authorized personnel and when monitoring returns of unused cards, and must maintain a copy of the signed receipt.

11.1.12.2. At least once every calendar month, the DO or designated representative must inventory all Smart Cards secured in the vault, counting open containers individually and by unique sequential number. Damaged or tampered containers must be opened, and all cards must be individually counted and their unique sequential numbers verified. The disbursing office must retain a detailed inventory record showing total cards on hand and unique sequential numbers by card type. At least once each calendar quarter, the agency's cash verification team must conduct an unannounced verification of any Smart Card stock (e.g., U.S. Debit Cards, EagleCash, EZpay), covering cards received, issued, returned, and on hand, and a copy of the inventory must be attached to their quarterly cash verification report.

11.2    DAILY REPORTING REQUIREMENTS FOR STORED VALUE CARD

The scenarios that follow impact the DO Cash TAS and must be properly reported to Treasury.

11.2.1. Issued cards may be funded by personal check, cash, split pay, or transfer from the cardholder's home financial institution. Funding through split pay or the cardholder's home financial institution does not impact the DO's accountability/DO Cash TAS; funding by personal check or cash increases the DO's accountability/DO Cash TAS.

11.2.2. Before departing a deployed environment or ship, or being separated from active duty, a cardholder may transfer remaining value to their home financial institution or request a cash-out from the DO paid in cash or by U.S. Treasury check. Vendors using a POS terminal may request a cash-out equal to their POS terminal transactions. Transfer of value to a home financial institution does not impact the DO's accountability/DO Cash TAS; cash-out transactions decrease it.

11.3    U.S. DEBIT CARD PROGRAM (USDC)

11.3.1. Card Funds Access After implementation of the USDC program, the agency disburses payments to a card account and the funds are accessed via a debit card issued to a Federal payment recipient. Cards may be funded through a Card Funding Account (CFA) owned by the agency and held by the financial agent, through EFT via the ACH network, or by utilizing the Automated Standard Application for Payments system to authorize the financial agent to draw down agency funds. Funds held in a CFA must be reflected in the DO Cash TAS. DOs establish funds in a CFA through an EFT for Cash and record the funds on the DD 2657. Disbursements out of the CFA must be reported as cash disbursements.

title: Section 12.0: Electronic Commerce and Deposit of Public Funds
content:
12.0    ELECTRONIC COMMERCE AND DEPOSIT OF PUBLIC FUNDS

12.1    GENERAL

12.1.1. Per 31 U.S.C. §§ 3302 and 3322, disbursing officers (DO) may deposit public funds and draw public funds from the Treasury or a depositary only as necessary to make payments. Additional statutes, regulations, and other guidance are referenced under each section of this chapter.

12.2    ELECTRONIC FUNDS TRANSFER (EFT)

12.2.1. Per 31 U.S.C. § 3332, EFT is mandatory within the DoW. Exceptions are provided in I TFM 4A-2000.

12.2.2. Payment and payroll files must transmit to the Federal Reserve Bank (FRB) by electronic file transmission.

12.2.3. Official Authorization List (OAL) for the FRB

12.2.3.1. Each DO must validate the contact form for the DO's office at least annually. If changes are required, follow the process in the FRB Service guidance on the FRB Services web page in Table S.4 (Sending Point and Service Provider Contact form). Once completed, send a copy to DFAS, Enterprise Solutions and Standards, Disbursing (DFAS- IN/JJFKCD), 8899 East 56th Street, Indianapolis, IN 46249-2700 (dfas.indianapolis- in.jjf.mbx.ess-disbursing@mail.mil), and submit the original to the Fiscal Service, who will sign and forward it to the FRB.

12.3    CARD ACQUIRING SERVICE (CAS)

12.3.1. Activities participating in the CAS must comply with I TFM 5-7000 when processing credit and debit card transactions. To establish a processing relationship, activities must complete and submit the Card Acquiring Service Application (CASA) to Fiscal Service for approval. Before submission, activities must coordinate with their servicing DO.

12.3.2. All activities must settle (balance or reconcile) daily, regardless of the amount accumulated that day. Activities that fail to settle electronically every day must pay the assessed non-qualifying interchange fee. The network bank informs the activity of its cutoff times for deposits. In an electronic environment, settlement should occur through an Electronic Data Capture/Point of Sale during the day, or once at the close of business, to meet the deposit cutoff time.

12.3.3. Based on the report requirements in the participation agreement with the network bank, the network bank makes reports of the merchant's credit and debit card activity available electronically to the participating DoW activity (merchant). The summary details deposit dates, deposit dollar amounts, number of transactions processed, adjustment charges, and chargebacks. The activity must use this report to reconcile any differences between the report and accounting system entries. The activity must also reconcile the report with the DoD (DD) Form 1131, Cash Collection Voucher, submitted to the DO or Deputy DO, and with the deposit information posted in the Collection Information Repository (CIR).

12.3.4. Each participating DoW activity must establish internal control procedures to ensure the credit and debit card transaction documentation supporting all DD 1131s submitted to the DO is properly safeguarded. The activity must make the documentation available for the DO's quarterly cash verification board, the collection agent audit board, and other audit purposes.

12.4    INTRA-GOVERNMENTAL PAYMENT AND COLLECTION (IPAC) SYSTEM

12.4.1. Originating the IPAC Transactions

12.4.1.1. A collection or disbursement voucher (e.g., DD 1131; Standard Form (SF) 1080, Voucher for Transfers Between Appropriations and/or Funds; or SF 1034, Public Voucher for Purchases and Services Other than Personal) must be prepared for each bill or payment entered in the system and processed through the DO in the same manner as other vouchers, except that no check or cash payment is sent or received.

12.4.1.2. DoW IPAC transactions require three additional data elements beyond the Treasury required information: when initiating a payment or collection in IPAC, the sender Business Event Type Code (BETC), receiver BETC, and receiver Treasury Account Symbol (TAS) are required for every transaction. An ALC may also require specific or descriptive data necessary to process the transaction completely; this information should be in the Buy-Sell Agreement agreed upon by the participating ALCs. See I TFM 2-5135 for TAS/BETC reporting of accounts F3500 (Collections and/or Payments Default) and 3502 (IPAC Default). Agencies must correctly reclassify, in the Classification Transactions and Accountability, all system defaulted transactions to a valid receipt or expenditure TAS by the third business day following the close of the accounting month.

12.4.2. The IPAC system is available through the last day of each month to enter bills or transfers for that month. However, unless the Buy-Sell Agreements set a different cutoff date and time, agencies must not process new transactions during the last five business days of the month, to avoid month-end accounting problems. When revising Trading Partner Agreements (TPA) to incorporate the five-workday cutoff, agencies must use Fiscal Service Forms 7600A and 7600B as the Department continues to migrate toward G-Invoicing. Each DoW reporting entity must apply the General Terms and Conditions (GT&Cs) for intragovernmental transaction account reconciliation, derived from I TFM 2-4700, to all transactions with internal DoW trading partners currently using G-Invoicing for GT&Cs. Cancelling year transactions must also conform to the fiscal year (FY) cutoff requirement in paragraph 12.9.

12.4.3. Recording IPAC Transactions

12.4.3.1. DoW financial reporting entities should include IPAC in intra-governmental transactions and must develop and implement internal controls to ensure receipt and acceptance is properly documented. Entities must make this documentation available within the timeframe an auditor prescribes when requested during audits.

12.5    PAY.GOV

12.5.1. Implementation

12.5.1.1. Before implementing Pay.gov, activities must obtain the approval of the servicing DO.

12.6    DEPOSITS OF FUNDS

Under 31 U.S.C. § 3302, custodians of money (e.g., DOs) holding cash or negotiable instruments in excess of either current requirements or the amount authorized to be held at personal risk, whichever is less, must make a prompt deposit in an authorized depositary of the Treasury for credit to the Treasurer of the United States. This does not apply to instruments to be returned to remitters in the form received (e.g., deposits of unsuccessful bidders for the sale of government property). Process all physically received negotiable instrument deposit transactions through the Over-the-Counter Channel Application (OTCnet) and cite a valid TAS and BETC at the time of the deposit.

12.6.1. Cash collected and deposited before the end of the business day does not impact the DO Cash TAS. Deposited funds must cite the appropriate TAS/BETC that appears on the DD 1131.

12.6.2. Cash reflected on the DD 2657, Daily Statement of Accountability (on the ending accountability and deposited lines), must cite the DO Cash TAS/BETC at the time of the deposit.

12.6.3. OTCnet

12.6.3.1. Process all physically received negotiable instrument deposit transactions through OTCnet. Agencies unable to use OTCnet for deposits of negotiable instruments due to contingency operations must establish depositary arrangements with US Bank's Mail-In Treasury General Account (MITGA) through the FRB of St. Louis. This includes the deposit of commercial checks and U.S. Treasury checks. For more information on MITGA, see subparagraph 12.6.5.1.2.

12.6.3.2. At a minimum, Block 6 of the OTCnet deposit ticket must identify the depositing entity's name and location and the deposit preparer's name, email address, and phone number. The extent of additional information required in Block 6 is at the discretion of the DO.

12.6.3.3. After scanning items in OTCnet, retain the scanned negotiable instruments until you verify they reside within OTCnet and a good image is on file. This verification must take place within 14 calendar days. Secure scanned items awaiting approval in an approved manner (see Section 4.0, paragraph 4.2). Once verified, destroy the negotiable instruments.

12.6.4. Depositaries

12.6.4.1. III TFM 2-1000 describes general depositaries as commercial banks or other financial institutions designated and authorized by the Treasury to maintain a demand account in its name to accept deposits to the TGA. These depositaries are designated only where needed to receive deposits of public funds for credit to the TGA or to furnish cash to DOs for official disbursements. If more than one bank is authorized at a base, station, installation, or command, the local commander must give equal recognition when recommending designation of authorized financial institutions as TGA depositaries. After Treasury approval, the commander should reasonably distribute official financial transactions among the approved depositaries. Deposit public funds only in a financial institution approved as a general depositary, except as shown in subparagraph 8.2.4, and mail deposits to a TGA only when given specific Treasury authorization.

12.6.4.2. DOs formally request authorization to deposit collections with a general depositary, or change from one authorized depositary to another, per I TFM 5-2000. This requirement also covers instances when on-base banks or credit union offices undergo changes such as acquisitions or mergers. Send the completed request, no later than 35 calendar days before the desired deposit start date, to the DoW Banking and Credit Union Office by email to dfas.dscc.jjf.mbx.dod-financial-institutions-tga@mail.mil for review, coordination, and submission to the FRB of St. Louis.

12.6.4.3. The DO must advise DFAS-JJF/CO of the date on which the need for a general depositary ceases to exist, and the reason.

12.6.4.4. Limited depositaries are designated only to receive deposits made by or on behalf of DOs for credit to their official non-symbol checking accounts maintained with such depositaries. Limited depositaries may not accept deposits for credit to the Treasury. For additional information on limited depositary accounts, see Section 15.0.

12.6.5. Deposit Requirements

12.6.5.1. Deposit all funds received for credit to the Treasury's account promptly.

12.6.5.1.1. Agencies must deposit receipts totaling $5,000 or more on the same business day received, before the depositary cutoff time. Make deposits as late as possible before the cutoff time to maximize daily deposit amounts. Collections totaling less than $5,000 may be accumulated and deposited when the total reaches $5,000. However, make deposits by Thursday of each week, regardless of the amount accumulated. For additional information, review
I TFM 5-2065.

12.6.5.1.2. Send mailed deposits to US Bank's MITGA rather than to the FRB. The MITGA receives deposits of commercial checks, U.S. Treasury checks, and, at the direction of the DO, cash. Before mailing deposits, the DO must establish depositary arrangements with US Bank's MITGA through the FRB of St. Louis. Once approved, establish the MITGA within OTCnet and use OTCnet in conjunction with the MITGA. When using the MITGA during contingencies (when OTCnet is not available), the DO must contact the FRB of St. Louis to obtain permission to mail a deposit. Once approved, the requestor receives a special form to complete and mail with the deposit. The former SF 215 (manually prepared deposit ticket) may not be used.

12.6.5.1.3. For Navy vessels at sea, when daily mail service is not available, receipts consisting only of personal checks, money orders, and other negotiable instruments may accumulate up to $5,000 before they must be deposited, provided a deposit of all receipts on hand is made at least once each week. The DO prepares the deposits for mailing by registered mail and delivers them to the military post office onboard. The DO may not hold negotiable instruments pending arrival at the next scheduled port of call. Regardless of the total amount, the interval since the last deposit, and the type of instruments on hand, DOs on board naval vessels must make a deposit on the last regular business day before leaving port and on the first regular business day after returning to port for any at sea period exceeding 1 week.

12.6.5.2. Deposit negotiable instruments (e.g., personal checks, traveler's checks, cash, and money orders) payable in U.S. dollars for credit to the Treasury's account at an approved general depositary. DOs may deposit Treasury Checks at Military Banking Facilities overseas.

12.6.5.3. Checks drawn on foreign banks in U.S. dollars, payable through a bank in the United States, must have an American Bankers Association (ABA) routing and transit number (RTN) printed on the item and be magnetic ink character recognition encoded with a U.S. bank's ABA RTN at the bottom left side of the check. Group these checks on a single deposit ticket and deposit them as described in subparagraph 8.3.2.1.

12.6.5.4. In conjunction with OTCnet, deposit cash, checks, drafts, or money orders in person with an authorized TGA. If an in person cash deposit is impracticable at an authorized TGA, the next most preferred method is by armored car. The least preferred method of depositing cash is by registered mail to the MITGA. Because delivery confirmation may require an additional fee to request a copy of the signature record with return receipt, the DO must ensure funding is available. Charge costs for a cashier's check or money order to operations and maintenance or working capital funds available to the DO. If cash must be mailed, the cash must be either double wrapped or placed in an inner and outer container. Deposit damaged or mutilated currency per Section 4.0, subparagraph 4.4.7.

12.6.5.5. Agent officers or any authorized collection officer may make deposits on behalf of the DO when an approved designated depositary is available. These individuals must use OTCnet for deposits.

12.6.5.6. When an approved designated depositary is not available, agent officers or any authorized collecting officers may send cash to the DO by conversion to postal money order, bank money order, or cashier's check. Pay the fee for purchase of the cashier's check or postal/bank money order in cash at the time of purchase and attach the receipt to the DD 1131. Deduct the cost of the cashier's check or postal/bank money order from the total amount collected. Show in the body of the DD 1131 the total amount collected, the fee for the cashier's check or postal/bank money order, the net collection, the bank, and the date of the money order.

12.6.5.7. When using the OTCnet Deposit Reporting function, all negotiable instruments in payment of an obligation due the United States, regardless of the payee to which drawn, must be endorsed on the back in the 1 1/2 inch space along the trailing edge. Insert the component's name (e.g., Army, Navy, or DFAS) first and then the 4-digit disbursing activity's DSSN in the blank following "DSSN." Enter these manually, mechanically, or as part of the stamp. Enter the date of the deposit in the blank following "Date" to correspond with the bank's business day. See subparagraph 8.3.1.

12.6.5.8. Do not accept checks with conditional endorsements (e.g., "Payment in Full"). Return these checks to the drawers and advise them that the DoW cannot legally accept conditional endorsements.

12.6.5.9. DOs must keep a complete record of negotiable instruments mailed or presented to depositaries, consisting of scanned or photocopied images of both sides of each instrument. If imaging is not possible, prepare a typed or written list showing the source, financial institution on which drawn, type of instrument, serial number, payee, maker, endorser (name of person from whom received when other than the drawer), date drawn, and amount. Copies of collection vouchers or other documents showing the same data are acceptable. Because the DO bears pecuniary liability for an item lost in banking channels when the maker cannot be identified for replacement, the DO must retain these images or lists in active files until CIR confirms receipt of the deposit.

12.6.5.10. When a negotiable instrument is lost, whether before or after deposit, the DO must adjust the affected accounts and immediately request that the maker stop payment and replace it with a new check or other form of payment. DOs must inform members of their legal obligation for the check and offer them another opportunity to replace it. If the military member refuses, the DO may pursue involuntary collection action against the member's pay, as with any other debt.

12.6.5.11. A DO who is transferred or reassigned without being relieved by another DO must deposit all funds before the transfer or reassignment occurs. This includes all funds held by deputies, agents, or cashiers, including imprest and change funds. The DO must report each deposit made during the period, including the final deposit.

12.6.6. Deposit Transactions

12.6.6.1. The DO must immediately record all debit vouchers received on the DD 2657 and include them in the SF 1219 for the month received. Depositaries may process a debit voucher to charge the depositing DSSN when a check is returned unpaid or lost after deposit, and depositaries and the Treasury may issue debit vouchers for other valid charges against a DO's account, such as exchange fees and collection charges on foreign instruments deposited.

12.6.6.2. DOs must comply with debit vouchers received from a depositary whenever any one of these conditions exists: the deposit including the lost or dishonored check was made during the incumbency of the current DO; the deposit was made during the incumbency of a DO whose account is in the 90-day local retention period; or the maker or endorser of the lost or dishonored check is locally available for collection action. If none apply, the current DO must forward the debit voucher by cover letter to the activity designated to settle the former DO's account, and must also send either the original dishonored check returned by the depositary or, for lost checks, a copy of the relevant abstract from the listing of instruments deposited. The cover letter must include the most recent information on the present location and status of the maker or endorser, and the DO must send a copy of the cover letter to the issuing depositary.

12.7    PAYMENT INFORMATION REPOSITORY (PIR)

12.7.1. Reconciliation of EFT Transactions

12.7.1.1. DOs must reconcile their EFT payment data, such as EFT debit vouchers, with PIR. If the purpose of an EFT transaction cannot be determined at the point of origin (time of transaction), the DO must credit either F3875 and F3885 (Budget Clearing Account (Suspense)) or Shared Accounting Module default clearing accounts F3500 for proprietary payments and collections and F3502 for Intra-Governmental Payment and Collection, as appropriate, and follow the guidance in Volume 4.

12.8    CIR

12.8.1. DOs must confirm deposits using CIR. For guidance on deposit reconciliation, see subparagraph 12.8.2.

12.8.2. Deposit Reconciliation – General

12.8.2.1. DOs or their designees must reconcile DoW financial system data daily with CARS and maintain a manual or mechanized subsidiary record of all debit voucher differences. If the purpose of a deposit cannot be determined at the point of origin (time of transaction), the DO must credit either F3875 and F3885 (Budget Clearing Account (Suspense)) or Shared Accounting Module default clearing accounts F3500 for proprietary payments and collections and F3502 for Intra-Governmental Payment and Collection, as appropriate, and follow the guidance in Volume 4.

12.8.2.2. CARS reporters must ensure there are no uncleared statements of differences before becoming a "Full" CARS daily reporter. Agencies that use the online application within CARS for interagency billings and payments for goods and services no longer receive a statement of difference report (formerly Financial Management Service (FMS) Form 6652) and are no longer required to follow the FMS 6652 guidance. The Treasury compares the value of deposits and debit vouchers reported on DOs' activity reports to those reported through
CIR.

12.8.2.3. Treat all differences that have not been reconciled within 60 days of the transaction, and that are validated as meeting the criteria of an actual physical loss of funds, as a loss or overage of funds with the associated pecuniary liability prescribed in Section 7.0. Do not treat timing differences or reporting errors as a loss of funds, but the DFAS site must pursue aggressive action to clear the differences with appropriate offsetting transactions, through the departmental level, Treasury, or agency, within 60 days of the offsetting transaction.

12.8.2.4. DOs must strictly follow the preparation requirements for deposit tickets and debit vouchers and must report all deposit tickets and debit vouchers promptly and properly.

12.8.2.5. Once deposit tickets are released to a depositary, the documents cannot be recalled, corrected, or resubmitted, and the Treasury prescribes specific instructions to approved depositaries on adjusting errors discovered after the day of deposit. DOs must take aggressive action to reconcile or clear all differences as rapidly as possible after the Treasury notifies them that a difference exists.

12.8.2.6. To maintain control, the DO or the DO's designees must monitor deposit activity daily using CIR and maintain a manual or mechanized subsidiary record of all deposit differences. They must review the record of differences at least weekly to ensure the differences clear, and must retain the evidentiary documentation supporting the review for the retention period in Section 16.0, paragraph 16.2. These records need not be certified. Each time there is a change of DOs, the incoming DO must validate the unresolved differences. If the departing DO cannot provide the incoming DO with documentation supporting the unresolved items, the departing DO must process the unsupported items as a loss or overage of funds (see Section 7.0).

12.8.3. Deposit Reconciliation – Discrepancies

12.8.3.1. If the depositary does not confirm a deposit presented by mail within a reasonable period of time, the DO must initiate follow-up action with the depositary to determine the deposit's status. A reasonable period of time is the normal mailing time from the date mailed to the depositary until the deposit is confirmed, based on past experience, and tactical DOs must consider unit movement schedules and locations when the deposit was mailed. In any event, the DO must initiate follow-up action within 30 days from the date of mailing a deposit.

12.8.3.2. A follow-up request to a depositary must include a copy of the applicable deposit ticket and a description or copies of the instruments in the deposit.
