The depositary provides confirmation information in response. If the depositary acknowledges receipt of the deposit but refuses to report the transaction to the Treasury, the DO must provide written notification, with copies of all correspondence and documents involved, to DFAS-JJF/CO, which then pursues resolution through the Treasury and provides the DO written instructions on additional actions to take.

12.8.3.3. Depositaries generally prepare debit vouchers only to adjust erroneous amounts on deposit tickets and debit vouchers, to return dishonored negotiable instruments, or to adjust deposit tickets for counterfeit currency, and all debit vouchers depositaries prepare are reported automatically to the Treasury. Unless the DSSN on the debit voucher is not the DSSN of the DO receiving it, the DO must record the debit voucher on receipt and include it in the detailed deposit activity report. This requirement applies regardless of whether the debit voucher is deemed erroneous or the reason for the charge needs further clarification.

12.8.3.4. Daily CIR monitoring alerts the DO that a depositary has issued a debit voucher. The DO must confirm the information in CIR and include the debit voucher on the DD 2657 and detailed deposit activity report during the month of receipt. The DO must report the debit voucher using the month and year of issue reported by the depositary in CIR, not the month and year in which it is being recorded. Section II, Part B, Column (3) of the SF 1219 must indicate the actual month and year of the debit voucher as reported by the depositary, and the detailed deposit activity report must use the same actual month and year.

12.8.3.5. If a transaction occurs near the end of the month and the DO cannot process and report it in the transaction month, a deposit difference will occur. To correct it, the DO must obtain the transaction documentation and process both the payment and the debit voucher on the DD 2657, SF 1219, and detailed deposit activity report during the current month. The DO must report the debit voucher using the actual month and year of the payment reported by the depositary in CIR, not the month and year in which it is being reported, and must include it in the detailed deposit activity report using that actual month and year.

12.8.3.6. Daily CIR monitoring alerts the DO that the depositary has issued a new debit voucher. DOs using depositaries that routinely process debit vouchers this way should contact the depositary in writing to request an explanation and ask that the depositary process the debit vouchers the DO provides with the payment files. If the depositary refuses to process the DO's debit vouchers, the DO must provide written notification, with copies of all correspondence and documents, to DFAS-JJF/CO, which will pursue resolution through the Treasury and provide the DO written instructions on any additional actions to take.

12.9    CLOSED/CANCELLED ACCOUNTS

On September 30 of the fifth fiscal year after the period of availability for an obligation of a fixed appropriation account ends, the account must be closed and any remaining balance, whether obligated or unobligated, must be cancelled and is thereafter not available for obligation or expenditure for any purpose, unless exempt by a provision of an appropriation law. Collections authorized or required to be credited to an appropriation account but not received before the account closes must be deposited in the Treasury as miscellaneous receipts per 31 U.S.C. Sec 1552(a). All cancelling-year transactions, such as transactions to be paid from an appropriation cancelling at the end of the current fiscal year, must be submitted to DFAS no later than September 15 each year, or the business day before when September 15 falls on a weekend.

title: Section 13.0: Questionable and Fraudulent Claims
content:
13.0    QUESTIONABLE AND FRAUDULENT CLAIMS

13.1    GENERAL

13.1.1. This chapter establishes policy for processing questionable and fraudulent claims presented for certification or payment that a Certifying Officer (CO) or Disbursing Officer (DO) believes to be illegal or improper. Determining potentially fraudulent claims is the responsibility of the CO and DO. The CO and DO must research claims and base their determinations on the criteria in this chapter and the legal opinions of the supporting Staff Judge Advocates (SJA) or other legal counsel. A fraudulent claim is any intentional deception designed to unlawfully deprive the United States of something of value or to secure from the United States a benefit, privilege, allowance, or consideration to which a claimant is not entitled. This chapter also addresses a CO's, DO's, or head of an agency's right to request an advance decision from the appropriate authority.

13.1.2. Authoritative Guidance

13.1.2.1. Under Title 31, United States Code (U.S.C.), section 3529 (31 U.S.C. § 3529), a CO, DO, or head of an agency may request an advance decision on the propriety of any prospective payment from an authorized official. This authority does not cover legal decisions on payments already made or hypothetical cases.

13.2    ADVANCE DECISIONS

13.2.1. The submitter of an application states the facts and evidence supporting the reasons for the request and on which to base the decision. An application must generally include a specific claim or voucher. The submitter sends applications through the Office of General Counsel (OGC) of the DoW Component or the DFAS to the DoW Deputy General Counsel (Fiscal) (DoW DGC(F)) for determination. The affected Component or DFAS OGC must attach a legal memorandum discussing the legality of the proposed payment under the circumstances. The responsible activity, DFAS site, or appropriate OGC may return cases involving entitlement questions already clearly decided authoritatively, with a determination that no advance decision is necessary. A submitter may resubmit such a determination through the responsible activity for reconsideration.

13.2.2. An advance decision is conclusive for the specific payment involved on the question presented. Although an advance decision is conclusive only for the specific payment reviewed, COs must use the principles cited in the decision when making future entitlement decisions.

13.3    FALSE, FICTITIOUS, OR FRAUDULENT CLAIMS

13.3.1. If there is reason to suspect that a claim presented for certification or payment contains fraudulent information, the CO must request that their commander or comparable authorized civilian initiate an investigation into the suspected fraud. A DO who suspects that a certified voucher is fraudulent must return it to the CO. The requirement to request an investigation applies regardless of the dollar value. Once the investigation and legal review by the supporting SJA or other legal counsel are complete, the investigating officer (IO) gives the CO and DO a copy of the completed report of investigation (ROI). See Section 7.0 for ROI guidance.

13.3.1.1. If the ROI does not support a finding of fraud, the CO may certify the voucher for payment of all amounts to which the claimant is entitled. The CO must document the reasons for the determination and maintain the documentation in the CO's records.

13.3.1.2. If the ROI confirms that some items of the claim are fraudulent, the claimant may submit to the CO a new claim for the items the ROI identified as not fraudulent. A claimant who protests the determination of fraud and insists on payment of the entire claim may submit a new claim for the items denied because of fraud. The CO processes the reclamation for the disallowed items as prescribed in subparagraph 13.3.3.

13.3.2. A CO or DO who suspects that a claim was paid based on fraudulent information or documents must review the retained copy of the claim to determine whether it contains false information.

13.3.2.1. A CO or DO who suspects that a paid claim is fraudulent must inform his or her commander or comparable authorized civilian, who then initiates an investigation of the suspected fraud regardless of the dollar value involved. See Section 7.0 for ROI guidance. After the investigation, the supporting SJA or OGC reviews it for legal sufficiency. The IO then gives the CO and DO each a copy of the final ROI.

13.3.2.2. On learning of an improper payment based on suspected fraud, the CO or DO sends an ROI to the supporting DFAS site through their commander or comparable authorized civilian equivalent. The ROI must include a basic statement of the irregularity, the date, amount, and identification of the individuals involved. On completion of the final recovery, investigative, or other negative action, the CO or DO advises the supporting DFAS site.

13.3.2.3. If the CO determines that some or all items of a paid claim are fraudulent, the CO may not certify any of the items for repayment.

13.3.2.4. Losses resulting from fraudulent acts are improper payments, except losses within the disbursing office. The DO leaves them charged to the appropriations cited on the payment vouchers (see Section 7.0). Any losses, regardless of the dollar amount, where there is evidence of fraud within the disbursing office (for example, embezzlement or fraudulent acts by disbursing personnel) are physical losses (see Section 7.0).

13.3.3. Reclamation of Items Disallowed or Recovered Due to Fraud

13.3.3.1. The CO sends reclamations for items disallowed or recouped due to fraud through the appropriate office in his or her chain of command to the DoW DGC(F). For a claim denied in its entirety, submit the original claim. Send the completed claim with a cover letter or memorandum from the CO stating why the claim is fraudulent, with the statement: "I have not certified and will not certify this claim for payment unless authorized by competent authority." Include the original and two copies of all supporting documents and the orders with all endorsements for a travel claim, and a copy of the paid voucher for the items free of fraud.

13.3.3.2. A CO may not certify a reclamation claim for any or all of an amount recovered by the government due to an illegal or improper payment of any voucher item obtained by fraud or misrepresentation processed under subparagraph 13.3.3.

13.3.3.2.1. The CO or DO must send paid fraudulent claims to the appropriate pay office and local OGC or SJA for referral to the Defense Criminal Investigative Service or military criminal investigative organization. Recover payments based on substantiated claims of fraud by direct repayment from the employee through salary offset or by other procedures in Volume 16. The CO or DO may take no further action on the paid fraudulent claim until OGC or SJA gives the CO or DO specific processing and disposition instructions.

13.3.3.2.2. Under 37 U.S.C. § 1007(c) and the guidance in this chapter, the CO or DO collects debts owed by military members. When a debtor requests reconsideration of a fraud determination, the creditor organization submits the debtor's evidence or statements to the local SJA for review.

title: Section 14.0: Foreign Disbursing Operations
content:
14.0    FOREIGN DISBURSING OPERATIONS

14.1    GENERAL

14.1.1. Overview

14.1.1.1. Where U.S. currency use is prohibited or diplomatic or financial considerations make it inadvisable, the senior commander must consult other U.S. military commanders and U.S. Department of State (DoS) representatives in the area to determine the local government's foreign currency control regulations, and must issue instructions that conform to DoS procedures and those local regulations. Disbursing Officers (DOs) must follow the disbursing guidance in Section 10.0 on voucher certification and substantiation before executing payment transactions, including advances, equitable claims, and payments to third parties.

14.1.1.2. The same policies governing domestic disbursements apply to foreign currency disbursements. Except where U.S. diplomatic or financial relations make use of the U.S. dollar (USD) inadvisable, U.S. currency or Treasury checks are the only media of exchange for:

14.1.1.2.1. Basic salaries, special and incentive pay, and allowances (e.g., subsistence and housing) in USDs for U.S. military personnel stationed overseas;

14.1.1.2.2. Salaries and differentials to similarly situated U.S. citizen civilian personnel in fulfillment of U.S. contractual or statutory obligations in USDs;

14.1.1.2.3. Per diem;

14.1.1.2.4. Travel expenses; and

14.1.1.2.5. Purchases from appropriated and nonappropriated fund activities located in the foreign currency area.

14.1.1.3. A disbursement voucher may serve as both a payment voucher and a collection voucher for transactions involving setoff or deduction to recover an amount owed by the payee, with the net amount due disbursed to the payee. All disbursements must be supported by formal disbursement vouchers (see Section 10.0, paragraph 4.0). The Volume 1 financial records retention requirements apply to contingency operations.

14.1.1.4. International Treasury Services (ITS.gov), the U.S. Department of Treasury's comprehensive international payment and collection system, is the preferred method to issue foreign currency payments electronically and to issue international USD wire transfer payments.

14.2    EXCHANGE OF U.S. DOLLARS FOR FOREIGN CURRENCY

14.2.1. When it is not practical to use ITS.gov, or the DO does not have a limited depositary account (LDA) in the currency to be paid, the DO may acquire foreign currency. An appointed DO may obtain foreign currency only for official purposes, such as paying U.S. Government creditors and exchanging foreign currency or other negotiable instruments for which the DO is accountable. Foreign currency obtained may be held as currency or in an LDA (see Section 15.0). DOs may obtain foreign currency from the sources in subparagraph 14.2.2 and from sources authorized by the government of the country concerned. When DOs exchange USDs for foreign currency, the following guidelines apply:

14.2.1.1. Exchange foreign currency only when it is needed for immediate funding requirements. DOs must ensure that payment for foreign currency purchases is made on the value date.

14.2.1.2. Speculation in foreign currency is prohibited.

14.2.1.3. Any change in program costs resulting from foreign currency use in international financial arrangements is the responsibility of the involved U.S. or foreign program agencies.

14.2.1.4. Foreign currency must not be purchased by forward contracts directly from foreign governments, private firms, or individuals at a negotiated rate without prior Treasury authorization. Submit such requests through DFAS, Disbursing Policy (DFAS-ZPTA), 8899 East 56th Street, Indianapolis, IN 46249-0500 (dfas.indianapolis-in.zpf.mbx.disbursingdebtmanagementpolicy@mail.mil).

14.2.1.5. Limit DO foreign currency holdings in a safe, vault, or LDA to no more than a seven-business-day requirement, unless the Treasury authorizes an increase (see
Section 15.0, subparagraph 15.3.10.2.1). This limit includes foreign currency held by all authorized deputies, agents, and cashiers within the disbursing office and at remote locations.

14.2.1.6. Acquire foreign coins only to fill specific needs or when received as change incident to an official cash payment in foreign funds.

14.2.1.7. Prepare foreign currency reports per paragraph 7.0.

14.2.2. Procurement of foreign currency from U.S. Government or commercial sources requires a certificate or statement showing the amount purchased, the rate of exchange, the amount of USDs paid, the date, and the source or seller. Include the certificate or statement with the monthly financial reports. DOs may use ITS.gov to acquire foreign currency via electronic funds transfer. Each exchange voucher must be submitted in support of the disbursing office accounts and attached to the monthly Standard Form (SF) 1219, Statement of Accountability. A DO may also obtain foreign currency from the following sources:

14.2.2.1. Other U.S. Government sources include DoW DOs, U.S. DOs (USDOs), cashiers at American Embassies, or the Federal Reserve Bank of New York (FRBNY). Normally, the DO draws a U.S. Treasury exchange-for-cash check and endorses it to the order of the officer furnishing the foreign exchange. When foreign currency is purchased from a USDO or an American Embassy cashier, the check may be issued to the American Embassy. When foreign currency is purchased from the FRBNY, the DO makes appropriate shipping arrangements; and

14.2.2.2. DoW Military Banking Facility (MBF). When possible, DOs can purchase foreign currency from a MBF (includes funds for LDAs) using a U.S. Treasury exchange- for-cash check.

14.2.3. Absent ready access to the Federal Reserve System, the DO may request Treasury approval to establish currency custody LDAs with the government's contractor-operated MBF. The DO must settle daily with the MBF. Report the balance held in custody accounts on the Custody or Contingency Cash line of the DoW DD Form 2657, Daily Statement of Accountability, reflected in the DO Cash Treasury Account Symbol (TAS), and on the SF 1219.

14.2.4. Subject to subparagraph 3.3.4, DOs may purchase foreign currency from individuals. DOs may also receive foreign currency as refunds from foreign vendors or in payment for sale of excess foreign property per DoD Manual (DoDM) 4160.21-V1. Foreign currency sales receipts from post offices, exchanges, commissaries, and other nonappropriated fund activities are not collections by the disbursing office, but may be acquired by purchase only to the extent necessary to acquire foreign exchange for the LDA.

14.3    FOREIGN EXCHANGE TRANSACTIONS

14.3.1. Policies for Financial Transactions

14.3.1.1. Withdraw dollars from the Treasury on behalf of any program management organization only as needed, based on the recipient organization's funding requirements to carry out the project.

14.3.1.2. Negotiate dollar outlays as close as possible to the need for current program expenditure to support international programs requiring U.S. funding.

14.3.1.3. Obtain the U.S. Government share of funding required to support a program by appropriation, with no part derived from interest earned on U.S. contributions. DoW Components must ensure that any interest earned is deposited promptly to the Treasury General Fund Receipt Account 3220 (General Fund Proprietary Receipts, Not Otherwise Classified, All Other).

14.3.1.4. Consider the fiscal needs and funding policy concerns of each participating country or international organization, provided that U.S. Government cash management policies are not compromised.

14.3.1.5. Accommodate the financial policies of each participating country or organization to the maximum extent feasible. Except for arrangements entered into solely to implement U.S. international monetary policy, retain USDs in the Treasury until actually required for immediate disbursement, to minimize interest cost on the public debt.

14.3.1.6. Act on requests from a foreign country or international organization for the temporary deposit and safekeeping of USDs in trust in a Treasury account on their own merit. Base the decision on the reason for the request, the specific financial arrangements proposed, and the relevant U.S. Government political and general financial considerations. All requests must include a recommendation from the local commander and be submitted to DFAS-ZPTA/IN (dfas.indianapolis-in.zpf.mbx.disbursingdebtmanagementpolicy@mail.mil).

14.3.1.7. DoW Components must not invest funds on behalf of a foreign country or international organization when receipt of such funds serves as a basis for creating contract obligation authority for the DoW Component or other U.S. Government department or agency.

14.3.1.8. DoW Components must ensure that their administrative practices do not compromise application of these general policies in negotiations with foreign countries and international organizations.

14.3.2. Accommodation Exchange Services

14.3.2.1. Commanders may approve and implement accommodation exchange services only after determining that:

14.3.2.1.1. Contract MBFs, other on-base financial institutions, exchanges, commissaries, or U.S. Postal facilities cannot fulfill the needs of DoW personnel;

14.3.2.1.2. The DO or agent has an immediate need for the foreign currency repurchased; or

14.3.2.1.3. Resources are available to provide these services without impacting levels of other financial services (e.g., primary disbursing and related functions).

14.3.2.2. When satisfactory local banking facilities are not available to conduct accommodation transactions, and after the commander approves a written check cashing policy, DOs may use official funds to:

14.3.2.2.1. Disburse foreign currency for checks, drafts, bills of exchange, and other instruments payable in USDs; and

14.3.2.2.2. Cash foreign currency checks drawn by accountable officers of the U.S. on non-symbol checking accounts for the same currency in which drawn, when the currency is needed by the officer for official purposes.

14.3.2.3. MBFs normally make accommodation exchanges of foreign currency at installations served under the DoW MBF contract, and DOs providing accommodation exchange services in those countries obtain needed foreign currency from the MBF at the accommodation rate. DoW personnel must not receive accommodation exchange service from USDOs or Treasury DOs in areas where DoW DOs provide those services; DoW personnel assigned or attached to U.S. embassy duty may use available embassy cashier services. DOs, agents, and cashiers making these accommodation exchanges must maintain the DD Form 2664, Currency Exchange Record, Record of Individual Exchange Transactions, daily to ensure implementation of the requirements in paragraph 7.0.

14.3.2.4. DOs are prohibited from purchasing foreign currency from individuals in areas served by MBFs under DoW contract. In areas not served by contract MBFs, DOs may purchase foreign currency or instruments payable in foreign currency in exchange for USDs or dollar instruments before an individual's departure on home leave or completion of a foreign assignment. When making such purchases, DOs must comply with the following:

14.3.2.4.1. If the foreign currency presented does not exceed the sum of the individual's salary and allowances for two biweekly pay periods, it may be purchased without requiring any documentation from the departing individual.

14.3.2.4.2. If the foreign currency presented exceeds the amount authorized in subparagraph 3.3.4.1, the requestor must submit a written application to the commander for approval of the purchase. The application must include a statement describing the source of the currency and a statement affirming that none of it was acquired in violation of the local regulations or exchange control laws of the country concerned.

14.3.2.4.3. The purchase of foreign currency with USDs must consider the DO's immediate foreign currency disbursing requirements. A DO may suspend making accommodation exchanges for such time and to the extent necessary to carry out other responsibilities.

14.3.2.4.4. Purchase the foreign currency at the prevailing market rate.

14.3.2.4.5. Keep a DD 2664 daily to reflect the amount and source of purchased funds.

14.3.2.5. The appropriate commander establishes foreign currency accommodation exchange services for dependents of DoW personnel at safe haven areas to which they were ordered by competent authority in an emergency evacuation. These services must be consistent with the amount of exchanges authorized for dependents of U.S. personnel employed by other U.S. Government agencies.

14.4    CURRENCY RATE OF EXCHANGE

14.4.1. Prevailing Rate of Exchange

14.4.1.1. Unless otherwise authorized by the Treasury, carry all foreign currency, including amounts held in LDAs, at the prevailing rate of exchange. Foreign currency acquired without purchase includes burdensharing contributions made in host nation currency and held in accounts authorized by 10 U.S.C. § 2350j. Compute disbursements for official expenditures or accommodation exchange transactions to avoid gains or deficiencies due to exchange rate fluctuations to the extent possible. If no rate of exchange is established by agreement between the U.S. Government and the foreign country, or where no MBF is available, conduct foreign currency transactions at the prevailing rate using the recomputed rate of exchange per subparagraph 14.4.2.

14.4.1.2. When purchasing from sources other than the U.S. Government, DOs must acquire foreign exchange at the best rate available (e.g., fixed or non-fixed legal rate) in the currency in which the exchange will be expended. Follow DoS regulations or the currency-control laws of the country where the currency will be used. Draw Treasury checks to obtain foreign exchange from commercial sources in favor of the DO and endorse them to the order of the banking institution or commercial enterprise providing the funds.

14.4.1.2.1. The best fixed legal rate to the U.S. Government, depending on the circumstances in each country, may be any officially established buying rate for dollars, including diplomatic rates or special rates established by agreement with the country's authorities. When a fixed legal rate prevails, purchase foreign exchange at the best applicable rate for the particular transaction. Purchases at fixed legal rates may be made without obtaining bids, but a statement signed by the seller must evidence each purchase and set forth the pertinent data: the date, amount of purchase, and exchange rate. The DO must retain the statement as a supporting document with the SF 1219 (see Section 16.0, paragraph 16.8).

14.4.1.2.2. When rates legally applicable to the particular transaction are not fixed, or when such rates are fixed but the use of other rates is also legal for the transaction, DOs must purchase foreign exchange at the best obtainable rate. When foreign exchange can be purchased at a non-fixed legal rate, DOs must solicit bids from at least three sources if available.

14.4.1.2.2.1. When practical, solicit bids from sources outside the country of the currency involved. Accept the bid providing the most beneficial exchange rate to the U.S. Government. The DO must include a copy of the certified and accepted bid as a supporting document with the financial reports and keep a copy to substantiate the place of purchase if some of the currency is eventually sold through commercial channels. The DO must retain documentation of the most beneficial bid, accepted and certified, with the SF 1219.

14.4.2. The DO must recompute the operating rate of exchange when the rate of exchange of newly acquired foreign currency differs from that of the DO's current balance. The DO then disburses from the account using the recomputed rate of exchange.

14.4.2.1. Credit gains or charge deficiencies due to rounding to account 6763 (Gains and Deficiencies on Exchange Transactions) using DD Form 1131, Cash Collection Voucher, or SF 1034, Public Voucher for Purchases and Services Other Than Personal, as appropriate. Attach a Certificate of Adjustment, as prescribed in subparagraph 14.4.2.1, to the voucher to support the transaction.

14.4.2.2. The DO or DDO must prepare and sign a Certificate of Adjustment Due to Rounding when a minor gain or deficiency results.

14.4.2.3. Any change in the prevailing rate of exchange causes a gain or deficiency by revaluation because the USD value of the foreign currency changes, except when using the method in subparagraph 14.4.2.1. Whenever possible, revalue the foreign currency on hand (including LDAs) at the beginning of the business day on which a rate change occurs. Determine the new USD value by dividing the total foreign currency on hand (including LDAs) by the new exchange rate, and determine whether a gain or deficiency by revaluation occurred by comparing the USD value at the old rate to the USD value at the new rate. Because DOs carry foreign currency held in the disbursing account at the USD value, adjust that value by the gain or deficiency (loss), recording the revaluation as a collection or disbursement transaction in the DO's account.

14.4.2.4. Gains and deficiencies may occur due to rounding or revaluation. Except when using the method in subparagraph 14.4.2.1, credit foreign currency gains using a DD 1131 and charge foreign currency deficiencies using an SF 1034. Report gains and deficiencies through Classification Transactions and Accountability, citing an increase or decrease to account 6763, the DO Cash TAS, and the proper Business Event Type Codes. Calculate gain/deficiency values for each currency individually by DO/DDO/agent/cashier to keep personal accountability accurate.

DOs may consolidate the net change for all currencies on a single DD 1131 or SF 1034, as appropriate.

14.4.2.5. Code all credits and charges to account 6763 as USD transactions. Use account 6763 only for gains and deficiencies due to foreign currency revaluations. Account 6763 has no relationship with the Foreign Currency Fluctuations, Defense (FCFD) or the Foreign Currency Fluctuations, Construction, Defense (FCFCD) accounts, which are used for differences between the budgeted foreign currency rates at which obligations are recorded and the rates at which they are liquidated. Reflect the FCFD and FCFCD portions of foreign currency disbursements separately on disbursement vouchers as charges to the appropriate foreign currency centrally-managed allotment account established for that purpose.

14.4.2.6. Service members stationed overseas are authorized an advanced overseas housing allowance for security deposits to obtain leased housing. As authorized by the Defense Travel Management Office, the supporting DO pays the necessary amount in the appropriate local currency and charges the appropriate military pay appropriation for the USDE. The preferred method for paying the advanced housing allowance is an LDA check in the local currency of the area involved.

14.4.2.7. The supporting finance office must maintain a tracking system, either by input into the master military pay account (MMPA) or by manual methods, showing the amount of the advance paid in local currency, the USDE, and the exchange rate on the date of payment.

14.4.2.8. At lease termination, service members return the total deposit in local currency to the supporting disbursing office in exchange for a receipt. The supporting disbursing office credits the USDE, based on the rate of exchange in effect on the date of return, to the appropriation charged when the deposit was advanced; compares that rate with the rate in effect on the date of the advance; and posts any gain or deficiency (loss) due to currency fluctuation as a charge or credit, as appropriate, to the current military pay appropriation.

14.4.2.9. If the security deposit was paid in USD, the service member takes the full value of the security deposit in foreign currency to the MBF, converts it to U.S. currency, obtains a receipt indicating the exchange rate, and turns in the U.S. currency and receipt to the disbursing office. The disbursing office prepares a collection voucher for credit to the appropriate military pay appropriation, indicates return of the security deposit, verifies with the MMPA or local record whether a gain or deficiency occurred at the current exchange rate, and prepares the appropriate voucher to credit or debit the gain or deficiency to the appropriate military pay appropriation. The office must ensure the member does not experience any gain or deficiency due to foreign currency fluctuations.

14.5    USE OF FOREIGN CURRENCIES FOR TRANSPORTATION

14.5.1. To the maximum extent possible, use U.S.-owned foreign currencies for transportation when certified air carriers are available and will accept such currencies in payment for U.S. Government-financed, commercial, foreign air transportation of persons or property. Review DoD Directive 4500.09E, Transportation and Traffic Management, for guidance on using these air carriers and determining their availability. When issuing and exchanging Government Transportation Requests (GTRs), Government Bills of Lading (GBLs), transportation warrants, or other procurement documents, state clearly 'PAYMENT IN (foreign currency)' on the form; otherwise, the carrier may demand payment in USD.

14.5.2. In the 'BILL TO' portion of the GTR, GBL, transportation warrant, or other procurement document, DOs must include the name of the requesting agency, address to be billed, and instruction on payment in foreign currency.

14.6    DISPOSITION OF FOREIGN CURRENCY AND NEGOTIABLE INSTRUMENTS

14.6.1. DOs may use foreign currency for payments to foreign personnel and vendors. For miscellaneous advance payments, see Volume 10.

14.6.2. When possible, transfer excess foreign currency to other DoW DOs, USDOs, U.S. Embassies, or accountable officers in a locality with immediate disbursing needs. When the collection of foreign currency causes a noninterest-bearing LDA to exceed immediate disbursing requirements, see Section 15.0, subparagraph 15.3.10.2.1.

14.6.2.1. A DO may sell excess foreign currency to an MBF whenever the currency cannot be sold to another DoW DO. The selling DO uses the MBF buy rate as the rate of exchange on the date it sends the currency to the MBF and accounts for any gain or deficiency due to exchange rate fluctuations when it receives the USD from the MBF.

14.6.2.2. If foreign currency cannot be sold to a DoW DO or MBF, a DO may sell it through commercial channels. If the rate of exchange has been established by agreement between the U.S. and the foreign country, sell or otherwise dispose of the foreign currency for U.S. currency or USD checks at the established rate of exchange.

14.6.2.2.1. For this type of sale, the bank or other entity buying the foreign currency must provide a statement showing the amount of USD supplied, the rate of exchange, the amount of foreign currency received, the date, and the name and address of the bank or entity. The recipient's representative signs the statement, and the DO includes it with the financial reports. A DO may also conduct foreign currency sale transactions with a bank or entity approved by the Treasury (e.g., an MBF) to establish LDAs in the currency purchased (see Section 15.0, paragraph 15.3).

14.6.2.2.2. When the rate of exchange is not established by agreement between the U.S. and the foreign country, or when no bank or entity is approved by the Treasury to establish LDAs, use a DD 2668 to request at least three bids from reputable banking institutions or dealers in foreign exchange, if available. Sell the foreign currency to the bidder submitting the most beneficial bid, as certified by a commissioned officer other than the DO; the DO accepts the bid and includes it with the financial reports to support gains or deficiencies in foreign currency transactions.

14.6.2.3. If disposition is not possible through a DoW DO or an MBF, follow guidance in I TFM-5-6000 for depositing foreign currency and checks drawn on foreign banks.

14.6.3. Dishonored foreign instruments received by DoW DOs are subject to the regular debt collection procedures. DOs must request removal of dishonored-item deficiencies for instruments received that become uncollectible (see Section 5.0, subparagraph 5.5.1).

14.6.4. DOs must take every possible precaution to prevent acceptance of mutilated foreign currency as a collection, payment, or exchange transaction. A DO holding mutilated foreign currency must contact local banks or fiscal authorities to arrange the exchange of mutilated or unfit currency for fit currency.

14.6.5. DOs must take every possible precaution to prevent acceptance of counterfeit currency as a collection. If the collection is counterfeit, see section 2030.50 in I TFM 5-2000. If no agreement exists with the foreign government, ship the currency to the appropriate investigative agency or nearest military security agency. Obtain a receipt for the currency and account for it in the DO's records in the same manner prescribed in Section 4.0, paragraph 4.6 for counterfeit U.S. currency. A DO at fault in acquiring counterfeit foreign currency is accountable for the value of the currency and must submit a request for relief of liability per the process in Section 7.0, paragraph 7.6. This is the same process used for accountability for receipt of counterfeit U.S. currency.

14.7    RECORDS AND REPORTS

14.7.1. Treat transactions involving foreign currency as cash transactions and follow the same principles and guidelines established for controlling U.S. currency. DOs, DDOs, agents, and cashiers who engage in foreign currency transactions (e.g., collections, disbursements, and accommodation exchanges) must document them on the DD Form 2663, Foreign Currency Control Record. This form shows current balances of foreign currency on hand (all foreign currency held by cashiers, in the vault, or by other agents of the DO) and in LDAs, as well as the detailed transactions that increase or decrease these balances.

14.7.2. Maintain separate DD 2663s for each type of foreign currency used (e.g., Kuwaiti Dinar, Euro, and Japanese Yen). Also maintain a separate DD 2663 for accommodation exchange foreign currency carried at an exchange rate different from that used for disbursements. DOs may maintain separate DD 2663s for foreign currency on hand and in LDAs.

14.7.3. Foreign Currency Reports

14.7.3.1. Include with the foreign currency reports a cover sheet with the following headings: Country of Currency; Monetary Unit; Number of Units Purchased; Total Dollar Outlay; and Memorandum-Dollar Outlay for Accommodation Exchanges. Reports are due within 15 calendar days after the close of each quarter to the supporting DFAS site. Reports may be combined and submitted as one report.

14.7.3.1.1. The Cumulative Report of Foreign Currency Purchased With USD From Sources Outside the U.S. Government is cumulative for the fiscal year. Include the amounts acquired through accommodation exchange transactions as well as purchases from banks and other dealers in currency exchange.

14.7.3.1.2. The Report of the Balance of Foreign Currency Held Under Dollar Accountability is due by the end of each quarter to the same DFAS site as the cumulative report. It may be combined with the cumulative report.

14.7.3.1.3. The Report of Foreign Exchange Received by DOs and Credited Immediately to Miscellaneous Receipt Accounts of the Treasury is a cumulative report of outside purchases and a quarterly report of balances of foreign currency on hand. These funds are received for items such as fees and services and are immediately purchased by DOs with appropriated funds for their operating needs. Exclude repayments to appropriations.

14.7.3.2. DFAS sites must consolidate the DOs' quarterly reports and forward them to DFAS, Departmental Reporting Directorate, Treasury Division, Reporting Operations Branch, Column 334Z-1, 8899 E. 56th Street, Indianapolis, IN 46249, in time for delivery to the Treasury 45 calendar days after the close of each quarter.

14.7.3.3. Report foreign currency balances held in USDE on the SF 1219, including those in LDAs.

title: Section 15.0: Limited Depositary Checking Accounts
content:
15.0    LIMITED DEPOSITARY CHECKING ACCOUNTS

15.1    GENERAL

15.1.1. If Treasury’s International Treasury Services (ITS.gov) will not support mission requirements, DoW disbursing officers (DOs) may maintain official limited depositary accounts (LDAs) for check or electronic funds transfer (EFT) payments in foreign currencies with banks Treasury designates as "Depositaries of Public Moneys of the United States." LDAs are cash and investments held outside Treasury funds and must be reflected in the DO Cash Treasury Account Symbol. LDA transactions follow the same reporting process to the Payment Information Repository (obtaining funds) and to Classification Transactions and Accountability (cash disbursement and collections) as U.S. dollar transactions, and must be recorded on the DD 2657, Daily Statement of Accountability, and the SF 1219, Statement of Accountability.

15.2    SOLICITATION

15.2.1. Overview

15.2.1.1. When anticipating a new LDA, a DO (or designated deputy DO (DDO)) confers with the local U.S. Embassy or Consulate to determine which banks meet the criteria, then solicits all American-owned and leading local financial institutions in the area to find the most beneficial arrangement. The solicitation must be competitive, letting all banks submit written information on identical questionnaires or requests for banking proposals. To determine the most beneficial arrangement, a DO weighs, in descending order of importance: (1) standard operating services minimally required; (2) customary local banking practices (for example, telex cost or armored car service); and (3) other special services a particular country or circumstance may require (for example, payment of interest on the account or waiver of miscellaneous charges). The required services must include capability to honor payments to payees in outlying areas, processing of checks and, if possible, EFTs and deposits, provision of a daily or a monthly bank statement as needed, and acceptance of the DO’s funding procedures.

15.2.1.2. DOs must ensure LDA banks are valid, reflect a high level of American ownership, and are financially secure, dependable, and reliable, to avoid losses and protect U.S. Government funds. Unsolicited proposals to operate an existing LDA may be received at any time, and the LDA is open to all interested financial institutions.

15.2.2. After selecting a reliable financial institution with beneficial banking arrangements, a DO must send a request for approval and designation of an LDA to DFAS Enterprise Solutions and Standards (ESS) Disbursing, Indianapolis (DFAS-JJFKCD/IN), 8899 E. 56th Street, Column 301S, Indianapolis, IN 46249 (dfas.indianapolis-in.jjf.mbx.ess-disbursing@mail.mil). ESS Disbursing reviews the request and sends it to Treasury’s Bureau of the Fiscal Service before the account is established.

15.2.2.1. Requests for U.S. dollar (USD) accounts must include documentation showing the DO requested and received a commitment from the proposed bank to pledge collateral. If the bank agrees to pledge collateral, the DO may request a USD operating account; otherwise, the DO may request only a USD zero-balance account.

15.3    ESTABLISHING AND MAINTAINING AN LDA

15.3.1. Once Treasury approves a request, establish the LDA in the name of the assigned DO, DDO, or another agent the DO designates. Limit authority to sign checks drawn on the LDA to the DO and other appointed DDOs or agents. A DO who transacts business in multiple foreign currencies must establish and maintain a separate LDA for each currency.

15.3.2. The commander must certify by letter the name and rank of the DO assigned to the activity, stating that the DO is authorized to maintain an LDA with official U.S. funds in the name of the activity. If the LDA custodian is a DDO or another agent of the DO, the commander’s letter must identify that DDO or agent and:

15.3.2.1. Certifies that the account is subject to checks issued by the DO, other appointed DDOs or agents, and their successors in the office;

15.3.2.2. Includes signature specimens of the DOs and authorized DDOs and agents, and a certification that the signatures are those of the personnel authorized to transact business with the limited depositary (LD); and

15.3.2.3. Requests the bank acknowledge acceptance by endorsement of the letter, in triplicate. The bank should retain the original letter and return two copies to the activity.

15.3.3. Blank LD Checks

15.3.3.1. Control and safeguard blank LD checks the same way as Treasury checks under Section 8.0, subparagraph 8.2.4. If LD checks are lost or stolen, the DO must immediately notify the LD of the serial numbers, place stop-payments against them, and submit copies of the stop-payment requests with the next original LD reports.

15.3.4. Preparation of LD Checks

15.3.4.1. DOs must maintain a record of all LD checks issued, including payee names, voucher numbers, amounts (in the check’s currency), check serial numbers, check dates, and the activity name under which the account is established. Other information about the purpose of the checks and local identification codes is optional at the issuing DO’s discretion. The record may be on paper, electronic, or data-processing media. Keep a separate record for each LDA, and include records of check issues with the retained disbursing records.

15.3.5. When a payment is made with an LD check, enter the notation "LD Check No. X" on the disbursement voucher. A receipt is not generally required for a check payment, but local laws may bar LD checks drawn outside the United States from being returned to the drawer. In those cases, show evidence of receipt of the payment on the voucher on which the LD check payment appears.

15.3.6. Before mailing any LD checks outside the country in which the LD is located, the DO must verify that doing so is not prohibited by the Status of Forces Agreements or the banking laws of the countries involved (see Section 8.0, subparagraph 8.5.4).

15.3.7. When an irregularity occurs after check delivery and the check is still outstanding, the DO must stop payment on the check and provide a complete report of the facts with the stoppage request. If the irregularity is discovered after the check is paid, the DO must notify the depositary of the irregularity.

15.3.8. Some LDs pay interest on LDAs. When possible, the DO must obtain interest on the LDA, canvassing the market for the highest interest rate legally available consistent with disbursing requirements, and must monitor interest-bearing accounts to ensure interest is paid timely under the agreements between the DO and the banks. When notified that interest has been credited, the DO prepares a DD Form 1131, Cash Collection Voucher, crediting receipt account 3220 (General Fund Proprietary Receipts, Not Otherwise Classified, All Other) for the U.S. dollar equivalent (USDE) of the interest, and records the transaction as both a collection and an increase.

15.3.9. Keep daily LDA balances as near zero as possible and maintain them solely to support disbursing requirements. Draw LDA checks against new deposits only after the LD confirms the deposits. If foreign currency collections cause a non-interest-bearing LDA to exceed a 5-to-7 business day supply and all attempts to sell the currencies to other DOs are exhausted, the DO must sell the foreign currency for USDs for deposit to a bank designated as a Treasury General Depositary, or request a waiver per subparagraph 3.10.2.2. LDAs approved to hold funds beyond the 5-to-7 business day supply do not require a balance reduction but must comply with any stipulations in the LDA request approval (see paragraph 2.2.1). Do not use LDA balances, or the forfeiture of potential interest earnings, to subsidize banking services otherwise funded through the appropriation process.

15.3.10. Review of LDA

15.3.10.1. Commanders must require review of the LDAs a DO maintains to ensure compliance with this chapter. The cash verification team (see Appendix A) performs this unannounced review quarterly, upon transfer of accountability to a successor DO, before the outgoing DO departs the command, upon deactivation of the LDA, or upon a change in the designated settlement office.

15.3.10.2. DOs must review LDAs on a continuing basis to ensure:

15.3.10.2.1. Balances must not exceed immediate needs (typically a 5-to-7 business day supply). Transfer excess funds beyond the immediate need to other DoW DOs, State Department U.S. DOs, or a U.S. Embassy; withdraw and deposit the funds with Treasury; or obtain Treasury approval to exceed the 5-to-7 business day supply. Waivers to exceed the 5-to-7 business day supply must be requested from Treasury (see I TFM 4A-30140.20). Contact DFAS- JJFKCD/IN at the email address in subparagraph 15.2.2 for procedural guidance on waiver requests.

15.3.10.2.2. At least every three years, for each account, the DO must determine whether it would be cost effective to solicit competitive proposals from all American- owned and leading local financial institutions in the area to secure the most beneficial banking agreement.

15.3.10.2.3. Watch for significant events that affect the designated bank (for example, bank closure). Upon learning of such an event, the DO must immediately notify Treasury’s Over-the-Counter Revenue Collection Division through DFAS-JJFKCD/IN at the email address in subparagraph 15.2.2.

15.3.11. See Volume 12 for the overall policy and responsibilities for accepting, receiving, using, and reporting burdensharing and relocation monetary contributions to the DoW. DOs must include any burdensharing and relocation monetary contributions held in an LDA in the semiannual cash holding authority requests (see Section 4.0, subparagraph 4.1.3) and in their ending accountability on the DD 2657 and the DO Cash Treasury Account Symbol. Burdensharing and monetary contributions held in an LDA in excess of the 5-to-7 business day supply must be approved with the original LDA request or require an approved waiver from Treasury.

15.4    VOIDED AND SPOILED LD CHECKS

15.4.1. Treat original LD checks that are not to be issued as voided or spoiled. Void LD checks with writing errors (for example, a wrong name or amount), checks physically damaged during preparation, and checks for which the entitlement area has withdrawn the voucher. Mark these checks conspicuously to prevent their negotiation, whether in error or through fraud. Prepare separate listings of voided and spoiled checks monthly and attach them to the SF 1149, Statement of Designated Depositary Account.

15.4.2. The functional area authorizing payment of a voucher may request that a check be voided. The DO bases that decision on the payee’s non-entitlement to payment or an error in the way the check was drawn. Do not report voided checks as issued in the DO’s check report. Upon deciding to void a check, render it non-negotiable. Do not store voided checks in the safe or vault of the DO or any deputy or agent. At the end of each month, prepare a listing entitled "Voided Checks" showing the accounting month, the LD name, and the LDA number, and send the listing with the originals of all voided checks with the monthly SF 1149.

15.4.3. Spoiled Checks

15.4.3.1. Replace a spoiled check with the next available serially numbered check, entering the same information that appeared on the original check except for the check serial number and the issue date. Render the original check non-negotiable.

15.5    TRANSFERRING PROCEEDS OF LD CHECKS

15.5.1. An uncurrent LD check is one that has not been negotiated through the LD one fiscal year after the fiscal year in which it was issued, except where local laws require a shorter negotiable period. The amount of these checks must be transferred to Treasury or credited to the original appropriation. A transfer of LDA check proceeds may arise from undeliverable checks or checks due to deceased or incapacitated payees.

15.5.2. The DO who issued the original check, a successor DO, or a settlement officer designated by the supporting DFAS site must transfer proceeds of uncurrent checks to Treasury each October.

15.5.2.1. The DO must immediately give a copy of the uncurrent check listing to the LD, request that it place stop-payments on all listed checks, and instruct the LD to advise any payee presenting a listed check to submit it to the disbursing office for transmittal to and settlement by the Department of the Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service, Attn: Fiscal Accounting, Budget Reporting Branch, 3201 Pennsy Drive, Building E, Landover, MD 20785.

15.5.3. Transferring Proceeds

15.5.3.1. Hold undeliverable LD checks only until the DO determines they cannot be delivered with the information available, but no longer than 60 days from the date of issue.

15.5.3.2. Record undeliverable LD checks on a DD 2658, Returned and Undeliverable Check/Bond Record, including a complete description of the checks, the disbursing voucher numbers, the dates the checks were returned, the disposition of the checks, the disbursing official authorizing the disposition, and the disposition dates. The DO, DDO, or a third person with the DO’s written authorization must approve disposition of undelivered checks.

15.5.3.3. Protect undeliverable LDA checks held in the disbursing office the same as cash, and file them in the order best suited for easy retrieval and identification.

15.5.4. Claims for the Proceeds of Undeliverable Checks

15.5.4.1. When there is any question of law or fact, send claims for the proceeds of undeliverable checks to DoW, Office of the General Counsel (OGC), 1600 Defense Pentagon, Washington, DC 20301-1600.

15.6    CANCELING LD CHECKS

15.6.1. Cancel LDA checks when their proceeds are not due to payees or their estates but are for credit to an appropriation or fund account. The procedure to cancel these checks depends on whether the account is open or closed, whether the check is current or uncurrent, and whether the check is available or unavailable to the DO maintaining the LDA. Contact DFAS-JJFKCD/IN at the email address in paragraph 15.2.2 for procedural guidance and processing instructions.

15.6.2. If a payee or the payee’s estate is not entitled to a check, only the functional area that submitted the certified payment may request the DO to cancel it. Except as provided in this paragraph, use an SF 1098 to list and report all such canceled checks. Where practicable, the functional area that authorized the original payment prepares the SF 1098.

15.7    REPLACING MISSING, MUTILATED, AND FORGED LD CHECKS

15.7.1. On receipt of a claim for a check reported as not received, lost, stolen, destroyed, mutilated, forged, or defaced, the DO must determine from the LD or from retained records whether the check is outstanding. The DO issues a replacement check under this chapter only when the check is reported outstanding and unpaid before the end of the fiscal year following the fiscal year it was issued, and the issuance involves no question of law or fact.

15.7.2. The payee or other claimant must notify the DO in writing (with signature) when a check has been lost, stolen, mutilated, or destroyed and request that payment on the check be stopped. The notification must provide all information available on the check. The federal agency must attempt to obtain a replacement without an Agreement of Indemnity. When a replacement cannot be obtained without an Agreement of Indemnity, the agency requests one from Fiscal Service; the specific documents required for an indemnification request are listed in
I TFM 5-5035.20.

15.7.3. This guidance for claims on paid checks applies to all LDAs. The payee must immediately notify the DO in writing (with signature) when a check has been paid on a forged endorsement, providing all available information identifying the forged check. The payee completes the Financial Management Service (FMS) Form 1133, Claim Against the United States for the Proceeds of a Government Check, and returns it to the DO who issued the original check within 90 days of the date on the FMS 1133.

15.7.4. If the original LD check is recovered before a replacement check is issued, suspend the replacement action and request that the LD remove the stop-payment against the original check, which the payee may then negotiate. If the replacement check has already been released, render the original check non-negotiable.

15.7.5. Referral to DoW Office of General Counsel

15.7.5.1. Send cases involving questions about a payee’s or owner’s entitlement to a substitute or settlement check, and cases where the court has appointed no legal representative for a deceased or incapacitated payee or owner, through command legal channels to the DoW OGC. Include an assessment or determination from the appropriate entitlement area about the underlying obligation. Before referring a case, see paragraph 15.6.

15.7.5.2. Send cases involving any question of law or fact through command legal channels for settlement action.

15.7.5.3. Send cases involving checks outstanding more than one fiscal year after the fiscal year in which they were issued through command legal channels for settlement. Include an undertaking of indemnity for the proceeds of a lost, stolen, destroyed, mutilated, or defaced LD check; the check in question, when available, or any identifiable portions of it; and any other supporting documentation.

15.7.6. The DO must retain approved claims and supporting documents, or copies where the originals have been transferred to the supporting DFAS site, as part of the retained records.

15.8    ADJUSTMENT OF CHECK-ISSUE DISCREPANCIES

Internal, Government Accountability Office, or other agency audits, or DO-initiated control measures, disclose LD check-issue discrepancies. These LDA differences are chargeable to DOs, and the DO must make and record adjustments immediately upon discovery. This guidance does not apply to voided, spoiled, or canceled LDA checks, which are addressed in paragraphs 15.4 and 15.5. These discrepancies occur when: the LD pays a check in an amount different from the disbursement voucher and the record of checks issued; the disbursing office draws a check to the wrong payee; the disbursing office issues a check in an amount different from the disbursement voucher; the disbursing office voids, spoils, or cancels a valid check in error while simultaneously issuing a check that was the subject of an action to void, spoil, or cancel; or the payee advises of a possible overpayment or underpayment. Contact DFAS-JJFKCD/IN at the email address in subparagraph 15.2.2 for procedural guidance and processing instructions.

15.9    LDA TRANSACTION DOCUMENTATION

DOs must implement controls to assure that LD checks are drawn in strict conformance to certified disbursement vouchers. LDAs are part of the DO’s accountability for public funds. The DO must maintain complete and accurate records and make them available for audit to ensure the integrity of the LDAs. Treat a loss from a bank failure as a physical loss (see Section 7.0). Contact DFAS-JJFKCD/IN at the email address in subparagraph 15.2.2 for procedural guidance and processing instructions.

15.10    TRANSFERRING AND CLOSING AN LDA

LDAs that are closed or transferred must be reconciled. Before attempting to reconcile an LDA, the DO’s agent serving as LDA custodian contacts the LD and requests a current statement of the account and, if available, all paid LD checks since the last regular statement. Reconcile the account by preparing an SF 1149. Contact DFAS-JJFKCD/IN at the email address in subparagraph
15.2.2 for procedural guidance and processing instructions.

title: Section 16.0: Disbursing Officer Accountability Reports
content:
16.0    DISBURSING OFFICER ACCOUNTABILITY REPORTS

16.1    GENERAL

16.1.1. Overview

16.1.1.1. All disbursing officers (DOs) are accountable to the U.S. Department of the Treasury (Treasury) for the cash and cash equivalent items (including receivables) in their possession. DOs must submit financial reports to support DoW accountability to the U.S. Government for all public funds collected and disbursed. These reports are the basis for official audits and settlement of accounts by the U.S. Government Accountability Office and provide information to maintain administrative accounting controls.

16.1.1.2. DOs maintain daily accountability on the DD Form 2657, Daily Statement of Accountability. The DO's official monthly accountability is recorded and reported on the Standard Form (SF) 1219, Statement of Accountability. DOs report disbursement and collection transactions on both the DD 2657 and the SF 1219, with collections reported net of disbursements on the SF 1219. Every DO must keep detailed records of all transactions, and these records must be available for examination by authorized representatives. Daily reporting does not affect the use and distribution of the DD 2657; SF 1219; DD 2665, Daily Agent Accountability Summary; and DD 1081, Statement of Agent Officer's Account. DOs must continue to submit financial reports to supporting DFAS sites based on each site's instructions.

16.2    POLICY
16.2.1. Balancing of Accounts

16.2.1.1. DOs keep documents representing cash in their vault or safe and account for them daily on the DD 2657 and monthly on the SF 1219. The DD 2657 is the permanent written record of the DO's daily balance of cash in possession. When accounts are inspected, DOs must present the DD 2657 to the inspectors for examination.

16.2.1.2. Deputy DOs (DDOs), cashiers, and disbursing agents perform most DO cash transactions. The DO or primary DDO balances all DDOs, cashiers, disbursing agents, paying agents, and collection agents daily using the DD 2665. The DD 2665 is the report of their accountability to the DO, and the DO or primary DDO prepares it from a physical count of all cash and negotiable instruments in their possession.

16.2.2. DDOs, cashiers, and disbursing agents who are geographically distant from the DO (for example, a DO in Indiana and an agent in Afghanistan) must still record transactions by preparing a DD 2665, but they need not submit the DD 2665 to the DO daily. DOs establish the timing of agent turn-ins for their operations. Agent turn-ins must include all DD 2665s, supporting documentation (such as collection vouchers, disbursement vouchers, and deposit tickets), and the
DD 1081.

16.2.3. DOs aboard Navy vessels balance their cash using the DD 2657. DDOs, cashiers, and disbursing agents must use the DD 2665 to balance at least weekly, immediately before and after each payday, on the last day of each month, and anytime the DO suspects an irregularity has occurred. When workload and staffing conditions allow, DOs aboard Navy vessels should balance cash accounts for all DDOs, cashiers, and disbursing agents daily.

16.3    DAILY AGENT ACCOUNTABILITY SUMMARY (DD 2665)

The DD 2665 is a stand-alone document that provides a complete picture of a DDO's, cashier's, or disbursing agent's accountability transactions from day to day. Each DDO, cashier, and disbursing agent prepares a DD 2665 for each day during which they transact business. It must summarize that day's business and record the transactions in U.S. dollar values. Paying agents appointed to work with contracting for contingency operations prepare a DD 2665 on the day they turn in all their business to the DO. Avoid a turn-in during the middle of a business day when possible. If a turn-in is required mid-day, prepare a DD 2665 up to and including the turn- in period, then prepare another DD 2665 for the rest of the business day.

16.4    STATEMENT OF AGENT OFFICER’S ACCOUNT (DD 1081)

16.4.1. Agent officers (DOs, cashiers, and disbursing agents) prepare a DD 1081 as a summary of cash transactions and a receipt for cash and vouchers on hand between DOs and their agent officers. The form is prepared when a DO advances funds to an agent and to summarize cash transactions for the period covered by the turn-in. When agent officers settle their account, the DO or principal DDO verifies the DD 1081, signs the original and a copy, keeps the original and supporting documents, and returns the signed copy to the agent officer. The DO or principal DDO must perform a physical count of cash at the time of the turn-in or settlement. The agent officer keeps the signed copy as a record of the opening cash balance for the next period of duty and for record purposes if the account is balanced to zero.

16.4.2. Subject to the parent DO's approval, paying agents in remote operational contingency locations may transmit electronically scanned or facsimile copies of the DD 1081 to the parent disbursing office. A paying agent is solely responsible to ensure that all documentation is legible and that:

16.4.2.1. The scanned or facsimile copies were produced from original documents and cannot be altered;

16.4.2.2. The copies are retained until the applicable retention period expires; and

16.4.2.3. Access to the images is limited to authorized personnel. When paying agents transmit documents electronically, the DO must verify the electronic submissions are in fact from the paying agent. The DO is responsible to ensure that adequate internal controls are implemented to prevent posting duplicate items when receiving electronic and original documents from the operational contingency location. The DO must also provide for the confirmation and acceptance of digitally signed documents and the return of the accepted DD 1081 to the agent.

16.5    DAILY STATEMENT OF ACCOUNTABILITY (DD 2657)

The DD 2657 summarizes the total disbursements and collections made during the business day by the DO and all DDOs, cashiers, and disbursing agents. Section I of the DD 2657 reflects the total DO accountability to the Treasury at the end of each business day. If disbursing operations were to cease, the total amount listed in Section I for the last operational business day would be the amount that the Treasury would seek to recover from the DO.

16.6    STATEMENT OF ACCOUNTABILITY (SF 1219)

In a daily reporting environment, the SF 1219 is no longer required to be submitted to the Treasury. DOs may continue to complete and submit the SF 1219 at month's end to DFAS for reporting requirements based on each site's instructions. The SF 1219 continues to reconcile deposits, collections, disbursements, and cash balances with Treasury monthly. DOs must still balance to the Treasury monthly account statement, which summarizes the financial activities of federal agencies. DoW has established processes for creating and reconciling the SF 1219 monthly. There is no warrant or apportionment for DO cash and no formal funds control system documentation that legally places responsibility on the DO for the cash; the SF 1219 is a recognized means of establishing responsibility for a specific, verified balance at a point in time. It aligns with accounting reporting cycles (the Governmentwide Treasury Account Symbol Adjusted Trial Balance System bulk file submission), which transmits the end-of-month balance in the DO Cash account(s) and must match the sum of the SF 1219s for each Service to facilitate reconciliation with the general ledger.

16.7    FINANCIAL REPORTS

16.7.1. Overview

16.7.1.1. DOs submit financial reports to DFAS on a calendar-month basis, except for months during which accountability begins or ends on other than the first or last day of a month.

16.7.1.1.1. For a new disbursing office, the accounting period begins on the first day official business is transacted. When one DO relieves another, the accounting period for the relieved officer ends on the date of relief, and the accounting period for the relieving officer normally begins on the next calendar day. Whenever possible, relief of a DO should occur on the last day of a month to avoid submitting an additional set of financial reports for that month.

16.7.1.1.2. An accounting period may not extend beyond the end of a calendar month. Exceptions may occur when a DO is relieved from disbursing duty before the last day of a month or commences disbursing duty on other than the first day of a month. The first day of the accounting period coincides with the date of commencement of disbursing duty notification forwarded under Section 3.0. For any month during which accountability ends because of a Disbursing Station Symbol Number closing, the DO must submit the financial reports from the first day of the month through the date of closing.

16.7.1.2. DOs may submit supplemental reports to Treasury to adjust prior-period reporting, correct original reporting, or report additional current-month transactions.

16.7.1.3. DOs submit financial reports to the supporting DFAS site based on each site's instructions.

16.7.2. When a DDO, cashier, disbursing agent, paying agent, collection agent, or imprest fund cashier has a physical loss of funds, forward the DD 2667 to DFAS-ZPTC/IN within five calendar days after the end of each month (see Section 7.0, subparagraph 7.4.2.2).

16.8    DISBURSING OFFICE RECORDS

16.8.1. DoW Record Retention

16.8.1.1. DOs must apply the most stringent record retention requirements to support accounting records of initial entries and support records such as checks, electronic fund transfers, and invoices, and must keep them until all outstanding issues are resolved. Before disposing of contingency operations documents, DOs must contact their legal counsel about document retention beyond the NARA and DoW guidance for financial records. Records must be available and accessible to all authorized users. A DO or designated settlement official must keep records to complete the reconciliation of payment or collection discrepancies until resolved.

16.8.2. Other Records

16.8.2.1. The requirement to retain original records applies to any record a DO receives that accompanies payment or collection transactions or supports financial reports. It applies to both paper and electronic records kept as original supporting documents at both the functional and disbursing offices. Certifying officials send electronic payment files only to the DO and keep supporting documentation per the guidance referenced in subparagraph 16.8.1. For Foreign Military Sales document record retention, see Volume 15.

16.8.2.1.1. The disbursing office must put hardcopy and electronic records storage controls in place to ensure that only authorized personnel have access to any paper documents and electronic images.

16.8.2.2. Individual records may be unclassified, but when information is aggregated the security classification (and storage requirement) may change. Per DoD Instruction 5200.48, Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), unclassified records do not require special security or storage controls and may be stored in open files or cabinets. Store these records with controls that readily identify:

16.8.3. Transfer

16.8.3.1. Transfer all disbursing office records to the incoming (relieving) DO as part of the relief process described in Section 3.0, subparagraph 3.4.6. When a disbursing office is deactivated, package and mail all disbursing office records to the office designated to settle the accounts.

16.8.3.2. When a DO of a tactical unit or naval vessel is relieved from disbursing duty, the incoming DO keeps the outgoing DO's disbursing records for 90 days from the date of relief. After the 90-day period, the incoming DO packages the disbursing records and sends them to the supporting DFAS site or alternate site designated by DFAS for retention until the required retention period expires. For deployed units, the 90-day period begins after the unit or vessel returns to homeport.

16.8.3.3. When a DO of a tactical unit or naval vessel is relieved from disbursing duty due to deactivation of the disbursing office, or when a vessel or unit is decommissioned from service, the DO must package and send all disbursing office records to the supporting DFAS site or alternate site designated for retention.

title: Section 17.0: Safekeeping Funds and Valuables for Individuals and Morale, Welfare, and Recreation Activities
content:
17.0    SAFEKEEPING FUNDS AND VALUABLES FOR INDIVIDUALS AND MORALE, WELFARE, AND RECREATION ACTIVITIES

17.1    GENERAL

17.1.1. DoW disbursing officers (DOs), deputy DOs (DDOs), and agents may accept cash and checks from individuals and morale, welfare, and recreation (MWR) activities for which safe custody otherwise would not be available. When a DO, DDO, or agent is unavailable, or when it is impractical for one of them to accept and account for safekeeping deposits, a commander may appoint and terminate any military member or DoW civilian employee as a safekeeping custodian to accept and account for safekeeping deposits using a separate DD Form 577, Appointment/Termination Record - Authorized Signature.

17.1.1.1. Keep safekeeping deposits in a secured safe and establish procedures to maintain accountability. Treat funds accepted for safekeeping as funds held in trust for which the United States is accountable, but not within the DO's financial accountability reported to the U.S. Department of the Treasury (Treasury) on the SF 1219, Statement of Accountability.

17.1.1.2. Deposits and withdrawals are subject to local command regulations that establish necessary and proper restrictions on the time, place, and frequency of deposits and withdrawals and the types of objects classified as valuables. Impose controls to prevent interruption of the activity's priority fiscal operations, such as special and regular payroll activities. Do not allow safekeeping services to be abused by depositing objects not usually afforded additional protection. Limit deposited valuables to funds; negotiable instruments including bonds, credit cards, travelers' checks, and checkbooks; and objects classified as jewelry having intrinsic value requiring additional protection. Items such as wallets, snapshots, keys, or items lacking intrinsic value are prohibited.

17.1.1.3. Commanders appoint custodians responsible for the proper handling of and accounting for safekeeping deposits. Appointments must state the specific duties the custodian is authorized to perform. Pecuniary liability does not attach to safekeeping deposits because they are not public funds. Paragraph 17.2 applies to the safekeeping of nonappropriated funds (NAF) for MWR activities. Losses of NAF are not recorded on the DO's SF 1219. If a loss occurs, notify the depositor of their right to submit a claim for reimbursement under applicable DoW Component regulations. The depositor need not defer submission of a claim to await findings of any investigation initiated to determine responsibility for the loss.

17.1.1.4. When the volume or nature of safekeeping deposit transactions warrants, the custodian may formally appoint an assistant custodian for initial receipt and temporary custody of safekeeping deposits pending their delivery to the designated custodian. Provide separate safekeeping facilities for the assistant custodian. Cover all custody transfers between the custodian and assistant custodian with a receipt. An assistant custodian is responsible for proper accounting and handling, including receipt and delivery of safekeeping deposits to a permanent custodian. Process losses under subparagraph 17.1.1.3.

17.1.1.5. Receive and handle safekeeping deposits of postal funds under the Military Postal Service (DoD Instruction 4525.09), identifying these as postage stamp fund or postal money order fund, as applicable, on the safekeeping deposit receipt.

17.1.1.6. Follow subparagraph 17.2.1 to receive and handle safekeeping deposits of funds by military banking facilities, NAF custodians, and other DoW-sponsored activities. Identify on the safekeeping deposit receipt the deposit, the depositing agency, and the custodian making the deposit.

17.2    SAFEKEEPING OF NONAPPROPRIATED FUNDS FOR MWR ACTIVITIES

17.2.1. Custodians may collocate funds when the volume of safekeeping deposits warrants and it is desirable to accommodate more than one deposit or withdrawal transaction in non- individual safekeeping deposit accounts at non-tactical activities. Place the deposits in a separate container identified as safekeeping funds to prevent commingling with official funds. At activities other than Navy ships, if the total value of collocated safekeeping funds on hand is large, a bank checking account may be established (see subparagraph 17.2.2).

17.2.1.1. In addition to individual ledger sheets, the custodian keeps a cash-on- hand ledger control sheet, entering the amount of each deposit in the debit column and the total amount on deposit by all depositors in the balance column. If preferred, the custodian may make a daily summary posting to the ledger control sheet showing inclusive deposit numbers. The balance of the ledger control sheet must agree with the combined balances of the individual depositors' ledger sheets.

17.2.1.2. The depositor presents the original deposit receipt(s) to the custodian when requesting a full or partial withdrawal of the funds on deposit. Before releasing the funds requested, the custodian confirms the depositor's account balance and obtains a signature in the applicable section of the retained copy of the DD 2674, verifying it against the signature on the deposit record or the individual ledger sheet. For a full withdrawal, the custodian voids the original DD 2674 in the presence of the depositor. A depositor may make up to three partial withdrawals of a safekeeping deposit. If the deposit is not withdrawn in full after two requests, the custodian voids the original DD 2674 and issues a new DD 2674 for the new deposit amount. The custodian enters the withdrawal as a credit in the depositor's individual ledger sheet and the custodian's ledger control sheet. Instead of individual entries, the custodian may post a daily summary showing inclusive withdrawal numbers on the ledger control sheet.

17.2.1.2.1. Return the identical currency the depositor presented when the deposit is withdrawn. For example, a deposit made in Japanese Yen cannot be withdrawn in U.S. dollars.

17.2.2. Bank Accounts

17.2.2.1. Custodians of commingled safekeeping funds, with command approval, may establish and maintain a checking account in a local bank or credit union (insured by either the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation or the National Credit Union Share Insurance Fund, as appropriate) for the deposit of safekeeping funds if the amount available for deposit is large enough to preclude the payment of service charges or other fees. The financial institution collateralizes funds in excess of the insured limits per Title 31, Code of Federal Regulations, Part 202. Establish the account in the name of the disbursing activity, the safekeeping fund, and the custodian (for example, "U.S. Naval Activity, Boston, MA, Safekeeping Deposit Fund, Lieutenant J. A. Hancock, SC, U.S. Navy, Custodian"). Loans or investments from safekeeping deposit funds are prohibited.

17.2.2.2. All checks must be serially pre-numbered. Maintain a complete record of all checks drawn, deposits made to the safekeeping checking account, and a running account balance in the checkbook. Reconcile statements from the financial institution immediately upon receipt and file them with the bank ledger control sheet. Mark spoiled checks as "VOID" and file them in sequence.

17.2.2.3. Deposit checks, money orders, and cash received for safekeeping to the authorized account, except for cash required to be kept on hand to meet safekeeping withdrawal requirements. Checks and money orders may be accepted for deposit, subject to collection. Withdrawals are not authorized until enough time has elapsed for the checks and money orders to clear through the banking system.

17.2.2.4. Draw checks for withdrawals of safekeeping funds on the safekeeping deposit fund account whenever practical. Checks may be drawn on the safekeeping fund account only for payment to a depositor for withdrawal, an authorized transfer of a depositor's account to another activity, replenishment of cash-on-hand (through an exchange-for-cash check) needed to meet safekeeping withdrawal requirements, or transfer of unclaimed monies.

17.2.2.5.
