At a minimum, the listing must include the PRO's name and address, the labor organization or association the listing pertains to, employee names and the dues deducted for each, the total amount collected, and system-generated remarks that explain any lack of deductions.

10.2.3.9. The PRO must provide a transmittal report to the Central Campaign Administrator to include: The employing agency, e.g., Army, Navy, Air Force; the employee names and deduction amounts per individual employee; the pay period number; and the pay period date of the CFC data. See 5 CFR 950.801.

10.2.4. Quarterly Reports

10.2.4.1. Upon request, the PRO must furnish feeder data to the appropriate HRO on total wages paid to civilian employees for specific calendar quarters. The HRO must prepare and submit the final report.

10.2.4.2. The employing activity must report the parking fringe benefit valuation directly to the servicing PRO quarterly to ensure proper reporting of income and collection of taxable wages on the W-2.

10.2.4.3. The report must include the monthly value of the transportation fringe benefits and the reportable taxable benefit.

10.2.4.4. When directed, the PRO must furnish data to the appropriate functional organization on civilian employees participating in Direct Deposit/Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT). DoW managers use this feeder information to report payment volumes and the percentage of payments made by EFT to the Bureau of the Fiscal Service within 25 days after the end of each quarter.

10.2.4.5. For SF 113-G, Monthly Report of Full-Time Equivalent/Work-Year Civilian Employment, the PRO must provide feeder data to the Defense Manpower Data Center for reporting to OMB.

10.2.5. Semiannual Reports

10.2.5.1. For the Report of Work Years and Personnel Cost, the consolidated PRO must provide feeder-type data on the leave data for part C. OMB uses this report to estimate the cost of proposed federal pay increases, evaluate the financial effects of proposed legislation on civilian compensation and benefits, and analyze federal employee pay and personnel benefits.

10.2.6. Annual Reports

10.2.6.1. The PRO must issue a W-2 to each employee no later than January 31st of the year following the applicable tax (calendar) year, including employees who died or separated during the year. If an individual requests the form earlier in writing, the PRO must issue it within 30 calendar days after receipt of the request or after the final payment, whichever is later. DoW PROs must use the DFAS-approved standardized W-2 each year.

10.2.6.2. Each DoW Component with Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System (DCIPS) positions must submit an annual report on its foreign language pay program to the Under Secretary of War for Intelligence through the Director, Human Capital Management Office, per DoW Instruction (DoWI) 1400.25-V2016. Each annual report must:

10.2.6.2.1. Include a copy of the Component's current foreign language pay policy or guidance, and copies of any related documents or communications issued on foreign language pay since the previous report.

10.2.6.2.2. Identify the total number of language-coded authorizations and official tasking that requests language and proficiency in support of mission requirements.

10.2.6.2.3. Identify the total number of DCIPS employees receiving foreign language pay and whether they are assigned to designated foreign language positions. Include a breakout of the number of DCIPS employees receiving foreign language pay by each language.

10.2.6.2.4. Identify the total amount of foreign language payments made in the past calendar year and a breakout of the amounts by language.

10.2.6.2.5. Identify, for Interagency Language Roundtable Level 3 proficiency and above (combined), the percentage of recipients paid, by language.

10.2.6.2.6. Discuss the current state of recruitment and fill of foreign language positions, including overages, trends, shortfalls, recommendations on foreign language pay policy, payment trends (by language and amount) from the previous year, and a brief statement on the effectiveness of incentive pay in recruitment.

title: Section 11.0: Special Category Employees
content:
11.0    SPECIAL CATEGORY EMPLOYEES

11.1    Overseas Employees

11.1.1. Canadian Employees

11.1.1.1. Canadian legal holidays are observed with no charge to leave. If an emergency requires work on a Canadian holiday, the employee must be paid premium pay at 1.5 times the regular rate of pay, plus either holiday pay equal to regular wages earned in the four weeks before the holiday divided by 20, or compensatory time off (subject to local labor laws per DoWI 1400.25-V1231). The legal Canadian holidays are listed in the FMM.

11.1.1.2. Canadian employees accrue sick leave at 4.25 hours each pay period, except 6.25 hours in the last pay period of the leave year. Total annual accumulation is 112.5 hours (15 days).

11.1.1.3. For Canadian employees, the workday is 7.5 hours and the workweek is
37.5    hours.

11.1.1.4. Canadian employees receive step increases until they reach the top step. A step increase requires the supervisor's written certification that the employee demonstrated an acceptable level of competence during the waiting period. The certification must be forwarded to the Human Resources Office before the effective date. Step increases are effective at the start of the first pay period after the anniversary date.

11.1.1.5. Retroactive pay adjustments for Canadian employees are based on the agreements covering Canadian Civil Service employees and are payable to employees separated during the retroactive period.

11.1.1.6. For Canadian employees, aggregate LWOP of more than 80 hours during the step-increase waiting period delays the increase. Extended LWOP also affects leave accruals.

11.1.1.7. Canadian national employees are eligible for all awards except quality step increases.

11.1.1.8. Employee Canada Pension Plan contributions are deducted from Canadian employees' salaries, and the U.S. Government pays the employer's contribution.

11.1.1.9. For Canadian employees, the U.S. Government pays an amount equal to the employee's contributions to the Registered/Retirement Pension Plan, up to the legal maximum of annual salary set under applicable Canadian law.

11.1.1.10. Canadian employees are paid a lump-sum severance amount per the schedule that follows.

11.1.1.10.1. Lay-off: two weeks of pay for the first complete year of continuous employment and one week for each additional complete year, to a maximum of 28 weeks.

11.1.1.10.2. Resignation: an employee who resigns with 10 or more years of continuous employment is paid one-half week of pay for each complete year, up to a maximum of 26 years, to a maximum of 13 weeks.

11.1.1.10.3. Retirement: an employee entitled on retirement to an immediate annuity (or an immediate annual allowance had the employee been under the Canadian Government Public Service Superannuation Act) is paid one week of pay for each complete year of continuous employment, to a maximum of 28 weeks.

11.1.1.10.4. Death: the employee's estate is paid one week of pay for each complete year of continuous employment, to a maximum of 28 weeks.

11.1.1.11. Canadian employees enrolled in the Ontario Health Insurance Plan are reimbursed an amount equal to the Canadian government contributions under the plan. Reimbursement claims must be supported by receipts and submitted annually by the end of the calendar year.

11.1.1.12. The U.S. Government participates in the Canadian Employment Insurance Program for Canadians employed in Canada by the DoW. DoW installations employing personnel in Canada must follow Canada Revenue Agency guidance. The U.S. Government contributes an amount equal to that paid by a Canadian government employer, and the employee's contributions are deducted from salary.

11.1.1.12.1. The PRO must use the Canada Revenue Agency T4001 Employer's Guide - Payroll Deductions and Remittances to determine insurable employment and earnings for withholding.

11.1.1.12.1.1. Funds must be withheld from the pay of all insurable Canadian employees at the rate set in the Canada Revenue Agency T4001 Employer's Guide.

11.1.1.12.1.2. The employer's share must equal 1.4 times the amount withheld from the employee's pay on each payroll voucher. The contribution is charged to the fund from which the employees' salaries are paid.

11.1.1.12.2. The DoW must not make retroactive payments of deductions to the Canada Revenue Agency if the employee has not given correct information to the employing installation. This includes adjudicated cases.

11.1.1.12.3. DoW records of deductions, contributions, and remittances are subject to audit by Canadian authorities. The PRO must send copies of records required by Canadian authorities on request; audit requirements may be met by sending copies of covered- personnel records and insurance remittance documents to the proper Canada Revenue Agency district office.

11.1.1.13. Canadian employees' income tax contributions are deducted from their biweekly salary.

11.1.1.14. Accidental life insurance is a voluntary contribution deducted from the Canadian employee's biweekly salary at the employee's request.

11.2    Reemployed Annuitants

11.2.1. Purpose

11.2.1.1. The Secretary of War has authority under 5 U.S.C. § 9902 to reemploy annuitants without a reduction in pay or annuity, as implemented in DoWI 1400.25-V300. A reemployed annuitant hired by DoW on or after November 25, 2003, may receive full annuity and salary upon appointment, with no salary offset for the annuity and no further retirement deductions. Exception: a discontinued service retirement (DSR) annuitant whose annuity is based on involuntary separation for reasons other than misconduct or delinquency, hired by DoW on or after November 25, 2003, may instead elect retirement contributions and earn further retirement credit rather than receive full salary plus annuity. See CSRS/FERS Handbook, Chapter 44.

11.3    Deceased Employees

11.3.1. Payment

11.3.1.1. When payment is to be made to the duly appointed legal representative of the estate or to a person entitled under the law of the deceased's domicile, the servicing PRO may require the claimant to submit evidence of entitlement under state law. Such evidence includes, but is not limited to, funeral expense receipts, a small estate affidavit, trust documents, court orders granting summary administration, letters of administration, and, where necessary, the deceased person's will.

11.3.1.2. If the beneficiary's actions caused the death of the employee, the servicing PRO must not pay the employee's unpaid compensation to that person unless the PRO receives and determines that evidence clearly absolves the beneficiary of any felonious intent.

11.3.2. Computation

11.3.2.1. Allotment deductions for the pay period in which death occurred are not withheld.

11.3.3. The PRO does not deduct retirement, federal, state, or local income tax, health benefits, or life insurance from the lump-sum accrued-leave payment.

11.3.4. Death Gratuity Payments for Federal Employees

11.3.4.1. The gratuity payment is not wages for Social Security, Medicare, or federal, state, or local tax withholding. The Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) must prepare an IRS Form 1099-R, Distributions From Pensions, Annuities, Retirement or Profit- Sharing Plans, IRAs, and Insurance Contracts, and forward it to the personal representative.

11.3.4.2. Under 5 U.S.C. § 9904, DoW civilian employees assigned to certain activities outside the United States determined to be hazardous to life or health or that involve specialized security requirements may be eligible for benefits comparable to those the Secretary of State provides Foreign Service members under 22 U.S.C. § 3973. Per 22 U.S.C. § 3973, a death gratuity is paid when an employee dies from injuries received in the performance of duties. The gratuity amount equals Level II of the Executive Schedule under 5 U.S.C. § 5313 at the time of the employee's death. This gratuity must be paid as follows, regardless of other designated beneficiaries: First, to the widow or widower, as defined under 5 U.S.C. § 8101(6) and (11); or Second, to the child, or children as defined under 5 U.S.C. § 8101(9), in equal shares, if there is no widow or widower; or Third, to dependent parent, or dependent parents, defined under 5 U.S.C. § 8101(7), in equal shares, if there is no widow, widower, or child. If there are no survivors as indicated in subparagraph 5.9.2, the death gratuity must not be paid.

11.4    Legally Incapcitated Employees

11.4.1. The servicing HRO initiates an SF 50 action showing the employee's separation for mental incapacity, and may place the employee on extended leave of absence by an SF 50 action. Once the servicing PRO is notified that the employee is declared legally incapacitated, no payments are made to the employee. A claim must be filed on the employee's behalf before the pay account can be settled. No specific form is required to claim amounts due mentally incapacitated or former employees, but the claim must be filed in writing over the signature of the person claiming on the employee's behalf. If the claimant is not a guardian or committee, the servicing PRO must consult its Office of General Counsel before making payment.

11.4.1.1. The initial claim filed by the guardian or committee of the estate of a legally incapacitated employee must include a court certificate showing the claimant's appointment and qualification as guardian or committee. After the first payment, subsequent recurring payments may be made to the same payee without further claim as long as the appointment remains in effect and the matter is otherwise free from doubt. Each subsequent payment voucher must cite the voucher on which the initial claim was paid.

11.4.1.2. If a guardian or committee has not been and will not be appointed, the initial claim must be supported by a sworn statement that includes the following information: the claimant’s relationship to the legally incapacitated employee, if any; the name and address of the person having care and custody of the legally incapacitated employee; a remark that any amount paid to the claimant must be applied only to the use and benefit of the legally incapacitated employee; and a remark that no appointment of a guardian or committee is contemplated.

11.4.2. Claims for unpaid amounts owed to legally incapacitated employees may be paid once the claim and the claimant's entitlement have been verified.

11.5    Missing Persons, Captured or Interned

11.5.1. An employee in a missing status is entitled to receive or have credited to their account, for the period in that status, the same pay and allowances to which the employee was entitled at the start of that period or becomes entitled to after (5 U.S.C. § 5562). The servicing PRO retains responsibility for the employee's pay, leave, and retirement records.

11.5.2. Termination

11.5.2.1. If the employee returns from missing status, a statement of the special leave account balance must be furnished to the HRO. The employee must elect in writing to receive either a payment or a credit for the leave. If the employee requests payment, the payment is made using the employee's rate of pay in effect at the time the leave was forfeited.

11.5.2.2. If the employee returns from missing status, the agency must charge the pay adjustment or final settlement, including local allotment payments to dependents, to the employee’s appropriated fund account.

11.6    Temporary and Term Employment

11.6.1. Purpose

11.6.1.1. Temporary and term appointments fill positions when there is no continuing need for the job. Employees in either category are not entitled to competitive status or reinstatement eligibility based on this service. Within DoW, temporary and term appointments may last longer than the time restrictions of 5 CFR Part 316 and may allow such employees consideration for permanent employment.

11.6.2. Temporary Employment

11.6.2.1. Per DoW policy, a component may make a temporary appointment to:

11.6.2.1.1. Noncompetitively fill a short-term position based on a critical hiring need not expected to last more than 1 year. A critical hiring need means the need to fill the position(s) to meet mission requirements brought about by circumstances such as extraordinary workload or unusual or unanticipated events creating the need to fill the position(s). Such appointment may be extended up to 6 additional months but must not exceed a total of 18 months and does not convey noncompetitive conversion to any other appointment. See Deputy Secretary of War Memorandum, "Noncompetitive Temporary and Term Appointments to Meet Critical Hiring Needs in the Department of Defense," dated July 14, 2017; and

11.6.2.1.2. Temporarily fill a position for less than 1 year and extend such appointment in increments of up to 1 year, not to exceed a total of 3 years. See the OUSD (P&R) Memorandum "Modification of Temporary and Term Appointments Within the Department of Defense," dated June 12, 2017 as modified by Deputy Secretary of War Memorandum "Extensions of Term Appointments in the Competitive Service in the DoW," dated August 10, 2018 and 5 CFR 316.401.

11.6.3. Term Employment

11.6.3.1. Per DoW policy, a component may make a term appointment to:

11.6.3.1.1. Noncompetitively fill a short-term position based on a critical hiring need expected to last more than 1 year. Critical hiring need means the need to fill the position(s) to meet mission requirements brought about by circumstances such as extraordinary workload or unusual or unanticipated events creating the need to fill the position(s). Such appointment must not exceed a total of 18 months and does not convey noncompetitive conversion to any other appointment. See Deputy Secretary of War Memorandum, "Noncompetitive Temporary and Term Appointments to Meet Critical Hiring Needs in the Department of Defense," dated July 14, 2017;

11.6.3.1.2. Fill a position initially for more than 1 year, but not more than 6 years. Components may extend term appointments beyond 6 years and up to 8 years in increments of up to 1 year according to policy. Under certain conditions prescribed in policy, an employee in a term position may be noncompetitively converted to a career or career-conditional appointment. See the OUSD (P&R) Memorandum "Modification of Temporary and Term Appointments Within the Department of Defense," dated June 12, 2017 as modified by Deputy Secretary of War Memorandum "Extensions of Term Appointments in the Competitive Service in the DoW," dated August 10, 2018; and

11.6.3.1.3. Per the direct-hire authority, initially appoint a current post- secondary student for a period expected to last more than 1 year and not to exceed the time limits stated in 5 CFR 316.301, to include any future legislative or regulatory modification to those limits. Within 120 days of successful completion of their academic program, the student may be noncompetitively converted into a career or career-conditional appointment. See the OUSD (P&R) Memorandum "Modification of Direct-Hire Authority for the Department of Defense for Post-Secondary Students and Recent Graduates," dated January 15, 2019.

11.7    Air Traffic Controllers (ATC)

11.7.1. Differential pay is authorized for certain DoW employees. The Secretary of War has authorized 5 percent ATC premium pay under 5 U.S.C. § 5546a(a)(1). Payment of the premium is mandatory for DoW ATCs in the GS-2152 occupational series who occupy a position no lower than GS-9 at air traffic control centers, terminal or flight service stations. The HRO provides this information to the servicing PRO via an SF 50.

11.8    Personnel on Long-Term, Full-Time Training

11.8.1. Leave

11.8.1.1. Personnel on long-term, full-time training continue to accrue annual leave. Ordinarily, an employee is charged annual leave during school vacation periods that fall on government workdays unless the employee returns to the work site or has made documented arrangements with their DoW point of contact to be actively involved in academic work. These documented arrangements should be made well in advance of the vacation periods. Annual leave charges are reported on the employee’s time and attendance report. See OPM Training and Development Policy.

11.9    Emergency Medical Technician (EMT)

11.9.1. EMTs and paramedics work various schedules including the basic 40-hour workweek, compressed work schedules, and uncommon tours of duty. An uncommon tour of duty means an established tour of duty that exceeds 80 hours of work in a biweekly pay period. See 5 CFR 630.201. Schedules and changes to tours of duty for an EMT or paramedic working uncommon tours must be on file in the employing activity/timekeeper site. Sleep and meal time must also be documented. The EMT’s hourly rate is multiplied by 40 hours, and base pay and premium pay are based on this weekly rate regardless of the hours in the scheduled tour of duty for that week.

11.9.2. The HRO determines the amount of premium pay for the irregular tour of duty and reports it on the SF 50. An EMT employed as an intermittent employee is not entitled to premium pay on an annual basis or to paid leave. An EMT is paid under regular overtime rules. Refer to 5 CFR Part 551 for additional guidance on pay administration for EMTs under FLSA.

11.10    Firefighters

11.10.1. Trade-of-Time

11.10.1.1. Both firefighters in a trade-of-time arrangement must be supervised by the same fire chief and must be capable of performing the core duties that could be required during traded hours. If one firefighter under an arrangement is at a lower grade than the other, the fire chief may withhold approval when the affected unit would not have the skills among those assigned to an affected shift to accomplish its mission.

11.10.1.2. Firefighters may trade only hours within the firefighter's regular tour of duty established for leave-charging purposes. Trading time is not restricted to the same pay period.

11.10.1.3. Firefighters may agree to substitute either entire shifts or a portion of a shift.

11.10.1.4. All trading time agreements must be in writing and signed by both firefighters and the fire chief before a trade can occur. The agreements must contain the elements required by OPM's Memorandum, Firefighter Trading Time Policy.

11.10.1.5. Proposed trade-of-time arrangements are not entitlements. Reasons for disapproval may include, but are not limited to:

11.10.1.5.1. The proposed arrangement would result in either firefighter having a balance of committed but not-yet-executed substitution hours, under one or more pending-completion qualified trade-of-time arrangements, in excess of 144 hours.

11.10.1.5.2. A proposed substitution would occur more than 1 year after the date the qualified trade-of-time arrangement was approved.

11.10.1.5.3. Either firefighter owes a debt of hours to the agency, as described in subparagraph 16.11.3.5.

11.10.1.5.4. The arrangement involves trading hours for which pay is computed using a different methodology. The pay of both firefighters must be determined using the same methodology.

11.10.1.6. If a substituting firefighter fails to work during the agreed-upon substitution period, the excused firefighter is entitled to credit for hours and pay as if the substitution had been made. The substituting firefighter becomes indebted to the agency and must later perform work outside the firefighter's tour of duty to satisfy the debt of hours, as assigned by an authorized agency official.

11.10.1.6.1. Debt-repayment hours are not credited as hours of work in determining the firefighter's pay entitlements in the pay period in which they are performed.

11.10.1.6.2. A substituting firefighter who, without authorization, fails to report when scheduled to substitute under a qualified trade-of-time arrangement is considered AWOL and subject to appropriate discipline, unless the DoW component retroactively approves the absence after reviewing the circumstances.

11.10.1.6.3. A firefighter who owes a debt of hours and, without authorization, fails to report when scheduled to perform work to satisfy that debt is considered AWOL and subject to appropriate discipline, unless the DoW component retroactively approves the absence after reviewing the circumstances.

11.10.1.7. A firefighter with a debt of hours may not enter into a new trade-of-time arrangement until the debt is eliminated.

11.10.1.8. A firefighter owing a debt of hours may be allowed to reduce or eliminate the debt by agreeing to adjustments in the firefighter's balances of annual leave, compensatory time off (for overtime work, travel, or religious observances), or paid time-off awards, if allowed by DoW component policies.

11.10.1.8.1. If a firefighter owes a debt of hours when separating from Federal service, transferring to a different agency, or moving to a position in the same agency in which the employee is no longer an eligible firefighter, the debt must be recovered to the extent possible by offsetting any balances of annual leave, compensatory time off (for overtime work, travel, or religious observances), or paid-time-off awards.

11.10.1.8.2. Any remaining hours debt must be converted to a monetary debt owed to the agency. The monetary debt is determined from the firefighter's pay entitlements at separation and the hourly value of the hours using the same method used to compute the cash value of annual leave hours, except that no increase based on post-separation pay-rate increases applies (the increases that would otherwise apply in the lump-sum annual-leave payment based on projection of the lump-sum leave period). See 5 CFR 550.1204.

11.10.1.9. Credit for hours and associated pay for an excused firefighter must be determined as if the excused firefighter performed the work performed by the substituting firefighter; a substituting firefighter may not receive credit for hours and associated pay based on periods of substitution. Hours worked by a substituting firefighter under a qualified trade-of-time arrangement must be disregarded when determining that firefighter's eligibility for overtime pay or calculating such pay under 29 U.S.C. ch. 8 (Fair Labor Standards Act) and 5 U.S.C. 5542(h)(1)(A). Instead, the excused firefighter must be credited with hours worked by the substituting firefighter in determining the excused firefighter's overtime pay entitlements.

11.10.1.10. Hours worked by a substituting firefighter under a qualified trade-of- time arrangement are included in creditable service for leave accrual, retirement, and other purposes for the excused firefighter, not the substituting one.

11.10.1.11. A firefighter injured while substituting for another firefighter under a qualified trade-of-time arrangement is not, by reason of that substitution, affected in the substituting firefighter's possible entitlement to workers' compensation benefits.

11.10.1.12. A substituting firefighter is considered to be in the performance of duty during a period of substitution for workers' compensation purposes, except that any payments (such as continuation of pay) for the remainder of the affected biweekly pay period must be based on pay to which the substituting firefighter is entitled, without regard to pay for hours worked on behalf of an excused firefighter.

11.10.1.13. Excused firefighters are not considered to be in the performance of duty during the period when a substituting firefighter is working on their behalf.

11.10.1.14. If a firefighter had been scheduled, before the work injury, to work as a substituting firefighter during a future period when the firefighter is receiving continuation of pay or wage-loss compensation, the firefighter's leave status is considered to satisfy the firefighter's work-hours obligation, but only if the other firefighter under the affected qualified trade-of-time arrangement had already completed their part of the trade.

11.10.1.15. If neither firefighter had completed their respective parts of the trade before the work injury leading to workers' compensation benefits, the trade-of-time arrangement is automatically cancelled.

11.10.1.16. DoW components must keep records of a qualified trade-of-time arrangement, including uncompleted arrangements, for 4 years after the last substituted work performed under the arrangement.

11.10.1.17. DoW components must keep current records showing pending-completion qualified trade-of-time arrangements for each firefighter, including the current balance of hours committed but not yet executed for substitution, as required to apply the rule in subparagraph 16.11.3.4.1.

11.11    Judges
11.11.1. Judges

11.11.1.1. Upon becoming eligible for retirement, judges may elect to receive a retirement annuity from the DoW Military Retirement Fund (MRF) in lieu of an annuity under CSRS or FERS; survivor and former-spouse annuities may also be elected. See 10 U.S.C. 945. The DFAS Indianapolis site serves as the payment-records office for retiree and survivor entitlements and must perform functions such as:

11.11.1.1.1. DFAS must maintain individual retirement records of individuals who elect annuity benefits under 10 U.S.C. 945.

11.11.1.1.2. DFAS must issue annuity payments from moneys in the DoW MRF, including collecting applicable federal and state income taxes and debts owed the U.S. Government.

11.11.1.1.3. DFAS must arrange with OPM for transfer of moneys, including interest payments authorized under 10 U.S.C. 945(a)(3)(A), from the Civil Service Retirement and Disability Fund (CSRDF) to the DoW MRF.

11.11.1.1.4. DFAS must withhold, as appropriate, contributions from the annuity for FEHB and FEGLI, make correct agency contributions, and transmit these moneys to the CSRDF.

11.11.1.1.5. DFAS must readjust the annuity payment when events change the retiree or survivor entitlements.

11.11.1.1.6. DFAS must account for retirement moneys received from OPM and disburse them to benefit recipients, insurance carriers, and federal and state tax entities.

11.11.1.1.7. DFAS must cease annuity payment if the employee elects judiciary retirement benefits under 10 U.S.C. 945(g).

11.11.1.2. Judges receiving an annuity under 10 U.S.C. 945 must notify WHS of their election of judicial retirement benefits under 10 U.S.C. 945(g).

11.12    Auxiliary Chaplains and West Point Military Academy Chaplains

11.12.1. Civilian clergy may be assigned to perform essential religious services of the chapel program beyond the staffing capabilities of commissioned officer Armed Forces chaplains. Auxiliary chaplains normally perform their services on military installations. To serve as auxiliary chaplains, civilian clergy must be ordained or accredited by a faith group recognized by the Armed Forces Chaplains Board and must meet any additional qualifications required by the Armed Forces.

11.12.2. Appointing and Paying Auxiliary Chaplains

11.12.2.1. Auxiliary chaplains may be appointed by the HRO on an intermittent basis. They are paid on a fee basis from the employing activity's appropriated funds for civilian personnel, such as Operation and Maintenance funds. The HRO may appoint auxiliary chaplains under the excepted service authority in 5 CFR 213.3101.

11.12.2.2. Auxiliary chaplains employed on an intermittent basis have no work schedule. They are paid for religious services performed.

11.12.2.3. Auxiliary chaplains have no entitlement to leave.

11.12.2.4. The employing activity's HRO determines the pay scale for auxiliary chaplains. Social Security, Medicare, and federal and state income tax withholdings are made per the tax documents the chaplain files. These withholdings do not apply to chaplains under non-personal service contracts.

11.12.3. Under 10 U.S.C. § 7437, the President may appoint a chaplain to serve at the United States Military Academy at West Point. The civilian chaplain is entitled to a monthly housing allowance equal to the basic allowance for housing (BAH) allowed a lieutenant colonel and to fuel and light for quarters. Because utility costs are already factored into the BAH rate, no separate allowance for fuel and light is paid. The chaplain's salary is taxable and subject to income, Social Security, and Medicare tax withholding. The BAH is not subject to income tax withholding under 26 U.S.C. § 107, which excludes from a minister's gross income the value of rental allowances received for a home. Social Security and Medicare taxes must be withheld from the
BAH.

11.13    Service Secretaries

11.13.1. Time and attendance is not reported for Service Secretaries. Accrual or use of annual and sick leave is not authorized. Military Department Secretaries are not eligible for premium pay.

11.14    LEOS

11.14.1. Premium Pay

11.14.1.1. The HRO determines the rate of annual premium pay for standby duty and sends it via SF 50 to the servicing PRO. (See Section 5, Table 4-1 for the deductions withheld.) Standby duty pay is generally not used for federal law enforcement employees; for more information, refer to Section 4. Standby duty pay under 5 CFR 550.141 may not be paid to an LEO receiving availability pay. See 5 CFR 550.163.

11.15    Military Sealift Command (MSC)

The pay of officers and crew members of vessels must be fixed and adjusted from time to time as nearly as is consistent with the public interest per prevailing rates and practices in the maritime industry. See 5 U.S.C. § 5348. Hours of work and premium pay for MSC civil service mariners are covered by Department of the Navy Civilian Marine Personnel Instruction 610, Hours of Work and Premium Pay, approved by the Department of the Navy's Office of Civilian Human Resources. Base wage and premium pay scales for MSC civil service mariners are approved by the DoW Wage Setting Authority in coordination with OPM.

11.16    De Facto Employees

11.16.1. Payment of De Facto Employees

11.16.1.1. Payment of de facto employees for services rendered to the government depends on the facts of each individual's situation. The employing agency must make a determination identifying the employee as a de facto employee who acted in good faith and must convey that determination to DFAS. The employing agency must submit a payroll processing request to initiate payment of a de facto employee. An agency de facto determination invalidates any debt established for wages paid.

11.17 Highly Qualified Experts (HQES) and Highly Qualified Experts-Senior Mentors
(HQES-SMS)

11.17.1. Employees hired as HQEs are given "Excepted Not-to-Exceed" appointments (up to 5 years) under an Experts Other pay plan. The HQE or HQE-SM must sign a written service agreement.

11.17.2. HQEs and HQE-SMs are not eligible to receive performance awards.

11.18 Research Positions in the Scientific and Technology Reinvention Laboratories (STRL)

The 2023 NDAA (PL 117-263) authorized the Secretary of War to carry out a program to fix the rate of basic pay, not to exceed 150 percent of Level 1 of the Executive Schedule, for certain research and technology positions in the DoW STRL. These positions are term and temporary appointments not to exceed 5 years. See 10 U.S.C. § 4094 and 87 FR 40200.

title: Section 12.0: Allotments and Voluntary Deductions
content:
12.0    ALLOTMENTS AND VOLUNTARY DEDUCTIONS

12.1    Allotments

12.1.1. Mandatory Allotments

12.1.1.1. An employee may file an SF 1188, Cancellation of Payroll Deductions for Labor Organization Dues, to cancel an allotment. However, any written request signed by the employee that contains sufficient information may be acceptable. Unless the collective bargaining agreement states otherwise, the employing activity must furnish the SF 1188 to employees upon request.

12.1.1.2. If an employee is suspended or expelled from membership in the labor organization, termination of dues is effective the first pay period after the Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) receives written notification from the labor organization that the employee was suspended or expelled.

12.1.1.3. The agency must automatically terminate a labor organization dues allotment when the employee ceases to be a member of the bargaining unit. The employee need not submit a cancellation form or take any other action to terminate the allotment. If the agency does not terminate the allotment in a timely manner, the PRO must refund any erroneously deducted dues, without interest, to the employee. The agency has a claim against the labor organization for the overpayment amount.

12.1.1.4. If the salary is sufficient to cover the deduction, the PRO must deduct the full allotment amount each pay period even if the employee is in a pay status for only part of a pay period. The PRO must make no deduction if the salary is insufficient to cover the full allotment deduction.

12.1.1.5. The PRO must not make retroactive deductions for a period during which the employee's net pay was insufficient to cover the allotment, and must not make adjustments in future pay periods for amounts it failed to deduct during a current pay period.

12.1.1.6. Eligible employees enrolled in a high deductible health plan (HDHP) may establish a Health Savings Account (HSA) with a trustee or custodian and request allotments to fund it. The allotment continues until the employee revokes or modifies the election, and an employee may modify an HSA allotment at any time to effect a prospective change. Employees are responsible for ensuring their enrollment and contributions comply with IRS rules and stay within annual limits set under 26 U.S.C. 223. Payroll providers are not responsible for verifying employee eligibility or confirming that employee contributions are within annual limits.

12.1.2. Discretionary Allotments

12.1.2.1. An employee may elect to contribute voluntarily to the Military Welfare Societies (MWSs) as an authorized charitable campaign. The MWSs include the Army Emergency Relief Society, the Navy-Marine Relief Society, and the Air Force Aid Society. Except for the Combined Federal Campaign (CFC), MWSs must not solicit Federal civilian employees.

12.2    Federal Employees Health Benefits (FEHB)

12.2.1. FEHB Premium Contributions

12.2.1.1. The PRO must not deduct the regular biweekly FEHB premium withholding from an employee's lump-sum leave (LSL) payment. The PRO may collect from the LSL payment any previously established debt resulting from the employee's underpayment or failure to pay premiums.

12.2.1.2. When an employee transfers from one PRO to another without a break in service of more than 3 days, health plan enrollment and coverage continue without change. Each PRO is responsible for FEHB premium withholdings and contributions for the time the employee occupied a position it serviced. If the employee transfers to a different PRO other than on the first day of the pay period, the PRO must prorate the withholdings and contributions using the Daily Proration Rule (see paragraph 3.2.7).

12.2.1.3. If an employee retires and is eligible to continue enrollment as an annuitant, the PRO's responsibility for FEHB premium withholdings and contributions is based on the annuity start date. If the annuity starts after the end of the final pay period, the PRO makes withholdings and contributions for the entire final pay period. If the annuity starts before the end of the final pay period, the PRO makes withholdings and contributions through the day before the annuity start date using the Daily Proration Rule. OPM makes withholdings beginning with the annuity effective date.

12.2.1.4. If an employee dies and there is no survivor annuity, or the employee maintained self-only enrollment, the PRO must make full FEHB premium withholdings and contributions for the pay period in which the employee dies. If a survivor annuitant is eligible to continue enrollment, the PRO must prorate the calculation using the Daily Proration Rule and the employee's date of death.

12.2.1.5. An employee restored to duty retroactively after an erroneous suspension or removal may elect to have enrollment retroactively reinstated or may enroll in the plan and option of choice as a new employee. If the employee elects retroactive reinstatement, the PRO must take premium deductions for the suspension or removal period from the retroactive pay adjustment (back pay award) and must make the government premium contributions as though the suspension or removal had not occurred.

12.2.1.6. If enrollment is terminated or reinstated because of an employee's entry into or return from military service, the PRO must apply the Daily Proration Rule. The effective date of the action is the date the employee entered or returned from military service.

12.2.1.7. During LWOP or insufficient pay, the employee remains responsible for paying the employee's share of the FEHB premium unless the employee terminates enrollment. The PRO must not withhold the employee's share for a pay period when the employee is on LWOP or has pay insufficient to cover the full premium. The PRO must continue to forward the full FEHB premium (government contribution and employee share) to OPM each pay period, must advance salary to cover the employee's share, and the employee incurs a debt for the advance.

12.2.1.8. The payroll system must be capable of identifying all employees on LWOP or with pay insufficient to cover premiums. The PRO must provide written notice to the employee as soon as it becomes aware that premium payments cannot be withheld from the employee's salary. The PRO must provide the notice per the FEHB Handbook and 5 CFR 890.502(b), sent by first-class mail or delivered in person; if mailed, the notice is considered received 5 days after its date. The notice must advise the employee of the following: Options for continuing or terminating enrollment; effect of termination; if the employee decides to continue coverage, the employee must agree to pay the premium directly, incur a debt, or pre-pay premiums; if the employee elects to incur a debt or fails to pay the entire amount due, the employee thereby agrees to repay the debt in full and allow the debt to be collected by salary offset. The notice should indicate that if the debt cannot be collected by salary offset, it will be recovered from a LSL payment, income tax refunds, retirement payments, or any other source available for the recovery of a debt due the government; and if the employee does not complete the election indicating whether the employee chooses to continue or terminate enrollment and return the notice within 31 days after receipt (45 days if the employee lives overseas), enrollment will automatically terminate.

12.2.1.9. If the employee elects to continue coverage, the employee may pay premiums directly to the employing agency while on leave (pay-as-you-go), incur a debt for unpaid premiums while on leave (catch-up), or pre-pay premiums before going on LWOP. The PRO must notify the employee of the available choices (using the notice in paragraph 3.2.6.3) and must provide the employee a method to make direct premium payments. An employee who elects to incur a debt must repay it in full or be subject to debt collection. Pre-paid premiums may be deducted from pay or paid out-of-pocket; out-of-pocket payments are after-tax monies.

12.2.1.10. If the employee does not sign and return the written notice within 31 days of receipt (45 days for overseas employees), the PRO must terminate the enrollment on the SF 2810. The effective date of termination is retroactive to the end of the last pay period in which premiums were withheld from pay.

12.2.1.11. If the employee does not continue to make premium payments during LWOP, the PRO must recover the employee's share of the FEHB premium from the annuity or workers' compensation benefits payment. If the employee's share was paid during LWOP and withholding is also taken from the annuity or workers' compensation benefits for the same period, the PRO must refund the duplicate amounts to the employee. If the disability retirement annuity does not begin on the day after the last day of pay, the PRO must not refund premium payments until it receives an OPM notice that the disability retirement application is approved.

12.2.1.12. A temporary employee enrolled in FEHB must pay both the employee share and the government share of premiums during LWOP. If the employee accepts a temporary position with another employing office, the enrollment must transfer from the original office to the new office. If the employee is still in LWOP when the temporary position at the new office ends, the enrollment must transfer back to the original office. The original office must determine the remaining time the employee may continue FEHB coverage under LWOP and must terminate the enrollment if the original temporary position has expired. Both offices must coordinate so that withholdings and contributions are made timely.

12.2.1.13. The Daily Proration Rule is the formula used to calculate partial employee withholdings and government contributions for FEHB premiums. Unless otherwise provided, the PRO must make the full withholding and contributions for each pay period even if the employee is in pay status for only part of the period. The PRO uses the Daily Proration Rule to compute partial withholdings and contributions under the following circumstances: The employee transfers to a position serviced by a different PRO other than at the beginning of a pay period; The employee retires other than at the end of a pay period and is eligible to continue FEHB enrollment; The employee dies, and there is a survivor annuitant eligible to continue FEHB enrollment; or The employee terminates or reinstates enrollment because of entry into or return from military service.

12.2.1.14. Each PRO (gaining and losing) is responsible for FEHB withholdings and contributions for the actual time the employee occupied a position the PRO serviced. The PRO must compute daily FEHB premium withholding and contribution rates as follows.

12.2.1.15. The PRO must record payments received or payroll deductions withheld in the OPM deposit fund for FEHB withholdings. If the employee separates, the PRO must offset the amount owed against any entitlements due. If the employee retires and final pay does not cover the debt, the PRO must use OPM Form 1522 to offset against a CSRS or FERS annuity and annotate the SF 2806 (CSRS) or SF 3100 (FERS) that the separating employee was indebted. There is no minimum amount subject to offset. The PRO must refund any duplicate payments that are later offset.

12.2.1.16. When an employee with a debt for unpaid FEHB premiums transfers to a different PRO, the PRO must show the date of last withholding and amount due on the SF 1150, Record of Leave Data. The gaining PRO must collect amounts due, pay them to the former employing office, and report them to OPM.

12.2.2. Retroactive Changes and Adjustment of Errors

12.2.2.1. If an employee retroactively changes from self and family to self only, the PRO must make corrective adjustments to refund premiums back to the beginning date of the coverage change the employing agency provided. The Barring Act (statute of limitations) under 31 U.S.C. 3702(b)(1) does not apply to these changes.

12.2.2.2. If the PRO overdeducts the FEHB premium owed by the employee, the PRO must refund the overdeduction to the employee and adjust the government contribution in a subsequent pay period.

12.2.3. Temporary Continuation of Coverage (TCC)

12.2.3.1. Once the HRO establishes TCC eligibility, the HRO must forward the election form to the National Finance Center (NFC), which administers the TCC program for DoW. The NFC notifies eligible individuals, provides benefit information, processes enrollment changes and cancellations, collects premiums, and sends them to OPM.

12.3 Allotments for Federal Flexible Spending Account Program (FSAFEDS)

12.3.1. Allotments for FSAs

12.3.1.1. Allotments withheld from the employee’s pay must be forwarded to BENEFEDS on the same date payroll is paid.

12.3.1.2. Upon the employee’s return to pay status, the PRO must restart the allotment. FSAFEDS recalculates future allotment amounts based on the number of pay dates remaining in the benefit period so the employee reaches the annual election amount.

12.4    Federal Employees Group Life Insurance (FEGLI)

12.4.1. FEGLI Premium Withholdings and Contributions

12.4.1.1. During each pay period in which an insured employee is in pay status for any part of the period, the PRO must withhold the employee’s share of the FEGLI premium from biweekly pay. Premium withholding is subject to the following requirements.

12.4.1.1.1. If the employee dies or separates during a pay period, the PRO bases the withholding on the amount of insurance in force on the date of death or separation.

12.4.1.1.2. If the employee’s BIA changes during the pay period, the PRO bases the withholding amount on the BIA last in force during the pay period.

12.4.1.1.3. If the employee works less than 52 weeks per year, the PRO must convert the biweekly rate to an annual rate, then prorate the annual rate over the number of pay periods in the year to determine the withholding amount.

12.4.1.1.4. The PRO must report FEGLI withholdings and contributions to OPM each pay period as described in Section 10. See 5 CFR 870, subpart D.

12.4.1.2. Withholdings must be made from an employee’s salary when the employee is in pay status for any part of a pay period. If salary is insufficient to permit all payroll deductions, the PRO must use the order of precedence for deductions in Section 5. After all other required deductions are made, if pay is not enough to cover the full life insurance premiums, the amount withheld must first apply to Basic insurance, then any remaining pay must apply to Optional insurance (first Option B, then Option A, then Option C). See 5 CFR 870.404(f).

12.4.1.3. The HRO must review and determine insufficient pay when an employee’s pay, after all other applicable deductions, is expected to be insufficient to cover the premiums for 6 months or more, and must notify the employee. The employee may reduce or cancel other deductions or reduce FEGLI coverage to increase available pay, or may elect to make direct payments to the employing office for periods of insufficient pay. If the employee does not make direct payments, adjust, or cancel coverage, the HRO will terminate coverage as follows:

12.4.1.3.1. The HRO must terminate all coverage if pay is not sufficient for any premium withholding.

12.4.1.3.2. If the employee has pay available to cover part of the premiums, the HRO must administratively terminate as much coverage as necessary to allow premium withholdings in the following order: Multiples of Option C, Option A, Multiples of Option B, then Basic insurance.

12.4.1.4. If the HRO terminated coverage administratively, the HRO must automatically reinstate FEGLI coverage when the employee’s pay becomes sufficient to cover the withholdings. If an employee paid premiums directly, the employing office must start withholding premiums as soon as the pay becomes sufficient.

12.4.1.5. Except as described at subparagraph 6.10.1, the PRO makes no FEGLI premium withholdings from back pay awarded to an employee determined to be erroneously suspended or terminated.

12.4.1.6. No insurance premium is withheld from the LSL payment when the employee separates from Federal service. If the employee has an established debt being collected for underpayment of premiums, the agency may collect the debt from the LSL payment.

12.4.2. PROs must cooperate with the OFEGLI when it requests pre-payment verification. The OFEGLI must obtain verification before paying beneficiaries of enrollees with $200,000 or more of FEGLI coverage, and will request the insured's current salary, annual salary (if different), and Optional insurance enrollment details, if applicable.

12.4.3. Retroactive Changes and Adjustment of Errors

12.4.3.1. If an employee receives a retroactive pay increase delayed beyond its effective date due to administrative error or oversight, and the increase raises life insurance premiums, the PRO must apply the increased premium deductions retroactively.

12.4.3.2. When the PRO erroneously overwithholds premiums from an employee's salary, the PRO must refund the erroneous withholding to the employee the next pay period. This automatically corrects the excess government contribution.

12.4.3.3. When less than the proper amount of FEGLI premiums is withheld from an employee's salary, the underdeduction is an overpayment of regular pay that must be collected as a debt (see Volume 16); collection may be exempt from due-process requirements under 5 CFR 550.1104(c). The agency must submit the uncollected amount due, including government contributions, to OPM within 60 calendar days after the agency discovers the underdeduction, regardless of whether collection from the employee has been made. Government contributions must be adjusted when payment is received from the employee.

12.4.3.4. When the PRO must adjust withholdings for a separated employee, it withholds the adjustment from the final salary payment to the employee (or, if deceased, to the employee's beneficiary or estate).

12.5 Disability Insurance for Employees of the Uniformed Services University of the Health Sciences (USUHS)

Full-time civilian faculty appointed to an Administratively Determined (AD) position of the USUHS School of Medicine receive mandatory long-term disability insurance coverage. To participate, the employee must be covered under the Teachers Insurance and Annuity Association College Retirement Equities Fund (TIAA-CREF) or the Fidelity Investments program. The employer and employee each contribute 50 percent of the premium. USUHS AD employees covered under FERS or CSRS are not eligible for the plan.

12.6 National Guard Association of United States (NGAUS) Insurance Trust (IT) Program

Army and Air National Guard Technicians (Title 32 Technicians) may choose to participate in the NGAUS Insurance Trust (NGAUS-IT), which provides disability and life insurance through its underwriter, ReliaStar Life Insurance Company. Participating Technicians agree on the NGAUS-IT enrollment form to have premiums deducted from their biweekly pay. ReliaStar confirms enrollment approval and notifies the CSRs of deduction start dates, amounts, and any revisions due to age or salary changes; CSRs enter the deduction information into the DCPS. The PRO deducts premiums for the entire pay period regardless of the day of termination, and proration is not required.

12.7    Thrift Savings Plan (TSP)

12.7.1. Correction of Late Contributions

12.7.1.1. The PRO must submit late contributions to TSP as soon as the error is discovered and must show the "as of" date for the contributions. TSP calculates breakage for both employee and agency contributions per 5 C.F.R. 1605.15.

12.7.2. Correction of Employing Agency Errors

12.7.2.1. The PRO must issue written notification to the employee acknowledging that an agency error caused a smaller amount of employee contributions than should have been made. The notification must advise the employee that they may, but are not required to, elect a schedule to make up the deficient contributions through future payroll deductions. The employee has 30 days from receipt of the notification to set up a makeup schedule.

12.7.3. Corrections Following

12.7.3.1. The employee receives the tax benefit in the year the contributions are made. The PRO must annotate retroactive employee contributions by year on the IRS Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement.

12.7.4. Contributions Missed

12.7.4.1. The PRO must deduct USERRA makeup employee contributions from future pay. Employees must meet the conditions in 5 C.F.R. 1620.40. The allowable makeup amount is offset by amounts the employee contributed to TSP while performing military service, and total contributions must not exceed the IRS limit in effect for the year the contribution would have been made.

12.8    Post-56 Military Deposit

12.8.1. General

12.8.1.1. An employee may make a Post-56 Military Deposit in installments or a lump sum. Installments must be in whole dollar amounts of not less than $25 per pay period, except the last payment, which may be any amount to complete repayment. Unpaid balances accrue interest at the rate OPM sets through BALs. The employee must submit payments other than payroll deductions directly to pay.gov or to DFAS-Cleveland, ATTN: J3DCBB/559, 1240 East 9th Street, Cleveland, OH 44199. Payment must be a negotiable instrument payable to "Disbursing Officer." Mailed payments must reach the disbursing officer by the close of business on the last regular business day before the interest accrual date; the date of receipt by the disbursing officer, not the postmark, is the date of payment. The PRO computes interest on the unpaid balance on the employee's interest accrual date.

title: Section 1.0: General
content:
1.0    GENERAL

1.1    Overview

The policies addressed in Volume 9 apply to all personnel traveling under orders funded by the DoW. The scope and provisions in the volume align with the Joint Travel Regulations (JTR) which is the overarching directive for travel and entitlements.

This includes military members, civilian employees, members of the Reserve Components, dependents on official orders, and travelers on DoW invitational travel authorizations. Individual DoW Component travel implementing guidance remains in use to provide direction for travel order preparation, administration and accounting. General policy guidance to official travelers on transportation allowances is also provided.

1.2    Authoritative Guidance

Refer to the authoritative guidance document on the AskDFAS webpage.

1.3    Definitions

Refer to the Glossary of terms document on the AskDFAS webpage.

1.4    Procedures

Refer to the procedures document listed on the AskDFAS webpage.

title: Section 2.0: Volume Information
content:
2.0    VOLUME INFORMATION

The policies addressed in this section apply to all personnel traveling under orders funded by the DoW. This includes military members, civilian employees, members of the Reserve Components, dependents on official orders, and travelers on DoW invitational travel authorizations.

2.1    Additional Guidance

2.1.1. Additional guidance pertinent to the U.S. Air Force and Space Force is in the Department of the Air Force Instruction 24-602, Volume 1, Passenger Movement.

2.1.2. Additional guidance pertinent to the U.S. Navy is available in the Navy Passenger Transportation Manual (OPNAVINST 4650.15C CH-1).

2.1.3. Additional guidance pertinent to the U.S. Marine Corps is in the Marine Corps Assignment, Classification, and Travel System Manual (ACTSMAN).

2.1.4. Additional guidance pertinent to the use of Nonappropriated Funds is in the DoW Instruction 1400.25, Volume 1405.

2.2    Exceptions

The Office of the Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller) (OUSD(C)) is the approving authority for exceptions to policy. Requests for exceptions must include a justification, a recommendation and approval from the appropriate DoW Component command channel at or above the level of the Deputy Chief Financial Officer (DCFO), OUSD(C). Send requests through the appropriate DoW Component to the Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS), Director, Accounting and Finance Policy Division (DFAS-ZPT), 8899 E. 56th Street, Indianapolis, IN, 46249. DFAS-ZPF will review and recommend approval/disapproval to the DCFO, OUSD(C), who will make the final decision.

2.3    Effective Date of JTR Changes

See the information on “EFFECTIVE DATE OF REGULATION CHANGES” in the Introduction to the JTR for explanations of JTR effective dates. The DFAS-ZPT may release policy memorandums affecting Volume 9 that implement PDTATAC determinations, if necessary. These policy memorandums remain in effect until published in a change to Volume 9.

2.4    Responsibilities

The OUSD(C) has ultimate responsibility for the policies contained in Volume 9. The DoW Components may submit requests for changes to DFAS-ZPT. The DFAS-ZPT will review requests and initiate recommended changes to Volume 9 if necessary.

title: Section 3.0: Transportation Allowances
content:
3.0    TRANSPORTATION ALLOWANCES

This section provides general policy guidance to official travelers on transportation allowances.

3.1    Use of Privately Owned Vehicle (POV)

An Authorizing Official (AO) may authorize, but cannot direct a traveler to use a POV in connection with travel on official Government business. This limitation also applies to travel as a passenger in a POV.

3.2    When POV Use is More Advantageous to the Government

POV use on a temporary duty (TDY) assignment is not automatically considered to be advantageous to the government.

3.3    Allowable Travel Time Policy

The standard DoW procedure for administering travel time for all DoW travelers is based on the official distance, the type of transportation authorized, and the transportation used.

3.3.1. Day of Arrival at the TDY Point. When the traveler is required to perform duty at the TDY point on the day of arrival, that day is a day of duty. Travel time is granted prior to that first duty day. When the traveler performs no duty at the TDY point on the day of arrival, that day is a travel day.

3.3.2. Day of Departure From the TDY Point. When a traveler is required to perform duty at the TDY point on the day of departure, that day is a day of duty. Travel time is granted after that last day. When a traveler is not required to perform duty at the TDY point on the day of departure from the TDY point, that day is a travel day.

3.4    First Class Or Business Class Accommodations

It is DoW policy that travelers using commercial air carriers for official travel must use economy or coach accommodations. This does not preclude the traveler from accepting a complimentary seating upgrade offered by the carrier.

3.5    Unused/Lost/Stolen Transportation Requests Or Tickets

If a traveler does not use the ticket (paper or electronic) for Government-procured transportation, the traveler must return that ticket to the TO/TMC. Travelers utilizing electronic tickets for which they do not have an issued boarding pass must return a copy of their itinerary to the TO/TMC. The traveler must complete and have the issuing authority (i.e., TO/TMC) sign an original and one copy of a DD Form 730, Receipt for Unused Transportation Requests and/or Tickets, Including Unused Meal Tickets. The Standard Form (SF) 1170, Redemption of Unused Tickets, may also be used if its use is in accordance with Service regulations. The traveler must attach a copy of the DD Form 730/SF 1170 (or other receipt) to the travel claim. If a traveler loses a paper ticket or transportation request, the traveler must contact the TO/TMC for assistance. A traveler remains financially responsible to the Government for the cost of a lost or stolen paper ticket or transportation request, regardless of fault or negligence. See 31 U.S.C.§ 3711 and Volume 16. If the travel order directs use of Government-procured transportation, do not reimburse the traveler for personally procured transportation unless the AO provides a statement to allow reimbursement. See DoW Instruction 5154.31, Volume 2.

3.6    Involuntarily Relinquished Airline Accommodations

Penalty payments or credits issued by air carriers under certain provisions of their tariffs for failing to furnish accommodations for confirmed reserved space belong to the U.S. Government, and not the traveler. Travelers must request that the transportation carrier show “Treasurer of the United States” as the payee on the compensation check and forward the payment according to Service/DoW Agency directives.

3.7 Reimbursement for the Cost of Damages to Commercial Rental Vehicles

Rental cars covered by the DTMO rental car agreement include full liability and vehicle loss, and damage insurance coverage in the Government rate. Reimbursement or payment to the rental agency for damages must be made by the Government, or by the traveler if it is determined that the traveler was not within the scope of employment when the loss occurred. When Government reimbursement is approved, and extra collision insurance is not purchased or included in the basic rental contract (e.g., in accordance with DTMO negotiated agreements), the traveler may be reimbursed for personal funds paid to the rental agency for the full amount of damage sustained, or the deductible amount (when contained in the rental agreement), for a vehicle properly rented and damaged in the performance of official business.

3.8    Prohibition on Self Approval

Appointed AOs and approving officials may not approve their own vouchers for payment of local travel.

title: Section 4.0: Temporary Duty Travel (TDY) and Travel Advances
content:
4.0    TEMPORARY DUTY TRAVEL (TDY) AND TRAVEL ADVANCES

This section identifies the DoW financial management policies and guidance governing travel administration for travelers performing Temporary Duty (TDY) travel, and for travel advances.

4.1    Responsibilities

Departmental Accountable Officials (DAO) must be appointed and terminated using a DoW (DD) Form 577, Appointment/Termination Record - Authorized Signature.

4.2    Reviewing Officials

The person appointed as a reviewing official may not serve concurrently as a certifying or disbursing officer. Except where impracticable within afloat or tactical operating forces, persons appointed as reviewing officials must not be in the supervisory chain of command of a certifying or disbursing officer.

4.3    Certifying Officers.

Certifying Officers are pecuniarily liable under Title 31 United States Code (U.S.C.),
section 3528 (31 U.S.C. § 3528). Also, see Title 41 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) (41 CFR § 301-71.203) and Volume 5. Responsibilities for individuals appointed as Certifying Officers are applicable to both Defense Travel System (DTS) and non-DTS travel claims.

4.4    Responsibilities of Others Involved in the Travel Process

Government Travel Charge Card (GTCC) Agency Program Coordinators (APCs). APCs implement and execute the GTCC program. See DoW Instruction (DoWI) 5154.31, Volume 4 and the DoW GTCC Regulations for additional information and APC responsibilities.

4.5    Automated Information System (AIS) Administrators.

The AIS administrators operate and maintain systems to support travel management. They support the allowance, certifying, and disbursing systems.

4.6    Suspected False Claims Travelers

Suspected False Claims Travelers are liable under 18 U.S.C. § 287 and 18 U.S.C. § 1001, and the False Claims Act 31 U.S.C. §§ 3729 through 3731, if they knowingly submit false, fictitious, or fraudulent claims. When a suspected fraudulent claim is presented for payment, certifying officers or disbursing officers must follow the policies and procedures outlined in Volume 5.

4.7    Travel Orders

Travel orders are prepared in accordance with DoW Component management guidance and administrative instructions including the JTR, paragraph 010206 for Service members and civilian employees, and the JTR, paragraph 030501 for invitational travel authorizations. The travel order establishes in writing the conditions for official travel and transportation at government expense.

4.8    Funding

4.8.1. All orders, wherever possible, must be funded by the traveler's organization unless group orders or alternative methods are more efficient. If funding is to be provided by another office, the traveler's organization must obtain a fund cite from that office in an amount sufficient to pay for the travel prior to issuing travel orders.

4.8.2. In the event of a split-year funded trip, the traveler must return to his or her official duty station if no DoW Appropriation Act has been signed or continuing resolution has been enacted. Expenses incurred in returning to the traveler's duty station will be posted in the new fiscal year as necessary costs to close down operations.

4.9    Itinerary Variations

Variations Authorized. The authorization of travel variations should not be used in place of adequate advance planning, nor must they be used to grant an open travel authorization. Variations must be authorized in the order and are permitted only when considered mission essential in accordance with Per Diem, Travel, and Transportation Allowance Committee (PDTATAC) Travel Orders.

4.10    Object Classification Accounting

Object Classification Accounting for TDY travel is accomplished through the use of a single object classification code. All TDY orders must be issued using the single object classification code of 21, “Travel and Transportation of Persons.” Temporary exemptions to the mandatory use of the two-digit (21) object classification code to accommodate component-unique accounting requirements may be permitted only with the advance approval of the Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller) or designee.

4.11    Registration Fees

All registration fees incurred while DoW travelers are on TDY travel must be charged to object classification code 21, “Travel and Transportation of Persons.”

4.12    Travel Advances

4.12.1. Policy. Advance payment of travel allowances may be issued to Service members (37 U.S.C. § 452) and civilian employees (5 U.S.C. §§ 5705 and 5724). However, travel advances must not be authorized unless an exemption to GTCC use is granted in accordance with the GTCC Regulations, section 0406. Personnel who are exempted from mandatory use of the GTCC may obtain travel advances only via EFT. See section 5.0 for limitations on advances. The Commander or supervisor, in coordination with the disbursing officer, may authorize cash advances in limited situations where no other process is available to accomplish the mission. See DoWI 5154.31, Volume 4 for additional guidance on the GTCC program. To determine if an individual is exempt from mandatory use of the GTCC, see the GTCC Regulations.

4.12.2. Cadets and midshipmen travel in accordance with the policies of the respective service academy. If a cadet or midshipman requires a travel advance or seeks settlement at a disbursing office.

4.13    Invitational Travel Authorizations

Travel advances may be authorized for travelers using invitational travel authorizations. The amount of the advance must be approved by the order-issuing AO and included on the invitational travel authorization. Limit advances to the authorized amount.

4.14    Travel Advance Limitations

When GTCC use is exempted in accordance with the GTCC Regulations, section 0406, DoW Components must limit travel advances to those estimated expenses that a traveler is expected to incur for authorized travel including travel incident to TDY, permanent duty travel (PDT) or civilian employee temporary change of station (TCS). This limitation applies to all advances. See Procedural Guide for more detailed information on advances.

4.15    Household Goods (HHG) Amount

4.15.1. Civilian Employees. An advance for the cost of HHG transportation must be limited to the cost of shipping the estimated weight of the civilian employee’s HHG within the maximum weight for which a civilian employee is eligible at the applicable rate and distance shown in the commuted rate table. An advance for the cost of temporary storage must be limited to the applicable commuted rate for the weight of HHG and period of storage, not in excess of 90 days and not in excess of the maximum HHG weight for which a civilian employee is eligible.

4.15.2. Service Members. An advance for the cost of HHG transportation is limited to 60 percent of the constructed cost of the personally procured move monetary allowance. See the JTR, subparagraph 051502.G.3.

4.16    Temporary Lodging Amount

4.16.1. Civilian Employees. Advances may be paid for Temporary Quarters Subsistence Expense (TQSE) in 30-day increments for subsistence expenses covered in the JTR, Table 5-84. The initial advance of funds for TQSE must not exceed the maximum amount allowable under the JTR, Table 5-85 for the first authorized period of 30 days or less. Thereafter, advances for subsequent 30-day periods may be paid as authorized by the DoW Component. When an advance is needed for the second and subsequently authorized 30-day periods, DoW Components should advise civilian employees to submit the request for advance in sufficient time to allow for processing, approval, and issuance of the advance. *

4.16.2. Service Members. An advance for the cost of Temporary Lodging Expense (TLE) may be paid for the average number of days that TLE is paid in connection with a PCS. See the JTR, paragraph 050602.

4.17    Dislocation Allowance (DLA)

DLA advance payments may be issued to Service members 30 days prior to travel rather than 10 days prior to travel as directed for other travel advances. All other conditions related to the advance payment and final settlement of travel allowances remain in effect.

4.18    Group or Charter Arrangements.

When payment for transportation under group or charter arrangements cannot be made to a carrier with Government-procured transportation documents, an advance may be paid based on the estimated cost of the transportation to be furnished.

4.19    Requesting an Advance.

4.19.1. Requesting an Advance. Subject to the conditions in subparagraph 4.19.2 an advance must, upon request, be paid to a civilian employee or Service member. The appropriate office must compute the amount paid. An exception to this requirement is authorized when individual travel orders are received via the Department of the Navy certified Automated Travel Order delivery system. An advance is subject to the conditions stated in the following subparagraphs:

4.19.2. Number of Advances Authorized. Ordinarily, only one advance may be paid for a specific purpose under the same travel order. An exception to this rule may be made for civilian employees or Service members on TDY in excess of 45 days aboard Navy ships or civilian employees or Service members on other TDY assignments under an individual travel order in excess of 45 days at a place where there are no facilities available for processing travel vouchers. The total of the amounts advanced during the TDY assignment may not exceed the total amount authorized to be advanced in the traveler’s orders.

4.20    Advance Repayment

4.20.1. General. A civilian employee or Service member who has received an advance must submit a travel claim voucher within 5 working days of the civilian employee’s or Service member’s return after the end of each trip so that settlement of the advance account can be made. The responsible settlement office that accounts for funds against which the advance is charged is responsible for settlement or collection action in accordance with the applicable Component’s accounting or disbursing regulation. The DoW Components must implement internal controls to assure that:

4.20.1.1. Travelers with outstanding travel advances are notified of any delinquencies in filing vouchers and repaying outstanding travel advances, and

4.20.1.2. Outstanding travel advances and unpaid travel vouchers are reviewed and settled prior to an individual’s separation.

4.20.2. Accounting for Advances. Accounting for advances for travel purposes, recovery, and reimbursements must be in accordance with procedures prescribed by the Government Accountability Office (GAO). See the GAO Policy and Procedures Manual for Guidance of Federal Agencies, GAO Title 7, Fiscal Guidance.

4.21    Advances for Service Member Separatees or Retirees

A Service member who is separating or retiring may be paid an advance through EFT incidental to separation/retirement no more than 10 days prior to the Service member and/or dependent(s) actual travel dates. Upon completion of the travel, a Service member who has received an advance must submit the travel claim to the appropriate settlement office.

4.22    Travel Status

4.22.1. General Travel. Status begins when a traveler departs the home or office and ends when the traveler returns to the office or home. See the JTR, paragraph 010203, and Appendix A.

4.22.2. Aircrew. Generally, aircrew travel status begins with take-off from the PDS and ends with landing at the PDS. See the JTR, subparagraph 010203.D.

4.23    Furnished Meals

4.23.1. Complimentary Meals Furnished by a Hotel. When a traveler is furnished a complimentary meal by a commercial lodging establishment for which a charge is not added in the lodging cost, that meal is not a deductible meal. There is no deduction from the M&IE rate regardless of whether the meal is consumed by the traveler. For rules concerning lodgings and meals furnished by Government contract, see the JTR, paragraph 020304. Additional information on what constitutes deductible/non-deductible meals can be found in the JTR, Table 2-18.

4.23.2. Meals Furnished at Conferences. When some but not all meals are included in conference fees, the proportional meal rate applies on each day one or two meals are provided, except on travel days to and from the PDS. Light refreshments, including a continental breakfast, are a deductible meal when served at a mealtime (e.g., breakfast 0600-0800). Light refreshments served during a break (not at a mealtime) are not a deductible meal. See the JTR, subparagraphs 030201.B and 030201.C.

4.24 Government Quarters and Government Dining Facility Availability

Travelers are not required to obtain written non-availability statements before obtaining reimbursement for commercial lodging costs and the local M&IE rate. The availability of Government quarters, contract quarters, and dining facilities must be confirmed when a reservation request is made.

4.25    Temporary Duty (TDY) at an Installation

4.25.1. Military Personnel TDY to an Installation. Service members are required to check for Government quarters availability when TDY to a U.S. installation. Availability or non-availability documentation must be obtained per the JTR, paragraph 020303. Service members should use adequate available Government quarters when TDY to a U.S. installation; however, when adequate Government quarters are available on that U.S. installation and other lodgings are used, lodging reimbursement is limited to Government quarters cost. See the JTR, paragraph 020303.

4.25.2. Civilian Personnel TDY to an Installation. A civilian employee is encouraged, but not required, to use available Government quarters unless traveling to an ILP site. A civilian employee is required to use Government quarters at an ILP site. See the JTR, subparagraph 020303.B.2. If the electronic reservation system cannot reserve Government quarters, then make reservations through Department of Defense Lodging, or by contacting the Government quarters facility directly. In compliance with the requirement to exercise prudence when incurring expenses, civilian employees should exercise the same care in incurring expenses for Government travel that a prudent person would exercise if traveling at personal expense. An AO should request reduced per diem when a per diem rate is more than the amount necessary, based on known lodging or meal cost reductions in effect due to prearrangements, special discounts, or other reasons. The AO must request and authorize reduced per diem before travel occurs. Only a DoW Component head may authorize a reduced per diem rate for a civilian employee, except as otherwise specified in the JTR. See the JTR, paragraphs 010102, 020303, and 020308.
