4.26    Special Status and Per Diem Rates

Reduced or zero per diem rates for a special status, such as field duty, sea duty, hospitalization, rehabilitation, and essential unit dining, take effect at 12:01 a.m. the day after the traveler enters the status and ends at 12:00 a.m. the day preceding the day the traveler leaves that status. See the JTR, paragraph 020315.

4.26.1. Occasional Meals or Lodging. Occasional meals or occasional lodging may be authorized or approved when a traveler must either purchase meals from commercial or nonappropriated funds (NAF) sources, or obtain lodging through commercial, Government, or NAF sources when per diem is not otherwise authorized. See the JTR, paragraph 020305.

4.26.2. Travel Orders. Travel orders must identify the reduced per diem rates, availability or non-availability of Government quarters, authorization for Government or proportional meal rate as applicable, identification of special status, and reference to the letter or message in which they were established.

4.27    Consecutive TDY

4.27.1. Per Diem. Per diem is payable for the interval between two periods of TDY if the interval exists through no fault of the traveler and the traveler either remains at the first TDY location or travels to the next TDY location within the allowable travel time.

4.27.2. Authorized Delay En Route. A traveler may receive per diem if awaiting transportation at an authorized delay point between TDY locations. To attain savings to the Government, combine what would have been two separate TDY trips into one longer trip and provide for AD at an intermediate location. Per diem is payable for the interval between the two periods of TDY. The amount of per diem paid is based on the location of the AD.

4.28 Leave, Permissive TDY, or Administrative Absence In Conjunction with Funded TDY

4.28.1. Permissive/Administrative Travel Time. A traveler who takes leave, permissive travel, or an administrative absence before or after a funded TDY is entitled to travel allowances from the PDS to the funded TDY location and return to PDS. If the traveler takes leave, permissive travel, or an administrative absence between two TDY locations, the traveler is entitled to allowances for direct travel between the two TDY locations.

4.28.2. Travel Time When Using a POV. Permissive or administrative travel time is authorized when a traveler is authorized to travel by POV for personal convenience on funded TDY and reimbursement is based on a constructive schedule. Compute the allowable travel time based on the provisions of the JTR, paragraph 020302. Permissive or administrative travel time is not authorized when the orders direct a mode of transportation and that mode is available but not used. Per diem is not authorized for the additional period.

4.29    Return to the PDS During TDY

Authorized Return When a travel order authorizes return to the PDS, the traveler is authorized travel, transportation allowances, and per diem for travel from the TDY site to the PDS and return to the TDY site.

title: Section 5.0: Permanent Duty Travel (PDT)
content:
5.0    PERMANENT DUTY TRAVEL (PDT)

This section provides general policy for the preparation, submission, and processing of permanent duty travel (PDT) claims for travelers. There are a number of PDT benefits or allowances that DoW members and civilian employees may be authorized when traveling from one Permanent Duty Station to another at the direction of the Service or agency for which they are working.

5.1    Defense Travel System (DTS)

The DTS does not currently support PDT, and should not be used by DoW travelers for arranging travel or settling claims involving PDT.

5.2    Personally-Procured Move (PPM) Monetary Allowance

A Service member or a deceased member’s next of kin may elect to personally-procure HHG transportation and be paid a monetary allowance of 100 percent of the Government’s “Best Value” cost for the actual HHG weight transported up to the maximum authorized weight allowance. The member must have orders authorizing PDT, temporary duty (TDY) with HHG allowances, or a short distance HHG move in accordance with the JTR, section 0519. The TO will provide the member with a DoW (DD) Form 2278, Application for Personally Procured Move (PPM) and Counseling Checklist. This form shows the Government Constructed Cost (GCC) or contract cost for moving the HHG, based on a weight estimate provided by the traveler. A Service member, or next of kin who personally arranges for HHG transportation without going through a Government transportation office is responsible for all issues and costs related to circumstances outlined in the JTR, subparagraph 051502.A.

5.3 Actual Expense Reimbursement for Personally-Procured Shipment or Storage of HHG

5.3.1. Supporting Documents.

5.3.1.1. Receipts for expenses of $75 or more

5.3.2. Payment. If the claim is proper and supported by the appropriate documentation, the disbursing office must pay the claim.

5.4    Dislocation Allowance

DLA is paid to members as specified in the JTR, section 0505. If a change of grade occurs between the issue date of orders and the effective date of orders, a copy of the promotion/demotion orders may be submitted with the claim versus an amended order.

5.5    Effect of Assignment to Quarters

A member without dependents, who is above the pay grade of E-5, may receive DLA if the member elects not to occupy assigned quarters of the United States or a housing facility under the jurisdiction of a uniformed service, and the quarters or facility do not meet the minimum adequacy standards established by the Secretary of Defense for members in such grade. Do not advance or pay DLA to a member under these circumstances without a statement from the gaining organization that assigned quarters do not meet the minimum adequacy standards. See the JTR, subparagraph 050505.B.

5.6    DLA Advance Payments

DLA advance payments may be issued 30 days prior to travel rather than 10 days prior to travel as directed for most other travel advances in Chapter 5. All other conditions related to the advance payment and final settlement of travel allowances as outlined in Chapter 5 remain in effect. Components may alternatively opt to authorize use of the Government Travel Charge Card (GTCC) for DLA expenses in accordance with the DoW GTCC Regulations, paragraph 040505.

5.7    Civilian Temporary Quarters Subsistence Expense (TQSE)

A DoW employee's PDT orders must authorize the initial TQSE period and specify whether the Lodgings Plus (LP) method or the Lump Sum (LS) method is authorized. Additional periods of TQSE (LP) require amended orders. The employee must provide a statement in advance selecting TQSE (LS), which certifies that TQSE expenses will be incurred. The disbursing office does not determine the number of TQSE days authorized. Receipts are required for all TQSE (LP) lodging expenses as specified in the JTR, Chapter 5, subparagraph 054206.C. Advances and payments for TQSE are based on the provisions of the JTR, Chapter 5, paragraph 054206.G.

5.8    Home Marketing Incentive Payment (HMIP)

The document submitted for payment of HMIP may be a locally-developed form used as an attachment to the travel settlement claim, DD Form 1351-2. The form, at a minimum, must contain the following information:

5.8.1. Employee’s name (last, first, middle initial);

5.8.2. Employee’s Social Security Number;

5.8.3. Employee’s present position, title, grade;

5.8.4. Employee’s current organization;

5.8.5. Employee’s current duty phone;

5.8.6. Computation of HMIP to include the final payment amount (the relocation services company must complete the amended sale transaction and submit the employee’s real estate invoice for payment before the computation can be completed);

5.8.7. Traveler’s signature; and

5.8.8. Order approving official’s signature.

5.9    HMIP Income Tax Considerations

HMIP is considered income, and a W-2 must be processed showing the taxes withheld and the employee income. No authority exists to pay either a withholding tax allowance (WTA), or a relocation income tax allowance (RITA) to offset the Federal, state, and local income taxes on the incentive payment. Payment offices must obtain an approved document (as described in paragraph 10.2) with a DD Form 1351-2 and a valid copy of PDT orders for payment.

5.10 Payment of Travel Vouchers Involving OCONUS Permanent Duty Assignment for DOW Civilian Employees

Proceeding To, or Round Trip Travel From, a PDS OCONUS. Reimbursement vouchers for travel to a PDS OCONUS under an original agreement, or for round trip travel from a PDS OCONUS under a renewal agreement, must be prepared upon completion of the travel and submitted to the travel computation office servicing the OCONUS station for payment.

5.11    Transfer From PDS OCONUS

When employees transfer from OCONUS duty stations, they must submit reimbursement vouchers to the travel computation office that supports the new duty station.

5.12 Returning From OCONUS Employment for Separation From the Service

5.12.1. General. Prior to departure from an OCONUS duty station, an employee who is being returned for separation for any reason must be furnished written instructions by the releasing activity on the following:

5.12.1.1. How to record trip itinerary,

5.12.1.2. Which travel expenses are reimbursable,

5.12.1.3. How to keep a record of these items, and

5.12.1.4. How to complete and sign documents that are to be forwarded for the purpose of finalizing pay and reimbursement of travel claims.

NOTE: Except as provided in subparagraph 11.3.2, the OCONUS releasing activity, in conjunction with the servicing travel computation office, must process final pay and settlement of travel claims for employees who are returned for separation.

5.12.2. Navy Employees. Travel claims of the following Navy employees must be submitted to the office that supports the location to which the employee returns:

5.12.2.1. Employees who are returned from OCONUS for separation under overseas agreements or for purposes of retirement, and

5.12.2.2. Foreign nationals who are returned to their places of residence in foreign countries for separation under employment agreements or for purposes of retirement.

5.12.3. Allowance Determination. The appropriate finance office must determine an employee’s travel, transportation, and relocation allowances. The allowance determination must occur prior to processing the employee’s separation. Travel, transportation, and relocation allowances previously furnished and/or to be furnished are computed by the activity where the violation occurred.

5.12.4. Statement of Liability or Credit. For each transportation agreement violation, the finance office must provide the employee with a statement of the employee’s liability or credit that indicates in detail the liabilities, obligations, and credits (and an explanation of how the credits are used or applied). A copy is sent to the civilian personnel officer for inclusion in the employee’s personnel folder. The employee must also be informed of the right to file a claim if he or she disagrees with the statement of liability or credit.

5.12.5. Collection. If the finance office determines that an employee is indebted to the Government, the office must immediately initiate collection action.

title: Section 6.0: Evacuation Allowances
content:
6.0    EVACUATION ALLOWANCES

This section provides general financial policy for evacuated military/uniformed member dependents and civilian employees and/or their dependents.

6.1    Orders

Copies of the departure orders support evacuation advances and payments. If departure orders are not available, refer evacuees to the local personnel organization. The Defense Travel System does not support evacuation travel. For more information see the Defense Travel Management Office’s “Who may use the Defense Travel System” document.

6.2    Evacuation From Foreign Locations

6.2.1. Military Member Dependents. The JTR, Chapter 6, sections 0602 and 0603 cover allowances for the dependents of Service members authorized or ordered to evacuate from locations outside the continental United States. Uniformed members are not evacuated; however, they may be issued orders for temporary duty (TDY) travel as required.

6.2.2. DoW Civilian Employees and/or Families. Title 5, United States Code (U.S.C),
section 5725 (5 U.S.C. § 5725) provides authority for transportation at the Government’s expense for an employee’s dependents and household goods to a safe haven location when an evacuation is authorized or ordered. The JTR, Chapter 6, section 0604 addresses regulations governing evacuations from foreign areas. Title 5 U.S.C. § 5522 provides authority for advance pay, allowances, and differentials when an employee and/or their dependents are authorized or ordered to evacuate the employee’s permanent duty station. The DSSR, section 600, “Payments During An Ordered/Authorized Departure” relates to the evacuation of civilian employees of the United States and their dependents from or within any foreign area.

6.3 Evacuations From United States and Non-Foreign Outside the Continental United States (OCONUS) Locations

6.3.1. Military Member Dependents. The JTR, Chapter 6, sections 0602 and 0603 cover allowances for the dependents of Service members authorized or ordered to evacuate from locations within the United States. Uniformed members are not evacuated; however, they may be issued orders for TDY travel as required.

6.3.2. DoW Civilian Employees and/or Families. Evacuations within the United States and non-foreign OCONUS locations (including evacuations during a pandemic health crisis) are administered under authority cited in 5 CFR 550.401 through 550.409.

6.4    Finance Office Guidance

The finance office that supports the evacuation point or safe haven area must assist any evacuated traveler with all financial matters.

6.5    Claims

6.5.1. Claims Preparation. All claims for payment of evacuation allowances should be submitted to the appropriate supporting DoW component. The supporting finance office must assist evacuees with claim preparation.

6.5.2. Payment Method. Initial evacuation advance payments are usually mass evacuation payments. Finance offices are encouraged to use DoW (DD) Form 1351-6, Multiple Payments List, as a supplement to DD Form 1351-2, Travel Voucher or Subvoucher, to expedite payments. However, this alternative payment method does not lessen the need for proper documentation. Payments to dependents must be made only upon presentation of a valid travel order issued by a competent authority.

title: Section 7.0: Processing Travel Claims
content:
7.0    PROCESSING TRAVEL CLAIMS

This section provides general policy to travelers for the preparation, submission, and processing of travel claims for electronic submission through the DTS and for PDT and Temporary Duty Travel forms for hard-copy submission.

7.1    Payment Method

Electronic funds transfer is the mandatory travel-claim settlement method within DoW. Split disbursement -- direct EFT payment to the Government Travel Charge Card (GTCC) contractor for GTCC charges and to the cardholder for any residual amount -- is also mandatory. Supervisors may authorize an alternative payment method in limited cases where the traveler lacks access to a financial institution capable of receiving EFT transmissions.

7.2    Adjustments of $10 or Less

The Disbursing Officer (DO) must pay the traveler all amounts due on the original settlement claim. The DO is not required to collect amounts of $10 or less on final settlement or on an overpayment of $10 or less subsequently detected. The DO must process supplemental payments of $10 or less only when specifically requested by the traveler.

7.3    Over Advances

If upon a travel-claim settlement the DO determines that a traveler received an excessive advance and the excess is greater than $10, the DO must issue a letter of indebtedness and provide the traveler an opportunity to repay the excess immediately. If immediate payment is not made, the DO must initiate collection action per DoW FMR Volume 16.

7.4    Overpayments

If the DO detects an overpayment greater than $10, the DO must issue a letter of indebtedness requesting remittance. The traveler must pay the indebtedness within 30 calendar days of the notification date; otherwise, the DO must initiate collection action per DoW FMR Volume 16.

7.5    Income Taxation of Reimbursable TDY Allowances

When a civilian employee performs a TDY assignment at one location for more than a year, the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) considers the duty station to be permanent, and any reimbursement (e.g., per diem) is considered taxable income (see Title 26, United States Code (U.S.C), section 162(a) and Internal Revenue Ruling 99-7). The IRS may consider a TDY assignment at one location for less than a year to be permanent, depending upon the specific circumstances. Travel Authorizing Officials must determine, IAW the JTR, paragraph 010206, that the assignment is not a Temporary Change of Station (TCS) or a Permanent Change of Station (PCS) move before authorizing a long-term TDY assignment away from the permanent duty station (PDS) for more than 180 days. When TDY reimbursements are taxable income, the travel office must compute all applicable tax withholdings, deduct them from the traveler’s claim(s), and issue an IRS Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement, to the traveler. The IRS Form W-2 must include income and the tax withholding amounts. Civilian employees who perform long-term TDY assignments for which TDY allowances are taxable are also authorized an Extended TDY Tax Reimbursement Allowance (ETTRA) IAW the FTR, Part 301-11, Subpart F. At a minimum, travelers will submit a DoW (DD) Form 1351-2, Travel Voucher or Subvoucher, a copy of their travel orders, and the IRS Form W-2 issued from the travel settlement office to claim the ETTRA. NOTE: The traveler must submit travel claims involving taxable TDY allowances on a DD 1351-2 to the appropriate travel settlement office. DTS does not compute claims involving income taxes; do not use DTS in these instances.

7.6    Claim Preparation

7.6.1. Completion. The traveler is responsible for preparing their DD 1351-2 to claim reimbursement for official travel. Even when another party prepares the claim, the traveler retains responsibility for the truth and accuracy of all information. When the traveler or a legally appointed designee signs the form, the traveler attests that all statements are true and complete and acknowledges liability for filing a false claim. All claims and attached statements must be completed in ink, by typewriter, or by computer-generated form.

7.6.2. Reimbursements for Other Traveler’s Expenses. Reimbursement to travelers for expenses incurred by other travelers is prohibited. Travelers are reimbursed only for expenses they themselves incur. Approving Officials, Authorizing Officials, and Certifying Officers must deny all travel claims that include expenses of other personnel. Approving such a claim subjects the approving official to potential pecuniary liability (see Chapter 5, paragraphs 2.1 and 2.2).

7.6.3. Statements for Common Carrier Reimbursement. When a traveler claims reimbursement for common carrier transportation paid in cash, the traveler must include the following statement on the claim: "I hereby assign to the United States any rights I may have against other parties in consideration with any reimbursable carrier transportation charges described herein."

7.7    Other Instructions

The traveler must attach all lodging receipts regardless of amount and receipts for all other expenses of $75 or more to the claim. If a receipt is impracticable to obtain or has been inadvertently lost or destroyed, the traveler must provide a written statement explaining the circumstances.

7.8    Authorizing Official Responsibilities

7.8.1. The AO must confirm authorized travel and ensure the following before reviewing and signing a travel claim:

7.8.2. Approving Items. Before approving an item involving a transportation mode not authorized in a travel order, the AO must require the traveler to explain the necessity for that mode on the claim. When a traveler claims a POV expense under orders authorizing travel by common carrier or Government vehicle and the travel-approving official does not determine that POV use is in the Government's best interest, reimbursement is limited per JTR paragraphs 020210 and 020302. An AO may also approve:

7.8.3. Items Requiring Advance Authorization. The following items require advance authorization and may not be approved after the fact on the travel claim:

7.8.3.1. Use of reduced fares for group or charter arrangements,

7.8.3.2. Payment of a reduced per diem rate for subsistence expenses,

7.8.3.3. Acceptance of payment from a nonfederal source for travel expenses, and

7.8.3.4. Travel expenses related to attendance at a conference.

7.9    Review

7.9.1. The traveler must submit original lodging receipts regardless of amount.

7.9.2. The traveler must submit receipts for all single expense items of $75 or more.

7.10    Submission of Travel Claims

Travelers must submit all TDY and PDT travel claims within five working days of return to, or arrival at, the PDS. For extended TDY over 45 days, and for reservists on Annual Training, Active Duty Training, or Inactive Duty Training known to exceed 45 days, travelers must submit a claim for each 30-day period within five working days after that period ends.

7.11    Travel and Transportation for Funeral Honors Detail

Funeral honors duty travel allowances may be authorized for Reserve Component (RC) military members and individuals not employed by the Government per the JTR. Claims for the Funeral Honors Duty Allowance $50.00 stipend authorized in Volume 7A, Chapter 58, and Volume 7B, Chapter 22, are not travel allowances and must be submitted to and paid through the appropriate Military Pay office.

7.12    Separated or Retired Members

7.12.1. A separated or retired member who has not received an advance must forward the claim to the disbursing office responsible for that person's pay accounts before separation or retirement. The DO must pay all claims submitted within one year of separation or retirement. The disbursing office supporting U.S. Marine Corps separatees or retirees must pay all claims submitted within 60 days of the month of separation or retirement. Claims received after these filing periods must be forwarded to the applicable Service address:

Army: Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS), ATTN: Travel Pay, MilPCS, 325 Brooks Road, Rome, NY 13441-4501

Navy: Travel Processing Center at the separatee's or retiree's separation point

Air Force: Member's last servicing Financial Services Office (FSO)

Marine Corps: Member's last servicing Finance/Disbursing Office (FO/DO)

7.12.1.1. Officers. Travel allowances payable to a separating or retiring officer must be applied to offset any indebtedness to the Government when paid as an advance or settlement.

7.12.1.2. Enlisted Personnel. Travel allowances payable in advance to separating or retiring enlisted personnel for personal travel home may not be applied to offset any debts to the Government. Travel allowances payable to enlisted members after they have returned home must be withheld and applied against their debts.

7.12.1.3. Dependents and Household Goods Claims. Advances and settlements of dependent travel allowances and household goods allowances must be withheld and applied to indebtedness to the Government.

7.13    Deceased and Next of Kin

7.13.1. Attendance at a Deceased Member’s Memorial Ceremony

7.13.1.1 Claims. ITAs must be issued to eligible family members attending a memorial service. The traveler must complete this trip within 2 years following the member's death, unless the Service Secretary waives the time limitation.

7.13.2. Unsettled Claims for Deceased Travelers. The individual designated by the Service to settle a deceased member's affairs is responsible for preparing the travel claim for the deceased member's travel. The finance official computes and forwards all claims to the supporting DFAS/Service site (see paragraph 6.6.4 for address) for payment or collection. For deceased civilian employees, the surviving spouse, legal representative, executor, or administrator must sign any outstanding travel claims; the travel office computes these claims locally. Travel settlements for GTCC holders are subject to split disbursement per 10 U.S.C. § 2784(a) and the DoW GTCC Regulation. Following payment to the GTCC issuer, any remaining expense reimbursement must be forwarded to the member's or civilian employee's pay activity for inclusion in the death claim payment. All reimbursements for non-card holders must likewise be forwarded to the appropriate pay activity for inclusion in the death claim payment.

7.13.3. Claims for Dependents of Deceased Members. If classification of a TDY order is necessary, the order must be classified, marked, and handled per the applicable DoW Component security regulation.

7.14    Travel Under Classified Orders

If classification of a TDY order is necessary, classify, mark, and handle the special order according to the applicable DoW Component security regulation.

7.14.1. Voucher Support. Distribute classified orders only to persons with the proper clearance who require a copy of the order. An unclassified extract from a classified order may support the payment voucher if it provides sufficient information, permitting an unclassified travel claim. For classified locations, the traveler must indicate each location in the travel claim itinerary as site 1, site 2, and so forth. The DO must pay the claim when the per diem rate can be applied. If the disbursing official does not have knowledge of the location, or the traveler declines to show the location, the DO must process the travel claim and documentation per Service instructions.

7.15    Navy Oceanographic Office

The disbursing office of the ship must pay travel claims of civilian employees of the Navy Oceanographic Office for travel aboard survey ships when presented before completion of travel. The disbursing office of the traveler's duty station must pay travel claims filed after return to the traveler's duty station.

7.16    U.S. Coast Guard

7.16.1. Coast Guard members who travel on orders citing DoW appropriations must file travel claims using the same procedures as active-duty DoW members at the disbursing office of the unit whose funds are cited. Disbursing offices must settle these vouchers on the same basis as those of any other member. If excess travel time is involved, forward a copy of the settlement voucher to:

Commanding Officer (TVL) U.S. Coast Guard Pay and Personnel Center 444 SE Quincy Street Topeka, KS 66683-3591

7.16.2. U.S. Coast Guard Travel on Other Than DoW Appropriations When a Coast Guard member requests a travel advance or settlement payment on orders citing a non-DoW appropriation, the disbursing officer may provide payment and seek reimbursement from:

Commanding Officer U.S. Coast Guard Finance Center 1430A Kristina Way Chesapeake, VA 23326-1000

7.17 Travel and Living Allowance (T&LA) for International Military Students and Guest Instructors.

International Military Students and Guest Instructors paid Travel and Living Allowance (T&LA) as defined in DSCA Manual 5105.38-M (Security Assistance Management Manual), Chapter 10, must submit travel claims along with copies of their travel orders/authorization and required receipts to the appropriate travel settlement office per DSCA Manual, Chapter 10, Section
C10.13.

7.18 Advance Decision, Doubtful Claims and Reclaim or Reconsideration Requests

7.18.1. Request for Advance Decision

A DoW (DO) or certifying officer may request an advance decision on any questionable claim presented for payment. Accountable officials and others with final adjudication responsibility may also request an advance decision on doubtful claims (those involving doubtful questions of law or fact) before a claim is prepared or presented. The request must be prepared and submitted per Volume 5. Submit the original request package and two copies to the DFAS Indianapolis office through the supporting DFAS site for the DoW Component funding the travel order. An accountable officer seeking an advance decision on a JTR interpretation issue must forward the request through the Per Diem Travel and Transportation Allowances Committee. Forward requests to the applicable address:

Army, Marine Corps, Navy, and all Defense Agencies:

DFAS-IN/JJFKCE, (ESS Travel Pay 8899 East 56th Street, Indianapolis, IN 46249

Air Force: Member's last servicing Financial Services Office (FSO)

7.18.1.1. Amounts Over $250. The supporting DFAS site must review each advance decision request and contact the DO to resolve any questions. Requests for amounts over $250 require advance decisions by the Defense Office of Hearings and Appeals (DOHA) for Service members and the Civilian Board of Contract Appeals (CBCA) for DoW civilian employees. All requests for advance decisions must be forwarded through the General Counsel of the requesting Component or DFAS to the General Counsel, DoW, before referral to any authorized official outside DoW (see Volume 5, Chapter 12, Section 3.0).

7.18.1.2. Amounts Under $250. If the advance decision request is for $250 or less, the General Counsel, DoW, may refer the request to the General Counsel, DFAS. The General Counsel, DFAS, must review the request and issue an advance decision per DoWI 1340.21, Enclosure 8, paragraph E8.5.3.

7.19    Reconsideration Requests and Reclaims

When the travel office makes an allowance determination that the traveler disagrees with, the travel office must issue the traveler a written explanation and advise the traveler of the right to have the claim reconsidered. If the traveler does not accept the explanation, the DO must assist with resubmission of the claim. To have a claim reconsidered (see exceptions in paragraph 8.4), submit:

7.19.1. Submit a letter of position from the travel computation office, through the major Command, to the appropriate DFAS site. The DFAS site must respond to the DO or traveler. If the traveler does not accept the decision, the DFAS site may forward the claim as a reclaim or appeal to DOHA or the CBCA. A reclaim or appeal is forwarded because the claimant is unwilling to accept the decision, not because the travel office or accountable official has doubts about whether the claim should be paid. The travel office or accountable official must forward such claims through the appropriate DFAS site to DOHA for Service members and to CBCA for DoW civilian employees at the following addresses:

Defense Office of Hearings and Appeals (DOHA), Claims Division PO Box 3656 Arlington, VA 22203-1995

Civilian Board of Contract Appeals (CBCA) ATTN: Clerk of the Board 1800 F Street, NW Washington, DC 20405

7.20    Waivers

Travelers or Components must submit waiver requests for erroneous travel payments and transportation allowances to the DFAS Indianapolis site. See Volume 16, Chapter 4, for waiver processing procedures.

7.21    Unions and Third-Party Review
When a traveler's claim is covered by a collective bargaining agreement, neither the Department, the Office of Personnel Management, the CBCA, nor DOHA has jurisdiction over the claim unless the collective bargaining agreement explicitly excludes travel claims from its grievance procedure.

7.22    Claim for Late Payment Fee

7.22.1. Submission of Travel Claim. Travelers must submit a properly prepared travel claim to their supervisor/approving official within five working days after completion of travel. The disbursing office must pay the travel claim within 30 calendar days after the claim is signed and dated as received by the supervisor/approving official. The supervisor/approving official or the travel computation office has seven calendar days to notify the traveler if the travel claim is not proper or complete for payment.

7.22.2. Late Payment Fee and Charges. If the disbursing office does not pay a travel claim within 30 calendar days after the approving office receives it, that office may be required to pay a late payment fee. The fee accrues at the Prompt Payment Act interest rate beginning on the 31st day after the submission of a proper travel claim and ending on the date the Government disburses payment. No fee is required for amounts less than $1.00. Interest payment funding instructions are in Volume 10, Chapter 7, paragraph 2.9. The Government must also pay the traveler an amount equal to any late payment charge the card contractor would have been able to charge had the traveler not paid the bill. The IRS has determined that the late payment fee is reportable as interest and that the equivalent of the late payment charge is reportable as additional wages. Travelers must also be reimbursed for late fees imposed by the bank when the Government's untimely processing caused the nonpayment; the bank does not assess late fees until 75 days following the billing statement.

7.22.3. Claims for Late Payment Fees. Late payment fees must be calculated and paid at the time the travel claim is processed. Travelers who believe late payment fees were not included in their travel claim calculation may submit supplemental travel claims for late payment fees. Claimants must submit each supplemental claim through the office where the claim is reviewed and approved. That office must annotate the claim with the date of receipt of the original travel claim.

7.22.4. Receipt of Travel Claim for Late Payment Fee. Upon receipt of a travel claim for a late payment fee, the travel computation office must review the claim and calculate the number of elapsed calendar days beginning with the supervisor/approving official's signature and date of receipt and ending with the date the claim was paid. The date the supervisor/approving official receives the proper travel claim counts as day 1; the payment date counts as the last day. If the elapsed days exceed 30 calendar days, the travel computation office must multiply the amount paid on the delayed travel claim by the daily Prompt Payment Act interest rate by the number of days in excess of 30. The disbursing office must pay the traveler by EFT, or by check if the previous payment was by check. The disbursing office must use the same accounting classification as the original travel claim for the supplemental claim amount. When required, the disbursing office must prepare IRS Form 1099-INT (Interest Income) for the traveler per IRS regulations.

7.22.5. Travel Claim Forwarded to Another Activity. When a travel claim requires review by another activity, the 30-day clock continues to run. If the travel computation office disallows a claim, the claimant earns no late payment fee. If the travel computation office allows part of the claim, that portion is subject to the late payment fee and earns interest from the original submission date. Claims returned to the traveler for errors or because the claim is incomplete do not earn interest. The 30-day clock begins when a corrected claim is submitted to the supervisor/approving official.

title: Section 1.0: General
content:
1.0    GENERAL

1.1    Purpose

Volume 10 establishes the financial management policy for the entitlement, computation, certification, and disbursement of payments to vendors, contractors, and other payees under Department of War contracts and related instruments. It states the binding policy only; procedures, implementation guidance, definitions, and data tables reside in the companion documents identified below.

1.2    Authoritative Guidance

Please refer to the authoritative guidance document on the FMR webpage.

1.3    Definitions

Please refer to the Glossary of terms document on the FMR webpage.

1.4    Procedures

Please refer to the Volume 10 Supplemental document listed throughout this volume.

title: Section 2.0: Financial Control of Vendor and Contract Payments
content:
2.0    FINANCIAL CONTROL OF VENDOR AND CONTRACT PAYMENTS

2.1    GENERAL

2.1.1. DoW officials must ensure DoW organizations maintain control of payments to vendors and contractors. Internal control and limitation requirements ensure payments are based on the terms and conditions in accepted purchase orders, contracts, and unilateral and bilateral modifications.

2.2    INTERNAL CONTROLS

2.2.1. Per the Federal Managers’ Financial Integrity Act (FMFIA), the DoW Component Head must establish controls that reasonably ensure obligations and costs comply with applicable law; that funds, property, and other assets are safeguarded against waste, loss, unauthorized use, or misappropriation; and that revenues and expenditures are properly recorded to permit reliable financial reporting and accountability over assets.

2.2.2. Financial managers must develop detailed policies, procedures, and practices for contract and vendor pay entitlement operations and ensure they remain a continuous, integral part of ongoing operations, consistent with the Government Accounting Office (GAO) Standards for Internal Control in the Federal Government and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular A-123, Appendix D.

2.2.3. DoW must make timely and accurate payments and collections per applicable laws and regulations, including requirements to identify, report, and reduce improper payments. Financial managers responsible for internal controls must:

2.2.3.1. Create, document, and maintain an organizational structure and business processes that appropriately segregate assigned duties, emphasize adherence to policies and procedures, and use sound internal accounting and system access controls.

2.2.3.2. Implement finance and accounting systems that comply with the federal financial management systems requirements, maintain accurate and complete accounting and entitlement records from contract execution through closeout, and monitor the causes of late payments and interest penalties. Subject any effort to develop or modify a critical financial management system to the compliance process.

2.2.3.3. Establish systematic controls that provide adequate audit trails to trace financial events from source documents to general ledger account balances through successive levels of summarization and financial reports and statements. Ensure all transactional data is accurately coded and errors are researched and corrected.

2.2.3.4. Use electronic processes and digital signatures, as prescribed by OMB Circular A-130, Appendix II, whenever possible and in the best interest of the Government.

2.2.3.5. Use systems that ensure the authenticity of electronically transmitted data, including the electronic signature. These controls must provide reasonable assurance that deliberate or inadvertent manipulation, modification, or loss of data during transmission is detected.

2.2.3.6. Ensure prevalidation and payment documentation to vendors and contractors is retained per Volume 1 and readily available to support future audits. Retain original payment documentation and associated supporting documentation per Section 8.0. The documentation must be of sufficient quality to let an independent third party understand and verify the basis of the prevalidation and the payments. Electronic record storage requires adequate controls to ensure digital images accurately represent the corresponding paper documentation and to detect changes to an original digital image. The certifying officer must retain documentation, both paper and electronic.

2.2.3.7. Implement finance and accounting data structures that comply with the Standard Financial Information Structure (SFIS) and the Standard Line of Accounting (SLOA).

2.2.4. Managers responsible for determining entitlements, authorizing, or executing payments and collections must:

2.2.4.1. Periodically (minimum annually) validate cash management and payment performance quality and effectiveness.

2.2.4.2. Periodically (minimum annually) test the effectiveness of internal controls, document the results, and take necessary corrective actions.

2.3    PREVALIDATION

2.3.1. General Prevalidation

2.3.1.1. Before payment, the undisbursed balance of each applicable obligation must be sufficient to cover the planned disbursement and all previously scheduled disbursements.

2.3.1.2. Prevalidation must validate the line of accounting on the planned disbursement against that on the obligating document before the financing or invoice payment is made.

2.3.2. The following prevalidation thresholds apply to Non-Mechanization of Contract Administration Services (non-MOCAS) and MOCAS payments.

2.3.2.1. All non-MOCAS payments must be prevalidated.

2.3.2.2. The following prevalidation thresholds must be used for MOCAS payments:

2.3.2.2.1. All dollar value payments on contracts awarded after fiscal year (FY) 2004 must be prevalidated.

2.3.2.2.2. For contracts issued during FY 2004 and prior, payments greater than $5,000 must be prevalidated.

title: Section 3.0: Discount Offers and Rebates/Refunds
content:
3.0    DISCOUNT OFFERS AND REBATES/REFUNDS

3.1    POLICY

3.1.1. Discounts

3.1.1.1. Per 5 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 1315.7(a), when a vendor offers a DoW Component a discount, whether stipulated in the contract or offered against an invoice, the Component must take the discount if economically justified, but only after acceptance of the goods or services. Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 32.111(b) requires FAR 52.232-8, "Discounts for Prompt Payment," in all fixed-price supply and service contracts. The contractor may extend the discount period or increase the discount percentage beyond a previous offer. The offer may be written or, for specific invoices, oral. For an oral offer, the entitlement office must attach to the invoice a conversation record showing the name, position, and telephone number of the person offering the discount, the discount terms, and the date of the offer. The entitlement office may require written confirmation of the oral offer.

3.1.1.2. Entitlement offices must schedule discounted payments as close to, but not later than, the last day of the discount period. Per 5 CFR 1315.4(h), payment is considered made on the date printed on the check or on the electronic funds transfer settlement date. If the payment office cannot apply the discount, it must make payment per the payment due date guidelines in 5 CFR 1315.4(g).

3.1.1.3. Components must take cash discounts when the discount terms applied in the conversion formula yield an effective annual discount rate equal to or greater than the Current Value of Funds Rate (CVFR), calculated with the Fiscal Service Discount Calculator. DoW Component payment systems must build in processes that take cash discounts as a matter of routine, without special handling.

3.1.1.4. When the discount terms in the contract and the invoice differ, DoW Components must take the most cost-effective discount.

3.1.1.5. Compute discounts on the approved gross amount of the invoice, except as follows.

3.1.1.5.1. Deduct separately listed taxes or freight charges.

3.1.1.5.2. Deduct taxes that are not proper charges under international or status-of-forces agreements.

3.1.1.5.3. Compute the discount on the actual cash balance due when there is a trade-in.

3.1.1.5.4. When the entitlement system can trace and pay individual line items on an invoice, the invoice may be split into multiple payments. Each line item must meet the receipt and acceptance requirements to take the discount offered against the invoice.

3.1.1.5.5. When a contract or purchase order modification changes or adds discount terms, take the discount on any later payment made by the new or revised discount date.

3.1.1.6. Discounts may be taken on amounts legally withheld and later released if related amounts were paid per the discount terms. The discount period for the released payment begins when the entitlement office receives notice of the release.

3.1.1.7. The following requirements apply when liquidated damages apply and a contract for supplies, services, research and development, or construction includes FAR 52.211 - 11, FAR 52.211-12, or DFARS 252.217-7009.

3.1.1.7.1. When liquidated damages apply and the contract or invoice offers a discount for early payment, compute the discount on the gross contract price without regard to the liquidated-damages amount.

3.1.1.7.2. When liquidated damages apply to a modified price and the contract offers a discount for early payment, compute the discount on the modified price without regard to the liquidated damages.

3.1.1.8. After a progress payment is made, the government is entitled to a discount on any part of delivery payments applied in liquidation of progress payments.

3.1.1.8.1. When the discount terms are met, take the discount against the gross amount of the invoice. If the discount date is not met, take the discount only against the liquidation amount.

3.1.1.8.2. If the contractor has had the use of these progress payments, the payment office is entitled to take a prompt payment discount on them when they are recouped.

3.1.1.8.3. If the discount is offered for the first time on an invoice and the contract has no discount clause, do not take the discount on the progress payment liquidation portion of the invoice.

3.1.1.9. A contractor may offer a voluntary discount after contract completion, including final payment. Voluntary discounts are discretionary with the contractor and do not reduce the amount obligated against the paying appropriation. Do not treat discounts received after contract completion as rebates; deposit them in the Miscellaneous Receipts Account of the Treasury.

3.1.1.10. When contracts have Free on Board Origin terms, payments made before delivery of supplies to the carrier or to the destination are entitled to the discount offered on the contract.

3.1.1.11. Components must track the amount of discounts lost, or not taken, as part of their overall payment operations. Entitlement or disbursement systems must be able to identify and periodically report discounts lost to management for assessment and appropriate corrective action.

3.1.1.12. Components must retain documentation supporting discount transactions per Volume 1 and keep it readily available to support audits. The documentation must let an independent third party understand and verify the basis of the entitlement and the determination of a discount.

3.1.2. Rebates/Refunds

3.1.2.1. Components must maintain internal controls and procedures to maximize sales/productivity refunds and to identify and collect corrective rebates. Components must retain documentation supporting rebate/refund transactions per Volume 1 and keep it readily available to support audits. The documentation must let an independent third party understand and verify the basis of the rebates/refunds.

3.1.2.2. Pay GPC billing statements as soon as administratively possible when the rebate offered exceeds the cost of funds defined in 5 CFR 1315.8. The Defense Finance and Accounting Service must determine and make available, as needed, GPC payment data comparing the Current Value of Funds to the rebate discount points for the payment cycle day. Components and the payment office must use this data for a cost-benefit analysis of the cost of early payment (the interest the DoW would earn at the CVFR for each day payment is not made), comparing the basis points offered by the card issuer against the corresponding basis points of the Treasury CVFR. DoW Components must forward approved GPC billing statements to the payment office in time to process the payment, receive a rebate for early payment, and avoid interest penalties per
5 CFR 1315.8.

3.1.2.3. The charge card issuer must calculate the rebate and return it to the DoW customer designated in the contract. DoW Component entities that receive and use rebates/refunds must employ internal controls and procedures to ensure rebates are received when due under their GPC contract and are calculated properly.

3.1.2.4. Per 10 U.S.C. 4754, DoW rebates attributable to GPC use may be credited to operation and maintenance and/or research, development, test, and evaluation accounts that are current when the rebates are received. For example, a rebate received in the new fiscal year against a bill paid in September of the prior fiscal year may be credited to the account(s) current after October 1 of the new fiscal year. This includes the operational portion of a nonappropriated or working capital fund account.

title: Section 4.0: Contractual Claims
content:
4.0    CONTRACTUAL CLAIMS

4.1    INTERNAL CONTROLS

Internal controls must prevent duplicative or erroneous payments (for regulatory compliance, refer to Section 2.0). Managers responsible for determining entitlements, authorizing or executing payments, and performing collections must perform periodic (minimum annual) risk assessments per the GAO's Standards for Internal Control in the Federal Government and OMB Circular No. A-123, to ensure sufficient management controls keep DoW funds spent appropriately and per all applicable laws and regulations. Refer to Volume 4, for additional guidance on improper payments and related risk assessments.

4.2    RETENTION

The certifying officer must retain payment documentation, both paper and electronic. Electronic record storage requires adequate controls to ensure digital images accurately represent the corresponding paper documentation and to detect changes to an original digital image. Refer to Volume 1, Figure 9-1 for DoW financial records retention policy. Title 44, U.S.C. § 2909 prescribes the authority to retain records longer than specified in the U.S. National Archives and Records Administration, General Records Schedules.

4.3    ASSIGNMENT OF CLAIMS

4.3.1. Conditions

4.3.1.1. If an agency pays a party other than the assignee when a properly filed and approved assignment of claims is on record, the Government may incur liability to the assignee.

4.3.1.1.1. When such an error occurs, the agency remains liable to the assignee for the amount of the payment, subject to potential defenses.

4.3.1.1.2. The agency must initiate collection against the payee for any erroneous payment.

4.3.2. Actions Required for Assignment of Claims

4.3.2.1. If the Administrative Contracting Officer (ACO) determines the assignment is valid, the disbursing officer of the designated payment office must acknowledge the notice of assignment and take the following actions:

4.3.2.1.1. Authorize payment to assignees only after receiving the following assignment documents:

4.3.2.1.1.1. A copy of the notice of assignment acknowledged by the contracting officer.

4.3.2.1.1.2. A copy of the signed notice and a true copy of the instrument of assignment from the assignee.

4.3.2.1.1.3. A copy of the notice acknowledged from the surety or sureties, if any, or a copy received from the surety or sureties via the assignee.

4.3.2.2. Components and agencies must maintain procedures ensuring the appropriate payment office receives a copy of the instrument of assignment and the signed notice of assignment.

4.3.3. Letter Contracts

4.3.3.1. If a letter contract is assigned, definitization of the contract does not void that assignment.

4.3.3.2. Contracting officers and the disbursing officer of the designated payment offices must accept receipt for, and honor the assignment of, the proceeds of a definitive contract superseding a letter contract.

4.3.4. Assignment of claims under open-end, call-type, or indefinite-delivery-type contracts is authorized, provided orders of $1,000 or more are placed before the assignment, or the basic contract imposes a minimum obligation of $1,000 or more. When the designated payment office cannot determine whether an assignment of claims applies to an individual call or order under an indefinite-delivery-type contract, the office must withhold payments until the ACO determines the status and validity of the assignment. Refer to FAR 16.1 for information on contract types.

4.3.5. Release

4.3.5.1. The designated payment office must make remaining payments to the contractor only after it receives the following release documents:

4.3.5.1.1. A true copy of the instrument of release of assignment.

4.3.5.1.2. The original and two copies of the release notice.

4.3.6. If a contractor attempts to change the payee identity by changing Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) or other information in the System for Award Management (SAM) without complying with the rules governing novation agreements and assignment of claims, the payment information will be incorrect within the meaning of the "Suspension of Payment" paragraph of the contract's EFT clause (FAR 4.1102(d)). Assignees must register separately in SAM to ensure the financial institution identified in the assignment meets the EFT requirement.

4.4    CONTRACT DISPUTES

4.4.1. The Bureau of the Fiscal Service (Bureau) administers and certifies payments from the Judgment Fund for the settlement and final judgment in a CDA case (Treasury Financial Manual (TFM), Volume 1, Part 6, Chapter 3100; 28 U.S.C. § 2517; and 31 U.S.C. § 1304). Reimbursement of the Judgment Fund is payable from funds current at the time the award is made by the activity accountable for the contract obligation, per 41 U.S.C. § 7108(c).

4.4.2. Questionable and Fraudulent Claims

4.4.2.1. Fraudulent and questionable claims must not be paid. For additional information, refer to Volume 5.

title: Section 5.0: Miscellaneous Advance Payments
content:
5.0    MISCELLANEOUS ADVANCE PAYMENTS

5.1    GENERAL

5.1.1. Title 31 U.S.C. § 3324 prohibits advance payments. Exceptions are authorized only by specific appropriation acts or other laws, or as granted by the President under 31 U.S.C. § 3324.

5.1.1.1. An electronic request for advance payment must contain all elements of a proper invoice (5 CFR § 1315.9(b)(1)). Electronic submission is preferred.

5.1.1.2. All claimants subject to the U.S. Internal Revenue Service code must provide a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) per 31 U.S.C. § 3325(d).

5.1.1.3. Advance payment requests must be submitted to the designated payment office per DoW and Component submission policies, using a vendor invoice, Standard Form (SF) 1034, Public Voucher for Purchases and Services Other Than Personal, or an electronic equivalent.

5.1.1.4. A designated approving official and a properly appointed certifying officer must approve all advance payments before disbursement, confirming the voucher information agrees with all supporting documentation. The certifying officer also certifies that the vouchers are correct and proper for payment from the appropriations or other funds cited, and that the proposed payments are legal, proper, and correct (Volume 5).

5.1.1.5. A copy of all supporting documentation must accompany each advance payment request to ensure auditability and validate entitlement systems' payment records. Certifying officers must retain all payment documentation (Volume 5).

5.1.1.6. A prevalidation process must match the proposed advance payment to the obligation of funds recorded in the accounting records before disbursement (Volume 3).

5.1.1.7. Agencies and organizations requesting and approving miscellaneous advance payments must ensure the advance does not exceed the value of the items or services being procured.

5.1.1.8. Components must establish controls for liquidating advance payments and assign responsibility for follow-up action. Before liquidation, internal controls must confirm validation and documentation show the items or services were received and met the organization's requirements. Components must resolve discrepancies promptly upon identification, which may include establishing and collecting debts from members, employees, or commercial, Federal, or state entities (see Volume 16 for debt collection).

5.2    STATUTORY ADVANCE PAYMENTS

5.2.1. Amounts may be paid in advance to licensed or regulated childcare providers for services to be rendered during an agreed period (40 U.S.C. § 590(g)(4) and 10 U.S.C. §§ 1791- 1800). Authorized advance payments for childcare in an approved program, in areas where DoW-provided childcare is not available, must include a copy of a signed contract between the family and the provider outlining the fees supporting the payment (DoD Instruction 6060.02).

5.2.2. Advance payment is authorized for subscriptions or other charges for newspapers, magazines, periodicals, microfilm libraries, and other publications for official use (31 U.S.C. § 3324(d)(2)). The total subscription cost is a valid charge to the appropriation for the fiscal year (FY) current when the subscription is ordered. A subscription may extend beyond the current FY, but the authorized payment must not cover more than a 1-year (12-month) subscription from the same FY appropriation.

5.2.3. Tuition may be paid in advance. 5 U.S.C. § 4109 provides general authority for advance tuition payments for civilian and military personnel, and 10 U.S.C. § 2396(a)(3) authorizes them for military personnel of friendly foreign countries. Advance tuition payments are payable when an educational institution requires payment at enrollment.

5.2.3.1. The SF 182, Authorization, Agreement and Certification of Training, must identify the training facility by name and address, the amount payable to the facility for the tuition advance, and the amount payable to the trainee for books and library and laboratory fees. The SF 182 must be submitted to the entitlement office to support the advance payment and be signed by an approving official and certifying officer before payment.

5.2.3.2. Controls must be in place to liquidate the advance payment (subparagraph 1.2.10). For tuition advances, controls must include obtaining documentation that the student successfully completed the training paid in advance. If the student owes the DoW, the Component must collect any outstanding amount due and forward a DoD (DD) 1131, Cash Collection Voucher, to the designated disbursing office to complete liquidation.

5.2.4. Title 10 U.S.C. § 2396 authorizes advances of Federal monies for compliance with foreign laws, rent in foreign countries, tuition, public utility services, pay and allowances, and supplies and services of Armed Forces of friendly countries.

5.3    INTRA-GOVERNMENTAL ADVANCE PAYMENTS

5.3.1. Overview

5.3.1.1. Agencies may make intra-governmental payments in advance of performance only in the areas identified in this section. Unless specifically authorized by law, legislative action, or Presidential authorization, the DoW Component must not advance funds to non-DoW Federal entities or pay advance billings without receipt of goods or services. Where a specific appropriation or law authorizes DoW to advance funds, that appropriation or law must be cited on the obligating and interagency agreement documents and orders (Volume 11A).

5.3.1.2. Components must establish follow-up actions and controls to ensure receipt and acceptance of the items or services before liquidating the advance payment, as prescribed by the Treasury Interagency Agreement Guide and subparagraph 1.2.10. Intra- governmental advance payments are made through the Intragovernmental Payment and Collection (IPAC) system or G-Invoicing; Fiscal Service requires federal entities to use G-Invoicing under 31 U.S.C. 3512(b) and 31 U.S.C. 3513.

5.3.2. With approval from the General Services Administration (GSA), one Federal agency may lease from another a portion of its leased office space (Federal Management Regulation, Subchapter C, section 102-73.60). The parties may agree to a lease payment in advance, or on another agreed basis, for the proportionate cost of the space, utilities, and services furnished (40 U.S.C. § 585).

5.3.3. Title 44 U.S.C. § 310 authorizes advance payments for printing, binding, or supplies ordered from the U.S. Government Publishing Office (GPO). The requesting agency must process these advance payments using IPAC to establish GPO deposit accounts.

5.3.4. Title 40 U.S.C. § 581(g) authorizes GSA to bill tenants for building rent in advance. The charge is a fixed rate per square foot of assigned space based on building operation and maintenance costs, and need not itemize separate cost factors for utilities, rent, or elevator service.

5.3.5. DoW authorizes annual advance payments to the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) for post office box rental (B-57828, 25 Comp. Gen. 834 (June 5, 1946)). Fees are for a six-month period and are payable for two periods at a time, not to exceed two consecutive six-month periods. Federal agencies whose payment period coincides with the Federal FY may pay box fees during the first quarter. USPS refunds a portion of the rental when the box is surrendered before the end of the rental period. Per 41 CFR 102-192.50, the following methods are available for advance payments for box rentals:

5.3.5.1. Payments to service providers other than USPS must use Fiscal Service payment methods, such as automated clearing house electronic funds transfer or another Fiscal Service approved means.

5.4    OTHER ADVANCE PAYMENTS

5.4.1. Attendance at Meetings and Conferences

5.4.1.1. Components may authorize payment of registration fees before attendance at meetings of technical, scientific, professional, or similar organizations.

5.4.1.2. DoW civilian employees and uniformed service members may attend and participate in conferences, meetings, and recognized professional organizations to maintain and improve professional competency at Government expense, subject to availability of funds, specific management approvals, and work responsibilities. Documentation supporting the approval must accompany the advance payment request (SF 182 or electronic equivalent), and a management official must approve the request before submission to the certifying officer.

5.4.1.3. If the payment is non-refundable and the individual fails to attend for reasons beyond their control, do not collect the registration fees from the individual. If the failure to attend is for a reason the DoW Component deems inexcusable, the individual must repay the amount advanced. If the individual does not voluntarily settle the indebtedness, the Component must act to collect the outstanding advance from money due the employee or member (salary offset policy is in Volume 16).

5.4.2. Advance payments to state and local governments for goods and services are authorized. Under FAR 32.409-3(e), the contracting officer may omit the requirement to deposit the advances in a special account if the approving official determines that other adequate security protects the Government's interest.

5.4.3. When submitting a petition for immigrant status for a person whose services are required, the fee must accompany the petition and is payable in advance to the U.S. Department of State (22 CFR 22.1-22.7). 22 CFR 22.3 prescribes remittances in the United States and 22 CFR 22.5 prescribes remittances to Foreign Service posts.

5.4.4. When approved, membership dues or fees in professional societies or associations acquired for the benefit of the DoW Component are payable in advance. Appropriated funds expended for membership must acquire services that benefit the Component, not an individual. The head of the agency or designee must determine the membership requirement, and the individual employee must provide verification of membership to validate the advance payment.

5.4.5. Components may authorize an advance payment for a license to use a patent or to purchase a copyright. The subject matter of the purchase must be within the authorization of the current FY appropriation (10 U.S.C. § 3793). FAR 27 and DFARS 227 prescribe the related patent, data, and copyright policies and contract clauses.

5.4.6. Payment of a utility service account activation fee or connection charge is allowable (FAR 41.1, FAR 41.2, and FAR 52.241-9). The U.S. Government pays connection charges, whether refundable or non-refundable, to the utility supplier for the required connecting facilities, which the supplier installs, owns, operates, and maintains. Refundable connection charges are an advance payment, and the Government recovers them through a specified monthly refund or a credit on the utility service billings.

5.4.7. Foreign Country-Related Requirements

5.4.7.1. Where a foreign country requires personnel to obtain motor vehicle driver permits to perform official duties, the permit fees may require an advance payment, and a tour of duty in a foreign country justifies the expenditure.

title: Section 6.0: Federal, State, Local, and Foreign Taxes
content:
6.0    FEDERAL, STATE, LOCAL, AND FOREIGN TAXES

6.1    GENERAL

6.1.1. Authoritative Guidance

6.1.1.1. IRS-published regulations take precedence over DoW policy for resolving tax-related issues. Components must consult their designated legal counsel on legal questions or apparent conflicts between this section and IRS regulations.

6.2    RESPONSIBILITIES

6.2.1. Defense Logistics Agency-Energy (DLA-Energy) DLA-Energy

6.2.1.1. DLA-Energy must make any application for tax refunds applicable to DLA-Energy programs. If DLA-Energy supports a Federal civilian agency, that civilian agency must collect the data needed to apply for tax refunds.

6.2.2. DoW Components must take maximum advantage of exemptions from excise taxes.

6.2.3. Contractors, Vendors, and Individual Payees

6.2.3.1. Per FAR 29.304, a DoW Component may require contractors, vendors, and individual payees requesting payment to take certain action on payment, nonpayment, refund, protest, or other treatment of state and local specified taxes. The Component acts in consultation with the contracting officer, varying the action by tax consequences, nature of the purchases, and applicable contract clauses. An entitlement or disbursing office must elevate any concern about a contractor tax-related payment request or refund to the contracting officer for resolution.

6.2.3.2. Per 31 U.S.C. § 7701(c) and FAR 4.902, and subject to the Internal Revenue Code, all payees doing business with the DoW must furnish their Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) as defined by 26 U.S.C. § 6109 (an SSN, Individual TIN, or Employer Identification Number). A payment office must not authorize payment without a TIN or SSN on record for the required payee, except as described in paragraph 6.5.

6.2.3.3. If a contractor or other payee believes a tax form (IRS Form 1099-MISC, 1099-INT, 1099-NEC, or 1099-C) was improperly issued or incorrect, the payee must provide written evidence to the appropriate tax office to obtain a correction.

6.2.4. The Fleet Card issuer (third-party payor) must work with DLA-Energy and DFAS to maximize excise tax reclamations; rules and procedures vary by state, and states generally require reclamations after payment is made. Refer to the GSA SmartPay website for additional Fleet Card tax information.

6.2.5. For entitlement systems managed by DFAS, and ERP-managed systems that have coordinated with DFAS (except the Defense Health Agency and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, where responsibility is otherwise assigned), DFAS must perform the duties listed in this paragraph.

6.2.5.1. DFAS must compute all appropriate tax withholdings, make deposits to the U.S. Department of the Treasury, and file the appropriate tax documents with the IRS.

6.2.5.2. DFAS must pay excise taxes as appropriate.

6.2.5.3. DFAS must reclaim Federal and state excise tax related to fuel purchases, based on data from DLA-Energy or Fleet Card issuers. DFAS reclamation responsibilities include filing for the National Guard.

6.2.5.4. DFAS must record any taxes recovered in the applicable accounting systems.

6.2.5.5. DFAS must review payment information to determine whether a payment is reportable under current IRS guidelines.

6.2.5.6. When DFAS serves as the disbursing office for entitlement or ERP systems it does not own, DFAS must perform the duties listed in this paragraph.

6.2.5.6.1. DFAS must issue annual instructions on the requirements for submitting necessary tax reports to DFAS for distribution to recipients.

6.2.5.6.2. DFAS must coordinate the issuance of hardcopy or electronic tax statements within the IRS-mandated timelines.

6.2.6. The Office of the Staff Judge Advocate or General Counsel must provide available payment data for all settlements of personnel cases. The document forwarded to the paying office must identify each settlement payment type (for example, compensatory damages, attorney fees, back pay, or interest) and the dollar amount for each type; the paying office uses this information to determine proper tax reporting. These offices must also provide the information required to report payments to attorneys under 26 U.S.C. § 6045(f), separate from the claims settlement payment.

6.2.7. Third-party payors must prepare and file IRS Form 1099-K, Payment Card and Third-Party Network Transactions, for certain payments they made, even if the items procured were delivered to DoW. DoW is not responsible for filing an IRS Form 1099-MISC when third- party payors make the covered payments.

6.2.8. Convenience Check Account Holder

6.2.8.1. The convenience check account holder must perform tax reporting on the convenience checks they issue and obtain a signed IRS Form W-9, Request for Taxpayer Identification Number and Certification. Refer to the IRS instructions for Form 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC for detail on payment types that are not reportable to DFAS. As checks are written, the account holder must capture the following check recipient data.

6.2.8.2. For certain DoW agencies, DFAS must report to the IRS the miscellaneous and non-employee income paid to vendors and contractors. DFAS coordinates with the GSA SmartPay contract designated bank and the account holder to obtain the information needed to issue tax forms and report to the IRS. Section 18 contains additional policy on the use of convenience checks.

6.2.8.3. The convenience check account holder must perform all backup withholding actions required upon receipt of an IRS CP2100 notice (see the IRS website, Backup Withholding "B" program). See paragraph 6.5 for additional information on backup withholding.

6.3    FEDERAL EXCISE TAX (FET)

6.3.1. Except for IRC exemptions set out in FAR 29, the Government must pay FET on fuel purchases. If a contract does not specify that the contract price excludes FET, assume the price includes the tax and pay only the contract price. If the contract price specifically excludes the tax, FET for fuel purchases must be billed on the invoice as a separately identified item, distinct from the contracted fuel price.

6.3.2. Refund requests must be filed on IRS Form 8849, Schedule 1, Nontaxable Use of Fuels.

6.3.3. Quarterly FET Return

6.3.3.1. Unless the IRS District Director otherwise notifies the accounting office responsible for reporting DLA-Energy activity, that office must prepare and submit quarterly FET returns. DLA-Energy must submit a monthly report to DFAS of sales to taxable customers. File the return on IRS Form 720, Quarterly Federal Excise Tax Return, for the first calendar quarter when the tax liability is incurred and each subsequent calendar quarter until a final return is filed. Mark final returns "FINAL"; they apply only when no FET is owed or reportable in future quarters. See IRS Pub 510 for additional guidance.

6.3.3.2. The accounting office must prepare IRS Form 720 per the IRS Instructions for Form 720.

6.3.4. Collections for FET

6.3.4.1. FET collections are made to deposit fund accounts. Transfer collected excise taxes per the most current IRS instructions. Transfers are generally required semi-monthly and must be made electronically to the Treasury.

6.3.4.2. Report the amounts of FET collected and deposited for the sale of aviation fuel other than for the exclusive use of the DoW.

6.4    STATE AND LOCAL TAXES

6.4.1. State and Local Taxes

6.4.1.1. Unless the contract states otherwise, state and local taxes are presumed included in the contract price. When a valid fixed-unit-price contract has no clause to adjust prices if state taxes are imposed on the contractor, there is no authority to pay taxes above the stipulated unit price.

6.5    CUSTOMS DUTIES

6.5.1. U.S. Customs Duties on Foreign Purchases

6.5.1.1. If an importation is not duty-free, charge the duty to the same appropriation and fiscal year used to fund the purchase, even when the importation and purchase fall in different fiscal years (expired funding is available for such adjustments per Volume 3). Customs and Border Protection's classification of imports generates the amount due. Prepare payment vouchers showing the payment amount, annotated with the source and calculated duty, with remittance addressed to the Collector or Deputy Collector at the port of entry. Before payment, the entitlement office must obtain the ACO's approval to ensure the customs duties are not already covered in the contract price and that exemption certifications have not been issued for the items.

6.6    MISCELLANEOUS

6.6.1. If a local government levies an environmental assessment that is a fee, the payment is authorized. If the assessment appears to be a tax of questionable legality, the payment is not authorized. Consult the Component's legal counsel to determine whether to pay.

6.6.2. Backup Withholding

6.6.2.1. In most instances, under 31 U.S.C. 3325, DoW may not make a payment without a valid TIN. If payment is appropriate without a TIN and a signed IRS Form W-9, and no exception to backup withholding applies, backup withholding must occur. Backup withholding requirements are enforced payment-by-payment, regardless of payment size. When an individual or entity has not provided a TIN and a signed IRS Form W-9, the backup withholding requirements in 26 U.S.C. 3406 apply.

6.6.2.2. DoW activities must perform backup withholding on reportable payments when the IRS informs the paying office that the payee provided an incorrect TIN and reportable payments total $600 or more during the calendar year, when an information return was required concerning the payee for the preceding calendar year, or when backup withholding was required from the payee for the preceding year.

6.7    FEDERAL TAX REPORTING

6.7.1. Taxable Payments

6.7.1.1. At the end of each calendar year, payment or entitlement offices must report certain payments to the IRS. 26 U.S.C. 6041, 26 U.S.C. 6041A, 26 U.S.C. 6045(f), FAR 4.904, and current IRS instructions establish the reporting requirements. Payment or entitlement offices must provide payees with an IRS Form 1099 by the IRS-specified date.

6.7.1.2. Various payments to military members and civilian employees are subject to IRS reporting on Form W-2 (for example, military award payments), and some require tax withholding reported on Form W-2. The appropriate system must make these payments so accurate withholdings are applied and reported on the annual Form W-2 by the IRS-specified date. Payment through a vendor pay office is authorized only if the proper withholdings are computed, included, and presented for payment. At year-end, payment or entitlement offices must report these payments on Form W-2 per current Social Security Administration and IRS guidelines.

6.7.2. Tax Reporting

6.7.2.1. Each DoW Component must prepare an IRS Form 1099 on its contract or vendor payments for applicable services that total $600 or more, or royalties of $10 or more, in a calendar year to a single person or business entity, unless an exception applies. For DFAS-serviced Components, DFAS prepares, prints, and distributes the Form 1099 to the payee and forwards the same information to the IRS. If a Form 1099 needs correction, the paying office that maintains the underlying payment record provides the information to make it; if the payee believes the form was improperly issued or incorrect, the payee must provide the written evidence needed for correction.

6.7.2.2. Consolidate payment data across the various payment systems for the same contractor to determine whether an entity was paid more than $600 in reportable payments.

6.7.3. IRS Form 1099 Information Reporting

6.7.3.1. When paying a complainant back pay on a claim that originated with a DoW activity whose civilians DFAS pays, forward the claim to a civilian pay office for payment and issuance of an IRS Form W-2. DoW activities must forward all claims representing back pay to their supporting payroll office.

6.7.3.2. The office forwarding personnel claims (see Section 11) for payment, such as taxable settlement awards, must provide the information required for tax reporting with the settlement documents. All settlement payments are presumed taxable unless the settlement agreement indicates otherwise or they meet a specific nontaxable category.

6.7.3.3. The total amount paid to an attorney for legal services, other than contractual legal services, must be reported on an IRS Form 1099 as required by 26 U.S.C. 6045(f). "Attorney" includes a law firm or other provider of legal services, such as a corporation. This requirement applies regardless of whether the legal services are provided to the Government and whether the attorney is the sole payee. For payment by check, payment is made to the attorney or law firm if it is named the sole, joint, or alternate payee. When a single payment requires two Forms 1099, issue one to the complainant and one to the attorney. The office forwarding the claim must provide information including payee name(s), payee TIN, amount paid, payee address(es), and settling-activity identification.

6.7.4. Filing Information Returns With the IRS

6.7.4.1. Activities preparing information returns must be able to reconstruct the data or records used to prepare the IRS Form 1099. Retain the data or records for at least three calendar years, plus the current calendar year, after filing the information return (see IRS General Instructions for Certain Information Returns). These records substantiate the reported amounts by showing all relevant payments, including payments from multiple contracts. The retention period for IRS Form 1099-C or backup withholding data is four calendar years after filing the information return. The issuing location must keep a copy of information returns or be able to recreate the tax document.

6.8    TAX ON CERTAIN FOREIGN PROCUREMENT PAYMENTS

6.8.1. Per 26 U.S.C. § 5000C and implementing regulations such as FAR 29.402-3, a 2% tax applies to certain foreign procurement payments unless an exemption in paragraph 6.8.2 applies. Inclusion of FAR 52.229-12 in the contract identifies the tax, effective for contracts issued after June 5, 2020 (date of the FAR final rule), and requires paying agents to withhold up to 2% of applicable payments.

6.8.2. Exemptions

6.8.2.1. If the vendor claims a full exemption in its offer, the vendor need not submit an IRS Form W-14 with each invoice, and the paying agent will not withhold the 2% excise tax. Per FAR clause 52.229-12, if circumstances change during contract performance and the full exemption no longer applies, the vendor must notify the contracting officer and begin submitting an IRS Form W-14 with each invoice.

6.8.2.2.
