If the vendor claims only a partial exemption, or no exemption, with its offer, FAR clause 52.229-12 requires the vendor to submit an IRS Form W-14 with each invoice, indicating the amount or percentage of the invoice that is exempt from the tax. The excise tax withholding is applied at the payment level, not at the contract level. The vendor must revise each IRS Form W-14 submission to reflect the exemption (if any) that applies to that invoice.

6.8.2.3. If the vendor has claimed only a partial exemption, or no exemption, in its offer and does not submit an IRS Form W-14 with an invoice, the default withholding percentage is 2% for that payment request.

6.8.3. Withholding Requirements

6.8.3.1. Unless the vendor has claimed a full exemption in its bid/offer, paying agents must withhold the tax from invoices per the IRS Form W-14 accompanying each invoice. Withholding is typically 2% of the invoice amount unless the vendor has claimed a partial exemption on the W-14 (for example, only a portion of the goods were manufactured, or services provided, in a country that has an international procurement agreement or tax treaty with the United States).

6.8.3.2. If the vendor has not claimed a full exemption in its offer and does not provide an IRS Form W-14 with an invoice, the default withholding is 2% of the invoice amount.

6.8.4. Responsibilities

6.8.4.1. The contracting officer must tell the paying agent whether the contractual payments are subject to the 2% Foreign Excise Tax by including the appropriate FAR provisions and clauses (52.229-11 and 52.229-12), and must identify in the contract whether the vendor claimed a full exemption in the original offer/proposal.

6.8.4.2. The paying agent must withhold the 2% Foreign Excise Tax per the IRS Form W-14 that the vendor/payee submits with each payment request, file the reports to report tax withholdings to the IRS, and submit the withheld funds to the IRS.

6.8.4.3. The acquiring agency and paying agent must make every effort to identify, withhold, and report applicable tax withholdings to the IRS. Per IRS guidance, if the acquiring agency fails to withhold the tax, the foreign contracting party must file a U.S. income tax return and pay the tax due. The acquiring agency or the paying agent is not liable for any tax not withheld (see the U.S. Government Reporting section on the IRS webpage).

6.8.5. Refunds for Over-withholdings

6.8.5.1. The paying agent may not refund over-withholdings claimed by a vendor. Per 26 CFR 1.5000C-2(e), if the foreign contracting party (payee) discovers that amounts withheld on prior payments exceeded the amount required to satisfy its tax liability under section 5000C, it may request the acquiring agency to decrease withholding on future payments for which withholding is required under section 5000C. The request must be in writing, signed under penalties of perjury, state the amount by which the foreign contracting party requests to increase or decrease future amounts withheld under section 5000C, and explain the reason for the request.

6.8.6. Payments on Classified Contracts

6.8.6.1. Payments against classified contracts are subject to withholding of the 2% Excise Tax. The acquiring agency or paying agent must determine whether reporting such tax/withholdings will compromise national security. If so, the reporting may be scaled back or eliminated.

6.8.7. The paying agent/office must file the following reports and submit withheld taxes to the IRS.

6.8.7.1. Paying agents must submit/deposit withheld funds to the IRS via the Electronic Federal Tax Payment System within the timeframes required by 26 CFR 1.5000C-3(b).

6.8.8. The paying agent withholding applicable taxes must retain all documentation supporting the contract payments and all tax-related information supporting the withholdings, per Volume 1. This includes any documentation supporting the determination of whether to withhold, how much to withhold, and what was actually withheld, such as contracts, invoices, receiving reports, payment/Electronic Funds Transfer information, and the vendor's IRS Forms W-14, 1042, 1042-S, and W-9.

title: Section 7.0: Prompt Payment Act
content:
7.0    PROMPT PAYMENT ACT

7.1    PROMPT PAYMENT ACT POLICY

7.1.1. Payment terms ordinarily imposed by contract, or by the PPA and its implementing regulations, may be replaced by payment terms imposed by another governmental authority. In this section, days are calendar days unless stated otherwise. The PPA applies to the following, unless the payment meets an exemption:

7.1.1.1. Procurement Contracts. All payments for contracts for the procurement of goods or services;

7.1.1.2. Vendor Payments. All vendor payments and payments to persons, organizations, or business concerns engaged in a profession, trade, or business and any not-for- profit entity operating as a vendor; and

7.1.1.3. Utility Payments. All utility payments, including telephone service, are subject to the PPA. Where state, local, or foreign authorities impose generally applicable late payment rates for utility payments, those rates must take precedence, and PPA interest rates will not apply.

7.1.2. Before making an invoice or interest payment, DoW Components must ensure appropriate payment documentation is established and matched: the contract, receipt/acceptance report, and a proper invoice, unless not required by the contract. Subparagraphs 7.1.2.1 and 7.1.2.2 identify when an invoice or receipt/acceptance report may not be required. DFARS 232.70 prescribes DoW policies for submitting and processing payment requests and receiving reports electronically, specifies exceptions, prescribes Wide Area Workflow as the accepted electronic form, and permits the TRICARE Encounter Data System as the electronic format for receiving reports for health care services. Retain payment documentation per Volume 1, readily available to support future audits. Retain original payment documentation and associated supporting documentation per Section 8.0.

7.1.2.1. The contract is an enforceable agreement between the agency and the contractor or vendor that supports payment of invoices and interest penalties. Contracts must contain the data elements required under 5 CFR 1315.9(a) as part of the payment documentation. If errors in a contractual document affect payment processing, the entitlement office must notify the contracting office to request corrective action. The payment office must not change contract terms; terms may be changed only by formal contract modification.

7.1.2.2. DoW payments must be based on receipt of a proper invoice, unless an invoice is not required by the contract (e.g., monthly rental payments), and on satisfactory contract performance. FAR 32.905(b) details the information required for a proper invoice. Per FAR 32.905(b)(2), an interim payment request under a cost-reimbursement service contract is a proper invoice if it includes all information required by the contract. The office designated by the purchase order, agreement, or contract to first receive and review invoices (the designated activity) must immediately annotate the receipt date and review invoices within 7 days after receipt. If an invoice is improper, the designated activity must return it to the vendor or contractor.

7.1.2.2.1. When the designated activity returns an invoice as improper, it must explain why and clearly mark the request to the vendor or contractor for a corrected invoice. Notification must be within 7 days of invoice receipt (5 days for perishable agricultural commodities, dairy products, and edible fats or oils and food products prepared from them; 3 days for meat, meat food, fish, and seafood products). If a DoW Component fails to notify within these timeframes, the days allowed to pay the corrected proper invoice are reduced by the days delayed beyond the allowable return-notification requirement. For example, a 30-day invoice returned as improper on the 11th day after receipt, minus 7 days allowed, equals a 4-day delay, reducing the corrected invoice payment due date by 4 days; the corrected invoice is payable in 26 days from receipt before interest accrues. Per FAR 32.906(b)(4), if a designated activity erroneously rejects a proper invoice, the original invoice receipt date is used to compute the payment due date and any interest penalties due.

7.1.2.3. Receipt of goods does not ordinarily provide a basis for payment. Payment must be based on acceptance of the goods or services, authenticated by the government official's signature. Acceptance must occur as a condition of payment except in the following instances.

7.1.2.3.1. For contracts incorporating the Fast Payment Procedure clause at FAR 52.213-1, payment offices may use the contractor's invoice submission as certification of delivery of supplies and as the basis for authorizing payment. Pay these invoices within 15 days after invoice receipt. Components must have policies and controls to follow up after payment to ensure receipt of acceptance documentation for the payment and contract files. Acquisition requirements governing the fast payment procedure are in FAR 13.4 and DFARS 213.4. Refer to paragraph 7.0 of section 9 for additional fast payment procedure financial management policy.

7.1.2.4. The agency receiving official must forward the receiving report, or other government documentation, to the designated payment office by the 5th working day after government acceptance or approval, unless other arrangements have been made.

7.1.2.5. Government acceptance is commonly deemed to occur constructively on the 7th day after the contractor delivers supplies or performs services per the contract, unless there is a disagreement over quantity, quality, or contractor compliance with a contractual requirement. A contract may specify a longer acceptance period; the date of actual acceptance or the date the acceptance period ends then substitutes for the 7th day after delivery (refer to DFARS 232.904).

The date the designated acceptance period ends is the constructive acceptance date. Constructive acceptance is used to calculate PPA interest and applies to both destination and source acceptance contract terms. Forward government proof of acceptance to the designated payment office.

7.1.2.5.1. If actual acceptance occurs within the constructive acceptance period, any interest penalty must be based on the actual date of acceptance.

7.1.2.5.2. If actual acceptance occurs after the constructive acceptance period, any interest penalty must be based on the constructive acceptance date.

7.1.2.5.3. The constructive acceptance requirement does not compel DoW Components to accept supplies or services or make payment before fulfilling their designated responsibilities and internal control activities.

7.1.2.6. If payments cannot be made due to non-receipt of receiving reports, copies of contracts, contract modifications, or other required documentation, the entitlement office must follow up with the contracting or receiving office to ensure these documents are forwarded timely. Make these follow-up requests in time to prevent loss of economically justified discounts where possible and to avoid unnecessary late-payment interest penalties.

7.1.2.7. When authorized, the head of the contracting activity of an operational area, in consultation with the cognizant comptroller supporting the contracting activity, must determine whether a contract and related payment are subject to the requirements of FAR 32.9 and include the applicable payment clause in the contract.

7.1.3. The billing office designated in the contract to receive the invoice must record the receipt date on the invoice immediately upon receipt of the contractor's invoice or payment request. The annotation must be clearly identifiable to the designated activity processing the payment. The receipt date determines the payment due date, the date by which an improper invoice must be returned, and the date interest begins to accrue if payment is late. If the designated activity fails to annotate the receipt date, the invoice receipt date is the date the contractor placed on the invoice. For electronically transmitted invoices, the invoice received date is the date the designated activity receives a readable transmission, or the next business day if received after normal working hours. For invoices made electronically available in feeder systems such as the Government purchase card bank system or the transportation Third Party Payment System, the invoice receipt date is the date the invoice is made available to DoW, not when invoices are transmitted to the entitlement office (Section 18.0).

7.1.4. For payments subject to FAR 32.9, the payment due date is the date by which payment must be made to avoid paying PPA interest.

7.1.4.1. If the payment due date is not specified in the contract, the date by which a proper invoice must be paid is the later of:

7.1.4.1.1. Thirty days after the date the designated activity receives the proper invoice; or

7.1.4.1.2. Thirty days after government acceptance of supplies delivered or services performed, or the applicable date of constructive acceptance, whichever is earlier.

7.1.4.2. A contract modification may be required to determine the payment due date (e.g., an award fee). If a payment cannot be entitled without a contract modification, the payment clock starts with the effective date of the modification.

7.1.5. The PPA requires timely payment and proper cash management of government resources. DoW must make payments no more than 7 days before the payment due date, but as close to the due date as possible, unless the Secretary of Defense or designee determines, on a case-by-case basis for specific payments, that earlier payment is necessary (FAR 32.906). Use this authority cautiously, weighing early payment benefits against the good stewardship inherent in effective cash management (5 CFR 1315.4(j)).

7.1.5.1. Per 10 U.S.C. 3801(b)(1) and NDAA FY 2021 Section 815, for a prime contractor that is a small business concern, DoW must, to the fullest extent permitted by law, establish an accelerated payment date with a goal of 15 days after receipt of a proper invoice for the amount due.

7.1.5.2. Per 10 U.S.C. 3801(b)(2) and NDAA FY 2022 Section 814, for a prime contractor that subcontracts with a small business concern, DoW must, to the fullest extent permitted by law, establish an accelerated payment date with a goal of 15 days after receipt of a proper invoice for the amount due if the prime contractor agrees to pay the subcontractor on the accelerated schedule, to the maximum extent practicable, without further consideration from or fees charged to the subcontractor.

7.1.5.3. Payment is considered made on the date printed on the check or on the Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) settlement date. To avoid late-payment interest fees, the EFT settlement date (the date funds are credited to the vendor's financial institution) must be no later than the calculated due date.

7.1.5.4. Checks must be mailed or transmitted on the same day the check is dated.

7.1.5.5. Payments due (including discount periods) on Saturday, Sunday, or legal holidays may be paid on Monday or the next working day without interest; this does not change the official payment due date.

7.1.6. If a vendor or contractor offers a DoW Component a discount, whether in the contract or on an invoice, the Component should take the discount if economically justified, but only after acceptance has occurred.

7.1.6.1. When a discount is taken, payment must be made as close as possible to, but no later than, the discount date.

7.1.7. When DoW Components fail to make payment by the payment due date, interest accrues from the day after the payment due date through the payment date.

7.1.8. DoW must pay late-payment interest penalties from either the funds available for administering the program for which the penalty was incurred (refer to 5 CFR 1315.10(b)(5)) or the funds financing the operation of the Military Department or Defense Agency associated with the invoice or contract payment (refer to 31 U.S.C. 3902). Charge all interest payments to the fiscal year(s) in which they accrue. If interest accrues at the end of the fiscal year but is not paid until the next fiscal year, cite the prior year's funds. If interest accrues at the end of the fiscal year and additional interest accrues in the new fiscal year, fund the total penalty citing each fiscal year's funds where the interest accrued, so the interest fund cite represents the bona fide need of the year the obligation arises. If the appropriation otherwise charged is cancelled, charge the appropriation current on the date of payment per 31 U.S.C. 1553(b)(1).

7.1.8.1. Entitlement offices must maintain detailed records supporting their determinations and must make these records available on request of any activity determined to have caused a late payment.

7.1.8.2. A contractor may waive interest entitlement by returning the interest paid by separate check or by returning the government check and requesting payment only in the amount invoiced. Besides returning interest penalties already received, a contractor may waive the right to PPA interest by express written statement or by acts and conduct indicating intent to waive. Written requests must be submitted to the applicable payment office established in the contract, be specific to each invoice or payment, and be for interest already earned or accrued. A contractor may not request waiver of interest not yet accrued or a blanket waiver for a group of contracts or invoices. Retain interest-waiver request documentation with payment supporting documentation.

7.1.8.3. Interest retained or waived is collected as a refund to the appropriation originally cited for the payment of interest. Credit all refunds of interest or penalties from contractors to the same line of accounting classification (including fiscal year) charged when interest was paid. If the appropriation is cancelled or closed, apply refunds to Miscellaneous Receipts of the U.S. Department of the Treasury.

7.1.8.4. The Foreign Military Sales (FMS) Trust Fund must fund late-payment interest penalties for procurements financed by an FMS contract. Refer to Volume 15, section 7.0 for additional information on FMS pricing.

title: Section 8.0: Commercial Payment Vouchers and Supporting Documentation
content:
8.0    COMMERCIAL PAYMENT VOUCHERS AND SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION

8.1    POLICIES AND REQUIREMENTS

8.1.1. Title 31 U.S.C. 3325 authorizes a DO to disburse money only when provided a voucher certified by a properly appointed certifying officer.

8.1.2. Title 31 U.S.C. 7701(c) requires all payees subject to the U.S. Internal Revenue Code who do business with DoW to furnish their TIN (which may be an SSN for individuals). DoW must not authorize payment without a TIN or SSN on record for required payees.

8.1.3. Payment Office Identification

8.1.3.1. MOCAS handles the most complex contracting and payment situations (financing payments, withholds, foreign currencies, and complex contract types and structures). Components must use their Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems as the payment office except where a contract's complexity requires an alternative such as MOCAS. See the joint Deputy Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment and Deputy Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller) policy memorandum for more information.

8.2    SUPPORTING DOCUMENTS REQUIRED TO PROCESS PAYMENTS

When entitling and certifying a payment, DoW Components must establish and retain appropriate payment documentation to support payment of invoices and interest penalties. This documentation normally includes the contract/purchase order, receipt/acceptance report, and a proper invoice. Refer to 5 CFR 1315.9 for required documentation. Subparagraph 8.2.3 defines the exceptions in which receiving reports are not required before payment.

8.2.1. If contractor/vendor invoices cannot be entitled and certified due to non-receipt of receiving reports, copies of contracts, contract modifications, or other required documentation, the entitlement office must follow up with the contracting or receiving office to ensure these documents are forwarded timely. The entitlement office, contracting office, and receiving activity must act timely to prevent loss of economically justified discounts and avoid unnecessary late- payment interest penalties.

8.2.2. Contract

8.2.2.1. A contract is a mutually binding legal relationship obligating the seller to furnish supplies or services (including construction) and the buyer to pay for them (FAR 2.101). Contracts must contain the information prescribed by 5 CFR 1315.9(a) to support payment of contractor/vendor invoices. If the entitlement office discovers an error in a contractual document, it must notify the contracting office to request corrective action. The entitlement office may not change contract terms; terms may be changed only through a formal contract modification. FAR 4.5 requires use of electronic commerce in Federal acquisition whenever practicable or cost effective.

8.2.3. Receiving Report

8.2.3.1. Acceptance must occur as a condition of payment in all cases except contract financing payments, interim payments on cost-reimbursement contracts for the acquisition of services, and use of the fast payment procedure as defined in Section 9.0. These payment-processing requirements do not negate the documentation requirements established in Volume 4, section 9.0.

8.2.3.2. If payment cannot be made due to non-receipt of a receiving report, the entitlement office must follow up with the contracting officer or receiving office to ensure the documentation is forwarded timely.

8.2.3.3. When a shipment is short of the quantity ordered, the entitlement office must pay, per the PPA (5 CFR 1315), the invoice amount supporting the quantity received and accepted, unless prohibited by the contract.

8.2.3.4. When the receiving report or invoice indicates the shipment is final but undelivered items remain under the contract terms, the entitlement office must pay, per the PPA (5 CFR 1315) and the variation authorized in the contract, the invoice amount supporting the quantity received and accepted. The entitlement office must also collaborate with the contracting officer, as needed, to advise and assist in resolving the differences.

8.2.4. Invoice

8.2.4.1. When using contracting officer approved or designated electronic techniques to submit invoices and electronically certified vouchers, the payment office need not transfer paper documentation for examination if the same supporting data are readily available and accessible in electronic media or through an electronic process.

8.2.4.2. The certifying officer must ensure the transmitted data relied upon to entitle and certify a payment contain the PPA information required by 5 CFR 1315.9 and FAR 32.905(b). Per Section 2.0, paragraph 2.0, the office must establish processes, controls, and routine testing to ensure the completeness, accuracy, authorization, and validity of electronic data received through system interfaces or transmission.

8.2.4.3. Contractors or vendors permitted to invoice non-electronically may submit invoices on any form that includes all required items of a proper invoice, unless their contract prescribes a specific invoicing form.

8.2.4.4. DoW payments must be based on satisfactory contract performance and receipt of a proper invoice, unless the contract does not require an invoice (for example, monthly rental payments). 5 CFR 1315.9(b)(1) and FAR 32.905(b) identify the items that must be included on a proper invoice.

8.2.4.5. If an invoice is improper or does not meet the contract requirements of FAR 32.905(b), the designated activity must return the invoice to the contractor or vendor and provide all details on the invoice deficiencies.

8.2.4.5.1. An invoice must be returned as improper if the entitlement office has not been provided a valid TIN for any designated payee subject to the U.S. Internal Revenue Code. If the TIN is not in the SAM, Corporate Electronic Funds Transfer, or supporting documentation (including the invoice or contract), the contracting officer must provide the contractor's TIN to the payment office (FAR 4.203(e)(2)).

8.2.4.5.2. An electronically transmitted payment request is treated the same as a paper payment request and must contain identical data elements (FAR 32.905(b)). Returned electronically transmitted payment requests must be returned in the same manner received, or in a manner practical for the entitlement system, accompanied by an electronic message stating the reason for return.

8.2.4.6. Non-electronic forms may be used as an invoice only if approved by the contracting officer and included in the contract. Such forms include the DD 250, SF 44, Delivery Ticket (refer to Section 7) and SF 1449.

8.2.4.7. Payments for services of a continuing nature (for example, rents or janitorial services) performed under agency-vendor contracts that provide for definite amounts at fixed periodic intervals may be made without contractor-submitted invoices or bills if the contract allows.

8.2.4.7.1. The contract must specify the payment due date. The voucher the payment office prepares to support these payments must show, at a minimum, the contract number, the period covered, the vendor name, the payment amount, and the account or appropriation to be charged. The payment voucher must be certified the same as all other payment vouchers.

8.2.4.7.2. Per TFM Volume 1, Part 4A, Chapter 2000, Section 2060, the office must establish and periodically test internal controls to ensure recurrent payments are on unexpired contracts or agreements, for correct amounts, for services actually received or leased space actually under contract, and not duplications of previous payments for the same goods or services.

8.2.4.8. If an original invoice is lost or destroyed, a duplicate must be obtained from the original submitter to support the voucher and marked as a duplicate. A full explanation of the loss or destruction and a statement that steps have been taken to prevent duplicate payments must be placed on or attached to the duplicate invoice. If the invoice information is already in the entitlement system, payment may be made from that information before a duplicate is obtained. When a duplicate cannot later be obtained, an annotation must document that payment was made based on existing records, that a hardcopy duplicate could not be obtained, and that the original was lost or destroyed. The specific existing records relied upon must be identified and documented, and management review and approval of the payment must occur and be documented before the disbursement. Refer to TFM Volume 1, Part 4A, Chapter 2000, Section 2050.10.

8.2.4.9. The Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) is the authorized representative of the ACO for approving interim contract payment vouchers for provisional payment, including interim vouchers for non-commercial and commercial Time and Material (T&M) and Labor Hour (LH) contracts, subject to final audit. Per DFARS 242.803, DCAA uses sampling to select interim vouchers for review before sending them to the payment office. Interim vouchers not selected for pre-payment review are provisionally approved and sent directly to the payment office. All provisionally approved interim vouchers are subject to later audit of actual costs incurred. DCAA does not provisionally approve the contractor's final voucher; the contracting officer must approve final vouchers. Refer to DoDD 5105.36 for DCAA's roles and responsibilities. The following invoices and vouchers require ACO approval before payment: completion vouchers under cost-plus, fixed-fee, or other cost-reimbursement type contracts; vouchers and invoices for termination costs under supplemental agreements, unless the termination modification specifies the costs to be paid; completion vouchers under T&M and LH contracts; invoices for progress and performance-based payments under fixed-price type contracts; vouchers and invoices where the contract requires ACO approval before payment; invoices for the release of "withhold" amounts previously instituted by the ACO; and any payment request where a DO requires an ACO signature.

8.3    DOCUMENT RETENTION

8.3.1. Original payment documentation and associated documents must be retained as government records in a format readily accessible to the entitlement office. Refer to Volume 1,
section 9.0, Figure 9-1, for specific policy and timeframes on record retention. Electronic record storage requires adequate controls to ensure digital images accurately represent the corresponding paper documentation and prevent changes to an original digital image (FAR 4.805(a)). The certifying officer must retain both paper and electronic documentation.

8.4    FOREIGN LANGUAGE DOCUMENTS

8.4.1. Documents Prepared in a Foreign Language

8.4.1.1. Invoices and supporting documents prepared in a foreign language must be translated before payment to ensure their contents satisfy the contractual document's requirements. Refer to DFARS 225.1103 for additional policy on contracts that may involve foreign-language documentation.

8.4.1.2. The documents must be translated in enough detail-contract number, item identification, unit of measure, price, and extension-to enable someone unfamiliar with the language to determine that receipts of material or services satisfy the contract terms.

8.4.2. If several invoices share a similar format and wording, a single translation is adequate, provided the like invoices support the same payment voucher and the required certification shows that all data not translated on other identified documents are the same as that translated, all non-common data on all invoices are identified and translated in enough detail to allow an audit by persons not familiar with the language, and a separate translation is attached for each group of different invoices.

8.4.3. The translation may be entered over or under the corresponding foreign wording or in any available space on the document; if space is not available, the English translation may be copied on a separate sheet. The translator completes and signs the following certification on each translated document found satisfactory for payment: "I certify that I am familiar with the ____ language, and that I have made a true and correct translation of the _____." (Printed Name, Signature, Date, and Contact Information). This certification, which pertains only to the translation, may be inscribed on a separate sheet and attached if space is not available on the foreign language document. A duly appointed (via a DD 577) certifying officer must ensure payment requirements are satisfied based on the translation.

8.5    PROCESSING ALTERED DOCUMENTS

8.5.1. Prohibited Pen and Ink Changes

8.5.1.1. Pen and ink changes are prohibited on all contractual documentation. FAR 43.301(a) prescribes the SF 30 for changes to contractual documentation.

8.5.1.2. Entitlement office personnel are prohibited from making pen and ink changes to the following information on requests for payment, receiving reports, and invoices: payee identification (including name, address, banking information, Commercial and Government Entity code, and TIN); order numbers (including contract, modification, call, task, and delivery order numbers); monetary amounts (any dollar value on any of the documents); Line of Accounting (LOA) data (all information pertaining to the LOA on any of the documents); names of officials and officers (including the certifying officer, approving official, contracting officer, and other related information as typed or printed on the documents); and dates (any dates impacting PPA interest or discounts).

8.5.2. Allowable Pen and Ink Changes

8.5.2.1. Entitlement offices may make pen and ink changes for administrative-type errors not described in subparagraph 8.5.1 on requests for payment, receiving reports, and invoice documents.

8.5.2.2. Entitlement office personnel may accept pen and ink changes on supporting documentation attached to an externally certified payment request that an appointed certifying officer certified and submitted. When submitting a certified payment voucher with manually altered supporting documents such as requests for payment and invoices, a properly certified SF 1034 identifying the correct total amount and fund citations must be provided to the entitlement office.

8.6    EMERGENCIES AND CONTINGENCY OPERATIONS

8.6.1. In addition to a contract, receiving report, and invoice, certifying officers supporting emergencies and contingency operations must ensure the entitlement package contains the specific information needed for valid certification and payment when the payment is exempt from the PPA. Payments subject to the PPA fall within the requirements of Section 7.0. For payments in support of an emergency or contingency operation not subject to the PPA, Appendix 1, Matrix for Payments in Support of Emergencies and Contingency Operations, identifies the critical data elements necessary for a proper certification.

8.6.2. Where information identified in Appendix 1 is not present on all documents (contract, receiving report, and invoice), the certifying officer may certify the payment if they can make a reasonable linkage among the documents. In certain circumstances explained in Appendix 1, the certifying officer may certify a payment missing a critical data element identified in the Appendix 1 matrix; however, they must justify in writing why they certified the payment.

8.6.3. All accounting offices that support emergencies or contingency operations must ensure that accounting and document-retention requirements are in place within 30 days of declaration of the operation. Adherence to these requirements is critical to DoW financial stewardship and control of funds.

title: Section 9.0: Payment Vouchers – Special Applications
content:
9.0    PAYMENT VOUCHERS – SPECIAL APPLICATIONS

9.1    INTRA-GOVERNMENTAL PAYMENTS

9.1.1. Billing Processes

9.1.1.1. Intra-governmental transactions (IGT) between or within DoW Components for the purchase of goods must be processed through the interfund billing system when initiated and supported by both trading partners' supply and accounting systems. In the interfund billing system, the supplier reimburses itself at billing from appropriations the customer designates, sends an automated billing to the billed office, and reports to the U.S. Department of the Treasury a reimbursement of the supplier's funds with an offsetting charge to the customer's funds. Only the billing office or the Central Accounts Office may adjust or reverse reimbursements reported to Treasury on behalf of the billing office. Refer to DLM 4000.25, Volume 4 for interfund billing system procedures.

9.1.1.2. Unless specifically authorized by law, legislative action, or Presidential authorization, a DoW Component must not advance funds to non-DoW federal entities or pay advance billings without receipt of goods or services. The constructive delivery and drop from inventory methods in paragraph 2.4 are exceptions to this prohibition. Refer to Volume 11A,
section 3.0 for advances to non-DoW entities via Economy Act Orders.

9.1.2. Completion

9.1.2.1. Work and shop orders must indicate the unit prices of articles or services furnished, or the actual value of personal services, materials, or other direct charges and overhead. When vouchers cover use of equipment, the itemized statement must carry the certification: "I hereby certify that the amount billed herein represents cost as determined under 31 U.S.C. § 1535 and 31 U.S.C. § 1536." When the account is billed on unit costs (for example, per hour, day, or mile) rather than itemization, those unit costs must include all expenses of operation and maintenance except depreciation. The purchase agreement between the entities determines the billing method.

9.1.2.2. An employee's services performed for another federal department or agency may be reimbursed to the providing agency only if a reimbursement agreement was made before the services were rendered. Copies of the agreement must be attached to the transfer voucher (SF 1080, 1081, or 1034) to support the payment.

9.1.2.3. The entitlement office must examine intra-governmental payment vouchers and supporting documentation to verify amounts and confirm required information and certifications are present (such as the equipment-use certification in subparagraph 9.1.2.1). The entitlement office must also verify accessorial charge rates when non-DoW Government activities levy them for issues, sales, and transfers of material, supplies, and equipment.

9.1.2.4. This verification must ensure charges do not include recurring reimbursement issues (sales) or non-reimbursable transfers of material to other DoW Components, except for sales and transfers under the military assistance grant aid program and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) programs. After the propriety review, the entitlement office must cite the accounting classification and verify the voucher is ready for payment.

9.1.2.5. Evidence of receipt and acceptance is required to support all intra- governmental and interfund transactions. DoW financial reporting entities must develop and implement internal controls to ensure receipt and acceptance is properly accomplished and documented for all IGT. Refer to Section 2 for internal control requirements and to Volume 4,
section 9.0 for receipt and acceptance requirements.

9.1.3. Constructive Delivery or Drop From Inventory

9.1.3.1. Delivery is evidenced by completed shipping documents, material shipment status of shipping documents, or a list of deliveries to a post office. Constructive delivery also applies to billings for goods accepted by an authorized inspector of another DoW Component providing direct shipment to the consignee. Such billings must be supported with a DoD (DD) Form 250, Material Inspection and Receiving Report, or other authorized documents from the inspector showing shipment. Under constructive delivery, bills are issued when the carrier accepts the goods for transport.

9.1.3.2. Constructive delivery bills are accepted and paid without waiting for delivery of the goods to the final destination. Components must perform follow-up procedures to confirm the goods were received and accepted and must obtain the documentation supporting receipt and acceptance for later audit.

9.1.3.3. Drop from inventory is the reduction of the quantitative inventory balance. Billing for shipments from stock must be at the standard price in effect when the stock is dropped from inventory. Refer to Volume 11B, section 15.0, paragraph 2.0 for inventory item pricing policy.

9.1.3.4. Following a supply activity requisition, reimbursable sales of material are billable after the material has been transferred using the drop from inventory method. Billing is based on drop from inventory or performance of services. Sales of bulk petroleum, oil, lubricants, and perishable subsistence, and FMS and military assistance grant aid shipments, are exceptions to this billing policy. Refer to DLM 4000.25, Volume 4, Chapter 2 for billing guidelines.

9.1.3.5. The supplying activity initiates a request for payment for items supplied to the DoW. Billings must, at a minimum, be supported by the document order number, description of the article or services, delivery or other performance date, quantity, and price. The document order number is normally the requisition document number, and the description is normally the National Stock Number. The supplying activity must notify the requisitioning activity of item substitutions and price or quantity changes. Refer to DLM 4000.25, Volume 4, Chapter 2 for billing procedures.

9.1.3.6. The requisitioning activity must record the amounts and quantities of items approved for payment at receipt and acceptance of the delivered items or services. The requisitioning activity must adjust the billing for unacceptable items or items unfilled by the supplying activity and reimburse only the adjusted amount. The requisitioning and supplying activities determine the disposition of unfilled items by mutual agreement.

9.1.3.7. If the requisitioning activity cancels requisitions, it is credited the amount billed, including accessorial charges. Accessorial costs are expenses incident to issues, sales, and transfers of materiel (packing, crating, and handling; transportation; and port loading and unloading; see Volume 11A, section 1.0, subparagraph 2.4.10). The alternate consignee for material diverted is billed the standard price and accessorial charges. If the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) orders direct shipment of non-stocked items and the requisitioning activity cancels the order, the requisitioning activity is billed via the SF 1080 for contract termination costs from the cancelation. Refer to DLM 4000.25, Volume 4, section 2.0 for MILSTRIP cancelation procedures.

9.1.4. Payment for services rendered by DWCF activities is based on the prescribed rates, tariffs, and billing procedures. DWCF payments follow the same policy as the constructive delivery and drop from inventory payments (see paragraph 9.1.3).

9.1.5. GSA

9.1.5.1. Ordering activities receive bills from GSA biweekly, monthly, or quarterly, after the fact, or in advance (for example, rental payments), as determined in the purchase agreement. Except for bills rendered in advance, GSA sends bills to Components only after evidence of actual delivery of material or services or receipt of evidence of shipment (constructive delivery). Components must perform follow-up procedures to confirm the goods were received and accepted and must obtain the documentation supporting receipt and acceptance for later audit. GSA may process requisitions of $1 or less without billing.

9.1.5.2. Payment for material is made through the IPAC system within 15 days after receipt of the GSA invoice. Bills are paid as rendered without pre-audit or receipt verification, subject only to availability of funds and adjustment for obvious significant errors in dollar amount. A follow-up process must be established to confirm the material paid for was received and accepted. Documentation supporting receipt and acceptance must be retained as billing support for future audit, per Volume 1, section 9.0 and the National Archives and Records Administration General Records Schedules.

9.1.5.3. Travel Pay sections process payments to GSA or contractors for vehicle rentals authorized by travel orders. The billing information must be compared to the obligation document; if an error is found, follow the applicable correction procedures. Payment is due within 30 days of the billing date (see subparagraph 9.1.2.5 for receipt and acceptance requirements).

9.1.5.4. GSA bills for federal telecommunication services are submitted monthly and paid in advance using the IPAC system, without pre-audit or receipt verification and subject only to availability of funds (see 10 U.S.C. § 2396 and 40 U.S.C. § 581(g)). These bills should be paid within 15 days after receipt of the GSA invoice. Components must perform follow-up procedures to confirm the services were received and must obtain the supporting documentation (receipt verification) for later audit.

9.1.5.5. Activities seeking credit from canceled requisitions for a material diversion must confirm the amount billed, including accessorial charges. The alternate consignee for material diverted is billed the standard price and accessorial charges. Activities canceling requisitions for material for which GSA ordered direct shipment of non-stocked items are billed by SF 1080 for contract termination costs from the cancelation. GSA promptly provides the bill to the activity cited in the canceled requisition.

9.1.6. Payments

9.1.6.1. DLA Document Services is the single DoW focal point for GPO ordering and management of document services per DoD Instruction 5330.03. An invoice is submitted to the requisitioning activity when printing services or supplies are furnished. The billed office prepares and processes the SF 1080 for payment and must attach an invoice to the SF 1080.

9.2    PARTIAL PAYMENTS

9.2.1. The entitlement office must maintain a separate partial payment record for each purchase order, contract, delivery order, or other obligation document requiring partial payments.

9.2.2. Payments made against blanket purchase agreements, call-type contracts, and blanket delivery orders, as defined by FAR Part 16, are not partial payments, except when more than one payment is required on an individual call or order.

9.3    CONTRACT FINANCING PAYMENTS

9.3.1. Progress Payments

9.3.1.1. Each contractor request for progress payment must be prepared and submitted through the WAWF module of PIEE as a separate progress payment document or SF 1443, Contractor's Request for Progress Payment, per DFARS 252.232-7003, with noted limited exceptions. The FAR and DFARS links provided cover progress payment computation, liquidation, reduction, suspension, and limitations.

9.3.1.2. When allocating progress payments across ACRNs, the payment office must establish controls to ensure disbursements do not exceed obligations at the ACRN level. To incorporate these controls, the office ordinarily charges progress payments, performance-based payments, and commercial item financing to an ACRN so the outstanding financing payment balance for each ACRN does not exceed that ACRN's Unliquidated Obligation (ULO) multiplied by the contractual liquidation rate. For ACRNs that fund both fixed-price and cost-type line items, the contract-financing allocation methodology applies only to the fixed-price portions (per
FAR 32.501-3).

9.3.1.2.1. If the contract's ACRN allocation instructions, based on the DFARS PGI payment instructions, deviate from the allocation process in 9.3.1.2, allocations in entitlement and accounting systems may reflect payment instructions that direct liquidation of contract finance payments from ACRNs with a shorter remaining period of availability for expenditure. This may facilitate liquidation of obligations under 31 U.S.C. §1553 before closure of the appropriation account by operation of 31 U.S.C. § 1552. If payment instructions direct liquidation of ACRN balances above the ULO balance multiplied by the contractual liquidation rate, the payment office must establish controls to ensure mixed-type-funding ACRNs (fixed and cost) are not over liquidated and the overall contract ceiling of 80% of contract price (FAR clause 52.232-16) is not exceeded.

9.3.1.2.2. If the contracting officer determines an alternate ACRN allocation methodology will be used to liquidate payments for a specific contract, as described in 5.2.4.2.1, the contracting officer must incorporate the DFARS PGI payment instruction of "Other" (prescribed by DFARS PGI 204.7108(d)(12)) and negotiate a written agreement to that methodology with the payment office before it may be used. The contract file and the payment office files must retain a copy of the written agreement, or the contractual modification identifying the specific payment instruction, for audit support.

9.3.1.3. Shifting work between contracts of the same contractor must comply with DoW progress payment policy of taking offsets whenever possible. A disbursement adjustment between contracts is a bookkeeping entry, not a payment transaction. When work is shifted between contracts of the same contractor, the progress payment is the net amount of the transactions involved on the contracts. A modification to each affected contract orders any transfer of work from one contract to another.

9.3.1.4. Recoupments are not accomplished involving both U.S. and FMS funds unless both fund the payment of the deliverable item. For a deliverable payment against U.S.- funded ACRNs, progress payments are recouped only against the U.S. ACRNs. For a deliverable payment against FMS-funded ACRNs, progress payments are recouped only against the countries involved with the FMS deliverable.

9.3.2. Advance

9.3.2.1. Subsidiary records of individual advances must be maintained to support the amount recorded in the general ledger account. The subsidiary record must include the amount and date advanced, the applicable contract number, and the disposition of the advance. At least quarterly, the subsidiary record must be reconciled with the general ledger balance; see Volume 4,
section 3.0.

9.3.2.2. The contractor request for an advance payment must be submitted to, approved, and certified for payment by the office(s) specified in the contract. The advance payment must cite a specific appropriation associated with the advance payment pool agreement. The approved request is forwarded to the payment or entitlement office cited in the contract for payment.

9.3.2.3. On receipt of a properly approved advance payment voucher, the entitlement office must review it for accuracy. If proper, the office entitles the voucher and forwards it to the disbursing office to be paid.

9.3.2.3.1. The payment must cite the appropriations identified on the contracts listed on the reimbursement voucher.

9.3.2.3.2. The entitlement office must maintain a record of all contract financing payments it makes.

9.3.2.3.3. Total payments must not exceed the total amount authorized on the contract.

9.3.2.3.4. Payments must be made within 5 to 10 workdays after receipt of a properly approved reimbursement voucher, but not earlier than the date specified in the pool agreement. These payments are a form of contract financing and are not subject to Prompt Payment Act (PPA) interest.

9.3.2.4. The payment office must establish controls (e.g., manual or electronic ledgers) to ensure cumulative payments, plus the amount advanced, do not exceed the ULO of all contracts awarded under the pooling agreement.

9.3.2.5. Do not make a non-advance contract payment when it would cause the ULO to fall below the advanced amount. If this condition occurs, notify the designated DoW Component and request further instructions. The Component will advise whether obligating documents are in transit or whether the payment must be processed to liquidate the amount advanced.

9.4    COST-REIMBURSEMENT-TYPE CONTRACTS

9.4.1. The Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) has sole authority to verify claimed costs and provisionally approve interim payment requests under cost-reimbursement, non- commercial and commercial time-and-materials, and labor-hour type contracts. This authority may include, on request, cost verification and provisional approval for state and local government- submitted claims under 2 CFR 200. Per DFARS 242.803, DCAA uses sampling methodologies to select interim vouchers for review before sending them to the payment office. Interim vouchers not selected for pre-payment review are considered provisionally approved and are sent directly to the payment office. All provisionally approved interim vouchers are subject to later audit of actual costs incurred. A Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) may not be delegated authority to approve these payments. The COR may review contractor billings but is expected to coordinate with DCAA when any cost verification is necessary to support surveillance responsibilities. The ACO approves the final payment request on the contract.

9.5    FAST PAYMENT

9.5.1. Payment must be made no later than 15 days after receipt of a proper fast pay invoice. If the payment office does not meet the 15-day requirement, PPA interest accrues under the procedures applicable to invoices to which the fast payment procedure clause does not apply. See section 7.0 for additional PPA policy and requirements.

9.5.2. The entitlement office, together with the contracting officer, must ensure the following conditions are in place when using the fast payment procedures.

9.5.2.1. A closed loop process must exist that matches payments to material receipts and resolves non-receipt or other discrepancies. This must consist of a management control or audit program by the entitlement office for the post-payment examination of payments made under fast pay.

9.5.2.1.1. Authorized personnel with direct knowledge of the receipt must document receipt of goods and services. This documentation, whether hardcopy or systemic, must be made available within the timeframe prescribed by a post-payment examiner when requested during audits. The audit must confirm receipt and acceptance and include matching with payment documents.

9.5.2.1.2. The first attempt to obtain missing receiving reports must be initiated no later than 45 days after payment. If the receiving report is not received within 45 days of the initial follow-up, the entitlement office must contact the contracting officer to verify receipt and acceptance, or issue a contract deficiency report to the contracting officer for non-compliance with contract terms so the entitlement office and the contracting officer can start collection actions.

9.5.2.2. Auditable evidence of receipt and acceptance of the goods or services must exist and be accessible. Audit evidence of receipt must show the date the items were delivered or the services were rendered, the printed authorizing official's name, and the authorizing signature or electronic/digital approval. Audit evidence of acceptance is the authorization that the receipt of goods or services matches the criteria identified on the originating order and acknowledges the items or services are of acceptable condition and quality.

9.5.2.3. An information flow must exist that links consignee (the post office, common carrier, or point of first receipt by the Government) receipt and discrepancy information to both the purchasing and bill entitlement offices.

9.5.2.4. A prevalidation process must exist that matches expenditures and obligations for fast pay transactions (see section 2.0 for additional information on prevalidation requirements).

title: Section 10.0: Payment as Reimbursement for Personal Expenditures
content:
10.0    PAYMENT AS REIMBURSEMENT FOR PERSONAL EXPENDITURES

10.1    PERSONAL EXPENDITURES

10.1.1. Military and civilian personnel must follow the standard personnel reimbursement procedures established by their Component or activity and must avoid using personal funds to pay Federal Government obligations. Personnel must be reimbursed only if the underlying expense was authorized, or an urgent and unforeseen public necessity existed, and the claim is legally payable. Personnel must not use this policy to avoid standard Component or activity reimbursement procedures or to circumvent other laws or regulations.

10.1.1.1. Electronic submission is preferred when requesting reimbursement for personal expenditures. The electronic claim must contain all elements of Optional Form (OF) 1164, "Claim for Reimbursement for Expenditures on Official Business," unless the Component's system captures the same data elements through other functionality that links directly to the claim and supports both internal and external audit requirements.

10.1.1.2. When submission is not electronic, OF 1164 is the authorized form for requesting reimbursement for personal expenditures under this section.

10.1.1.3. Claimants subject to the U.S. Internal Revenue Service code must provide a Tax Identification Number (TIN) for all payments per 31 U.S.C. § 7701, 31 U.S.C. § 3325(d), and Federal Acquisition Regulation subpart 4.9. For personnel, the TIN may be the claimant's SSN (26 U.S.C. § 6109(d)); an alternative identification number must be used whenever possible per DoDI 1000.30. Per DoDI 5400.11, "DoW Privacy and Civil Liberties Programs," Components must safeguard the privacy of all individuals and the confidentiality of all personally identifiable information (PII) and must protect any PII in a system of records used to conduct official business.

10.1.1.4. All claims for reimbursement must be submitted per DoW and Component submission policies and procedures (electronic or manual) and signed by the claimant, the appropriate approving official, and a properly appointed certifying officer before payment.

10.1.1.5. All claims for reimbursement require supporting documentation as proof of receipt, approval by a designated approving official, and certification by a properly appointed certifying officer before disbursement. Supporting documentation includes receipts, tickets, and invoices. Volume 1, section 9.0, Figure 9-1 prescribes the retention period for financial records supporting these payments; refer to 44 U.S.C. § 2909 for authority to retain records longer than disposal schedules specify.

10.1.2. Claim for Reimbursement for Expenditure on Official Business

10.1.2.1. Military and civilian personnel claiming reimbursement for personal- fund expenditures made without pre-approval must show an urgent and unforeseen public necessity existed. The claimant must prepare the claim and place on or attach to it the statement: "I certify this claim is true and correct. There was an unforeseen and urgent reason to spend my funds, and I have not received credit or payments." The claimant must sign and date the claim, and a designated Component or activity official must approve it before forwarding to the certifying officer.

10.1.2.2. Claims by non-Government personnel must carry signatures of the claimant, an approving official, and a properly appointed certifying officer. A certified copy of the document requesting the person to perform services, or documentation showing personally paid items, must support the claim.

10.1.2.3. Documents supporting certified vouchers must show the goods or services were received and essential. Mission-related expenses incurred while in travel status are not payable on a travel voucher or through the Defense Travel System. The JTR, sections 2.0, 3.0, and 5.0, prescribes items allowable for reimbursement in travel status for military members and DoW civilian personnel.

10.1.3. Reimbursement is authorized to Civil Air Patrol members for supplies, including fuel, lubricants, and other items required for vehicle and aircraft operations, through Air Force appropriations when the Patrol acts as an auxiliary of the Air Force. Reimbursement is also authorized to place equipment in serviceable condition or to improve and maintain equipment (including aircraft, motor vehicles, computers, and communications equipment) owned or leased by the Civil Air Patrol. Refer to 10 U.S.C. § 9494.

10.1.4. Conference Attendance

10.1.4.1. DoW requires specific approval to authorize and reimburse expenses for attending meetings of technical, scientific, professional, or similar private-membership non- Federal societies or organizations (JTR, Section 4, sections 0302 and 0321). Documentation supporting that approval must accompany the claim for reimbursement.

10.1.5. An employee required to serve as a notary public in connection with official duties is entitled to repayment of expenses incurred to obtain a notarial commission, as authorized by 5 U.S.C. § 5945. Reimbursable expenses include seals, embossing devices, recording and filing fees, and surety bonds required for notaries by state law. DoW Components must not reimburse claims for notarial professional-association dues or other non-essential services. The claim must include a statement that the notary commission is required to perform official duties as designated in Component or activity procedures, and a management official must approve the claimant's statement before submission to the certifying officer. There is no statutory authority to pay these expenses to military members.

10.1.6. Reimbursement of expenses to obtain professional credentials may be authorized for application fees, examinations, and certifications. The authority for reimbursement of professional accreditation fees is prescribed by 5 U.S.C. § 5757.

10.1.7. Personnel Held Captive

10.1.7.1. U.S. military personnel held captive who barter personal valuables during escape and evasion may file a claim for reimbursement. The claim must list the value of each article and show its age and condition at the time of barter. The appropriate commander or management official must approve the claim before submission to the certifying officer.

10.1.7.2. Civilian personnel held captive who barter personal valuables during escape or evasion should consult their Component's legal counsel when preparing the claim. The designated Component official must approve the claim before submission to the certifying officer.

10.1.8. In limited circumstances, the cost of room and board is reimbursable to sponsors of dependent children who require room and board away from their domicile (not within commuting distance), as prescribed by 20 U.S.C. § 926(b). See DoD Directive 1342.20, DoD Education Activity (DoDEA), for eligibility requirements for educating dependent children in overseas areas or at non-DoW schools, including its definition of dependent. A receipt for the sponsor's actual payment of room and board must support the claimed amount. A signed statement is also required from the school superintendent or principal that the room and board charges are reasonable for the area and that no less expensive alternative was available to provide adequate education at a school within the same comparable distance.

10.1.9. When DoW-operated schools are unavailable overseas, the DoDEA coordinates placing students in local public or private schools or in boarding schools. In limited circumstances, reimbursement for the education travel of student family members is authorized by 5 U.S.C. § 5924(4). A travel receipt must support the claim for reimbursement.

10.1.10. Title 10, U.S.C. § 1094a prescribes continuing medical education requirements. Individuals enrolled in approved medical correspondence courses may be reimbursed for course costs before course completion. Refer to 5 U.S.C. § 4109 and section 5.0 for additional guidance. The claimant must timely provide satisfactory proof of course completion to the certifying officer through appropriate Component channels to avoid debt collection for perceived non-completion.

10.1.11. Appropriated funds may be used for official representation purposes as prescribed in DoDI 7250.13. The Heads of DoW Components may authorize authorized individuals, or their designees, to expend Official Representation Funds only for official purposes. Receipts for personal expenditures must support the claim for reimbursement, and officials designated per DoDI 7250.13 must approve it before forwarding to the certifying officer for certification. See also the DoD Guidebook for Miscellaneous Payments (type payment codes OREV, ORGV, OREE, and ORGE) for additional policy.

10.1.12. Fees paid by award nominees, award recipients, and their supervisors and managers attending ceremonies may be reimbursed when the expenditures fall within the scope of the Government Employees Incentive Awards Act (5 U.S.C. §§ 4501-4506 and 10 U.S.C. § 1124). Fees may cover items such as meals, refreshments, plaques, and awards. DoW must not authorize advance payments. Individuals must request reimbursement on travel vouchers; if travel orders are not issued, the claimant must submit a claim with applicable receipts, approved by the designated management official, to the certifying officer.

10.1.13. Expenses for military attaché officers to maintain a suitable official residence are authorized, reimbursable, and may vary by location. The claimant must submit form DD281, "Voucher for Emergency or Extraordinary Expense Expenditures," to request and receive reimbursement. The Head of the DoW Component must approve claims before submission to the certifying officer. Title 10 U.S.C. § 127 prescribes policy for emergency and extraordinary expenses.

10.1.14. The JTR, Section 3, section 0206 prescribes allowable reimbursements for commonly incurred expenses for public or special conveyances used for transportation in and around duty stations. The claim for reimbursement must be supported by receipts and approved by the Component's designated approving official before submission to the certifying officer.

10.1.15. Military members assigned to a recruiting organization, or assigned recruiting duties as a primary or additional duty, are authorized reimbursement for actual and necessary expenses paid from personal funds. The JTR, Section 3, paragraph 020605 prescribes policy for reimbursement of actual and necessary costs. The claim must be supported by receipts and approved by the Component's designated approving official before submission to the certifying officer.

10.1.16. When local moves of military personnel's household goods are authorized per the JTR, Chapter 5, and made at personal expense, the claimant must submit a claim for reimbursement to the designated entitlement office. The claimant must support the claim with copies of the order directing the move, the authorization to move household goods at personal expense, and the paid receipt. The claimant must be reimbursed for documented receipts and expenses claimed per the
JTR.

10.1.17. Expenses Incident to Death of Personnel

10.1.17.1. Specific Component regulations authorize and prescribe the services and expenses for the care of deceased personnel. Title 10 U.S.C. § 1482 authorizes payment for services, supplies, transportation, and other expenses incurred by the next of kin and establishes limitations on the amount of reimbursement. The claimant must submit a claim for reimbursement supported by receipts for personal expenditures, and the Component's designated approving official must approve the claim before submission to the certifying officer. The payment of expenses incident to the recovery, care, and disposition of a decedent's remains is covered by
10 U.S.C. § 1481.

10.1.17.2. A contract with a local mortuary may cover primary expenses for active duty military. The Government pays primary expenses covered by the Prompt Payment Act (5 CFR 1315) directly to the mortuary.

10.1.17.3. Secondary expenses may be assigned to a mortuary or reimbursed to the next of kin for expenses incurred. Secondary expense payments, whether assigned or not, must be expedited.

10.1.18. Reimbursement

10.1.18.1. TRICARE limits beneficiaries' private-sector out-of-pocket costs to plan-specific copays, cost shares, and deductibles based on beneficiary category and selected plan. Health providers generally bill any excess cost directly to TRICARE, and the Managed Care Support Contractor pays it. Beneficiaries whose out-of-pocket payments for private-sector care exceed their plan limits may submit a claim for reimbursement. The claim must include paid, itemized invoices from the service provider and signatures of the claimant, approving official, and certifying officer. Visit www.tricare.mil to download the proper claim form, which includes full completion instructions.

10.1.18.2. Title 5, CFR, Subpart 339.203 prescribes policy for authorizing physical examinations to determine an employee's fitness for duty when such requirements are essential for performing the duties, clearly documented in the position description, and directed by the commanding officer or supervisor. Examinations may be procured through an approved agency purchasing method, or the employee may arrange and directly pay for the examination. Procured examinations are processed like other contractor invoices, or the employee may submit a claim for reimbursement. The employee must submit the claim to the appropriate official for approval before submission to the certifying officer. The claim must contain a chargeable line of accounting and the amount payable, supported by a paid statement from the physician or other evidence of payment. The activity requiring the examination must charge the reimbursement to its operating funds.

10.1.19. Title 5, U.S.C. § 4109 authorizes reimbursement for necessary expenses such as tuition and matriculation fees, library and laboratory services, and other services or facilities directly related to training. The claim for reimbursement must include receipts for each payment of $25 or more, details of the expenditures such as services received and dates rendered, signatures of the claimant and approving official, and certification by a properly appointed certifying officer before payment.

10.1.20. DCSA agents are authorized reimbursement for investigative costs such as parking fees, police and court record checks, transcripts, photographs, or miscellaneous investigative fees. DCSA Headquarters must provide the servicing entitlement office the accounting classification citation for the reimbursement. The claim must cite the appropriate legal, statutory, or other authority authorizing the reimbursement. The claimant must submit a claim supported by receipts and approval signatures from designated DCSA management officials.

title: Section 11.0: Miscellaneous Payments
content:
11.0    MISCELLANEOUS PAYMENTS

11.1    GENERAL

11.1.1. Purpose

11.1.1.1. A copy of all supporting documentation must accompany each payment request. Components must ensure the documentation is sufficient for an independent third party, such as an outside auditor, to understand and verify the basis of the entitlement, including the authority for the reimbursement as a liability of the DoW, and its value, timing, and funding source. The supporting documentation must clearly identify the parties approving and certifying the payment.

11.1.1.2. A designated approving official is appointed by the commanding officer, director, or designee, with oversight responsibility to ensure all payments or requests for reimbursement are necessary and for official Government purposes only. Components may also assign fiduciary responsibility to approving officials per Volume 5, section 5.0. Approving officials must provide information and data to certifying officers or disbursing officials in support of the payment, attesting to their accuracy. Approving officials must review all claims and verify that the request for payment or reimbursement of miscellaneous expenses was received per Component procedures.

11.1.1.3. All payment requests require supporting documentation for proof of receipt, approved by a designated approving official and certified by a properly appointed certifying officer before disbursement. Refer to Volume 5, section 5.0 for policy on appointing certifying officers via DD Form 577, Appointment/Termination Record - Authorized Signature, and distributing the form to the appropriate disbursing office. Certifying officers must make supporting documentation available for review by authorized personnel, as stated in Volume 5,
section 5.0.

11.1.1.4. Components must ensure all miscellaneous claims are paid from funds current and available to the accountable activity when the claim accrues, unless specifically authorized otherwise. All requests for payment or reimbursement of miscellaneous expenses must contain a valid line of accounting with funds obligated per Volume 3, section 8.0. Processing the request through a DoW payment system may require configuring unique standard document numbers.

11.1.1.5. Wage-related miscellaneous payments for awards and judgments must be submitted and paid through the civilian payroll office to ensure proper withholding of mandatory deductions. Refer to Volume 8, section 4.0 for mandatory payroll deductions.

11.2    FEES, CLAIMS, AND AWARDS

11.2.1. Attorney Fees Awarded

11.2.1.1. Attorney fees and other costs assessed in FOIA litigation are payable from operating funds of the Military Department, Defense Agency, Field Activity, or Combatant Command responsible for administering the initial FOIA determinations or contested record searches that are the subject of the litigation. The funding organization is not necessarily the organization named as a defendant. Components must make payments from funds current at the time of awarding attorney fees.

11.2.2. Attorney Fees Awarded under the Equal Access to Justice Act (EAJA)

11.2.2.1. Attorney fees and other expenses awarded to claimants under the EAJA are payable from funds available to the DoW activity at the time of the award. EAJA attorney fees are limited to $125 per hour (5 U.S.C. § 504), unless the adjudicating officer (deciding official), or the court in civil actions, determines the law allows a higher rate. Other expenses include those for expert witnesses and any study, analysis, engineering report, test, or project necessary to prepare the party's case. The amount payable is the amount approved by the adjudicating officer, or the court in civil actions, based on documentation from the adjudicating officer or the court.

11.2.3. Fiscal Service payments to the contractor will not include attorney fees payable in connection with an action filed by a contractor under the Contract Disputes Act of 1978 (41 U.S.C. §§ 7101-7109). Attorney fees awarded in these cases are payable from funds current at the time of award and available to the activity accountable for the contract obligation (28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)(4)).

11.2.4. Awards Made

11.2.4.1. Payment of the costs must occur within 30 days of their determination and acceptance by the contracting office. A copy of the decision, along with a statement of costs incurred and approved by the contracting officer, must support the certification of payment.

11.2.5. Counsel Fees and Other Expenses in Foreign Courts

11.2.5.1. When appropriate, contracts or letters of commission and understanding obligate the U.S. Government for payment of counsel fees, court costs, bail, and other expenses for obtaining copies of records, printing and filing fees, interpreter fees, witness fees, and other necessary and reasonable expenses. Payment of fines or civil damages is not authorized (32 CFR 845.5). Payment for bail is authorized when stated in an authorizing letter or message issued by the responsible officer citing 10 U.S.C. § 1037 as the authority. Members must sign an agreement to refund the U.S. Government the bail amount before posting bail (32 CFR 845.10). If the defendant forfeits bail, the individual must reimburse the DoW in cash or by payroll deduction via DD Form 139, Pay Adjustment Authorization.

11.2.6. Payment to Contractor When Contracting Officer Approves Claim under the Contract Disputes Act of 1978

11.2.6.1. If funds for the claim are available and the contractor does not appeal the contracting officer's decision, the responsible entitlement office must settle the claim from funds cited on the contract (41 U.S.C. § 7108 and 31 U.S.C. § 1304).

11.2.6.1.1. After final agreement with the contractor, the contracting officer must modify the contract using an SF 30, Amendment of Solicitation/Modification of Contract, to obligate the funds and document support for the payment, and must execute the modification before entitlement of the contractor's invoice.

11.2.6.2. If funds to pay the claim are not available, the contracting officer may refer the claim to the Armed Services Board of Contract Appeals (ASBCA) and request ASBCA approval of a settlement from the Judgment Fund. The Component must reimburse the Judgment Fund upon receipt of a bill from the Fiscal Service, from current and available funds or by obtaining additional funds (41 U.S.C. § 7108), as stated in section 2.11. Policy for payment of amounts under the Contract Disputes Act by the ASBCA or the Court of Federal Claims is in
section 2.10.

11.2.7. Payments to Reimburse the Fiscal Service for Payments in Settlement of Contractor Claims Upon certification by the Fiscal Service (TFM, Volume 1, part 6, chapter 3100), the amounts of contractor claims settled under the Contract Disputes Act of 1978 may be paid to the contractor by the Fiscal Service from the Judgment Fund. Amounts paid to contractors are reimbursable to the Fiscal Service from the appropriation available for the purpose of the contract or by obtaining additional funds for that purpose. If funds are not available in the proper account to cover invoices received from the Fiscal Service, the Component must request additional funds through appropriate channels. Amounts reimbursed to the Fiscal Service are not charged to the original fiscal year appropriation that funded the contract, unless the original appropriation was still current at the time of the judgment (Volume 3, section 8.0).

11.2.8. Interest Awarded Contractor

11.2.8.1. If claims involve antecedent liability, interest payments are chargeable to the appropriations current at the time the basic contract was executed (Volume 3, section 8.0), or by obtaining additional appropriations for reimbursement (41 U.S.C. § 7108).

11.2.8.2. This section excludes interest penalty claims related to the Prompt Payment Act (PPA) cited in 5 CFR part 1315. Per 31 U.S.C. § 3902, PPA interest must be paid from funds available for administering the program for which the interest was incurred, or from funds financing the operation of the Military Department or defense agency associated with the invoice or contract payment. All interest payments must be charged to the fiscal years in which they accrue. If appropriations are cancelled, any interest payment must be charged to the current fiscal year (31 U.S.C. § 1553(b)(1)).

11.2.9. Return

11.2.9.1. Rewards. Receipt of any authorized communication, oral or written, from a military or federal law enforcement officer or agency requesting active cooperation in apprehending or delivering to military control an absentee or deserter wanted by the Military Services constitutes the basis for a reward. A reward must not exceed the amount cited in 10 U.S.C. § 956 for apprehending absentees, deserters, or parole and mandatory supervised release violators.

11.2.9.2. Condition for Payment. A reward is payable only after notification is issued for the return to military control of the absentee, deserter, or escaped military prisoner. Notification consists of receipt of a DD Form 553, Deserter/Absentee Wanted by the Armed Forces, oral or written communication from military or federal law enforcement officials, or entry of the individual's name in the National Crime Information Center.

11.2.10. Cash Awards to Military Members

11.2.10.1. The award is payable against current funds available to the activity primarily benefiting, or the several funds or appropriations of the various activities benefiting (10 U.S.C. § 1124(e)). Refer to paragraph 11.1.1.5 for requirements on submission, payment, and mandatory payroll deductions. The claim must be submitted on an SF 1034, or electronic equivalent, and must provide the military member's Home of Record for state tax reporting. The only exception to withholding taxes on cash awards is payment to an enlisted member serving in a combat zone. See the Combat Zone Tax Exclusions in Publication #3 (2020), Armed Forces Tax Guide.

11.2.11. Under 10 U.S.C. § 2252, certain rewards are authorized and paid as follows:

11.2.11.1. A Military Department must not pay a reward of more than $500 in any case. Rewards are payable from current funds available for the Component concerned. The payment voucher must be supported by a copy of the reward offer and a statement by the commanding officer or designated representative that all conditions for payment of the reward and accountability for the property have been met.

11.3    PURCHASES OF SPECIAL ITEMS AND SERVICES

11.3.1. Advertising

11.3.1.1.
