Per 44 U.S.C. § 3702 and FAR 5.502, contracting officers must obtain written authorization from the DoW Component head, or from a person with written delegation of authority from the head of a DoW Component, before advertising in newspapers, trade journals, and similar publications (5 U.S.C. § 302(b)). This delegation cannot be re-delegated. Newspaper advertisements are not payable unless the claim includes the advertising bill and a copy of the written authority. Requirements for payment and retention of documents follow.

11.3.1.2. The requirement for written advertising authority from the head of a DoW Component, or from a person with written delegation of authority, does not apply to radio advertising (FAR 5.502(b)) unless required by Component policy. The other restrictive advertising provisions in 44 U.S.C. § 3702 do not relate to radio advertising. No statutory restrictions exist on using appropriated funds for radio advertising to promote objectives. Claimants must submit payment claims on an SF 1034, or other approved Component form, with a copy of the invoice and an affidavit of publication furnished by the advertising agency (FAR 5.503(d)).

11.3.2. Arbitrator services under negotiated grievance procedures of management and labor union agreements are authorized. These services are normally acquired by issuing a DD Form 1155, Order for Supplies or Services, which specifies payment terms and conditions and requires coordination between the civilian personnel office and the contracting support office. Funds must be reserved and obligated before executing the ordering or contracting action. On completion of services, the civilian personnel office, or a designated official, must certify receipt;

this certification is the receiving report required for payment. Payment is made using this certification, the arbitrators' billing statement, and the terms in the completed DD Form 1155. These payments are governed by the PPA (5 CFR part 1315), unless the DD Form 1155 contains a specific payment due date.

11.3.3. Using appropriated funds to buy or lease passenger motor vehicles must be specifically authorized by an annual appropriation act or other law (see 31 U.S.C. § 1343). The purchase cost limitation in 31 U.S.C. § 1343 excludes articles used with a car but not permanently attached to it or not an integral part of it (for example, tire chains, fire extinguishers, safety flares, removable seat covers, transportation of the vehicle, and taxes). Motor vehicles should be acquired from the most cost-effective source: purchase or commercial lease through the General Services Administration (GSA), or any other method less costly to the Government as validated by a cost comparison (DoD Manual 4500.36).

11.3.4. Appropriated funds may be used to purchase blood supplies from donors (24 U.S.C. § 30) or through civilian contracts (DoDI 6480.04) per the policies of the respective Military Services for persons entitled to medical treatment at Government expense.

11.3.5. The Component's designated personnel must prepare and certify payment of civilian uniform allowances on an SF 1034 or electronic equivalent. DoDI 1400.25, Volume 591, prescribes the amount payable per year and other uniform allowance policies. The payment voucher may include more than one employee. The payment must be charged to the same appropriation and subsidiary accounting data normally charged for the salary of the personnel concerned. See the Guidebook for additional information and policy.

11.3.6. Confinement of Prisoners in Civil Detention

11.3.6.1. Prisoners may be confined in civilian facilities used by the U.S. Marshals Service when DoW confinement facilities are not available or do not provide for the separation of male and female prisoners per DoDI 1325.07. Transferring commanders must determine whether a military confinement facility, including military or security police detention cells, is not reasonably available. If a facility used or approved by the U.S. Marshals Service is not reasonably available, a military prisoner may be transferred to a facility accredited by the American Correctional Association or by the State for confinement.

11.3.6.2. The Provost Marshal's Office, which transfers prisoners, must provide the entitlement office a certified voucher and supporting documents itemizing the confinement expenses (10 U.S.C. § 956). After entitlement, the disbursing office remits payment to the civil confinement facility. All military prisoners must be provided supplies necessary for personal hygiene and maintenance of good health. The Military Services may also provide supplies for a prisoner's comfort, set monetary or quantity limitations on any supplies, and set other limitations as Service corrections headquarters deems appropriate. Supplies issued to persons in a non-pay status are paid from appropriated funds. Health and comfort supplies provided to persons in a pay status are charged against their pay accounts or paid from their personal funds.

11.3.7. Fees required by local laws for certified copies or photocopies of public records, or documents required by a court or board, may be paid to the performing officials or legal entities. Current operation and maintenance funds may be used to purchase death certificates for deceased retired personnel. The claimant must sign a statement attesting that all resources to find beneficiaries were exhausted and none were found.

11.3.8. Discrimination Complaints

11.3.8.1. In discrimination complaint cases, attorney fees may be awarded under a no-fault settlement agreement, an informal adjustment, the decision of the Service director of Equal Employment Office (EEO), the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC), the Merit Systems Protection Board, an arbitrator, a Federal court, or other appropriate authority. After legal counsel reviews and approves the award letter, the EEO manager of the legal office must initiate or authorize the reimbursement claim. The Component's reimbursement request must be a joint payment to the complainant and the complainant's representative, supported by an award letter and approval. The claim must cite current operating funds. Policy on allowable and reasonable attorney fees is in 29 CFR part 1614.

11.3.8.2. The EEOC assigns an EEO Administrative Judge to hold hearings on formal discrimination complaints and otherwise process individual and class complaints for the EEOC. The activity where the alleged discrimination took place must fund expenses associated with these complaints, using operating funds current when the services are requested. The EEOC bills the activity for authorized and required expenses (29 CFR part 1614). The activity's chief EEO manager, or assigned designee, must review and approve the EEOC billing.

11.3.8.3. The chief office of counsel typically arranges court reporter services by submitting a request to the DoW Component contracting office. The activity where the alleged discrimination took place must pay court reporter costs, using funds current when services are requested. The activity's chief EEO manager, or assigned designee, must review and approve payment requests.

11.3.8.4. Interest payments related to discrimination cases, when permitted by statute, must be charged to funds current at the time of the award. The Treasury establishes the rate, which is not the rate used to compute interest under the PPA.

11.3.9. Emergency Notification Service (9-1-1)

11.3.9.1. If the telephone company imposes a 9-1-1 fee for its own service, duly permitted by the tariff to which all utility customers are subject, the charge is proper and payable by the DoW; the DoW has no immunity from such fees. If a state or local government imposes the charge and merely uses the telephone company as its agent, the charge is a tax from which the DoW is exempt.

11.3.9.2. If a military installation receives an invoice for a 9-1-1 charge imposed by a state or local government, the tax is not payable. If fees were improperly paid, refer to the collection policy in Volume 16, section 5.0 to recover them.

11.3.9.3. If it is unclear whether such charges are taxes or service charges, the designated entitlement office, or responsible certifying officer, must contact the base communications officer or higher authority. This clarification must be included in the entitlement and certification documentation supporting the payment request.

11.3.9.4. Telephone service to on-base residents is a private contract between the resident and the local telephone company. Residents charged for 9-1-1 services may not claim exemption based on immunity. If a resident of base housing lives in an area where the base provides all fire, police, and other emergency services, the charge may be for services the resident does not receive, and a challenge may be possible. Regardless of the basis for challenging a 9-1- 1 charge, it remains a private matter between the subscriber and the telephone company and is not a DoW reimbursable expense.

11.3.10. Hospital accreditation fees associated with the requirements in DoD Manual 6025.13, Enclosure 3 for medical facilities accredited by the Joint Commission on Healthcare Organization may be reimbursable. A deposit required for an initial customer may be reimbursable. Accreditation and certification on-site fees, invoiced 1 to 5 days after the survey event completes, are reimbursable for those requiring accreditation. Accreditation annual fees may also be payable, subject to the programs, services, volumes, and sites where service is provided.

11.3.11. If the loss was not caused by any fault or negligence of the Service member, reimbursement is authorized to compensate military personnel for clothing items destroyed, damaged, lost, abandoned, captured, or otherwise rendered unusable incident to military training or service (DoDI 1338.18). Personnel must submit an approved Service-specific Personal Clothing Claim form, or electronic equivalent. The Service member's activity billing office must prepare an SF 1034 or electronic equivalent for payment to the member.

11.3.12. Medical Services Provided by Civilian Non-Federal Sources

11.3.12.1. The military medical treatment facility (MTF) can refer members to civilian health care providers for diagnostic services, treatment, or both. On receipt of the civilian health care provider's itemized invoice, the claimant must submit a reimbursement request to their designated Component. The Component must prepare an SF 1034, or electronic equivalent, within 30 days from the later of receipt of an invoice or the date of acceptance of the care. The same standards apply to an approved claim for services rendered in connection with care of a deceased member.

11.3.12.2. Dependents and retired personnel are authorized certain medical care and diagnostic services under 10 U.S.C. §§ 1071-1085. When an MTF managing the care of dependent and retired personnel must refer them to civilian facilities for care beyond the MTF's capability, payment for related supplemental care is authorized. The claimant must submit the health care provider's itemized invoice to their designated billing Component. The Component must prepare an SF 1034, or electronic equivalent, within 30 days from the later of receipt of an invoice or the date of acceptance of the care.

11.3.13. The DoW must not pay for any service required to be provided by the local government when that service is financed from revenues raised by state or local taxation from which the Federal Government is exempt. Common examples are police and fire protection (10 U.S.C. § 2465(a)). Refer to 10 U.S.C. § 2465(b) for exceptions of authorized payments.

11.3.14. Per DFARS subpart 241.1 and DFARS subpart 241.2, the DoW may pay on the same basis as private users of services, based on the quantity of direct services received (for example, water and sewage). Generally, the DoW will not pay for municipal services unless private citizens and businesses also pay a charge for the same services.

11.3.15. Appropriated funds available for making or procuring supplies may be used to acquire copyrights, patents, and applications for patents; licenses under them; design, process, and technical data and computer software; and releases for past infringement or unauthorized use of technical data or computer software, if the acquisition relates to supplies or processes produced or used by or for, or useful to, the DoW (10 U.S.C. § 3793).

11.3.16. Absent express Presidential exemption, DoW facilities must abide by state or local laws for abatement and control of pollution. Facilities may incur costs complying with these laws to obtain permits and pay the associated natural-resource management fees. Submit an SF 1034, or electronic equivalent, to pay these expenses. The payment request must include supporting documentation identifying the permit application fee and other related fees, approved by the base civil engineer or assigned designee.

11.3.17. Reciprocal Mutual Aid Agreements for Fire Protection

11.3.17.1. If the claims affect current funding for fire protection, FEMA will contact the installation during its claim processing and adjudication procedures. The DoW installation must provide the information requested, in coordination with the civil engineer, fire protection unit, and staff judge advocate, and must provide the complete name and address of the disbursing office, including the Disbursing Station Symbol Number, and an appropriation fund cite for fire protection funding so the Treasury can bill for reimbursement for approved claims paid.

11.3.17.2. All sums received as reimbursements for fire-protection costs incurred by any DoW activity must be credited to the appropriation or fund from which the fire-protection expenses were paid. If that appropriation's period of availability for obligation has expired, credit the fund or appropriation currently available for the same purpose (42 U.S.C. § 1856d(b)).

11.3.18. Representation and Contingencies Fund Use

11.3.18.1. This paragraph applies to disbursements against funds separately appropriated in the contingencies program, including representation, special expenses, and contingencies. Each fiscal year, Congress appropriates contingencies program funds under the statutory authority in 10 U.S.C. § 127 for use by the head of each DoW Component. Funding documents provide authority to obligate and expend contingency funds as approved, or as adjusted later during the fiscal year.

11.3.18.2. The head of a DoW Component must authorize the expenditure of Official Representation Funds by commanders for official entertainment or other official purposes, per 10 U.S.C. § 127 and DoDI 7250.13.

11.3.18.3. The Appropriation Act language for contingencies usually reads: "For emergencies and extraordinary expenses, to be expended on the approval of the Secretary of the cognizant Military Service, and payments may be made on their certificate of necessity for confidential military purposes." The following policies apply, depending on the type of payment involved.

11.3.19. Where water supply systems serving DoW organizations do not meet the standards in 40 CFR part 141, subpart C, special drinking water may be purchased with appropriated funds only when necessary from the Government's standpoint. The reimbursement claim requires a statement attesting the drinking water is non-potable, plus a public announcement or a copy of the water testing results. Examples include public water unsafe for human consumption, an emergency failure of the installation's water source, a temporary facility with no drinking water available within a reasonable distance, or no water fit for drinking available without cost or at a lower cost to the Government.

11.3.20. Support of Armed Forces Personnel in Confinement

11.3.20.1. Purchase of health and comfort items for personnel confined on-base is authorized for all military prisoners, subject to DoDI 1325.07. Reimbursement must be claimed using an SF 1034 or electronic equivalent. Supplies issued to persons in a non-pay status are paid from appropriated funds. Health and comfort supplies provided to persons in a pay status are charged against their pay accounts or paid from their personal funds.

11.3.20.2. The Military Confinement Facility commander must provide suitable clothing, on a temporary loan basis, to a prisoner confined without essential clothing. Permanent issue items, except distinctive prisoner clothing, are subject to personal funds withdrawal if the prisoner is in a pay status. All necessary clothing for a prisoner confined in a non-pay status is provided at Government expense.

11.3.21. Telephone and Television Service

11.3.21.1. Appropriated funds normally must not be used to pay for telephone service to private residences, except as identified in 31 U.S.C. § 1348 and DoDI 1100.21. Long distance calls from private residences for official business may be paid from appropriated funds when supported by properly certified vouchers.

11.3.21.2. Charges for official telephone and metered services for a period beginning in one fiscal year and ending in another may be paid from the appropriation current at the end of the service period (31 U.S.C. § 1308). This rule also applies to leased wire and teletypewriter services.

11.3.21.3. Telephone services provided for Service clubs, motion picture service, military Exchange store activities, and officers' and non-commissioned officers' messes within the United States are subject to federal communications taxes (26 U.S.C. § 4251 and
26 U.S.C. § 4252).

11.3.21.4. The telephone service contract may provide for payment at legally established rates. Under such contracts, rate increases approved by rate-setting authorities may be paid. Increased rates billed before approval by rate-setting authorities may be payable, but are subject to adjustment if the increase is not approved.

11.3.21.5. The office designated to receive telephone company bills must coordinate preparation and certification of the SF 1034, or an electronic equivalent, for payment.

Local Component procedures must confirm the number and active status of the phone lines or numbers billed and ensure the related costs reflect charges for official or other authorized use.

11.3.21.6. Forward the SF 1034 to the designated payment office with the telephone company's summary billing statement, which includes totals for the monthly plan and long distance charges. The responsible office must retain the detailed listings and schedules supporting the bill and must not attach them to the payment voucher unless local procedures require. Components must follow established local ethical conduct and related personnel policies and procedures when addressing reimbursement of costs for unauthorized use. Handle any funds collected per the Component's appropriation and fund deposit rules and regulations.

11.3.21.7. Government communication systems and equipment are only for official use and authorized purposes. Non-official use of Navy communication systems and equipment is at the commanding officer's discretion, provided the Navy incurs no additional cost and mission readiness is not degraded (OPNAVINST 2060.8B). The communications officer must collect unauthorized or unofficial charges on a DD Form 1131, Cash Collection Voucher, from personnel using the ship's communication service in an unauthorized manner and must immediately turn over the amounts collected to the disbursing office. When the telephone company bills the ship, the designated payment office must pay the telephone company using an SF 1034 to substantiate the payment.

11.3.21.8. Tenant-paid charges for necessary telephone wiring maintenance in base housing may be reimbursable per 31 U.S.C. § 1348. Internal wiring repair charges in family housing are reimbursable from maintenance funds; charges for unaccompanied personnel housing are reimbursable from current base funds.

11.3.21.9. Appropriated funds may pay reconnection expenses when a move results from Government action beyond the member's control and is directed at Government expense. Exclude expenses incurred during a permanent change of station (PCS) that may be reimbursable under the PCS orders or other related regulations.

11.3.21.9.1. Payment is authorized, as directed by the base commander, for mandatory assignment to Government-owned housing facilities, involuntary relocation to Government or non-Government facilities because of base renovation or condemnation proceedings, or termination of assigned quarters because of death of qualifying dependents.

11.3.21.9.2. Members are not authorized reimbursement for moves involving voluntary termination of assigned quarters, termination due to demotion to an ineligible grade or adverse conduct by a member, termination due to family separation (no hardship involved), or the member's voluntary movement from off-base to on-base quarters.

11.3.21.10. Reimbursement of the member's claim or a direct payment to the contractor is chargeable against the appropriation covered by the service.

11.3.21.10.1. A Service member may submit the same documentation through the billeting officer or base civil engineer to the entitlement office for a direct payment to the contractor. These payments are not subject to the PPA. The payment voucher must contain the statement, "Payment is being made for the following individual(s) for reconnection services on the following dates." Activity controls and procedures must ensure no duplicate reimbursement is later paid to the Service member.

11.3.21.11. Support the reimbursement or direct payment to the contractor with the following:

11.3.21.11.1. The member's letter requesting reimbursement for reconnection charges already paid, or a direct payment to the contractor for charges not yet paid. The member must certify the invoiced amount includes only charges incurred restoring telephone or television services previously provided at the old location and includes no charges for new services or equipment.

11.3.21.11.2. A copy of the telephone or television company invoice, certified by the chief of services or base civil engineer, showing only reconnection charges. All other charges are the member's responsibility and must be paid separately.

11.3.22. Tuition and Training

11.3.22.1. Tuition and training reimbursements to employees are miscellaneous payments. 5 U.S.C. § 4109 authorizes reimbursing employees for necessary training expenses (for example, tuition and matriculation fees; library and laboratory services; purchase or rental of books, materials, and supplies; and other services or facilities directly related to employee training). Refer to DoDI 1322.25 for additional tuition and training guidance.

11.3.22.2. Tuition assistance for military personnel must be paid directly to the academic institution per that institution's contract terms. Reimbursing the member for other related expenses requires a properly certified SF 182, Authorization, Agreement and Certification of Training, or other Component-approved form. Component procedures must ensure specified annual and per-course-hour reimbursements do not exceed allowable limits and must prevent duplicate payments.

11.3.22.3. Direct reimbursements to employees for necessary training expenses, such as books and supplies, require a miscellaneous payment request. Employees must submit these requests on an SF 182 or other Component-approved form. Refer to DoDI 1400.25, Volume 410 for additional policies and procedures on training, education, and professional development activities for civilian employees.

11.3.22.3.1. The training must be a regularly scheduled, off-the-shelf course, training conference, or instructional service available to the public and priced the same for everyone in the same category (price per student, course, program, service, or training space). To minimize employee reimbursements, the preference is to pay the training provider directly.

11.3.22.3.2. Payments prohibited as tuition or other training expenses include overtime, holiday, and night differential pay, and membership fees, per DoDI 1400.25, Volume 410 and 5 U.S.C. § 4109.

11.3.22.4. Advance payment of tuition and other expenses is authorized (5 U.S.C. § 4109 and 31 U.S.C. § 3324) when the training facility renders, or refuses to render, a billing. The SF 182 must identify the training facility by name and address, the amount payable to the facility for the tuition advance, and the amount payable to the trainee for purchase of books, library, and laboratory services. Submit the SF 182 to the entitlement office to support paying the advance as a miscellaneous payment.

11.3.23. Tuition Refunds

11.3.23.1. When the DoD Education Activity (DoDEA) determines refunds are payable to sponsors of tuition-paying students at DoW-operated schools, refunds are normally a prorated tuition amount when enrollment terminates before the end of the grading period (DoDEA Administrative Instruction 7200.01). A refund of advance tuition payment is authorized only based on a full grading period. A grading period is any of the four periods established by the school and covered by student report cards.

11.3.23.2. The school administrator must ensure deposit funds are available and prepare an SF 1034 that includes the student's name, enrollment termination date, and the amount authorized for refund.

11.3.23.3. The entitlement office must pay the voucher only after reviewing it for propriety and confirming related funds are available in deposit fund accounts.

11.3.24. Contract quarters are reimbursable to the contractor for personnel traveling on official orders in connection with FMS. The Security Assistance Management Manual (DoD 5105.38M, Section 9), Volume 15, section 8.0, and other appropriate DoW Component regulations prescribe the applicable travel policy. The claimant must prepare an Optional Form (OF) 1164, Claim for Reimbursement for Expenditures on Official Business, an SF 1034, or other Component-approved form or electronic equivalent, and submit it with a copy of the official orders for reimbursement.

11.4    PROFESSIONAL LIABILITY INSURANCE (PLI)

11.4.1. Certain civilian employees (law enforcement officer, supervisor, management official, or temporary fire line manager) may be eligible for PLI reimbursement up to one-half of the insurance premium costs incurred annually, not to exceed $150 per year (see 5 U.S.C., chapter 59, subchapter IV and DoDI 1400.25, Volume 885).

11.4.2. An employee must submit the insurance policy and proof of payment to the servicing Human Resource Office/Civilian Personnel Office (HRO/CPO), plus a completed OF 1164, SF 1034, or other Component-approved form or electronic equivalent, certified by the HRO/CPO approving official, and an invoice from the insurance carrier. The invoice must include the issuing company's name, the policy number, and proof of payment. If it is not evident to the paying office that the carrier's invoice or the policy itself is a qualified professional liability policy, the paying office must return the invoice to the employee and request evidence that the policy's sole purpose is liability insurance. The reimbursement is not reportable as taxable income and not subject to IRS Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement, reporting.

11.5    GOVERNMENT CHARGE CARDS CENTRALLY BILLED ACCOUNTS (CBAS)

11.5.1. This section provides financial management policy for CBA billings ("invoices" in this policy). GSA's Government-wide SmartPay3 contract and applicable DoW-tailored task orders authorize CBA programs for DoW. The Government Travel Charge Card program has two types of travel cards: the Individual Billed Account (IBA) and the CBA. Section 18 contains the financial management policy for IBAs. CBA transportation accounts are issued to DoW activities and are restricted to purchasing air, rail, and bus tickets only for travelers not eligible for an IBA. Unit mission requirements determine CBA credit limits. There are two types of CBAs:

11.5.1.1. A unit travel card may be issued to an individual or unit for group travel only when cost-effective and in the mission's interest. Unit cards accommodate groups such as new recruits, prisoners, and foreign nationals participating in an official DoW-sponsored program or activity.

11.5.2. CBA contractors must furnish a monthly invoice or statement of account showing charges made during the billing cycle. The invoice must contain the elements specified in section
8.0. The date the Billing Office receives the invoice starts the PPA clock.

11.5.3. Officials must work together to ensure accuracy, propriety, and legality over centrally billed accounts and related payments. Volume 5, section 5.0 provides the roles and responsibilities of accountable officials for CBA programs. The certifying officer must ensure only certified payment packages are forwarded for payment.

11.5.4. Accountable officials must maintain documentation at all levels to support the integrity of Government CBA programs and to facilitate reconciliation and payment of CBA transactions. Accountable officials must establish clear audit trails for CBA transactions by maintaining documentation supporting each purchase, such as travel orders/authorizations; requisitions, including cross-references to any related Blanket Purchase Agreements; telephone and mail order logs; receipt records; and credit slips (DoDI 5154.31, Volume 4). Certifying officers must review payment packages to ensure the information agrees with all supporting documentation before certification and submission to the entitlement office for payment. Volume 5, section 15.0 prescribes certifying officers' responsibility to make records and supporting documents accessible to authorized users.

11.5.5. Government CBA owners must dispute, or report as fraud, questionable transactions with the issuing bank per the timetable and provisions of the issuing bank contract and local procedures. Approving officials must notify the entitlement office by annotating the invoice or invoice package to show reductions for disputed charges, and must maintain records tracking disputed transactions to full resolution.

11.5.6. Designated entitlement office personnel rely on the certifying officer to ensure the validity, legality, and accuracy of certified invoice packages. The designated entitlement office must ensure all certified invoice payment packages undergo prevalidation to confirm funding availability, and must ensure a DD Form 577 is on file to verify all manually and electronically certified payment packages.

11.5.7. Approving officials in billing offices submitting CBA Billing Statements must ensure proper audit trails exist and documentation is available to support all charges and CBA payments. The certifying officer must retain documentation, both paper and electronic records. Refer to Volume 1, section 9.0, Figure 9-1 for statutory retention requirements.

11.6    PAYMENTS UNDER REAL PROPERTY LEASES

11.6.1. Leases are subject to the statutory and regulatory provisions applicable to DoW contracts and to lease-specific statutory provisions. A lease is a contract conveying the use of land or buildings for a specified time at a specified rate of compensation. Leases describe the premises, period, purpose, rent amount, payment method, special or operational services included (such as heat, light, water, and janitorial services), and any restoration provisions. If the lessor fails to provide the services the lease calls for, the lessee (DoW) may pay the cost and deduct the amount from the lease rental payments.

11.6.2. Rent

11.6.2.1. Recurring rental charges are paid without individual vendor invoices. At the end of each rental period, the using activity or designated payment office must prepare an SF 1034 or an electronic equivalent. The claim must identify the lease, confirm the property's use or availability during the rental period, include all relevant supporting documentation, and be processed per the lease provisions. Refer to the Guidebook for SF 1034 preparation instructions. Intra-Governmental lease or rental payment transactions must be processed using the Intra- Governmental Payment and Collection (IPAC) System or the G-Invoicing process, as prescribed by the TFM, Volume 1, Part 2, Chapter 4700, Appendix 5, Section 3, and Appendix 8.

11.6.2.2. At the end of each calendar year, report yearly rental payments of $600 or more to the IRS. Do not report payments to real estate agents. See the DFAS Tax Office website and section 6.0 for additional information and policy on 1099 reporting.

11.6.3. Party Entitled to Rental Payment

11.6.3.1. If DoW occupies land under a lease, the rental payment cannot be avoided because of any defect in the lessor's title at the time of entering into the lease agreement.

11.6.3.2. If DoW occupies land owned by several tenants-in-common under an agreement with one of them, and without objection by the others, that tenant-in-common is entitled to receive the rent.

11.6.3.3. If property leased to DoW sells on one day and the deed of conveyance is executed on another day, the grantee is entitled to receive the rental only from and after the date the deed is executed.

11.6.3.4. Rent liability does not become payable day-by-day; it becomes due in total on the dates set forth in the lease. The payment is not prorated among several owners who owned the premises for portions of the rental period. When leased property is sold, the seller must furnish a copy of the deed of sale for association with the lease contract. If the lessee is properly notified, payment is made to the titleholder on the due date.

11.6.4. Payment for leased land is not payable in advance. Payment for leases in foreign countries for periods of time is directed by the laws and ministerial regulations of those countries or local customs (10 U.S.C. § 2396).

11.6.5. DoW lease agreements must be clearly written regarding provisions for laying conduit and wires, making alterations, performing repairs, or making other improvements. Unless the lease clearly provides for such improvements at DoW expense, payment of any associated cost is not authorized.

11.6.6. Although taxes are not payable by DoW as the owner of real property, such taxes are properly payable as part of the rent when specifically included in the lease terms.

11.6.7. The lease terms determine the basis of payment. Leases with the standard U.S. Army Corps of Engineers termination clause require payment for the day after the termination notice is mailed plus 29 days. Analyze leases with other termination provisions individually, in consultation with local legal counsel, to determine the rent due upon termination.

11.7    PAYMENTS UNDER INDIVIDUAL SET-ASIDE CONTRACTS

Reimbursements to medical health service providers serving under ISAs may be subject to Federal tax and the Federal Insurance Contributions Act, depending on the contract terms. If required, DoW must report ISA payments at year end to the IRS on a Form W-2 per Social Security Administration/IRS guidelines (IRS Publication 15, Circular E). The DoW Tax Reporting Office must perform the W-2 reporting. Refer to Volume 8, section 9.0 for disbursements to taxing authorities.

11.8    PAYMENTS OF FEES FOR GUEST SPEAKERS, LECTURERS, AND PANELISTS

Payment of expenses associated with honoraria (guest speaker fees) is allowable for individuals who are not Government personnel. Honoraria are ex gratia payments to a speaker who has discretion over the content of the speech, presentation, or panel discussion on the general topic. Honoraria limitations do not restrict payment for presenting materials under a training contract involving a program of instruction. Per the Deputy Secretary of Defense, honoraria greater than $2,000 must be approved by the next higher organizational echelon. Approvals must follow the Component's established procedures.

11.9    INTRA-GOVERNMENTAL TRANSACTIONS

The TFM, Volume 1, Part 2, Chapter 4700, Appendices 5 and 8 prescribes policy for agencies to process intra-Governmental expenditure transactions through the IPAC system or the G-Invoicing process. IPAC is an electronic, internet-based collections and payment system. Refer to Volume 5 for additional policy on IPAC and G-Invoicing.

11.9.1. Border Clearance Inspectors Overtime Expenses

11.9.1.1. If border clearance inspectors must work overtime, or on Sundays and holidays, at a DoW installation, the installation must pay the overtime expenses incurred, including travel and subsistence, per 19 CFR 24.16 and 19 CFR 24.17. Border clearance officials regularly assigned to DoW installations receive no payment for travel and subsistence. When additional inspectors supplement the regularly assigned inspection staff, the DoW installation pays their overtime, travel, and subsistence.

11.9.1.2. If a DoW aircraft lands at a site other than a DoW installation, the aircraft's home station must pay the charges. When a DoW aircraft lands at another DoW installation, the installation providing the landing clearance services must accept the border clearance and inspection expenses. Financial managers must ensure funds are reserved to pay these claimed expenses. The DoW official designated to make the arrangements must maintain accurate records, submit overtime requests, certify receipt and acceptance of services, and forward billings for payment. Invoices from one agency may be consolidated and paid using a single IPAC or G-Invoicing transaction.

11.9.2. GSA

11.9.2.1. Except for normal wear and tear, DoW is pecuniarily liable for loss of or damage to GSA motor pool vehicles caused by negligence, misconduct, abuse, or inattention of military or DoW civilian personnel.

11.9.2.2. When damage occurs to a GSA vehicle, the vehicle operator must notify the GSA fleet management center, the operator's supervisor, and the state, county, or municipal authorities as required by law (41 CFR 101-39.401). GSA charges DoW for all costs resulting from damage, including vandalism, theft, and parking lot damage, case-by-case after reviewing the documentation required by 41 CFR 101-39.406. Upon receipt of GSA's damage assessment, use the IPAC system, G-Invoicing, or an SF 1080, Voucher for Transfers Between Appropriations and/or Funds, to pay GSA. The DoW Component to which the vehicle was assigned must provide the fund cite. The SF 1080 must identify the damaged vehicle and include the vehicle registry number, date of damage, register number of the SF 91, Motor Vehicle Accident (Crash) Report, and, when applicable, an SF 94, Statement of Witness.

title: Section 12.0: Commercial Transportation Payments
content:
12.0    COMMERCIAL TRANSPORTATION PAYMENTS

12.1    POLICY

12.1.1. Valid Line of Accounting (LOA). Every transportation shipment, when initiated, must have a valid LOA, including the Standard Document Number, or an associated Transportation Account Code (TAC) representing a valid LOA, before processing shipment requests, automating obligation recording, and certifying and paying invoices.

12.1.1.1. The Transportation Officer (TO) or Traffic Management Officer (TMO) must not provide transportation services without first obtaining proper supporting documentation, which at a minimum must include an authorization to use, and a citation of, a valid and funded LOA provided by a designated Fund Manager (FM) or financial management official.

12.1.1.2. If funding data supporting the shipment request fails validation when processed, the TO/TMO must suspend further processing until the shipping customer provides written (electronic or hardcopy) verification that the LOA is valid.

12.1.2. Funded Line of Accounting (LOA) and Associated Transportation Account Code (TAC). Shipping customers requesting transportation services must provide the TO/TMO the FM's written or electronic verification of a funded LOA (funding document), or the associated TAC, before the Government contracts with a carrier. The FM verification may be annotated on the Movement Request Order, usually a DD Form 1348-1A, Issue Release/Receipt Document, or DD 1149C, Requisition and Invoice/Shipping Document.

12.1.3. Anti-Deficiency Act (ADA). Any transportation shipment request processed without an authorized, valid, and funded LOA that obligates the Federal Government could violate the ADA under 31 U.S.C. § 1341. See Volume 14, sections 2.0 and 3.0 for additional information on appropriations and ADA violations.

12.1.4. Internal Controls. Internal controls must be in place to prevent duplicative or erroneous payments and to ensure DoW funds are spent appropriately and per all applicable laws and regulations. Refer to section 2.0 for additional policy on internal controls.

12.2    RESPONSIBILITIES

12.2.1. DFAS. DFAS maintains the software and database support for the Transportation Global Edit Table (TGET).

12.2.1.1. Each Component must update the TGET and ensure it contains valid LOAs and TACs.

12.2.2. Shipping Customers. Shipping customers can be individuals (Service members or civilian employees), units, or organizations within the Military Services, Defense Agencies, and other Government (non-DoW) agencies (federal, state, or local) requesting shipment of freight or personal property. The shipping customer must obtain and present to the TO/TMO, in written or electronic form, a valid and funded LOA from a designated FM.

12.2.3. Transportation Officer (TO) and Traffic Management Officer (TMO). TOs and TMOs are designated to process approved shipment requests for transportation or storage of military goods and other items entitled to be transported or stored at Government expense, and related accessorial or special services. The TO/TMO responsibilities include:

12.2.3.1. Suspending, and not accepting for shipment, any shipment request that is incomplete or not fully supported by the proper funding authorization; and

12.2.4. Fund Manager (FM). FMs are legally responsible for managing the appropriate use of funds and must assist and advise the TO/TMO on all financial-related matters. The FM must maintain and issue authorizations to use LOAs; coordinate and administer changes and modifications to LOAs and ensure updated data is uploaded to the TGET when necessary; provide a properly formatted LOA and associated TAC for input into the shipper system; resolve edit exceptions with the appropriate finance and accounting office; work with the TO/TMO and certifying officer to correct fund citation edit exceptions; provide the shipping customer documentation supporting funds availability and record the commitment/obligation appropriately; monitor execution of transportation costs and make adjustments as needed; and coordinate with the contracting officer and TO/TMO on transactions not yet certified for payment.

12.2.5. Certifying Officer

12.2.5.1. Ensuring the use of and certifying a SF 1113, Public Voucher for Transportation Charges, and ensuring the form includes the correct amount and fund cites when processing requests for payment, invoices, and other transportation documents;

12.2.5.2. Returning, and not certifying, vouchers that are inaccurate, inadequate, improper, incorrect, impermissible by law, or that contain invalid or inadequate funding information; and

12.2.6. Payment Office. Each payment office must:

12.2.6.1. Ensuring that a valid electronic record of the transportation obligation is posted in the accounting system before disbursing funds;

12.2.7. Contracting Officer

12.2.7.1. Including in the solicitation and contract all applicable services, provisions, clauses, and instructions concerning first destination transportation charges and electronic invoicing. The solicitation and contract must also identify a separate LOA for prepaid freight.

12.3    PAYMENT, AUDITS, AND COLLECTIONS

12.3.1. Request for Payment. The payment office must process a request for payment per the applicable commercial rates, fares, or charges for transportation by any common carrier of any property for the United States, or on its behalf, as approved by the TO/TMO, or designee, and certified by the certifying officer. The payment office designated in the contract must make transportation payments.

12.3.2. Prepayment Audit Title 31 U.S.C. § 3726

12.3.2.1. The DoW must forward all relevant electronic transportation billing documents to the GSA Transportation Audits Division as soon as possible after the end of the month; the TPPS contractor accomplishes this and provides all available shipping and payment data supporting DoW transportation payments (FAR 47.103-1 and 41 CFR 102-118.80).

12.3.2.2. The payment office must ensure, during its prepayment audit of a hardcopy (non-TPPS) TSP bill, that the TSP completed the SF 1113 fully, including the taxpayer identification number and standard carrier alpha code. An SF 1113 must accompany all hardcopy (non-TPPS) billings (41 CFR 102-118.100).

12.3.3. Prompt Payment Act (PPA). Transportation payments are subject to the PPA. PPA regulations require agencies to pay transportation bills within a set time period and pay interest penalties on late payments; the Secretary of the Treasury sets the interest rate under the
PPA.

12.3.3.1. Unless the contract specifies differently, transportation charges must be paid within 30 days after the original completed BOL reaches the designated billing office and the carrier certification is completed on the document.

12.3.3.2. If an invoice or accompanying documentation is incomplete or incorrect, the agency must give the TSP written notice of an apparent error, defect, or impropriety within 7 days of receiving the bill. See FAR 32.905.

12.3.4. The Director of the GSA Transportation Audits Division may audit and settle all transportation-related accounts (31 U.S.C. 3726). When instructed by GSA, the payment office must offset, as appropriate, any overcharge amounts due the United States from an unpaid carrier's bill. GSA may audit but may adjudicate and settle only when there is a dispute between the contractor and a government party to the contract.

12.3.4.1. The payment office must inform GSA if it does not have, and is not likely to have, a subsequent voucher to collect an overcharge.

12.4    TRANSPORTATION PAYMENT DOCUMENTATION

12.4.1. DoW may receive payment requests for transportation and related services in various forms, such as paper or electronic BOLs or periodic billing statements. Transportation offices must use commercial payment practices and electronic processing to the maximum extent possible per DoW policy in DTR 4500.9-R.

12.5    TRANSPORTATION DELIVERY TERMS

12.5.1. Delivery Terms Delivery

12.5.1.1. If the shipping contract includes both FOB origin and FOB destination delivery terms, the payment office must process each payment per the assigned contract terms for the goods shipped. See FAR 47.304-1(b) when the contracting officer includes both options to obtain the most advantageous delivery point.

12.5.2. Prepaid Freight Contractor

12.5.2.1. Contractors must support prepaid transportation freight charges with a copy of the carrier's receipted freight bill or evidence of receipt from the carrier. Evidence of payment is a receipted freight bill or BOL stamped or marked "To Be Prepaid" showing the charges receipted by the carrier. If this is not present, the BOL must bear a notation of the contractor's check number, the date paid, and proof of shipment.

12.5.2.1.1. If a receipted freight bill is not available, the contractor may instead support the freight-charge reimbursement claim with a copy of the transportation company's pickup record or of the contractor's internal business document showing the contractor turned the material over to a particular shipper. The contractor must support either document with a copy of the transportation company's invoice and a statement that the charges have been paid.

12.5.2.2. The payment office must not adjust the amount of freight charges if deliveries are made to places other than the FOB point.

12.5.2.3. The payment office must not adjust freight charges when a contractor contends that it paid transportation expenses the Government was obligated to pay.

12.5.2.4. The payment office must not deduct for potential excessive freight charges paid by the Government. The payment office must submit such adjustments to the respective legal counsel for referral to GSA for direct settlement as claims.

12.5.3. Reimbursable Prepaid Freight Reimbursement

12.5.3.1. The contractor must list this expense as a separate item on the invoice.

12.5.3.2. Contractor prepaid freight is not authorized within overseas areas. A contractor may be reimbursed for prepaid freight within the United States to a stateside port of embarkation for further shipping by Government means to the overseas area.

12.5.4. Excessive freight charges are freight costs a contractor incurs that exceed costs from the FOB point specified in the contract, and they are not reimbursable. The contracting officer must determine whether to pay excessive freight charges and provide that determination to the payment office before the payment office may make any approved payment adjustments.

12.5.4.1. If a contractor prepays freight for a shipment contrary to the current contract terms, the payment office may pay the shipment charges after receiving a contract modification authorizing the prepaid shipment. The payment may not exceed the cost the Government would have incurred. The contractor must attach the prepaid freight receipt to the request for payment.

12.5.5. Funding Determination Guidelines

12.5.5.1. Transportation charges for material shipped from one U.S. Government installation to another are not part of the contract expense to buy the material.

12.5.5.2. Transportation charges incurred to transport exchange or commissary supplies are charged to the applicable exchange fund or to the Defense Commissary Agency.

12.5.5.3. If freight is damaged in shipment, transportation funds must not be used to pay for replacement or repair of the damaged goods, regardless of which entity is responsible.

12.5.6. The Government generally retains the risk of loss or damage to its property that is not the legal liability of the commercial carriers and generally does not buy insurance for its property in the possession of commercial carriers (FAR 47.102). Where loss or damage risk resides with the carrier under a contract, the payment office may deduct from amounts due the carrier as follows, per 10 U.S.C. 2636(a)(1) and (2):

12.5.6.1. If deducted due to loss of, or damage to, material in transit for a military department, the payment office must credit the amount to the proper appropriation, account, or fund from which the same or similar material may be replaced; or

12.5.6.2. If deducted as an administrative offset for an overpayment previously made to the carrier under any DoW contract for transportation services, or as liquidated damages due under any such contract, the payment office must credit the amount to the appropriation or account from which payments for the transportation services were made.

12.5.7. Non-DoW agencies that wish to use DoW transportation services must provide funds with the appropriate LOAs to the sponsoring DoW Component before services are provided. The sponsoring Component may set up a reimbursable account where the third-party billing system can continue to pay the TSP and may establish a Service/DoW LOA/TAC for the paying office to process. See Volumes 11A and 11B for additional reimbursable policy.

12.6    NON-TEMPORARY STORAGE (NTS) AND LOCAL DRAYAGE OF HOUSEHOLD
GOODS (HHG)

12.6.1. An authorized DoW official must determine whether local drayage and storage of HHG is authorized when it provides the best value to the Government. TO/TMO responsibilities include obtaining these transportation services to meet operational needs.

12.6.1.1. All invoices for NTS services must be processed electronically through a TPPS using the policy in paragraph 12.9.

12.7    MISCELLANEOUS TRANSPORTATION PAYMENTS

12.7.1. DoW recruits, including Department of Homeland Security Coast Guard recruits, use meal checks while in transit from the Military Entrance Processing Stations (MEPS) to the Service training centers. Only an appointed MEPS Transportation Assistant (TA), or designated alternate, may issue meal checks, and only to DoW recruits traveling under JTR provisions.

12.7.1.1. Meal checks must not be used to buy alcoholic beverages, when travel is by commercial aircraft and passage rates include meal service, when an advance allowance of per diem has been received, when any portion of travel is OCONUS, or for payment of a gratuity.

12.7.2. Meal Tickets Meal

12.7.2.1. Meal tickets must not be used to buy alcoholic beverages, when travel is by commercial aircraft and passage rates include meal service, when an advance allowance of per diem is received, for travel of civilian employees, for travel of military dependents except when a dependent is authorized per diem to escort a deceased military sponsor, or for payment of a gratuity.

12.7.2.2. These payments are due 30 days after they reach the designated billing office. Late payments are subject to interest under the Prompt Payment Act (31 U.S.C. §§ 3901- 3907).

12.8    CLAIMS BY TRANSPORTATION SERVICE PROVIDER (TSP)

12.8.1. If a TSP sends a claim to a payment office, the payment office must make every reasonable and legal effort to resolve the dispute directly with the TSP.

12.8.1.1. If the original payment office cannot resolve the claim, it must forward the claim to the GSA Transportation Audits Division.

12.9    DOW THIRD PARTY PAYMENT SYSTEM (TPPS)

12.9.1. All DoW Components using the TPPS service must implement local internal controls to prevent, detect, and report unauthorized transactions, as outlined in section 2.0, paragraph 2.2. Managers must ensure adequate separation of duties and limit system access to only those individuals necessary to accomplish assigned tasks. The annual-reconciliation policy in subparagraph 12.9.2.3 reinforces the DTR, Part II, Chapter 212, and Part V, Appendix A, which identifies the reviews and controls needed for timely, accurate processing of transportation bills. DoW Components and transportation offices must work closely with the DFAS to perform root cause analysis and develop automated tools and business process solutions to improve the reconciliation process, including use of Advanced Analytics where feasible. The infrastructure should also include performance metrics for Component accountability.

12.9.2. Certification, Reconciliation and Payment Processing,

12.9.2.1. The certifying officer must review and certify the monthly invoices, ensure each invoice contains valid and adequate funding information and is accurate, correct, and permissible by law, and identify any transactions that do not belong to their TPPS account. The certifying officer must apply the certification criteria in subparagraph 12.2.5, the DTR 4500.9-R, Part II, Chapter 212, and Volume 5, section 5.0.

12.9.2.2. The certifying officer, with the payment office, must reconcile the account activity section of each TPPS monthly summary invoice promptly to identify carrying- balance discrepancies, resolve past-due amounts, and verify that all fees and adjustments on each invoice are correct. Components must reconcile and pay all transportation accounts in full annually, by the end of the first quarter following the end of the FY; for example, charges incurred during FY 2021 must be reconciled and paid in full by the end of the first quarter of FY 2022. The certifying officer must communicate any reconciliation issues to the payment office promptly.

12.9.2.3. The certifying officer must return, and must not certify, any invoice that does not contain valid and adequate funding information or that is not accurate, correct, or permissible by law.

12.9.2.4. In addition to assisting the certifying officers when necessary, the payment office must ensure that the TPPS monthly invoice is paid on time. Late payments are subject to the applicable PPA interest penalty (31 U.S.C. §§ 3901-3907). All interest penalties paid appear in the next month's fees and adjustment section of the monthly summary invoice and must be reconciled with the total and interest payments previously made.

title: Section 13.0: Payment for Postal Services and Small Package Delivery Costs
content:
13.0    PAYMENT FOR POSTAL SERVICES AND SMALL PACKAGE DELIVERY COSTS

13.1    PAYMENTS

13.1.1. Methods of Payment for Postage

13.1.1.1. Payments to service providers other than the USPS must use Treasury payment methods, such as automated clearing house (ACH), electronic funds transfer (EFT), or another Treasury-approved means of paying the vendor.

13.1.2. Metered or permit-mail payments must use EFT transactions to commercial banks the USPS designates as its financial agents. Postage payments must not be held in postal vendor accounts unless the DoW Component has statutory authority or prior written Treasury approval.

13.2    INSTALLATION OFFICIAL MAIL MANAGERS (OMM)

13.2.1. OMM appointment must be in writing. OMM appointments are reserved for commissioned, warrant, and noncommissioned officers (Enlisted-6 or higher), or DoW civilians (General Schedule-9 or higher); this requirement may be waived when the activity has no personnel in the grades specified. The OMM function is inherently Governmental and must not be contracted out.

13.2.2. Each installation has an OMM who must plan and coordinate outgoing postal and delivery purchases. The OMM must work closely with facility personnel to minimize postage requirements and with managers to ensure the person who decides to send any significant volume of mail also controls the postage funds. The OMM is responsible for interpreting and carrying out the Private Express Statutes (USPS Publication 542) within the organization; the acquisition, use, or disposition of supplies and property; budgeting for and expending appropriated funds for postage and fees; overseeing the monthly reconciliation of trust and debit accounts; and reporting requirements.

13.3    CENTRALIZED TRUST AND DEBIT ACCOUNTS

13.3.1. CAPS

13.3.1.1. The GSA Smart Pay credit card may be used for all transactions for which the USPS accepts the card. When there is a choice, use the CAPS or CMRS trust account instead of a GSA Smart Pay card.

13.3.1.2. Advance deposit trust accounts at local post offices may be used when one of the preceding methods is not available. Advance deposit trust accounts are not authorized at military post offices.

13.3.2. CAPS account use is a local decision; CAPS accounts are not available at overseas military post offices. CAPS accounts may include customer meter, business reply mail (BRM), and permit imprint advance deposits. A payment into a centralized trust or debit account is an advance deposit payment to the post office. The OMM must monitor and reconcile each centralized trust or debit account to ensure receipt of services paid in advance. An OMM who establishes centralized trust or debit accounts must maintain a record of all transactions in each account and is responsible for each account balance.

13.3.3. Centralized Trust and Debit Account Payment Process

13.3.3.1. The OMM must request funds to set up or replenish each centralized trust or debit account by submitting a SF 1034, Public Voucher for Purchases and Services Other Than Personal. The OMM must ensure funds are available and approved by the designated approving official and a properly appointed certifying officer.

13.3.3.2. The OMM charges postal services against a trust or debit account as required. The USPS issues a receipt for each charge to a centralized trust or debit account. The OMM verifies services received on the postal receipt and reduces the advance by the amount shown on the receipts. The OMM must identify receipts to each trust or debit account.

13.3.3.3. One SF 1034 can establish or replenish more than one trust or debit account. The SF 1034 must identify the amount to be deposited into each centralized trust or debit account. Once the designated finance and accounting office makes a deposit into an account, the OMM has limited authority from the USPS to transfer funds between trust or debit accounts. If a transfer between accounts is necessary, the OMM must coordinate the transaction with the designated finance and accounting office and the USPS. The designated finance and accounting office must record the transfer using an Optional Form 1017-G, Journal Voucher, or equivalent.

13.3.3.4. The OMM must reconcile the trust accounts monthly with the USPS transactional documentation. The designated finance and accounting office confirms the balance in each centralized trust or debit account monthly with the OMM. The OMM must provide documentation supporting any unexplained difference and report those findings to the Comptroller of the designated finance and accounting office. The OMM and the designated finance and accounting office must jointly review any unresolved discrepancy. Service-specific or locally developed, automated or manual worksheets must be used to assist reconciliation and track postal expenditures. All Official Mail and Distribution Centers must maintain this information. The OMM must submit a written letter to the USPS to correct account errors.

13.3.3.5. Advance payments for any centralized trust or debit account are limited to the current quarter's postal requirements. The designated finance and accounting office and the OMM must review balances against the postal requirements monthly. When required, the OMM must adjust balances by allowing the trust or debit account to decrease with use, or by submitting a request (SF 1034) to the designated finance and accounting office to deposit more funds for quarterly postal requirements.

13.3.3.6. When the USPS refunds cash for unused services in a trust or debit account, the OMM must submit a written request to the USPS to process the refund to the appropriate DoW Component account via IPAC or EFT. If the USPS cannot send the refund via IPAC or EFT, the OMM must request reimbursement by check from the USPS using a Postal Service (PS) Form 3533, Application for Refund of Fees, Products and Withdrawal of Customer Accounts. Each PS 3533 is uniquely barcoded and no longer available online; the OMM must contact the local Post Office to secure a PS 3533 for each refund transaction. The OMM must submit the USPS refund check to the designated disbursing office with a DD Form 1131, Cash Collection Voucher, for deposit as a collection.

13.4    MISCELLANEOUS PAYMENTS

13.4.1. The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Document Services is the DoW single manager for printing services (DoDI 5330.03). All DoW Components must procure official business envelopes and other document services from DLA at the DLA Document Services link.

13.4.2. All DoW activities must use only prepaid postage. When the environment will not support the electronic processes, an OMM that purchases postage stamps for official use from the local post office may use a Government purchase card. Responsible commanders or their designated representatives, postal officers, and Military Post Office supervisors must audit all working postal accounts advanced by the USPS at least monthly.

13.4.3. Postage Due Costs

13.4.3.1. Under normal circumstances, DoW mail rooms do not accept postage due mail; they return it to the sender at the sender's expense.

13.4.3.2. As an exceptional circumstance, DoW Components engaged in a hostile environment or operating under arduous conditions may send official matter through the USPS when postage is not available. The addressee must not refuse postage due penalty mail from military units engaged in hostile operations and must pay the cost of postage.

13.4.4. Costs for address correction in CAPS are an ancillary service and must be paid by EFT. Supporting documentation must accompany each payment request.

13.4.5. Payment for express mail is made with stamps, metered postage, or through an express mail corporate account, which is similar to a trust account officially authorized by the OMM. Payments into an express mail account are advances to the USPS, controlled similarly to trust account payments; refer to section 13.3. The OMM submits PS Form 5639, USPSCA Application and Payment Authorization Form, to establish the account. The USPS provides the OMM a monthly statement. The OMM must reconcile this account with the USPS at least monthly. The designated finance and accounting office confirms the account balance with the OMM monthly.

13.5    SMALL PACKAGE DELIVERY COSTS

13.5.1. The approved method for billing and payment of commercial small package express shipments is the authorized electronic processes DoW uses for transportation. When the environment will not support the electronic processes, or business reasons preclude their use, a waiver may be requested from the Office of the Secretary of Defense (Transportation Policy) per the Defense Transportation Regulation, Chapter 212, section C.3. Waiver requests must contain detailed justification why electronic means cannot be used and a proposed date when the electronic requirement will be met.

title: Section 14.0: Payment Provisions for Grants and Other Instruments of Assistance
content:
14.0    PAYMENT PROVISIONS FOR GRANTS AND OTHER INSTRUMENTS OF ASSISTANCE

14.1    SUBMISSION AND PAYMENT RESPONSIBILITY

14.1.1. Administering Office

14.1.1.1. The award recipient must certify and forward payment requests for the performance period to the administering grants office or required payment request system. The responsibilities of the administering grants office for payment requests are specified in 32 CFR 22.810. When the DoW awarding office is not using a grant payment system as described in paragraph 2.1, payment requests must be submitted and authorized per section 22.810, and the administering grants office must review and certify that the payment request or electronic equivalent is legal, proper, and correct (Volume 5, section 5.0). The administering grants office must also ensure the payment request complies with the award terms and that the recipient will not have excess cash on hand, based on expenditure patterns.

14.1.2. The award must designate the specific payment office that will make payment (typically the Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS)). The payment office must verify the propriety, adequacy, and completeness of any required documentation substantiating amounts to be paid by the DoW, and must retain all hardcopy award documentation, or have access to electronic award documentation, supporting the payment file.

14.2    INTERNAL CONTROLS

14.2.1. The agency head must establish controls that ensure obligations and costs comply with applicable laws. Safeguards must be in place to ensure DoW grants comply with the awarded purpose, are adequate to pay the request, and are expended within the constraints reflected in the grant. The Single Audit process, and an agency's procedures for resolving related audit findings, are controls that help assure these objectives, consistent with OMB Circular A-123 and the Single Audit Act (31 U.S.C. 7501-7507) and the post-award responsibilities in 32 CFR Part 22, subpart H.

14.2.2. Each DoW agency that provides Federal awards must review recipient audits to determine whether audit findings require corrective actions and must perform follow-up procedures to ensure those corrective actions are implemented (2 CFR Part 200, Subpart F, 200.513(c)(3) and 200.514(e)).

14.2.2.1. DoW must rely on and use single audits, which independent auditors conduct in the oversight of Federal awards provided to states, local governments, Indian tribes, institutions of higher education, and non-profit organizations. DoW may request additional audits of such awards when required by regulation or as needed to ensure effective use of the awards, and must plan and implement any additional audit effort to avoid duplication and separately fund it.

14.3    PAYMENT REQUEST

14.3.1. Payment Request Forms Except

14.3.1.1. A DoW Component must obtain approval for any variation from OMB- approved forms or formats, including the use of additional or electronic data elements, or modification of the associated instructions for recipient entities submitting the information. For non-construction programs with states, local governments, institutions of higher education, and other non-profit organizations, recipients may request advance payments or reimbursements on SF 270, Request for Advance or Reimbursement, or electronic equivalent, or other prescribed forms or formats as necessary (32 CFR 34.12(d)).

14.3.1.2. For construction programs, each Federal awarding agency must use the SF 271, Outlay Report and Request for Reimbursement for Construction Programs, as the standard form, or electronic equivalent (41 CFR 105-72.302(m)(2)). DoW may use the SF 270 in lieu of the SF 271 when the DoW-awarding agency determines it provides adequate information to meet Federal needs.

14.3.2. For payments to commercial recipients, the grants office may authorize recipients to use SF 270 or SF 271, or prescribe other forms or formats as necessary (32 CFR 34.12(d)).

14.3.3. When the administrative grants office must authorize payment requests per 32 CFR 22.810, it must review each payment request to ensure the request complies with award terms, available funds are adequate to pay the request, and the recipient will not have excess cash on hand based on expenditure patterns. To ensure timely payments, the administrative grants office must certify and forward the request to the designated payment office at least 3 working days before the end of the following periods:

14.3.3.1. No more than 7 calendar days after the administering office receives the recipient's request when electronic commerce is used (for example, Electronic Data Interchange to request the payment and EFT to make the payment).

14.3.3.2. No more than 30 calendar days after the administering office receives the recipient's request when it is not possible to use electronic commerce.

14.3.3.3. No more than 7 calendar days after each date specified by the award when payments are authorized in advance on a predetermined payment schedule, provided the designated payment office received the payment schedule at least 30 calendar days before the scheduled payment date.

14.4    DEBT COLLECTION FOR GRANTS AND COOPERATIVE AGREEMENTS

14.4.1. Funds paid to the recipient in excess of the amount to which it is entitled constitute a debt to the DoW. Grants officers must perform post-award administration of grants and cooperative agreements per the DoDGARs. Primary responsibility for collecting debt resulting from a grant or cooperative agreement rests initially with the grants office (see 32 CFR 22.820). DoW awarding offices must use the Debt Collection Office (DCO) of the designated payment office as the primary debt collection option. If DFAS is not the designated payment office, DoW awarding offices may use the Debt Management Office of DFAS for further debt collection and administrative offset opportunities, after first using the DCO. Refer to Volume 16, sections 1.0, 2.0, and 5.0 for additional detailed policy.

14.4.1.1. If the recipient has neither paid the amount due nor provided notice of intent to file an appeal within 30 days of the grants officer's decision, the grants officer must send a demand letter to the recipient, with a copy to the DCO (see Volume 16, section 2.0 for general policy requirements of debt letter notifications).

14.4.1.2. The DCO of the designated payment office must conduct any further debt collection activity, including issuing any additional demand letters (32 CFR 22.820). The DCO must follow collection policy in Volume 16, section 5.0 unless the DoDGARs, or the applicable grant or cooperative agreement, explicitly prescribes a different procedure.

14.4.1.3. Grants offices must obtain each grant recipient's TIN via the SAM to collect and report delinquent debts.

14.4.2. Collecting delinquent debts owed by the recipient may require administrative offsets per OMB Circular A-129. When taking an administrative offset, the DCO must follow the due process in 31 CFR 901.2, Demand for Payment, and 31 CFR 901.3, Collection by Administrative Offset (also see Volume 16, sections 2.0 and 5.0 for additional policy concerning offsets). Administrative offset is not required in every instance in which a source of funds may be available. Either the payment office or the accounting office must make a case-by-case determination, with the grants officer responsible for the award against which the offset will be applied. Per 32 CFR 22.820(e), the following are examples when an offset must not be taken:

14.4.2.1. Debt recovery by an administrative offset must not occur when the grants officer determines that the offset will substantially interfere with, or defeat the purpose of, the program for which the offset is contemplated.

14.4.2.2. Generally, grants and cooperative agreements paid in advance are not subject to offset. If in the best interest of the Government, the payment office may request that the issuing grants officer convert the agreement to a reimbursable method of payment to enable an administrative offset.

title: Section 15.0: Contract Reconciliation
content:
15.0    CONTRACT RECONCILIATION

15.1    RESPONSIBILITIES

15.1.1. Responsible Contract Reconciliation Agents (RCRAs) manage daily contract reconciliation operations and must complete contract reconciliations. The RCRA must review the reconciliation request, determine the appropriate level of effort, set the priority, coordinate assistance, accept or reject reconciliation results, approve adjustments, and ensure refunds or demands for payment are initiated. The User Manual for the Standard Contract Reconciliation Tool (SCRT) contains instructions on the RCRA's role.

15.1.2. The Director, Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS), is the principal DoW executive for finance and accounting requirements and procedures per DoD Directive 5118.05, and must:

15.1.2.1. Assist in providing the specific instructions and computer-based tools needed to identify, analyze, reconcile, track, and correct differences among written contracts, entitlement, disbursement, and related accounting systems. The instructions must include criteria for determining the nature and scope of required analyses.

15.1.2.2. Provide entitlement and accounting system information to individuals participating in settlement negotiations.

15.1.2.3. Train and maintain a core group of individuals who meet the qualification requirements to perform the responsibilities prescribed by the SCRT manual, including RCRAs, reconcilers, and assistants.

15.1.2.4. Designate qualified DFAS personnel to be trained as part of the core group, and assign RCRA personnel to oversee and perform contract reconciliations.

15.1.2.5. Ensure that the Systems Support Office-DFAS Columbus supports the RCRAs and maintains the SCRT, a DoW-wide database listing RCRAs, core group members, and contracts being reconciled. SCRT users receive help-desk support at disa.global.servicedesk.mbx.application-ticket-request@mail.mil.

15.1.3. Heads of DoW Components that use ERP systems must provide data to support and coordinate contract reconciliation functions performed under DFAS direction.

15.1.4. All RCRA reconciliation partners (procurement contracting officers (PCOs), administrative contracting officers (ACOs), resource managers, and program managers) must perform their respective or combined duties as follows:

15.1.4.1. Participate in contract reviews and reconciliations, and assist in identifying and resolving differences among written contracts and entitlement, disbursement, and accounting systems.

15.1.4.2. Compare the contract ACRNs with data in the entitlement and accounting systems. When discrepancies occur, notify the appropriate entitlement and accounting office of any significant differences, and that office must provide the required supporting documentation.

15.1.4.3. Respond in a timely manner to reasonable requests for action, information, or documentation on a contract or modification.

15.1.4.4. Designate personnel from the DoW Components to be trained as part of the core group that oversees and performs contract reconciliations.

15.2    CONTRACT RECONCILIATION

15.2.1. Normally, at contract end, total payments to the contractor should match total funds obligated on the contract. When unexplained remaining or excess fund balances exist, reconciliation may be required to compare all source documents with the entitlement and accounting systems. MOCAS contracts must be forwarded to DFAS Columbus for reconciliation.

The designated entitlement office that administers payments must perform Non-MOCAS contract reconciliations. See the SCRT manual for reconciliation request guidance.

15.2.2. When a discrepancy between contract payments and accounting records is identified, the appropriate RCRA or designated entitlement office must perform a preliminary contract review to determine the needed corrective action. Qualified personnel must review and approve recommended adjustments before distribution to the appropriate locations for processing. Approved adjustments must be posted in a timely manner. The SCRT must identify reconciled records by registration, and any later adjustment of reconciled records must be based on a reconciliation registration per paragraph 3.5. All contract reconciliation actions must support the timely completion of funds review, deobligation of excess funds, and contract closeout under FAR
4.804. The related requirements for researching and correcting NULOs, UMDs, disbursements in suspense accounts, and disbursements in-transit are in Volume 3, section 11.0.

15.2.3. DoW Components must prioritize the analyses of discrepant conditions in view of applicable time limitations and other circumstances. High-priority conditions include those involving congressional or senior DoW management interest, potential ADA violations, prevalidation problems, insufficient funds for payment, suspected or identified overpayments, the highest-dollar-value transactions, and cancelling or closing-year appropriations.

15.2.4. Each contract nominated for reconciliation must be registered in the SCRT database of contracts being reconciled. Resources, procedural guidance, forms, and other reconciliation tools for the registration process are available from DFAS Columbus Accounts Payable - MOCAS, Reconciliation Division at dfas.dscc.jai.mbx.recon-maillog@mail.mil. For more on reconciliation tools, see paragraph 15.2.6.

15.2.5. The individual assigned to perform contract reconciliation, whether a Government employee or contractor, must compare databases; research differences among systems to determine whether errors exist, where they exist, the extent of those errors, and the required corrective actions; identify root causes; and recommend the adjustments needed to correct differences among contract, entitlement, and accounting records. The reconciler should make every effort to complete contract reconciliations within 90 days after initiation.

15.2.6. Documents accumulated during a contract reconciliation must be retained, made available for, and subject to internal review and audit.
