A waiver application that includes arguments about validity or amount may be returned without action or denied.

5.11.3. Application Filed by a Representative. A waiver application submitted by the debtor's agent or attorney must include a duly executed power of attorney or other documentary evidence of the agent's or attorney's right to act for the debtor.

5.11.4. Application Filed by a Guardian for Minor/Incompetent Debtors. If a guardian or committee has been appointed for a debtor who is a minor or incompetent person, the waiver application filed on the debtor's behalf must include a court certificate showing the appointment and qualification of the guardian or committee. If no guardian or committee has been appointed, the application submitted on the debtor's behalf must:

5.11.4.1. State the applicant’s relationship to the minor or incompetent person;

5.11.4.2. Provide the name and address of the person having care and custody of the minor or incompetent person; and

5.11.4.3. Include an affirmation that any money received will be applied to the use and benefit of the minor or incompetent person and that the appointment of a guardian or committee is not contemplated.

5.12 Suspension of Debt Collection Pending Waiver Determination. Collection of a debt should not routinely be suspended pending a waiver determination (refer to 31 CFR 903.2(c)(2)). The DCO must determine, in each case, whether suspension of collection under 31 CFR 903.2, or a delay in collection action, is appropriate based on the following criteria:

5.12.1. Waiver will likely be granted,

5.12.2. Erroneous payment can be recovered if waiver is not granted, or

5.12.3. Collection of the debt would cause undue financial hardship.

5.13 Standards for Reviewing Requests for Waiver. Standards for determining the appropriateness of a waiver are in DoWI 1340.23. Appropriateness depends on the facts of each case. Generally, a person who receives an erroneous payment from the U.S. Government acquires no right to the money and is bound in equity and good conscience to make restitution; if the payment was made by mistake, however careless the Government's act, the recipient must make restitution. A waiver is not a matter of right and is available only as equitable relief when warranted by the individual case. Economic or financial considerations play no role in the determination.

5.13.1. Indication of Fraud, Misrepresentation, Fault, or Lack of Good Faith. A waiver may be granted only when collection would be against equity and good conscience and not in the best interests of the United States. There must be no indication the erroneous payment resulted, in whole or in part, from the applicant's fraud, misrepresentation, fault, or lack of good faith.

5.13.1.1. Generally, a waiver is precluded when the individual, or another person with an interest in obtaining a waiver, receives a significant, unexplained increase in pay or allowances, or otherwise knows or reasonably should know an erroneous payment occurred and fails to inquire or notify appropriate officials. A waiver may be inappropriate even if the recipient inquires or notifies appropriate officials and is mistakenly advised the payment is proper. A Government administrative error is not, by itself, a sufficient basis for granting a waiver.

5.13.1.2. An individual does not acquire title to amounts paid erroneously and should hold the excess for eventual repayment to the U.S. Government. DOHA has held that a waiver will not be granted if the debtor had records (such as LESs) that, if reviewed, would have indicated an overpayment, and the debtor failed to review them for accuracy or otherwise failed to take corrective action. Such failure renders the debtor partially at fault and ineligible for a waiver.

5.14    Action of the DCMO or Designated Waiver Authority

5.14.1. If the aggregate debt is not more than $1,500 for civilian employees or $10,000 for military or National Guard members, the DCMO may grant or deny part or all of a waiver application.

5.14.2. If the aggregate debt is more than $1,500 for civilian employees or $10,000 for military or National Guard members, the DCMO must do the following:

5.14.2.1. Deny the waiver application in its entirety; or

5.14.2.2. Refer the waiver application to DOHA for its consideration, along with a recommendation that part or all of the debt be waived.

5.15 Appeal of Waiver Denial. Per DoWI 1340.23, a debtor may appeal the denial of a waiver application. The appeal must be submitted to the DCMO, or the designated waiver authority that made the determination, within 30 calendar days of receipt of the written denial. The DCMO may extend this period up to an additional 30 calendar days for good cause; no appeal will be accepted after that time expires. The DCMO must review the appeal and forward it to DOHA, and the debtor must submit the appeal to the DCMO rather than directly to DOHA. DOHA will review the appeal and affirm, modify, or reverse the DCMO's initial determination.

5.16    Waiver of SBP Overpayments

5.16.1. Authority. Recovery of debts resulting from erroneous SBP payments may be waived under 10 U.S.C. 1453. The Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller) delegated this waiver authority to the DFAS Director by memorandum dated February 1, 1991 (see DoWD 5118.05). The DFAS DCMO exercises this authority on behalf of the Director. Refer to the PGI for information on submitting and reviewing requests for waiver due to SBP overpayment.

5.16.2. Debts Not Eligible for Waiver. Debts resulting from unpaid SBP premium payments are not eligible for waiver under this provision.

5.16.2.1. Time Limit for Filing Application. Debtors must submit a waiver application within 3 years from the date the erroneous payment was discovered. The date of discovery is the date an appropriate official first determined an erroneous payment was made, typically the date the debt notification was issued. This timeframe cannot be extended or waived.

5.16.2.2. Contesting the Debt. By applying for waiver of a debt, an individual acknowledges no intent to dispute the debt's validity or amount. A waiver is not the forum to contest validity or amount; to contest validity or amount, an individual must petition for a hearing under section 3.0. A waiver application that argues validity or amount may be denied as ineligible for consideration.

5.16.2.3. Application Filed by Representative. If an annuitant has a representative payee authorized to receive payments under Volume 7B, Chapter 46, paragraph 2.2, the representative may submit a waiver application if the representative also holds legal authority to act for the annuitant. The representative must submit additional documentation the DCMO requires, such as a power of attorney or other evidence of the right to act for the debtor.

5.16.3. Suspension of Collection Pending Waiver Determination. Collection of a debt should not routinely be suspended pending a waiver determination (see 31 CFR 903.2(c)(2)). The DCO will determine case-by-case whether a formal suspension of collection under 31 CFR 903.2 is necessary or whether an informal delay in collection action is appropriate, based on the following criteria:

5.16.3.1. Whether the waiver will likely be granted,

5.16.3.2. Whether the erroneous payment can be recovered if waiver is not granted, or

5.16.3.3. Whether collection of the debt would cause undue financial hardship.

5.16.4. Standards for Reviewing Requests for Waiver. Waiver of the recovery of an SBP annuity overpayment may be appropriate when the debtor is not at fault, and recovery of the overpayment would be contrary to the purposes of SBP, or against equity and good conscience. The appropriateness of granting a waiver will depend on the facts of each particular case. Pursuant to Comptroller General (Comp. Gen.), B-133142 (1978), B-178696 (1978), the standards for reviewing a request for waiver of SBP annuity overpayment are the same as those used for considering waiver requests under 10 U.S.C. § 2774 and 5 U.S.C. § 5584. DFAS DCMO uses the standards set out in DoWI 1340.23 for considering waiver applications for debts resulting from SBP annuity overpayments. Refer to paragraph 8.5 for a discussion of the standards used in waiver application determinations.

5.16.5. Refund of Amounts Collected. Any amount collected before DFAS-IN receives the debtor’s waiver application will not be refunded. A refund is not authorized by law. If a waiver is granted, amounts collected after DFAS-IN received the completed waiver application from the annuitant may be refunded to the annuitant. Refer to Comp. Gen. B-184532 (1975) for information on when refund is appropriate.

5.16.5.1. Who May Appeal. A waiver applicant may appeal the DCMO's denial of all or part of a request to waive SBP annuity overpayments under 10 U.S.C. 1453. An applicant may also appeal the denial of a waiver application not received by DFAS within the required time limit.

5.16.5.2. Determining Official. The determining official on all appeals is a DFAS official assigned to review the DCMO's initial waiver determination. Under subparagraph 8.2.1 and 10 U.S.C. 1453, DFAS has delegated full authority to consider all waivers, including appeals and requests for reconsideration. Refer to the PGI for information on submission and adjudication of appeals.

5.16.5.2.1. Time Limit for Requesting Reconsideration. An applicant may ask the determining official to reconsider the final written determination of the appeal. A request for reconsideration must be received within 30 days from the date of that determination. This period may be extended up to an additional 30 days for good cause. The determining official must review any rebuttal submitted in support of the request and issue a written determination. Refer to the PGI for information on the review of requests for reconsideration.

5.16.5.2.2. The reconsideration response is a final action.

5.17 Other Waiver Authority. Other waiver authority may apply to payments that were not erroneously paid. The agency component generally exercises this authority. A debt from a non- erroneous payment may be eligible for waiver under the following statutory authorities:

5.17.1. Voluntary Separation Incentive Payment and Reemployment (5 U.S.C. § 3524(c)),

5.17.2. Employee Agreements, Service after Training (5 U.S.C. § 4108(c)),

5.17.3. Student Loan Repayments (5 U.S.C. § 5379(c)(3)),

5.17.4. Recruitment and Relocation Bonuses (5 U.S.C. § 5753(e)),

5.17.5. Quarters Allowances (5 U.S.C. § 5922(b)),

5.17.6. Physicians Comparability Allowances (5 U.S.C. § 5948(e)), or

5.17.7. Payments to Dependents of Missing Civilians (5 U.S.C. § 5566(g)).

5.18    Remission or Cancellation of Indebtedness

5.18.1 Remission or Cancellation of Indebtedness Due From Military Members. Title 10 U.S.C. 7837, 10 U.S.C. 8271, and 10 U.S.C. 9837 authorize remission or cancellation of indebtedness due from a military member. Remission or cancellation is limited to debts from overpayments of active duty pay and is not available for debts from overpayments of military retired pay. This authority may be exercised for any debt incurred on or after October 7, 2001. Title 32 U.S.C. 710(c) provides remission or cancellation for National Guard members. Remission or cancellation under these statutes is not available to DoW civilian employees.

5.18.2 Submission of Request for Remission or Cancellation. Requests for remission or cancellation from members of the Army, Air Force, Navy, Marine Corps, National Guard, or Space Force must be submitted on forms the respective Services designate and forwarded to the Service for processing. DFAS does not process remission or cancellation requests for any Service.

5.19    Indebtedness Which May Be Remitted or Cancelled

5.19.1. Debts to the United States. Generally, any indebtedness may be considered for remission or cancellation. Denial of a waiver under 10 U.S.C. 2774 does not preclude a member from applying for remission or cancellation of the debt. Debts arising from an erroneous payment of basic pay due to non-collection of court-martial forfeitures may not be remitted or cancelled.

5.19.2. Debts Within Jurisdiction of Military Service Concerned. The debt must be a debt over which the Military Department concerned has jurisdiction. For example, the Secretary of one Military Department may not remit a member's indebtedness for liability for damage to property of another Military Department.

5.20    Additional Options for Debt Relief

5.20.1 Claim for Refund. A military member may file a written claim on a DD Form 827, Application for Arrears in Pay, for any amounts considered erroneously collected from the member's pay account. The member must submit the form to the member's pay office or, if separated for more than a year, to DFAS-IN/JFEC, Department 3300 (ATTN: Claims), 8899 East 56th Street, Indianapolis, IN 46249-3300, or submit a ticket. If the claim is denied in whole or in part, the member may appeal to DOHA under 32 CFR 282, Appendix E.

5.20.2 Correction of Military Records. The Secretary of a Military Department, under procedures that Secretary establishes and the Secretary of Defense approves, and acting through boards of civilians of the executive part of that Military Department, may correct any military record of that department when the Secretary concerned considers it necessary to correct an error or remove an injustice. If an individual is owed money from a record correction, any earnings from civilian employment, self-employment, or an income-protection plan for that employment during the period active duty pay and allowances are payable must be deducted from the settlement. To the extent authorized by law and regulation, a settlement must be reduced by the amount of any existing indebtedness the individual owes the Government arising from military service. See Volume 7B, Chapter 10 for additional guidance on correction of records.

title: Section 6.0: Collection of Debts Owed by Contractors
content:
6.0    COLLECTION OF DEBTS OWED BY CONTRACTORS
The term Debt Collection Office (DCO), as used in this section, refers to vendor pay offices, contracting offices, and any other office that processes contractor debts. The DCO does not refer to the Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) Debt Management Office
(DMO).

6.1    Collection Actions

6.1.1 Contract Debts. Contract debts result from amounts that have been paid to the contractor, to which the contractor is not entitled under the terms and conditions of the contract, or amounts otherwise due from the contractor. For a list of what is considered a contract debt, refer to the PGI.

6.1.1.1 Once a contractor might be indebted to the DoW, the contracting officer or the payment office must issue a demand for payment to the contractor, provide an opportunity to inspect relevant records, and provide an opportunity to request a review of the debt as set forth in
Section 2.

6.1.2. Demand Letters. Demand letters must comply with the requirements in Section 2. The notice of indebtedness to a contractor must state that, per OMB Circular A-123, Appendix C, Part III, high-dollar overpayments may be reported on the Federal Government's improper payment website. Refer to Volume 4, Section 14 for the definition of a high-dollar overpayment.

6.1.2.1. The contracting officer has primary responsibility for determining the debt amount and ensuring collection for most types of contract debts, except debts resulting from payment-office errors. Refer to the PGI for a list of required suppoting documentation, and dollar referral thresholds, for debts referred to the DCO or DMO.

6.1.2.2. When a contracting officer or other authorized official requests that a payment office collect a debt and provides a copy of the contract, including the payment dates and amounts due from the contractor, the payment office must collect the debt.

6.1.2.3. If the contracting officer or other designated official receives the contractor's payment, that official must immediately forward the payment to the disbursing office with a request for confirmation of receipt.

6.1.2.4. The appropriate DoW Component contracting officer, or other designated official, must determine the debt amount and demand repayment for debts pursuant to FAR 32.6 and DFARS 232.6.

6.1.2.5. The contracting officer must send a copy of each demand for payment, and documentation identifying the line of accounting for distribution of the principal amount of the debt, to the payment office cited in the contract so the Accounts Receivable Office (ARO) applies the funds correctly.

6.1.2.6. The contracting officer must periodically follow up with the DCO, ARO, or supporting accounting office to ensure contract debts are collected and credited to the proper appropriations.

6.1.2.1. Payment offices are designated to make payments under a contract and to receive payments for amounts due to DoW. Payment offices must determine the amount of contract debts resulting from overpayments or erroneous payments and initiate collection action on those debts.

6.1.2.2. The payment office must also collect contractor debts when the amounts due and payment dates are in the contract and a copy of the contract has been furnished to the payment office with notice to collect as amounts become due.

6.1.2.3. When a contract modification (downward adjustment) issued after the date of a disbursement causes a contract to be in overpayment status, the result of that modification is not an erroneous payment for purposes of this Section. The payment office must contact the procuring or administrative contracting officer who issued the modification to ensure a demand letter is sent to the contractor for collection of funds.

6.2    Administrative Offset

6.2.1 To the extent practicable, debts must be collected by voluntary lump-sum repayment or by administrative offset of payments the DoW owes the contractor, unless an installment agreement is in place or a deferment of collection has been approved (FAR 32.607). If 30 days have elapsed since the due date in the demand for payment and no payment has been received, the DCO must offset the contractor's indebtedness against other monies owed to the contractor.

6.2.2. FAR 32.606 allows offsetting contractor payments to liquidate debts owed by the contractor. If additional payments are scheduled under the same contract, the DCO must administratively offset against those payments first. The DCO must coordinate with the payment office to apply administrative offsets against amounts due the contractor under other contracts if offset against the contract that gave rise to the debt cannot be accomplished. The disbursement voucher must be approved and the accounting classification charged for the total entitlement amount without regard to the deduction. The DCO must prominently annotate the face of the voucher, or the electronic equivalent, with the amount withheld and the accounting classification credited so that only the net amount is paid to the contractor, and the voucher must adequately inform the payee of the reason for the deduction.

6.2.3. Administrative offsets normally will not be taken when there is a valid assignment of claims, under the Assignment of Claims Act of 1940 (31 U.S.C. § 3727 and 41 U.S.C. § 6305), associated with the contractor. DCO personnel should seek guidance from their legal office, as appropriate, in determining whether an administrative offset may be taken when an assignment of claims exists.

6.2.4. Pursuant to 31 U.S.C. § 3716, and in accordance with 31 CFR 901.3(b)(2), a DCO must process an administrative offset to collect a debt when the name and TIN of a payee matches the name and TIN of a debtor, and all other requirements for administrative offset have been met.

6.3    Credit Invoice

6.3.1. A contractor may request to liquidate a debt against existing unpaid bills due to the contractor. As an exception, DCOs may accept a credit invoice only under special circumstances, and only when a current payable invoice exists to which the credit can be applied. On request, the contractor should furnish the DCO an invoice number, date, and the amount of the debt to be offset against the invoice, per the credit invoice.

6.3.3. If a contractor does not state that the credit-invoice amount can be deducted from other amounts due, the DCO must determine the most effective manner to collect the debt. In making this determination, DCOs must weigh both the relative costs DoW would incur under various options and the method expected to liquidate the debt at the earliest date. That latter factor depends on the expected volume and frequency of incoming invoices susceptible to administrative offset, and whether that option is more effective and efficient than a credit invoice.

6.3.4. DCOs must acknowledge receipt of the credit invoice and inform the contractor of its disposition. If direct remittance is required, the acknowledgment must state that DoW cannot accept the document as liquidation of the indebtedness and must ask the contractor to remit a check to the applicable address. The contractor may instead identify an invoice to offset. Receipt of a credit invoice by the due date stated in the demand letter does not preclude charging interest and administrative charges.

6.4    Installment Payment Plans

6.4.1 General. Whenever possible, payment to liquidate a debt, including a deferred payment, must be made in one lump sum. When a contractor establishes sufficient justification, the DCO may approve a series of installment payments to liquidate the debt within a reasonable period. Per 31 CFR 901.8, installment payments should be sufficient in size and frequency to liquidate the debt within 3 years. If the contractor requests a repayment term of more than 3 years, the DCO must refer the request to the DMO for a determination.

6.4.2 Installment Payment Approval Authority. The DMO is the approval authority for a contractor's installment-agreement request. The DMO may not deny a request without first obtaining consent from the creditor DoW Component's senior financial manager (FM) or designee. In that case, the DMO must send the request to the creditor Component's senior FM or designee within 3 working days after receiving the request.

6.4.3 Installment Payment Notification. The DMO must make installment agreements available to the office that referred the debt and to the creditor DoW Component's senior FM or designee.

6.5    Referral of Delinquent Debts to DMO

6.5.2 Delinquent Debts

6.5.2.1. DCOs must refer valid and legally enforceable debts that are equal to or greater than the thresholds in paragraph 5.1, individually or in aggregate, to the DMO no later than 90 days after the date on the debt notification. The DCO must validate debts before referral to the DMO. The DMO must annotate acceptance of the debt in the appropriate system, making the information available to the DCO and the supporting accounting office that maintains the official accounting records. Administrative charges may be assessed for the expenses of referring the debt.

Delinquent debts incurred under FAR 51.102 may be referred back to the authorizing agency if not satisfied by the contractor. Refer to the PGI for a list of required supporting documentation.

6.5.2.2. When referring a debt to the DMO, DCOs must submit the documentation listed in the PGI.

6.5.2.3. After referral, the DMO has full responsibility for collecting the delinquent debt. Accounting and reporting do not transfer to the DMO; they remain with the servicing accounting office, which uses status information the DMO provides. The DMO maintains only a memorandum accounts receivable record. Any office other than the DMO that receives a payment after referral must notify the DMO of the receipt and disposition within 3 business days. The ARO must notify the FM representative of the cognizant DoW Component when the debt should be closed. For dual-negotiated checks, the DMO must also notify the accountable payment office.

6.6    Referral of Debts to Treasury

6.6.1. The DMO must refer valid and legally enforceable debts delinquent more than 120 days to Treasury for debt collection and cross-servicing. While a debt is at Treasury, the DMO retains overall responsibility for tracking and monitoring it and must recall any uncollected debt with enough time to refer it to the Department of Justice for potential litigation or to write it off and close it out.

6.6.2. Components that have implemented the DDMG should refer delinquent debt over $25 directly to Fiscal Service, Debt Management Services for further collection action where applicable.

6.7    DISPUTES AND DEFERMENTS UNDER THE CDA

6.7.1 Under the Contract Disputes Act of 1978 (41 U.S.C., Chapter 71), a contractor may appeal a decision of indebtedness to the Armed Services Board of Contract Appeals (ASBCA) or through the U.S. courts. Actions filed under the Disputes Clause do not suspend or delay collection unless the contractor has been granted a deferment under paragraph 6.3 or has entered an installment payment plan under section 4.0. Interest, penalties, and fees continue to accrue on uncollected debts that have been formally disputed.

6.7.2 Crediting Collections in Dispute

6.7.2.1. When an amount, including interest and administrative fees, is collected from a contractor and the contractor formally disputes the debt, DoW must not account for the collected amount as settlement of the debt. The disputed amounts must remain available pending disposition of the dispute, and interest, penalties, and fees no longer accrue because the debt has been collected. The collection must be documented as a disputed contract collection; for example, debts collected by DFAS are coded as disputed in the Contract Debt System.

6.7.2.2. The payment office typically handles collection of a debt. If another office, including the ARO, supporting accounting offices, the DMO, contracting officers, contract administration officers, or legal offices, receives a payment against an existing debt, that office must forward the payment to the relevant DCO immediately.

6.7.2.3. The DCO and the responsible payment office must notify the contracting officer, the contract administration officer if applicable, the Service or agency contract finance officer, or another authority of any matters affecting the disputed collections. Those officers or offices must also inform the responsible payment office and the DCO of any actions taken that affect the disputed collection.

6.8    Deferments

6.8.1. Under the CDA of 1978, a contractor may appeal a decision of indebtedness to the ASBCA or through the U.S. court system. In accordance with FAR 32.607, the contractor may request, in writing, deferment of debt repayment until the appeal is decided.

6.8.2. In accordance with FAR 32.607, the contractor must submit the request for deferment to the contracting office.

6.8.3. The contracting office must promptly forward the deferment request to the appropriate DoW Component's senior FM or designee. The senior FM or designee must approve or deny the request and notify the contracting office and the DMO of the decision.

6.8.4. Collection of the debt must continue until the date the deferment is granted.

6.9    Write-Off and Close-Out of Accounts Receivable

6.9.1. Tax Reporting. The DFAS Tax Office will obtain information on all closed-out, uncollected public contractor debt. Per 26 U.S.C. 6050P, the Tax Office must issue debtors an Internal Revenue Service Form 1099-C, Cancellation of Debt, if the closed, uncollected debt is $600 or more for the calendar year.

6.10    BANKRUPTCY

6.10.1. Within DoW, the DFAS Office of General Counsel (OGC) will file contractor bankruptcy proofs of claim. DFAS-OGC is not responsible for litigating contractor bankruptcies; the litigation function remains with the DoW Component and is accomplished by the Department of Justice through the responsible U.S. Attorney. Per FAR subpart 42.9, the actions detailed in paragraphs 8.1 through 8.6 will be taken when the procuring contracting office or contract administration office receives notice of bankruptcy from the contractor or another source. Refer to the PGI for additional guidance on bankruptcy, to include notification requirements.

title: Section 7.0: Debt Owed to the DoW by Foreign Entities
content:
7.0    DEBT OWED TO THE DOW BY FOREIGN ENTITIES

7.1 DoW policy is to conduct timely, aggressive debt collection action, with follow-up as necessary, to ensure debt owed to the DoW by a foreign entity is collected and held to the absolute minimum. All collection activities related to foreign-entity indebtedness, including all Acquisition and Cross-Servicing Agreement (ACSA) debt, must comply with the applicable agreement or treaty with the foreign entity.

7.2 For purposes of this section, a foreign entity does not include foreign individuals or foreign vendors and will only refer to the following definitions:

7.2.1. Any government of a foreign country, and any subdivision, agency, or instrumentality thereof, including all foreign “official” institutions, even those located in the U.S.;

7.2.2. Any private relief, philanthropic, or other organization of a multinational or regional character with headquarters abroad; and

7.2.3. Any official multinational organization, defined as any international or regional organization (or affiliated agency thereof), created by treaty or convention between sovereign states.

7.3 Foreign-entity indebtedness means financial obligations owed to the U.S. Government by a foreign entity, as defined for purposes of this section. Foreign-entity indebtedness includes Foreign Military Sales (FMS) arrearages, accounts receivable for goods and/or services provided (where specified, includes goods and/or services provided through the ACSA program), and erroneous payments made to foreign entities. Foreign-entity indebtedness does not include principal payments or interest on short-term and long-term loans and credits.

7.4 This section establishes policy for DoW Components to identify, bill, collect, and manage foreign-entity indebtedness, including FMS and non-FMS. It does not establish policy for non-FMS fuel debts, foreign fuel exchange agreement debts, foreign direct bills, or FMS fuel debts. Unpaid debts related to fuel agreements, including Replacement-in-Kind/Equal Value Exchange settlements, foreign direct bills, and FMS, must be billed and elevated through the Defense Logistics Agency - Finance Energy (subparagraph 3.1.3.2 and paragraph 3.2 do not apply).

7.5    Billing AND FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS

7.5.1 Non-FMS, Foreign-Entity Debt

7.5.2. Due Date. All non-FMS foreign-entity debt is due 30 days from the date of the bill/demand letter, unless otherwise stated in the bill, contract, or agreement between the DoW Component and the foreign entity. The bill/demand letter must include a 60-day grace period. The debt becomes delinquent 91 days from the date of the bill/demand letter.

7.5.2.1. The ARO must prepare and send initial billings and notifications for goods and services for all non-FMS foreign-entity debt. The ARO must include the information listed in subparagraph 7.5.2.2 in the initial debt notification accompanying the bill.

7.5.2.2. The ARO must prepare and send the initial demand for non-FMS foreign- entity debts (see Exhibit 6-1 for a sample demand letter). The demand letter must include, at a minimum, the following information:

7.5.2.2.1. The basis for and amount of the indebtedness;

7.5.2.2.2. The date by which payment must be made in full;

7.5.2.2.3. The address where payment should be sent or information regarding submission of electronic payment;

7.5.2.2.4. The name, address, and telephone number of a point of contact in the ARO who can discuss alternative methods of payment; and

7.5.2.2.5. Any available documentation that substantiates the debt.

7.6    FMS Accounts Receivable

7.6.1. For sales from stock, AECA Section 21(b) (22 U.S.C. 2761) requires DoW to collect payments from foreign purchasers in advance or, if the President determines it to be in the national interest, upon delivery of a defense article or rendering of a defense service. After such a Presidential determination to bill upon delivery, interest must be charged under AECA Section 21(d) (22 U.S.C. 2761(d)) on any net amount due and payable that is not paid within 60 days after the date of billing.

7.6.2. The President delegated authority to determine if billing upon delivery is in the national interest in Executive Order 13637, and the Secretary of Defense further delegated the authority to the Director, DSCA, in DoW Directive 5105.65. The President may extend the period to 120 days upon determining that emergency requirements of the purchaser will exceed the ready availability of purchaser funds within the 60 days, submitting a determination with a special emergency request for authorization and appropriation of additional funds to finance such purchases under the AECA.

7.6.3. For sales from procurements (items sent directly from the source, not from DoW inventories), when the country is authorized a dependable undertaking, AECA Section 22(a) (22 U.S.C. 2762(a)) requires DoW to collect payments from foreign purchasers in time to meet contractual payments, including any damages and costs that may accrue from cancellation of such contracts. AECA Section 22(a) requires interest to be charged on any net amount by which a foreign purchaser is in arrears, considering all of its outstanding unliquidated dependable undertakings.

7.6.4. Due Date. Refer to Volume 15, Section 8 for policy regarding FMS billing due dates.

7.6.5. Initial Billing. DFAS SCA is responsible for issuing FMS billing documents. Billings for financial requirements must be initiated using the DD 645 or the special billing statement approved by DSCA. These billings must, at a minimum, identify the financial requirements, amount paid, and amount due. Specific policy on FMS billings is in Volume 15,
Section 8.

7.6.5.1. When the amount due per the DoW billing statement is not paid by the due date, that amount is considered delinquent, but that does not necessarily constitute an arrearage.

7.6.5.2. For FMS cases authorized to include a term of sale of "Payment on Delivery," and for FMS purchasers authorized “dependable undertaking” terms of sale, an arrearage occurs when the FMS purchaser’s total cash resources on deposit with the U.S. Government are insufficient to cover all its outstanding, billed amounts, unliquidated dependable undertakings, considered collectively. Reference Volume 15, Section 4, subparagraph 3.1.2 for information on dependable undertaking.

7.6.5.3. FMS purchasers are required to pay in advance of performance unless the President determines it to be in the national interest to collect upon delivery of the defense article or the rendering of the defense service. Refer to 22 U.S.C. § 2761. Therefore, in the FMS program, an arrearage is an unusual event.

7.7    INTEREST, ADMINISTRATIVE CHARGES, AND PENALTIES FOR FMS
ARREARAGES

7.7.1 Interest must be charged on FMS arrearages under 22 U.S.C. 2761(d) and 22 U.S.C. 2762(a). The final determination on assessing interest on FMS arrearages resides with DSCA. The interest rate is the rate set by the Secretary of the Treasury under the AECA (not less than a rate based on the current average market yield on outstanding short-term U.S. obligations as of the last day of the month preceding the net arrearage), computed from the date of net arrearage; the applicable rate is published by Treasury (see the FMM). For disposition of interest collected, refer to Volume 4, Section 3. Non-FMS foreign debts owed by any sovereign state are exempt from interest, administrative charges, and penalties. Refer to the PGI for additional information on assessing interest.

7.8    REFERRAL OF FMS INDEBTEDNESS

7.8.1 Authority to Refer FMS Indebtedness. DSCA must determine if an FMS arrearage will be forwarded to DOJ for litigation.

7.9 Preservation of Evidence. The ARO, DFAS PM, DoW Component, and DSCA must retain all files and records that may be needed by DOJ to prove the case in court. Refer to Volume 1, Section 9 for additional information on record retention.

7.10    COMPROMISE, SUSPENSION, OR TERMINATION OF COLLECTION ACTIONS
FOR FMS ARREARAGES DFAS SCA,

In cooperation with the DoW Component, must coordinate proposals to compromise, suspend, or terminate collection actions on FMS arrearages with DSCA. Refer to Section 2 for policy on compromise, suspension, or termination of collection actions.

7.11    WRITE OFF AND CLOSE OUT OF FMS ARREARAGES DSCA

DSCA is responsible for initiating and coordinating all actions necessary to write off and close out FMS arrearages. Refer to Volume 4, Section 3, paragraph 4.7 for write-off and closeout requirements.

7.12    REPORTING FOREIGN INDEBTEDNESS

7.12.1. Foreign indebtedness must be uniformly and accurately reported through appropriate reporting channels to Treasury and Commerce.

7.12.2. Required Reports

7.12.2.1. Grants, Loans, Credits, and Contingent Liabilities Involving Foreigners. The TFM, Volume I, Part 2, Chapter 4500 requires electronic submission of several reports on foreign obligors to Treasury by the 45th day following the end of the reporting quarter, if applicable. DFAS Security Assistance Accounting (SAA) Departmental prepares and submits these reports, extracting the data from the DSCA FMS Credit System. The TFM, Volume I, Part 2, Chapter 4500 provides detailed guidance, report formats, and submission instructions.

7.12.2.2. Data Editing. DFAS SAA Departmental must complete the quarterly data editing and approval process using Treasury's Foreign Credit Reporting System (FCRS) within 2 weeks after receiving notification that the reporting period data is available for editing. The FCRS Web Site Overview and Data Editing Guide for Agency Users contains instructions for the quarterly data editing and approval process. A list of the required reports may be found in the
PGI.

7.12.3. Preliminary Case Analysis Report of FMS Arrearages. The National Advisory Council (NAC) monitors major foreign arrearages. A major foreign arrearage is any country- program arrearage involving the sum of $250,000 or more. Periodically, DSCA will request a Preliminary Case Analysis Report (PCAR) from DFAS to satisfy NAC requirements. DFAS submits the PCAR directly to DSCA by email. The report must reflect any foreign arrearages so a determination can be made on whether interest should be charged.

7.12.4. Collecting and Reporting Foreign Debts Under Long-Term Loans and Debts. DSCA is responsible for administering FMS long-term loans and credit programs authorized by 22 U.S.C. 2763 and for determining foreign arrearages against these programs.

title: Section 8.0: Interest, Penalties, and Administrative (IPA) Charges
content:
8.0    INTEREST, PENALTIES, AND ADMINISTRATIVE (IPA) CHARGES

8.1    INTERNAL CONTROLS

All organizations that collect and manage IPA charges must follow the internal-control standards in DoW Instruction 5010.40, "Managers’ Internal Control Program Procedures," to ensure IPA charges owed to the DoW are managed and collected per this section and other applicable regulatory and statutory requirements.

8.2    APPLICATION OF CHARGES

Title 31, CFR, section 901.9 contains guidance on assessing IPA charges. Unless prohibited by law, IPA charges will be applied accordingly. Refer to Volume 4, Section 3 for requirements on the disposition of IPA charges.

8.3 All debts owed to the Government and not paid in full by the due date specified in the debt notification letter will accrue IPA charges back to the original date of the debt notification, and in accordance with 31 U.S.C. § 3717. These charges will continue to accrue until the debt is paid in full or otherwise resolved through suspension, compromise, termination, or the IPA charges are waived. Debts owed by any federal agency, or nonappropriated fund instrumentality, are exempt from IPA charges.

8.4    Interest Charges

Per to 31 U.S.C. 3717, interest rates must be established for each loan receivable and overdue debt from the public. The factors that affect the variability of interest rates (e.g., legislation, type of contract, an occurrence of an event, passage of time, debtor's income level, or federal funds rate) must be identified. In the absence of specific authority embodied in statute, regulation required by statute, contract, or other public notice, the interest rate, at a minimum, will be the same rate as the Current Value of Funds Rate (CVFR) established by the Secretary of the Treasury. Interest may not be compounded or assessed on administrative costs or penalties.

8.5    Penalty Charges

DoW Components must accrue and assess a penalty charge, not to exceed 6 percent per annum, on any portion of a debt delinquent more than 90 days from the date of the debt notification, including interest and administrative charges. A debt becomes delinquent if not paid by the established due date; therefore, penalty charges must be applied to those accounts reported in the aging category 91-180 days delinquent and beyond. This does not include current payments made under an agreed-upon installment plan or through salary offset. Components may determine what percentage, up to the maximum 6 percent, to apply to delinquent accounts. A Component must document its rationale for charging a lesser amount and make it part of the official debt file.

8.6    Administrative Charges

Components must calculate administrative charges based on the actual costs incurred to process and handle delinquent debt. If actual cost is not available, a Component may base the administrative charge on other historical costs or cost analyses, as long as the method used supports the charge and is documented in the official debt file. An administrative charge will be applied to all delinquent debts with due regard given to the length of time the debts are delinquent.

8.7    WAIVER OF ACCRUAL OF IPA CHARGES

8.7.1 Under 31 U.S.C. 3717(h), the DCO may waive IPA charges in whole or in part, either using the compromise standards in 31 C.F.R. 902.2 or when collecting IPA charges is against equity and good conscience (such as when charging IPA would cause the debtor undue financial hardship) or is not in the best interest of the United States (see also 31 CFR 901.9(g)). A DCO may waive IPA on its own or at a debtor’s request, and may waive IPA only in part. For example, circumstances may justify waiving penalties, which penalize untimely payment, but not interest and administrative costs, which compensate the Government. A DCO must make a decision on whether or not to waive IPA charges in accordance with the guidelines in paragraph 4.2.

8.8    Guidelines

8.8.1. IPA charges may be waived only after the DCO determines that a waiver is appropriate, including at the time the debt is terminated or compromised.

8.8.2. DoW Components must decide whether to waive the accrual and assessment of IPA charges on a case-by-case basis. Blanket waivers that waive IPA on an entire class of debts are not appropriate. Decisions on IPA waivers must be documented, include an explanation as to the reasons for the waiver, and retained as a part of the official debt file.

8.8.3. The same organizational level, or the same designee, authorized to approve compromises, write off indebtedness, or approve requests for waiver or remission of indebtedness, depending on the disposition of the basic debt, is authorized to approve waiver of the accrual of IPA charges.

8.8.4. Accrued IPA charges will be collected, reported, compromised, or written off in the same manner as the basic debt.

8.9    Write-Ooff of Accrued IPA Charges

When a debt is written off, the accrued IPA charges must also be written off. Write-off must be done in accordance with Office of Management and Budget Circular A-129. Volume 4,
Section 3 contains additional requirements on debt write-off.

L0:234.200-70 Definitions.

title: 234.201-70 Policy
content:
L0:234.201-70 Policy.
L1:(a) Applicability. Except for the exemption at paragraph (j) of this section, DoD applies the earned value management system requirement as follows:
L2:(1) For cost or incentive contracts and subcontracts valued at $50 million or more, the clause at 252.234-7999, Earned Value Management System, requires the contractor’s earned value management system to comply with the guidelines in Electronic Industries Alliance Standard 748, Earned Value Management Systems (EIA-748).
L2:(2) For cost or incentive contracts and subcontracts valued at $100 million or more, the clause at 252.234-7999, Earned Value Management System, requires the contractor to have an earned value management system that the cognizant Federal agency has determined to comply with the guidelines in EIA-748.
L2:(3) For cost or incentive contracts and subcontracts valued at less than $50 million—
L3:(i) The application of earned value management is optional and is a risk-based decision;
L3:(ii) Document the decision to apply earned value management in the contract file; and
L3:(iii) Follow the procedures at PGI 234.201(a)(3) for conducting a cost-benefit analysis.
L2:(4) For firm-fixed-price contracts and subcontracts of any dollar value—
L3:(i) The application of earned value management is discouraged; and
L3:(ii) Follow the procedures at PGI 234.201(a)(4) for obtaining a waiver before applying earned value management.
L1:(b) Review procedures. When an offeror proposes a plan for compliance with the earned value management system guidelines in EIA-748, follow the review procedures at PGI 234.201(b).
L1:(c) Defense Contract Management Agency responsibility. The Defense Contract Management Agency is responsible for determining earned value management system compliance when DoD is the cognizant Federal agency.
L1:(d) Additional guidance. See PGI 234.201(d) for additional guidance on earned value management.
L1:(e) Acceptability. The cognizant contracting officer, in consultation with the functional specialist, must—
L2:(1) Determine the acceptability of the contractor's earned value management system and approve or disapprove the system; and
L2:(2) Pursue correction of any weaknesses or deficiencies.
L1:(f) Compliance with system criteria. In evaluating the acceptability of a contractor's earned value management system, the contracting officer, in consultation with the functional specialist, must determine whether the contractor's earned value management system complies with the system criteria for an acceptable earned value management system as prescribed in the clause at 252.234-7999, Earned Value Management System.
L1:(g) Disposition of findings. (1) Reporting of findings. The functional specialist must document and report all findings and recommendations to the contracting officer. If the functional specialist identifies any material weakness in the contractor's earned value management system, the report must include detailed descriptions of the weaknesses or deficiencies.
L2:(2) Initial determination. (i) The contracting officer must review all findings and recommendations and, if no material weaknesses exist, must promptly notify the contractor, in writing, that the contractor's earned value management system is acceptable and approved; or
L3:(ii) If the contracting officer finds that one or more material weaknesses exist due to the contractor's failure to meet one or more of the earned value management system criteria in the clause at 252.234-7999, the contracting officer must—
L4:(A) Promptly make an initial written determination of any material weaknesses and notify the contractor, in writing, providing a description of each material weakness in sufficient detail to allow the contractor to understand the weaknesses (see PGI 234.201(g)(2));
L4:(B) Request the contractor to respond, in writing, to the initial determination within 30 days; and
L4:(C) Evaluate the contractor's response to the initial determination, in consultation with the functional specialist, and make a final determination.
L2:(3) Final determination. (i) The contracting officer must make a final determination and notify the contractor, in writing, that—
L4:(A) The contractor's earned value management system is acceptable and approved, and no material weaknesses remain; or
L4:(B) Material weaknesses remain. The contracting officer must identify any remaining material weaknesses and indicate the adequacy of any proposed or completed corrective action, and—
L4:(1) Request that the contractor, within 45 days of receipt of the final determination, either correct the deficiencies or submit an acceptable corrective action plan showing milestones and actions to eliminate the weaknesses;
L4:(2) Disapprove the system in accordance with the clause at 252.234- 7999 when initial validation is not successfully completed within the timeframe approved by the contracting officer, or the contracting officer determines that the existing earned value management system contains one or more material weaknesses in the EIA-748 standard guidelines.
L4:(3) Withhold payments in accordance with the clause at 252.242- 7998, Contractor Business Systems, if the clause is included in the contract.
L3:(ii) Follow the procedures relating to monitoring a contractor's corrective action and the correction of material weaknesses at PGI 234.201(g)(3).
L1:(h) System approval. The contracting officer must promptly approve a previously disapproved earned value management system and notify the contractor when no remaining material weaknesses exist.
L1:(i) Contracting officer notifications. The cognizant contracting officer must promptly distribute copies of a determination to approve a system, disapprove a system and withhold payments, or approve a previously disapproved system and release withheld payments to the functional specialist; payment office; affected contracting officers at the buying activities; and cognizant contracting officers in contract administration activities.
L1:(j) Exemptions. (1) General. Do not apply this subpart to contracts—
L3:(i) Primarily for software, including those using a software acquisition pathway in accordance with DoD Instruction 5000.87, Operation of the Software Acquisition Pathway; or
L3:(ii) Awarded to nontraditional defense contractors.
L2:(2) Waiver relating to nontraditional defense contractors. The head of the contracting activity may waive the exemption relating to nontraditional defense contractors by written determination that applying the requirement for an earned value management system to a nontraditional defense contractor is in the best interest of DoD. The HCA may delegate this authority to no lower than the chief of the contracting office.

title: 234.7202 Procedures
content:
L0:234.7202 Procedures.
L1:(a) Selection of contract type for major acquisition programs at Milestone B. For major defense acquisition programs at Milestone B—
L2:(1) The milestone decision authority (MDA) must select, with the advice of the contracting officer, the contract type for a development program at the time of Milestone B approval or, in the case of a space program, Key Decision Point B approval;
L2:(2) The acquisition strategy must document the basis for the contract-type selection. The documentation—
L3:(i) Must include an explanation of the level of program risk; and
L3:(ii) If program risk is determined to be high, must outline the steps taken to reduce program risk and the reasons for proceeding with Milestone B approval despite the risk; and
L2:(3) If the MDA selects a cost-reimbursement type contract, include in the contract file the MDA's written determination that—
L3:(i) The program is so complex and technically challenging that reducing program risk to a level that would permit the use of a fixed-price type contract is impracticable; and
L3:(ii) The complexity and technical challenge of the program does not result from failure to meet the requirements of 10 U.S.C. 4251.
L1:(b) Use of cost-reimbursement line items for production of major defense acquisition programs. (1) Do not use cost-reimbursement line items for the acquisition of production of major defense acquisition programs. See also PGI 234.7202(b) regarding additional contract-type approval requirements.
L2:(2) The prohibition at paragraph (1) does not apply where the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment (USD(A&S)), or the MDA when the MDA is the service acquisition executive of the military department that is managing the program, submits to the congressional defense committees—
L3:(i) A written certification that the cost-reimbursement line items are needed to provide a required capability in a timely and cost-effective manner; and
L3:(ii) An explanation of the steps taken to ensure that cost-reimbursement line items are used only to achieve the purposes of the exception.
L2:(3) Include, as applicable, in the contract file a copy of the congressional certification described in paragraph (2).
L1:(c) Low-rate initial production associated with major defense acquisition programs.
L2:(1) Do not procure more than one lot for low-rate initial production, as described at 10 U.S.C. 4231, associated with a major defense acquisition program if—
L3:(i) The MDA authorizes the use of a fixed-price type contract at the time of Milestone B approval; and
L3:(ii) The scope of work of the fixed-price type contract includes both the development and low-rate initial production of items for such major defense acquisition program.
L2:(2) The service acquisition executive may waive this limitation, delegable to no lower than one level above the contracting officer, if—
L3:(i) The service acquisition executive provides a written notification of the waiver, including associated rationale, to the congressional defense committees no later than 30 days after issuance of the waiver; and
L3:(ii) Include a copy of the waiver and such congressional notification in the contract file.
L1:(d) Sustainment criteria for weapons systems. (1) As provided by the program manager, include clearly defined measurable criteria for engineering activities and design specifications for reliability and maintainability in solicitations and resulting contracts for the technical maturation and risk reduction phase, the engineering and manufacturing development phase or the production phase of a weapon system, including embedded software.
L2:(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), if the program manager has determined that such criteria should not be included as described in paragraph (d)(1) of this section, include a copy of the justification, executed by the program manager, in the contract file.
L1:(e) Development and demonstration of initial or additional prototype units. (1) Subject to the limitations in paragraph (e)(2) of this section, a contract initially awarded from the competitive selection of a proposal resulting from a broad agency announcement (see 235.102) may include—
L3:(i) A line item or contract option using funds not limited to those identified in 235.102 for the development and demonstration or initial production of technology developed under the contract; or
L3:(ii) The delivery of initial or additional items if the item or a prototype thereof is created as the result of work performed under the contract.
L2:(2)(i) The line item or contract option must require only the minimal quantity of initial or additional items or prototypes that will allow for timely competitive solicitation and award of a follow-on development or production contract for those items.
L3:(ii) The term of the line item or contract option must not exceed 2 years.
L3:(iii) The dollar value of the work to be performed pursuant to the line item or contract option must not exceed $100 million in fiscal year 2017 constant dollars.
L2:(3) See PGI 234.7202(e) regarding the benefits derived from use of this competitive selection method.
L1:(f) Limitation on fixed-price options for low-rate initial production. (1) For a cost-reimbursement contract for the development of a major system, do not procure more than one lot for low-rate initial production, as described at 10 U.S.C. 4231, using fixed-priced options.
L2:(2) This limitation is subject to waiver upon a determination that such waiver is in the best interest of DoD issued by—
L3:(i) The service acquisition executive on a non-delegable basis; or
L3:(ii) In the case of a joint program, the Secretary of Defense, delegable to no lower than a service acquisition executive.

title: 252.234-7998 Notice of Earned Value Management System. (DEVIATION 2026-O0011)
content:
L0:252.234-7998 Notice of Earned Value Management System. (DEVIATION 2026-O0011)
L0:As prescribed in 234.203-70(a), use the following provision:
L0:NOTICE OF EARNED VALUE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (AUG 2026) (DEVIATION 2026-O0011)
L1:(a) If the offeror submits a proposal in the amount of $100 million or more—
L2:(1) The offeror must provide documentation that the Cognizant Federal Agency (CFA) has determined that the proposed Earned Value Management System (EVMS) complies with the EVMS guidelines in the Electronic Industries Alliance Standard 748, Earned Value Management Systems (EIA-748). (current version at time of solicitation). The Government reserves the right to perform reviews of the EVMS when deemed necessary to verify compliance.
L2:(2) If the offeror proposes to use a system that has not been determined to be in compliance with the requirements of paragraph (a)(1) of this provision, the offeror must submit a comprehensive plan for compliance with the guidelines in EIA-748.
L3:(i) The plan must—
L4:(A) Describe the EVMS the offeror intends to use in performance of the contract, and how the proposed EVMS complies with the EVMS guidelines in EIA-748;
L4:(B) Distinguish between the offeror's existing management system and modifications proposed to meet the EVMS guidelines;
L4:(C) Describe the management system and its application in terms of the EVMS guidelines;
L4:(D) Describe the proposed procedure for administration of the EVMS guidelines as applied to subcontractors; and
L4:(E) Describe the process the offeror will use to determine subcontractor compliance with EIA-748.
L3:(ii) The offeror must provide information and assistance as required by the Contracting Officer to support review of the plan.
L3:(iii) The offeror's EVMS plan must provide milestones that indicate when the offeror anticipates that the EVMS will be compliant with the guidelines in EIA-748.
L1:(b) If the offeror submits a proposal in an amount less than $100 million—
L2:(1) The offeror must submit a written description of the management procedures it will use and maintain in the performance of any resultant contract to comply with the requirements of the Earned Value Management System clause of the contract. The description must include—
L3:(i) A matrix that correlates each guideline in EIA-748 (current version at time of solicitation) to the corresponding process in the offeror's written management procedures; and
L3:(ii) The process the offeror will use to determine subcontractor compliance with EIA-748.
L2:(2) If the offeror proposes to use an EVMS that has been determined by the CFA to be in compliance with the EVMS guidelines in EIA-748, the offeror may submit a copy of the documentation of such determination instead of the written description required by paragraph (b)(1) of this provision.
L1:(c) The offeror must identify the subcontractors (or the subcontracted effort if subcontractors have not been selected) to whom the EVMS requirements will apply. The offeror and the Government will agree to the subcontractors or the subcontracted effort selected for application of the EVMS requirements. The offeror will be responsible for ensuring that the selected subcontractors comply with the requirements of the Earned Value Management System clause of the contract.
L1:(d) This provision does not apply to nontraditional defense contractors, as defined in DFARS 202.101.
L0:(End of provision)

title: 252.234-7999 Earned Value Management System. (DEVIATION 2026-O0011)
content:
L0:252.234-7999 Earned Value Management System. (DEVIATION 2026-O0011)
L0:As prescribed in 234.203-70(b), use the following clause:
L0:EARNED VALUE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (AUG 2026) (DEVIATION 2026-O0011)
L1:(a) Definitions. As used in this clause—
L1:Acceptable earned value management system means an earned value management system that generally complies with the system criteria in paragraph (b) of this clause.
L1:Earned value management system means a system that complies with the earned value management system guidelines in Electronic Industries Alliance Standard 748, Earned Value Management Systems (EIA-748).
L1:Material weakness means a deficiency or combination of deficiencies in the internal control over information in contractor business systems, such that there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of such information will not be prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis. A reasonable possibility exists when the likelihood of an event occurring is—
L2:(1) Probable; or
L2:(2) More than remote but less than likely (section 806 of Pub. L. 116-283).
L1:(b) System criteria. In the performance of this contract, the Contractor must use—
L2:(1) An Earned Value Management System (EVMS) that complies with the EVMS guidelines in the Electronic Industries Alliance Standard 748, Earned Value Management Systems (EIA-748); and
L2:(2) Management procedures that provide for generation of timely, reliable, and verifiable information for the cost and schedule reporting data items required by this contract.
L1:(c) If this contract has a value of $100 million or more, the Contractor must use an EVMS that has been determined to be acceptable by the Cognizant Federal Agency (CFA). If, at the time of award, the Contractor's EVMS has not been determined by the CFA to be in compliance with the EVMS guidelines as stated in paragraph (b)(1) of this clause, the Contractor must apply its current system to the contract and must take necessary actions to meet the milestones in the Contractor's EVMS plan.
L1:(d) If this contract has a value of less than $100 million, the Government will not make a formal determination that the Contractor's EVMS complies with the EVMS guidelines in EIA-748 with respect to the contract. The use of the Contractor's EVMS for this contract does not imply a Government determination of the Contractor's compliance with the EVMS guidelines in EIA-748 for application to future contracts. The Government will allow the use of a Contractor's EVMS that has been formally reviewed and determined by the CFA to be in compliance with the EVMS guidelines in EIA-748.
L1:(e) The Contractor must submit notification of any proposed substantive changes to the EVMS procedures and the impact of those changes to the CFA. If this contract has a value of $100 million or more, unless a waiver is granted by the CFA, any EVMS changes proposed by the Contractor require approval of the CFA prior to implementation. The CFA will advise the Contractor of the acceptability of such changes as soon as practicable (generally within 30 calendar days) after receipt of the Contractor's notice of proposed changes. If the CFA waives the advance approval requirements, the Contractor must disclose EVMS changes to the CFA at least 14 calendar days prior to the effective date of implementation.
L1:(f)(1) The Government will schedule integrated baseline reviews as early as practicable, and the review process will be conducted not later than 180 calendar days after—
L3:(i) Contract award;
L3:(ii) The exercise of significant contract options; and
L3:(iii) The incorporation of major modifications.
L2:(2) During such reviews, the Government and the Contractor will jointly assess the Contractor's baseline to be used for performance measurement to ensure complete coverage of the statement of work, logical scheduling of the work activities, adequate resourcing, and identification of inherent risks.
L1:(g) The Contractor must provide access to all pertinent records and data requested by the Contracting Officer or duly authorized representative as necessary to permit Government surveillance to ensure that the EVMS complies, and continues to comply, with the performance criteria referenced in paragraph (b) of this clause.
L1:(h) When indicated by contract performance, the Contractor must submit a request for approval to initiate an over-target baseline or over-target schedule to the Contracting Officer. The request must include a top-level projection of cost and/or schedule growth, a determination of whether or not performance variances will be retained, and a schedule of implementation for the rebaselining. The Government will acknowledge receipt of the request in a timely manner (generally within 30 calendar days).
L1:(i) Material weaknesses. (1) The Contracting Officer will provide an initial determination to the Contractor, in writing, of any material weaknesses. The initial determination will describe the underlying deficiency in sufficient detail to allow the Contractor to understand the weakness or deficiency.
L2:(2) The Contractor must respond within 30 days to a written initial determination from the Contracting Officer that identifies material weaknesses in the Contractor's EVMS. If the Contractor disagrees with the initial determination, the Contractor must state, in writing, its rationale for disagreeing.
L2:(3) The Contracting Officer will evaluate the Contractor's response and notify the Contractor, in writing, of the Contracting Officer's final determination concerning—
L3:(i) Remaining material weaknesses;
L3:(ii) The adequacy of any proposed or completed corrective action;
L3:(iii) System noncompliance, when the Contractor's existing EVMS fails to comply with the earned value management system guidelines in the EIA-748; and
L3:(iv) System disapproval, if initial EVMS validation is not successfully completed within the timeframe approved by the Contracting Officer.
L2:(4) If the Contractor receives the Contracting Officer's final determination pursuant to paragraph (i) of this clause, the Contractor must, within 45 days of receipt of the final determination, either correct the material weaknesses or submit an acceptable corrective action plan showing milestones and actions to eliminate the material weaknesses.
L1:(j) Withholding payments. If the Contracting Officer makes a final determination to disapprove the Contractor's EVMS, and the contract includes the clause at 252.242- 7998, Contractor Business Systems, the Contracting Officer will withhold payments in accordance with that clause.

title: 235.170 Contracting methods and contract type

title: 240.270-1 Scope
content:
L0:240.270-1 Scope.
L0:This section implements section 1656 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2018 (Pub. L. 115-91) and section 889(a)(1)(A) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2019 (Pub. L. 115-232).

title: 240.270-2 Definitions
content:
L0:240.270-2 Definitions.
L0:As used in this section—
L1:Covered defense telecommunications equipment or services means—
L2:(1) Telecommunications equipment produced by Huawei Technologies Company or ZTE Corporation, or any subsidiary or affiliate of such entities;
L2:(2) Telecommunications services provided by such entities or using such equipment; or
L2:(3) Telecommunications equipment or services produced or provided by an entity that the Secretary of Defense reasonably believes to be an entity owned or controlled by, or otherwise connected to, the government of a covered foreign country.
L1:Covered foreign country means—
L2:(1) The People's Republic of China; or
L2:(2) The Russian Federation.
L1:Covered missions means—
L2:(1) The nuclear deterrence mission of DoD, including with respect to nuclear command, control, and communications, integrated tactical warning and attack assessment, and continuity of Government; or
L2:(2) The homeland defense mission of DoD, including with respect to ballistic missile defense.

title: 240.270-3 Prohibition
content:
L0:240.270-3 Prohibition.
L0:In addition to the prohibition at FAR 40.202(d), unless the covered defense telecommunications equipment or services are subject to a waiver described in 240.270-5 the contracting officer must not procure or obtain, or extend or renew a contract (e.g., exercise an option) to procure or obtain, any equipment, system, or service to carry out covered missions that uses covered defense telecommunications equipment or services as a substantial or essential component of any system, or as critical technology as part of any system.

title: 240.270-4 Procedures
content:
L0:240.270-4 Procedures.
L1:(a) Representations.
L2:(1) (i) If the offeror selects “does not” in response to the provision at 252.204-7016, the contracting officer may rely on the representation, unless the contracting officer has an independent reason to question the representation. If the contracting officer has a reason to question the “does not” representation in 252.204-7016, then the contracting officer must consult with the requiring activity and legal counsel.
L3:(ii) If the offeror selects “does” in paragraph (c) of the provision at 252.204-7016, the offeror must complete the representation at 252.204-7017.
L2:(2)(i) If the offeror selects “will not” in paragraph (d) of the provision at 252.204-7017, the contracting officer may rely on the representation, unless the contracting officer has an independent reason to question the representation. If the contracting officer has a reason to question the “will not” representation in FAR 52.240-90 or 252.204-7017, then the contracting officer must consult with the requiring activity and legal counsel.
L3:(ii) If an offeror selects “will” in paragraph (d) of the provision at 252.204-7017, the offeror must provide the information required by paragraph (e) of the provision. When an offeror completes paragraph (e) of either of the provisions at FAR 52.240-90 or 252.204-7017, the contracting officer must—
L4:(A) Forward the offeror's representation and disclosure information to the requiring activity; and
L4:(B) Not award to the offeror unless the requiring activity advises—
L4:(1) For equipment, systems, or services that use covered telecommunications equipment or services as a substantial or essential component of any system, or as critical technology as part of any system, that a waiver as described at FAR 40.203-3 has been granted; or
L4:(2) For equipment, systems, or services to be used to carry out covered missions that use covered defense telecommunications equipment or services as a substantial or essential component of any system, or as critical technology as part of any system, that a waiver as described at 240.270-5 has been granted.
L1:(b) Reporting. If a contractor reports information to https://dibnet.dod.mil in accordance with the clause at FAR 52.240-91 or 252.204-7018, the Defense Cyber Crime Center will notify the contracting officer, who will consult with the requiring activity on how to proceed with the contract.

title: 240.270-5 Waivers
content:
L0:240.270-5 Waivers.
L0:The Secretary of Defense may waive the prohibition in 240.270-3 on a case-by-case basis for a single, one-year period, if the Secretary—
L1:(a) Determines such waiver to be in the national security interests of the United States; and
L1:(b) Certifies to the Congressional defense committees that—
L2:(1) There are sufficient mitigations in place to guarantee the ability of the Secretary to carry out the covered missions; and
L2:(2) The Secretary is removing the use of covered defense telecommunications equipment or services in carrying out such missions.
